Ōanamuchi-no-Mikoto and Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto joined forces to make the land, and established methods of treating illness for people and livestock and rites of spell-casting to ward off calamities caused by birds, beasts, and insects. Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto departed for the Eternal Land (常世郷) from the cape of Kumano (or, flung off by a millet stalk at 淡嶋 (reading unconfirmed)), and Ōanamuchi-no-Kami finished making the rest alone. The 幸魂 and 奇魂 (sakimitama and kushimitama) of Ōanamuchi-no-Kami, which appeared lighting up the sea, wished to dwell on Mount 三諸山 (reading unconfirmed) in the land of 日本 (Yamato); this is the deity of 大三輪 (reading unconfirmed), whose child was Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto (姫蹈鞴五十鈴姫命), who became the consort of Emperor 神日本磐余彦火火出見 (reading unconfirmed), according to the account (which also gives alongside this a tradition that Kotoshironushi-no-Kami (事代主神) became an eight-fathom bear-wani (八尋熊鰐), visited a woman, and begot her). Finally it tells how a small man who appeared in a boat made of the bark of 白蘞 was found to be Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto, child of Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto (高皇産霊尊).

dan09.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 2 — Age of the Gods (part 2)
dan09.title: The Pacification of the Central Land of Reed Plains and the Descent of the Heavenly Grandson (Section 9)
dan09.lead: Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto, wishing to make his grandson Ninigi-no-Mikoto (天津火瓊瓊杵尊) lord of the Central Land of Reed Plains, sends one envoy after another; at the demand of Futsunushi-no-Kami and Takemikazuchi-no-Kami, Ōanamuchi-no-Kami (大己貴神) withdraws from the land, and the imperial grandson descends to the peak of Takachiho in Hyūga. The main text and eight variant accounts transmit the story up to the point where the descended imperial grandson takes 鹿葦津姫 (reading unconfirmed; Konohanasakuya-hime, 木花之開耶姫) as wife and three children are born in a birth amid fire undertaken to clear his suspicion.

points.text: In the main text, the one who decides on sending the envoys and who covers the imperial grandson with the coverlet 眞床追衾 (reading unconfirmed) and sends him down is “the imperial ancestor” (皇祖) Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto; Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照太神) appears only by name in the genealogy at the beginning. In variant account 1, it is Amaterasu-Ōmikami who both gives the command to Ame-no-Wakahiko (天稚) and has the imperial grandson descend.

The envoys of the main text, Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto, his son 大背飯三熊之大人 (reading unconfirmed), and Ame-no-Wakahiko, in that order, all fail to report back, and finally Futsunushi-no-Kami and Takemikazuchi-no-Kami descend to the small beach of 五十田狹 (reading unconfirmed) in Izumo. Ōanamuchi-no-Kami, receiving the reply of his son Kotoshironushi-no-Kami, withdraws from the land, hands the two deities the broad spear (廣矛) he used when he pacified the land, and goes into hiding.

The three treasures (the Yasakani curved jewel, the Yata mirror, and the Kusanagi Sword), the accompaniment of the deities of the five groups (五部神), the command “coeternal with heaven and earth” (天壌無窮), and the exchange between the deity of the crossroads (衢神; Sarutahiko-no-Ōkami) and Ame-no-Uzume appear in variant account 1; the main text has no passage on the bestowal of the treasures. In variant account 2, Amaterasu-Ōmikami gives the treasured mirror to Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto (天忍穗耳尊) and commands that it be worshipped “on the same couch and in the same hall” (同床共殿).

In variant account 2, the transfer of the land is concluded when Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto shows Ōanamuchi-no-Kami that the imperial grandson will govern visible matters (顯露之事) while Ōanamuchi-no-Kami governs divine matters, and that the palace 天日隅宮 (reading unconfirmed) will be built and Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto made to worship him there. The same variant account contains the origin of short lifespans arising from the rejection of Iwanagahime (磐長姫) (Iwanagahime does not appear in the main text).

In the Kojiki, Amaterasu-Ōmikami and 高木神 (reading unconfirmed; Takamimusubi-no-Kami) give the command, Takemikazuchi-no-Kami (建御雷神) descends together with Ame-no-Torifune-no-Kami, and a contest of strength with Takeminakata-no-Kami is also told. In section 9 of the Nihon Shoki, the two deities who descend are Futsunushi-no-Kami and Takemikazuchi-no-Kami, and Takeminakata-no-Kami appears in neither the main text nor any variant account.

The deity-name database of Kokugakuin University notes that the story of the origin of short lifespans through Iwanagahime appears only in the Kojiki and in variant account 2 of the Nihon Shoki, and that the theory regarding it as the same type as the southern “banana type” tales, in which a choice is made between a stone and a banana, has become the established view. It also notes that whereas the Kojiki makes it a story about the lifespan of the emperors, an alternative version (一云) within variant account 2 makes it the origin of the short lives of humans in general.

story.text: 正哉吾勝勝速日天忍穗耳尊 (reading unconfirmed), the child of Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照太神), took as wife Takuhatachijihime (栲幡千千姫), daughter of Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto, and Ninigi-no-Mikoto (天津火瓊瓊杵尊) was born. The imperial ancestor Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto was especially fond of this grandson and thought to make him lord of the Central Land of Reed Plains. In that land, however, there were many deities that shone like the light of fireflies and evil deities as noisy as the buzzing of flies, and even the grasses and trees all spoke. Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto gathered the eighty deities and asked whom he should send, and he sent Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto, whom they all recommended, but Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto fawned on Ōanamuchi-no-Kami and did not report back even after three years. His son 大背飯三熊之大人 (also called 武三熊之大人; readings unconfirmed), who was sent next, also followed his father and likewise did not report back.

Next Ame-no-Wakahiko (天稚), son of 天國玉 (reading unconfirmed), was chosen, and he received the heavenly deer-bow (天鹿兒弓) and the heavenly feathered arrows (天羽羽矢) and descended. Ame-no-Wakahiko took as wife Shitateru-hime (下照姫), daughter of Utsushikunitama (顯國玉), and lived there, and, saying that he too wished to govern the Central Land of Reed Plains, did not report back. When Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto sent a nameless pheasant to find out how matters stood, the pheasant perched in the top of the many-branched 杜木 tree (湯津杜木) before Ame-no-Wakahiko's gate, and Ama-no-Sagume (天探女), seeing it, told Ame-no-Wakahiko. Ame-no-Wakahiko shot the pheasant dead with the bow and arrows he had received, and the arrow passed through the pheasant's breast and reached the place before Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto's seat. Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto saw the bloodied arrow and, thinking it might be because Ame-no-Wakahiko had fought with the earthly deities, threw it down; the arrow struck the breast of Ame-no-Wakahiko, who was lying asleep after the first-fruits festival, and Ame-no-Wakahiko died. This is said to be the origin of the saying people have, 「反矢可畏」 (“a returned arrow is to be feared”).

The sound of Shitateru-hime's weeping reached heaven, and 天國玉 (reading unconfirmed), learning that Ame-no-Wakahiko had died, had a swift wind carry the body up to heaven, built a mourning house, and held a temporary enshrinement (殯). He assigned the roles of the funeral to birds such as river geese and sparrows, and they wept and lamented for eight days and eight nights (a different arrangement of the birds' roles is also recorded in an “alternative version” (一云) in a small note). When Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami (味耜高根神), who had been close to Ame-no-Wakahiko, ascended to heaven to mourn, his appearance was the very image of Ame-no-Wakahiko, so the relatives, wife, and children clung to him, saying 「吾君猶在」 (“our lord is still alive”). Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami, angry at being mistaken for the dead, cut down the mourning house with the sword he wore, 大葉刈 (reading unconfirmed; also 神戶劔). The mourning house fell and became a mountain, and it is said that this is 喪山 (reading unconfirmed) at the upper reaches of the 藍見川 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Mino.

When Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto again consulted the deities, they all recommended Futsunushi-no-Kami. Then Takemikazuchi-no-Kami, the child of 熯速日神, who was the child of 甕速日神, who was the child of 稜威雄走神 (readings unconfirmed) dwelling in the Heavenly Rock Cave, came forward and asked whether Futsunushi-no-Kami alone was a brave warrior and he himself was not; so it was decided to have the two deities pacify the Central Land of Reed Plains. The two deities descended to the small beach of 五十田狹 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Izumo, thrust a ten-span sword upside down into the ground, squatted on its point, and asked Ōanamuchi-no-Kami whether he would withdraw from the land. Ōanamuchi-no-Kami said he would answer after asking his son, and sent the messenger 稻背脛 (reading unconfirmed) in the 熊野諸手船 (a many-oared boat of Kumano) to Kotoshironushi-no-Kami, who was enjoying fishing at the cape of 三穗 (reading unconfirmed). Kotoshironushi-no-Kami answered that his father should withdraw and that he himself would not resist; he built an eightfold fence of green brushwood (八重蒼柴籬) in the sea, stepped on the side of the boat (枻), and departed.

Ōanamuchi-no-Kami conveyed his son's words to the two deities and stated that he too would withdraw: if he resisted, the deities within the land would all resist with him, but if he withdrew, no one would oppose them. He then gave the two deities the broad spear he had used as a staff when he pacified the land, saying that if the Heavenly Grandson governed the land with this spear it would surely be at peace, and he went into hiding in 「百不足之八十隅」 (“the eighty corners, short of a hundred”). The two deities executed the demon-deities who would not submit and reported back. An “alternative version” (一云) in a small note holds that 香香背男 (reading unconfirmed), a star deity who refused to submit to the very end, was brought to submission by sending Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto (建葉槌命), the deity of 倭文 (reading unconfirmed).

Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto covered the imperial grandson Ninigi-no-Mikoto with the coverlet 眞床追衾 (reading unconfirmed) and sent him down. The imperial grandson left the heavenly rock seat (天磐座), pushed apart the eightfold clouds of heaven, and descended to the peak of Takachiho in 襲 (reading unconfirmed) in Hyūga. From there, by way of the Floating Bridge of Heaven (天浮橋) of 二上 (reading unconfirmed), he stood on a level place on a floating sandbank (浮渚在平處), and he proceeded along the hills through the barren, empty land in search of a country, arriving at the cape of 笠狹 at 長屋 in 吾田 (readings unconfirmed). A person there named 事勝國勝長狹 (reading unconfirmed) answered that there was a land here and that he should pass his time as he pleased, and the imperial grandson stayed there.

The imperial grandson met a beautiful woman of that land, 鹿葦津姫 (reading unconfirmed; also 神吾田津姫 and Konohanasakuya-hime, 木花之開耶姫), who declared that she was the child born when a heavenly deity took Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami (大山祇神) as wife. When the imperial grandson summoned her, she conceived in a single night, but the imperial grandson doubted, saying that he could not have made her conceive in one night and that the child was probably not his. Angered, she built a chamber without a door and entered it, vowed that if the child were not the Heavenly Grandson's it would be burned up, and if it were the Heavenly Grandson's the fire could not harm it, and set it on fire. When the smoke first rose, Honosusori-no-Mikoto (火闌降命; first ancestor of the Hayato and others) was born; while she was avoiding the heat, Hohodemi-no-Mikoto (火火出見尊) was born; and next Hoakari-no-Mikoto (火明命; first ancestor of the Owari no Muraji (尾張連) and others) was born. The children were three. Later Ninigi-no-Mikoto died and was buried in the 可愛之山陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum in Hyūga in Tsukushi.

quotes.note: This is the origin of people's saying that “a returned arrow is to be feared.”
Ōanamuchi-no-Kami's words as he withdraws from the land: “I shall now go into hiding in the eighty corners, short of a hundred (the distant recesses).”
Amaterasu-Ōmikami's command in variant account 1: the prosperity of the imperial throne shall be without end, together with heaven and earth.
Variant account 2: “My child, regard looking upon this treasured mirror as the same as looking upon me.”

figures.name: Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto (天穗日命)
figures.role: The first envoy. He fawned on Ōanamuchi-no-Kami and did not report back for three years (in variant account 2 he is regarded as the deity in charge of the worship of Ōanamuchi-no-Kami).

figures.name: 大背飯三熊之大人 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto and the second envoy. Also called 武三熊之大人. He followed his father and did not report back (a gloss gives the reading of 「大人」 as 「于志」).

figures.name: 天國玉 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of Ame-no-Wakahiko. Learning of his son's death from Shitateru-hime's weeping, he had the body carried to heaven and built a mourning house.

figures.name: Ama-no-Sagume (天探女)
figures.role: The one who found the pheasant and told Ame-no-Wakahiko (in variant account 1 regarded as an earthly deity, who urges him to shoot the pheasant). The reading follows the gloss 「阿麻能左愚謎」 in the original text.

figures.name: 稻背脛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The messenger sent to Kotoshironushi-no-Kami aboard the 熊野諸手船.

figures.name: 事勝國勝長狹 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The one at the cape of 笠狹 at 長屋 in 吾田 who answered the imperial grandson that there was a land. Variant account 4 makes him a child of Izanagi-no-Mikoto, with the other name Shiotsuchi-no-Oji (鹽土老翁).

figures.name: Honosusori-no-Mikoto (火闌降命)
figures.role: In the main text, the child born when the smoke first rose. Regarded as the first ancestor of the Hayato and others. The reading follows the gloss 「褒能須素里」 in the original text and the deity-name database.

figures.name: Honosuseri-no-Mikoto (火酢芹命)
figures.role: The name that appears in variant accounts 2, 6, and 8 in the position corresponding to Honosusori-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: Honosusumi-no-Mikoto (火進命)
figures.role: In variant accounts 3 and 5, the child said to have been born when the fire was at its height.

figures.name: Ame-no-Oshihi-no-Mikoto (天忍日命)
figures.role: In variant account 4, the deity who, as distant ancestor of the Ōtomo no Muraji, went before the Heavenly Grandson as armed vanguard.

figures.name: 天津甕星 (天香香背男) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In variant account 2, the evil deity of heaven whom the two deities first said they wished to execute. In the small note of the main text, as the star deity 香香背男, he is brought to submission by Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto, the deity of 倭文 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 1 — the sending of Takemikazuchi-no-Kami and Ōkuninushi-no-Kami's transfer of the land
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Ame-no-Torifune-no-Kami is attached to Takemikazuchi-no-Kami (建御雷神) and they descend to the small beach of 伊耶佐 (reading unconfirmed); after Kotoshironushi-no-Kami, Takeminakata-no-Kami challenges them to a contest of strength and flees as far as the sea of 州羽 in the province of 科野 (readings unconfirmed). In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, the ones who descend are Futsunushi-no-Kami and Takemikazuchi-no-Kami, and there is no story of Takeminakata-no-Kami.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 1 — the sending of Ame-no-Wakahiko (the funeral scene)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the father, wife, and children of Ame-no-Wakahiko (天若日子) come down from heaven and build the mourning house on that spot (on earth). In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, the body is carried to heaven by a swift wind, and the mourning house is built and the temporary enshrinement held in heaven.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 1 — the marriage of Ninigi-no-Mikoto
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami offers Iwanagahime (石長比売) in addition, and Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami himself states that because Iwanagahime was sent back, the lifespans of the children of the heavenly deities became short. In the main text of the Nihon Shoki Iwanagahime does not appear, and in variant account 2 it is Iwanagahime herself who, ashamed, utters the curse.

variants.name: Variant account 1
variants.text: It is Amaterasu-Ōmikami who gives the command; Ame-no-Wakahiko takes as wives many daughters of the earthly deities and does not report back for eight years, and a pheasant is sent on the plan of Omoikane-no-Kami. The heavenly deity throws the arrow back with the curse, “If he shot with an evil heart, let it strike Ame-no-Wakahiko,” and in the funeral scene two songs (rustic songs, 夷曲) by those gathered to mourn (in an “alternative version” (或云), by Shitateru-hime (下照媛), younger sister of Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami) are added. Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto looks down on the lower world from the Floating Bridge of Heaven and gives up descending; after the pacification by Takemikazuchi-no-Kami and Futsunushi-no-Kami, the imperial grandson who had been born descends in his place, accompanied by the three treasures and the deities of the five groups and having received the command “coeternal with heaven and earth”; on the way there is an exchange between the deity of the crossroads, Sarutahiko-no-Ōkami (猿田彦大神), and Ame-no-Uzume, and Ame-no-Uzume is given the title 猿女君 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Variant account 2
variants.text: The two deities first say they wish to execute the evil deity of heaven 天津甕星 (天香香背男) (reading unconfirmed). Ōanamuchi-no-Kami at first refuses, but after receiving a decree on such matters as the division between visible matters and divine matters, the building of the palace 天日隅宮 (reading unconfirmed), and Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto's being in charge of the worship, he complies, recommends Funato-no-Kami (岐神) as guide, and goes into hiding; Ōmononushi-no-Kami and Kotoshironushi-no-Kami submit, and Mihotsu-hime (三穗津姫) is given to Ōmononushi-no-Kami as wife. Amaterasu-Ōmikami bestows the treasured mirror and the rice ears of the sacred garden (齋庭之穂), the imperial grandson is born in mid-air and descends instead, and after Iwanagahime is rejected and the origin of short lifespans is told, Honosuseri-no-Mikoto (火酢芹命), Hoakari-no-Mikoto, and Hohodemi-no-Mikoto (火折尊, reading unconfirmed) are born in the birth amid fire.

variants.name: Variant account 3
variants.text: It gives the order of birth in the fire as Hoakari-no-Mikoto, when the fire first began to brighten; Honosusumi-no-Mikoto (火進命; Honosuseri-no-Mikoto), when the fire was at its height; and 火折火火出見尊 (reading unconfirmed), when avoiding the fire; and holds that mother and children were all unharmed. It adds that the umbilical cord was cut with a bamboo knife and that the discarded bamboo knife became a bamboo grove, so that the place was called 竹屋 (reading unconfirmed), and that heavenly sweet sake (天甜酒) was brewed from the rice of the 狹名田 (reading unconfirmed) fields that 神吾田鹿葦津姫 (reading unconfirmed) determined by divination.

variants.name: Variant account 4
variants.text: Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto wraps 天津國光火瓊瓊杵尊 (Ninigi-no-Mikoto) in the coverlet 眞床覆衾 (reading unconfirmed), opens the heavenly rock door (天磐戶), and sends him down. A point not in the main text is that Ame-no-Oshihi-no-Mikoto (天忍日命), distant ancestor of the Ōtomo no Muraji (大伴連), leading 天槵津大來目 (reading unconfirmed), distant ancestor of the 來目部 (reading unconfirmed), went before him as vanguard, bearing arms. 事勝國勝長狹 (reading unconfirmed) is made a child of Izanagi-no-Mikoto, with the other name Shiotsuchi-no-Oji (鹽土老翁).

variants.name: Variant account 5
variants.text: It makes the children born four, and from within the fire Hoakari-no-Mikoto, Honosusumi-no-Mikoto, 火折尊 (reading unconfirmed), and Hohodemi-no-Mikoto come out in turn, announcing their names. The Heavenly Grandson at first mocks the children, but later explains that, since there were those who doubted that she had conceived in a single night, he had done it to make everyone know that they were his children and that a heavenly deity can cause conception in one night, and that mother and children possess miraculous power.

variants.name: Variant account 6
variants.text: It makes the children of 天忍穗根尊 (reading unconfirmed) 天火明命 (reading unconfirmed) and 天津根火瓊瓊杵根尊 (reading unconfirmed), and makes Ame-no-Kagoyama (天香山), child of 天火明命, the distant ancestor of the Owari no Muraji and others. It transmits that the first nameless male pheasant stayed in the millet and bean fields and did not return (the origin of 「雉頓」), and that the next one, a female pheasant, was shot by Ame-no-Wakahiko; it gives the place of descent as the 添山 peak (reading unconfirmed) of Takachiho in 襲 (reading unconfirmed) in Hyūga, and the children born as Honosuseri-no-Mikoto and 火折尊 (Hohodemi-no-Mikoto). Because 豐吾田津姫 (reading unconfirmed) resented that the imperial grandson would not exchange words with her, the imperial grandson, troubled, composes a song.

variants.name: Variant account 7
variants.text: It has no story, and only lists variant genealogies. There are traditions such as one making 天之杵火火置瀨尊 (reading unconfirmed) the child of 天忍骨命 and 天萬栲幡千幡姫 (readings unconfirmed), and, as an “alternative version” (一云), a tradition making Hoakari-no-Mikoto, 火夜織命 (reading unconfirmed), and Hohodemi-no-Mikoto the children of 天杵瀨命 and 吾田津姫 (readings unconfirmed).

variants.name: Variant account 8
variants.text: It makes the children of 正哉吾勝勝速日天忍穗耳尊 (reading unconfirmed) and 天萬栲幡千幡姫 (reading unconfirmed) two: 天照國照火明命 (reading unconfirmed; distant ancestor of the Owari no Muraji and others) and 天饒石國饒石天津火瓊瓊杵尊 (reading unconfirmed). It holds that Ninigi-no-Mikoto (天津火瓊瓊杵尊) took Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto (木花開耶姫命) as wife and Honosuseri-no-Mikoto and Hohodemi-no-Mikoto were born, making the children two.

dan10.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 2 — Age of the Gods (part 2)
dan10.title: Sea-Luck and Mountain-Luck (Section 10)
dan10.lead: The younger brother Hohodemi-no-Mikoto (火火出見尊), having lost the fishhook of his elder brother Honosusori-no-Mikoto (火闌降命), goes with the help of Shiotsuchi-no-Oji (鹽土老翁) to the palace of Watatsumi-no-Kami (海神), the sea deity, returns with the hook and with the tide-flowing jewel (潮滿瓊) and the tide-ebbing jewel (潮涸瓊), and makes his elder brother submit. The main text and four variant accounts transmit the story up to the point where Toyotama-hime (豐玉姫), the sea deity's daughter, departs into the sea after being seen in the act of giving birth, and the child left behind is named 波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊 (Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto).

points.text: In the main text, the sea deity gathers the fish and questions them, and the hook is found in the mouth of 赤女 (reading unconfirmed; the name of a sea bream), which had not come because of an illness of the mouth. The sea deity instructed him to hand over the hook after secretly calling it a “poor hook” (貧鉤), gave him the tide-flowing jewel and the tide-ebbing jewel, and instructed him to drown his elder brother and to save him if he repented.

The elder brother Honosusori-no-Mikoto, in distress, admitted his offense, vowed to become “a people of performers” (俳優之民), and was pardoned; he is regarded as the original ancestor of the 吾田君小橋 (reading unconfirmed) and others. In variant account 2 this is told as the origin of his descendants the Hayato serving beside the palace fence by barking in place of dogs, and in variant account 4 as the origin of a performance imitating the elder brother's drowning, which has not died out even today.

Toyotama-hime's form when giving birth differs among the traditions: a “dragon” (龍) in the main text, an “eight-fathom great bear-wani” (八尋大熊鰐) in variant account 1, and an “eight-fathom great wani” (八尋大鰐) in variant account 3. In the main text, she wraps the child in grass, leaves it at the seashore, closes the way of the sea, and departs.

Variant account 4 alone reverses the brothers' luck, saying that the elder brother Honosuseri-no-Mikoto (火酢芹命) had the luck of the mountains and the younger brother 火折尊 (reading unconfirmed) the luck of the sea. It also has a scene in which the sea deity recognizes the Heavenly Grandson as the grandson of a heavenly deity by how he sits on the three couches in the sea deity's palace.

In the Kojiki, the elder brother is 火照命 (reading unconfirmed; ancestor of the Hayato 阿多君) and the younger brother 火遠理命 (reading unconfirmed); the fishhook is found in the throat of a red sea bream (赤海鯽魚), and Toyotama-hime (豊玉毘売) takes the form of an eight-fathom wani (八尋和迩). In the Nihon Shoki the elder brother is Honosusori-no-Mikoto or Honosuseri-no-Mikoto in every tradition, and the name of the elder brother made ancestor of the Hayato differs from the Kojiki.

The deity-name database of Kokugakuin University treats the framework of this story as a tale of the “lost fishhook type,” in which someone goes to another world to look for a lost fishhook, and introduces the observation that very similar tales are distributed in Indonesia and Micronesia. Regarding the scene of peeping at Toyotama-hime giving birth, it states that the leading theory sees it as a tale of a supernatural wife of the “Melusine type,” in which a wife whose “prohibition against looking” is broken departs.

story.text: The elder brother Honosusori-no-Mikoto originally had the luck of the sea, and the younger brother Hohodemi-no-Mikoto the luck of the mountains. The two tried exchanging their luck, but neither could get any catch. The elder brother, regretting it, returned the bow and arrows to the younger brother and asked for his own fishhook back, but the younger brother had already lost the hook. The younger brother forged his own cross-sword (横刀) into new hooks and gave them heaped in a winnowing basket, but the elder brother angrily said he would not accept them however many there were unless it was the original hook, and pressed him ever more harshly.

While Hohodemi-no-Mikoto was wandering by the seashore, deeply troubled, he met Shiotsuchi-no-Oji and told him the reason. The old man said there was no need to worry, made a basket without gaps, put him inside it, and sank it in the sea. He then arrived at a beautiful little beach, so he left the basket and went on, and at once arrived at the palace of the sea deity. The palace was well furnished with fences and towers; there was a well before the gate, and above it stood a many-branched 杜 tree (湯津杜樹) with thick branches and leaves.

As he stood lingering beneath that tree, a beautiful woman pushed open the door and came out, about to draw water with a jeweled vessel. Seeing him, the woman was startled and went back inside, and told her father and mother that there was an unusual guest beneath the tree before the gate. The sea deity spread out eightfold mats, welcomed him in, and asked why he had come. When he explained the circumstances in detail, the sea deity gathered the fish great and small and questioned them, and the fish answered that 赤女 (reading unconfirmed; the name of a sea bream) had lately not come because of an illness of the mouth. When 赤女 was summoned and its mouth searched, the lost hook was found.

He took the sea deity's daughter Toyotama-hime as wife and lived in the palace of the sea for three years, but there were times when he sighed, longing for his homeland. When Toyotama-hime heard this and told her father, the sea deity said to him that if he wished to return he would send him back, and gave him the hook that had been found. He then instructed him that when handing it to his elder brother he should first secretly call it a “poor hook” (貧鉤) and then hand it over; that if he soaked the tide-flowing jewel in water the tide would rise and he could drown his elder brother; and that if his elder brother repented and pleaded, he should soak the tide-ebbing jewel to make the tide recede and save him. At their parting, Toyotama-hime asked that, since she was pregnant and would come out to the seashore on a day of fierce wind and waves, he build a birthing hut and wait for her.

When Hohodemi-no-Mikoto, having returned to his palace, did as the sea deity had instructed, his elder brother Honosusori-no-Mikoto was tormented and admitted his offense, asking to be saved and saying that from now on he would be his people of performers. The younger brother granted his plea and pardoned his elder brother. Honosusori-no-Mikoto is regarded as the original ancestor of the 吾田君小橋 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

Later, as promised, Toyotama-hime braved the wind and waves and came to the seashore, bringing her younger sister Tamayori-hime (玉依姫). At the time of the birth, Toyotama-hime asked him not to look at her giving birth, but the Heavenly Grandson could not restrain himself and secretly peeped, and Toyotama-hime, in the midst of giving birth, had become a dragon. Toyotama-hime was deeply ashamed and said that, had she not been put to shame, she would have joined sea and land so that there was no barrier between them, but now that she had been shamed they could not form close ties; she wrapped the child in grass, left it at the seashore, closed the way of the sea, and departed. So the child was named 波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊 (Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto). Later Hohodemi-no-Mikoto died and was buried in the 高屋山上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum in Hyūga.

quotes.note: The words of the elder brother Honosusori-no-Mikoto: “From now on, I shall be your people of performers.”
Toyotama-hime, just as she was giving birth, had become a dragon.
Variant account 2: the Hayato and others serve (beside the palace fence) in place of barking dogs.
Variant account 4: this is the origin of sea and land not being connected with each other.

figures.name: Honosusori-no-Mikoto (火闌降命)
figures.role: In the main text, the elder brother who has the luck of the sea. He pressed his younger brother to return the hook, but in the end vowed to become a people of performers, and is regarded as the original ancestor of the 吾田君小橋 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: Honosuseri-no-Mikoto (火酢芹命)
figures.role: The name of the elder brother in variant accounts 1 to 4. In variant account 2 he is regarded as the one from whom originates the service of his descendants the Hayato, who bark in place of dogs.

figures.name: 火折尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The name of the younger brother in variant account 4 (here said to have had the luck of the sea).

figures.name: 鹽筒老翁 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In variant account 4, the old man who helped the younger brother and introduced him to the wani that the sea deity rides.

figures.name: 赤女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The fish that had not come because of an illness of the mouth, in whose mouth the hook is found. A small note in the main text says it is the name of a sea bream, and variant account 4 says a red sea bream (赤鯛).

figures.name: 口女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In variant accounts 2 and 4, the fish that had the hook in its mouth. Variant account 4 says it is a grey mullet (鯔魚).

figures.name: 一尋鰐 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In variant accounts 3 and 4, the one-fathom wani that delivered the Heavenly Grandson home within a single day.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 1 — the marriage of Ninigi-no-Mikoto (the birth of the three children) and the visit to the land of the sea deity
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the elder brother who, as 海佐知毘古 (the Sea-Luck Lad), quarrels with his younger brother is 火照命 (reading unconfirmed), and he is made the ancestor of the Hayato 阿多君 (reading unconfirmed). In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, the elder brother is Honosusori-no-Mikoto (in the variant accounts, Honosuseri-no-Mikoto), and he is regarded as the original ancestor of the 吾田君小橋 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 1 — the visit to the land of the sea deity (the instructions of Watatsumi-no-Kami)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the hook was stuck in the throat of a “red sea bream” (赤海鯽魚). In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, it is found in the mouth of 赤女 (reading unconfirmed; the name of a sea bream), which had an illness of the mouth, and in variant accounts 2 and 4 the name 口女 also appears.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 1 — the birth of Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Toyotama-hime takes the form of an eight-fathom wani (八尋和迩) and crawls on her belly, and later they exchange songs. The main text of the Nihon Shoki says she became a dragon, and the exchange of songs appears in variant account 3.

variants.name: Variant account 1
variants.text: The elder brother is Honosuseri-no-Mikoto. Shiotsuchi-no-Oji throws down a comb and makes it a bamboo grove, makes a basket from the bamboo and puts him into the sea, and at the sea deity's palace a beautiful woman attended by maidservants finds him. The sea deity instructs him to hand over the hook while reciting “貧窮之本。飢饉之始。困苦之根” (the root of poverty, the beginning of famine, the root of hardship); he returns riding on a great wani; Toyotama-hime, seen in the form of an eight-fathom great bear-wani, returns to the sea, leaving her younger sister Tamayori-hime to nurse the child; and the account makes the child's being born before the ridge of the birthing hut thatched with cormorant feathers was closed the origin of the child's name.

variants.name: Variant account 2
variants.text: He climbs the 杜 tree above the well, and Toyotama-hime, seeing his reflection in the well, drops her vessel and breaks it. The hook is found in the mouth of 口女 (reading unconfirmed; 赤女), and the sea deity decrees that 口女 shall not be able to swallow bait and shall not be served at the Heavenly Grandson's table. The elder brother, after once surrendering, goes back on his promise, and at last submits when the tide presses up over the mountains and trees; this is regarded as the origin of his descendants the Hayato and others still serving beside the palace fence by barking in place of dogs.

variants.name: Variant account 3
variants.text: After the younger brother rescues a river goose caught in a snare by the seashore, he arrives at the sea deity's palace in the small boat 無目堅間 (reading unconfirmed) made by Shiotsuchi-no-Oji, and is entertained on eightfold mats of sea-lion skins. The sea deity obtains the hook from the mouth of 鯛女 (reading unconfirmed), teaches him how to hand it over, has a one-fathom wani (一尋鰐魚), which declared it would take him in one day, carry him home, and instructs him that if his elder brother makes high fields he should make low-lying fields, and if his brother makes low-lying fields he should make high fields. Toyotama-hime comes riding a great turtle and is seen in the form of an eight-fathom great wani; she names the child herself and departs into the sea; and besides he and Toyotama-hime exchanging songs (擧歌), the origin of taking wet nurses to raise children is told.

variants.name: Variant account 4
variants.text: It holds that the elder brother Honosuseri-no-Mikoto had the luck of the mountains and the younger brother 火折尊 (reading unconfirmed) the luck of the sea; the one who helps is 鹽筒老翁 (reading unconfirmed), and on the advice of the eight-fathom wani that the sea deity rides, he rides a one-fathom wani into the sea. The sea deity knows him to be the Heavenly Grandson by the way he sits on the three couches, and the hook comes out of the mouth of 口女 (reading unconfirmed; a grey mullet, 鯔魚). The younger brother whistles to raise a wind and drowns his elder brother; the elder brother puts on a loincloth, smears his face and palms with red earth, performs an imitation of drowning, and vows to be a performer forever; Toyotama-hime wraps the child in the coverlet 眞床覆衾 (reading unconfirmed) and grass, leaves it at the water's edge, and departs, and this is regarded as the origin of sea and land no longer being connected.

dan11.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 2 — Age of the Gods (part 2)
dan11.title: The Birth of 神日本磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed) (Section 11)
dan11.lead: This is the last section of the Age of the Gods. It records that Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto (波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊) took his aunt Tamayori-hime (玉依姫) as consort, fathered four sons, Itsuse-no-Mikoto (五瀨命), 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed), Mikeirino-no-Mikoto (三毛入野命), and 神日本磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed), and died at the 西洲之宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. The main text is very short, and the four variant accounts transmit differences in the order and names of the four brothers.

points.text: Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto took as consort his aunt (his mother's younger sister) Tamayori-hime, and four sons were born: Itsuse-no-Mikoto, 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed), Mikeirino-no-Mikoto, and 神日本磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed). In the main text, 神日本磐余尊 is the youngest child.
The main text records that Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto died at the 西洲之宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace and was buried in the 吾平山上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum in Hyūga.

The four variant accounts differ slightly in the order of the brothers: 磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed) is placed fourth in variant account 1, also fourth in variant account 2 (though the order of 稻飯命 and 三毛野命 is switched), third in variant account 3, and second in variant account 4.

Variant account 1 explains that 狹野尊 (reading unconfirmed) was his name when young, and that the title 神日本磐余尊 was added because he later pacified the realm and governed the Eight Islands (八洲). In variant accounts 2 to 4, “火火出見” is attached to the name of 磐余尊.

The Kojiki also lists four children by Tamayori-hime (玉依毘売命): Itsuse-no-Mikoto (五瀬命), 稻冰命, 御毛沼命, and 若御毛沼命 (readings unconfirmed), and gives 神倭伊波礼毗古命 (reading unconfirmed) as another name of the youngest, 若御毛沼命. The Kojiki says that 御毛沼命 went into the Eternal Land (常世国) and 稻冰命 into the sea plain, but this does not appear in section 11 of the Nihon Shoki.

The deity-name database of Kokugakuin University draws attention to the element shared by “彦火火出見” in Emperor Jinmu's name and “日子穂々手見,” another name of 火遠理命 (reading unconfirmed), and introduces a theory that regards Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto (鵜葺草葺不合命) as a deity added later in order to make Emperor Jinmu a descendant of Amaterasu-Ōmikami in the fifth generation. In section 11 of the Nihon Shoki as well, “火火出見” is included in the name of 磐余尊 in variant accounts 2 to 4.

story.text: Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto took as consort Tamayori-hime, who was his aunt (his mother's younger sister). The main text lists in order the children born of this marriage.
First Itsuse-no-Mikoto was born, next 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed), next Mikeirino-no-Mikoto, and next 神日本磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed); the children were four sons in all.
After a long time, Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto died at the 西洲之宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. He was then buried in the 吾平山上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum in Hyūga.

quotes.note: He took as consort his aunt (his mother's younger sister) Tamayori-hime.
Variant account 1: he is called “狹野” because that was his name when young.
Variant account 2: he is also called 神日本磐余火火出見尊.

figures.name: Itsuse-no-Mikoto (五瀨命)
figures.role: The eldest of the four brothers. In the main text and in all four variant accounts he is said to have been born first.

figures.name: 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: One of the four brothers. He is placed second in the main text and variant accounts 1 and 3, and third in variant accounts 2 and 4. The deity-name database lists this name under the entry for 稲氷命 (reading unconfirmed) of the Kojiki.

figures.name: 狹野尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In variant account 1, regarded as the name of 神日本磐余尊 when young.

figures.name: 三毛野命 and 稚三毛野命 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: The names in the position corresponding to Mikeirino-no-Mikoto (三毛入野命) in variant accounts 2 and 3. Variant account 3 makes 稚三毛野命 the youngest child.

compare.where: Kojiki, end of Part 1 — the genealogy of Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto
compare.text: The Kojiki also says that Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto (鵜葺草葺不合命) married his aunt Tamayori-hime (玉依毘売命) and fathered four children, in the order Itsuse-no-Mikoto (五瀬命), 稻冰命, 御毛沼命, and 若御毛沼命 (readings unconfirmed), and, like the main text of the Nihon Shoki, makes 若御毛沼命, who corresponds to Emperor Jinmu, the youngest.

compare.where: Kojiki, end of Part 1 — the genealogy of Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto
compare.text: The Kojiki records that 御毛沼命 (reading unconfirmed) crossed over to the Eternal Land (常世国), treading on the crests of the waves, and that 稻冰命 (reading unconfirmed) entered the sea plain as the land of his late mother, but this passage is absent from the main text and the variant accounts of section 11 of the Nihon Shoki. On the other hand, the passage in the main text of the Nihon Shoki on the death of Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto (鸕鷀草葺不合尊) and the 吾平山上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum could not be confirmed in the corresponding part of Part 1 of the Kojiki.

variants.name: Variant account 1
variants.text: The order is the same as in the main text, but the fourth child is called 狹野尊 (reading unconfirmed), with the other name 神日本磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed). It explains that 狹野 was his name when young, and that because he later pacified the realm and governed the Eight Islands, the title 神日本磐余尊 was added.

variants.name: Variant account 2
variants.text: The order is Itsuse-no-Mikoto, 三毛野命 (reading unconfirmed), 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed), and 磐余尊 (reading unconfirmed), so that the second and third are switched compared with the main text. Another name of 磐余尊 is given as 神日本磐余火火出見尊 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Variant account 3
variants.text: The order is Itsuse-no-Mikoto, 稻飯命, 神日本磐余火火出見尊, and 稚三毛野命 (readings unconfirmed), placing 磐余尊 third and making 稚三毛野命 the youngest child.

variants.name: Variant account 4
variants.text: The order is Itsuse-no-Mikoto, 磐余火火出見尊 (reading unconfirmed), 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed), and Mikeirino-no-Mikoto, placing 磐余尊 second.

jinmu-tosei.title: Emperor Jinmu's Eastern Expedition
jinmu-tosei.lead: This page covers the period from the year 甲寅, when the emperor 神日本磐余彦 (Emperor Jinmu) left Hyūga and advanced east through the Seto Inland Sea, until he passed through Naniwa, Kumano, and 菟田 (reading unconfirmed) and entered Yamato. Though he lost his elder brother Itsuse-no-Mikoto in the fighting against Nagasunebiko, he received the help of the sword Futsunomitama (韴靈), the 頭八咫烏 (reading unconfirmed) crow, and a golden kite, and the account runs up to the submission of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto in the twelfth month of the year 戊午.

points.text: In the year 甲寅, the emperor, aged forty-five, stated that since the descent of the heavenly ancestor they had governed this western region, but that distant lands had not yet received the blessings of royal rule and each village had its own lord or chief contending with the others, and he decided to establish his capital in the “beautiful land in the east” of which he had heard from Shiotsuchi-no-Oji (鹽土老翁).

When he was defeated by Nagasunebiko at 孔舍衞坂 (reading unconfirmed) and Itsuse-no-Mikoto was wounded by an arrow, the emperor, thinking that “for a descendant of the Sun Deity to attack facing the sun is to go against the way of heaven,” withdrew and changed his plan to attacking with the sun at his back. Itsuse-no-Mikoto died at 竃山 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Kii.

The army, which had collapsed in Kumano from the poisonous breath of a deity, was revived by the sword “Futsunomitama” (韴靈), which 高倉下 (reading unconfirmed) obtained from his storehouse after a revelation in a dream, and it then entered 菟田 (reading unconfirmed) guided by the 頭八咫烏 (reading unconfirmed) crow, which Amaterasu-Ōmikami announced in a dream that she would send.

In the twelfth month of the year 戊午, a golden, miraculous kite perched on the emperor's bow and dazzled the eyes of Nagasunebiko's army. Nagasunebiko served Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto as his lord, but he did not stop fighting even after the heavenly feathered arrows (天羽羽矢) and quivers (歩靭) had been shown to each other, and Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto killed Nagasunebiko and submitted (he is regarded as the distant ancestor of the Mononobe clan).

The Kojiki holds that he set out east after consulting with Itsuse-no-Mikoto at the Takachiho palace, and that he stayed eight years at the 高嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Kibi, whereas the Nihon Shoki holds that the emperor himself proposed the eastern expedition, and that he spent three years at the 高嶋宮 palace in Kibi preparing ships and provisions.

According to the deity-name database of Kokugakuin University, the “速吸之門” (reading unconfirmed) where he met 椎根津彦 (reading unconfirmed; 槁根津日子 in the Kojiki) is identified with the Akashi Strait if one follows the Kojiki, and with the Hōyo Strait if one follows the Nihon Shoki, so that its location is regarded as differing between the two works.

story.text: The emperor 神日本磐余彦 (Emperor Jinmu) had the personal name Hikohohodemi (彦火火出見); he was the fourth child of Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto (彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊), and his mother was Tamayori-hime (玉依姫), the youngest daughter of the sea deity (海童). At fifteen he became crown prince, and he took as consort 吾平津媛 (reading unconfirmed) of the village of 吾田 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Hyūga, and 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed) was born. When he was forty-five, the emperor told his elder brothers and his children that since the heavenly ancestor Ninigi-no-Mikoto (彦火瓊瓊杵尊) had descended, more than 1,792,470 years had passed, but in distant lands each village had its own lords and chiefs who contended with one another. He said that he had heard from Shiotsuchi-no-Oji that in the east there was a beautiful land surrounded by green mountains, and that someone had flown down there in a heavenly rock boat (天磐船); that land, he said, was the center of the realm, and the one who flew down was probably Nigihayahi; and he proposed that they go there and establish the capital. The princes also agreed. This year was 甲寅.

In winter, in the tenth month, the emperor led the princes and a naval force east. At 速吸之門 (reading unconfirmed), a fisherman named 珍彦 (reading unconfirmed), who came in a small boat, declared himself an earthly deity and undertook to act as guide, so the emperor had him grasp the tip of a 椎 pole, drew him into the emperor's ship, and gave him the name 椎根津彦 (reading unconfirmed) (first ancestor of the 倭直部, reading unconfirmed). At 菟狹 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi, 菟狹津彦 and 菟狹津媛 (readings unconfirmed) built a one-pillared raised palace (一柱騰宮) and entertained them, and 菟狹津媛 was given as wife to the attendant 天種子命 (reading unconfirmed; distant ancestor of the Nakatomi clan). In the eleventh month they reached 崗水門 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi and in the twelfth month the 埃宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Aki; in the third month of the year 乙卯 they moved to Kibi and spent three years at the 高嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace preparing ships and provisions. In the second month of the year 戊午 they arrived at the cape of Naniwa, which they named 浪速国 (the land of swift waves) because the current of the tide was swift, and in the third month they reached the port of 青雲白肩之津 at the village of 草香 (readings unconfirmed) in the province of Kawachi.

In the fourth month, since the road to 龍田 (reading unconfirmed) was narrow, they tried to cross Mount 膽駒山 (reading unconfirmed) to enter the central land (中洲), but Nagasunebiko, declaring that “the children of the heavenly deities are coming in order to seize my land,” met them in battle at 孔舍衞坂 (reading unconfirmed), and a stray arrow struck Itsuse-no-Mikoto. The emperor, thinking that for a descendant of the Sun Deity to attack facing the sun was to go against the way of heaven, withdrew for a time, worshipped the deities of heaven and earth, and decided to attack with the might of the Sun Deity at his back. Because they set up shields and raised war cries (雄誥) at the port of 草香津 (reading unconfirmed), that port was named 盾津 (the Shield Port). In the fifth month, at 山城水門 in 茅渟 (readings unconfirmed), Itsuse-no-Mikoto, in pain from his wound, stroked his sword and raised a war cry, and that place was called 雄水門 (reading unconfirmed). When the army advanced to 竃山 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Kii, Itsuse-no-Mikoto died, and he was buried at 竃山.

In the sixth month they struck down 名草戸畔 (reading unconfirmed) at the village of 名草邑 (reading unconfirmed), crossed 狹野 (reading unconfirmed), and arrived at the village of 神邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Kumano. When they met a violent storm at sea, 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed) drew his sword, entered the sea, and became 鋤持神 (reading unconfirmed), and Mikeirino-no-Mikoto (三毛入野命) trod on the crests of the waves and departed for the Eternal Land (常世郷). When they struck down 丹敷戸畔 (reading unconfirmed) at 熊野荒坂津 (reading unconfirmed), a deity breathed out poisonous vapor and the whole army grew weak and collapsed. 高倉下 (reading unconfirmed) of Kumano dreamed that Takemikazuchi-no-Kami (武甕雷神), commanded by Amaterasu-Ōmikami (天照太神), would send down in his stead the sword with which he had pacified the land, and when he presented the sword that stood at the bottom of his storehouse, the emperor and his soldiers woke up. Further, Amaterasu-Ōmikami announced in a dream that she would send the 頭八咫烏 (reading unconfirmed); guided by that crow, 日臣命 (reading unconfirmed), leading 大來目 (reading unconfirmed), opened a mountain road and arrived at 菟田下縣 (reading unconfirmed), so the emperor changed 日臣命's name to 道臣 (reading unconfirmed).

In the eighth month, 兄猾 (reading unconfirmed) of 菟田 built a contraption in a new palace intending to kill the emperor, but 弟猾 (reading unconfirmed) reported it, and 兄猾, driven into it by 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed), was crushed to death by his own contraption (the origin of the name 菟田血原, reading unconfirmed). At the banquet held by 弟猾 the emperor composed a song, and this is called the 來目歌 (reading unconfirmed). At Yoshino he met earthly deities, among them 井光 (reading unconfirmed; first ancestor of the 吉野首部, reading unconfirmed), who came out of a well, shining and with a tail. In the ninth month, looking out from 高倉山 (reading unconfirmed) in 菟田, he saw that the 八十梟帥 (the Eighty Bandits) of 国見丘 (reading unconfirmed) and the army of 兄磯城 (reading unconfirmed) of the village of 磐余邑 (reading unconfirmed) were blocking the strategic points. Following the instruction of a heavenly deity in a dream and the advice of 弟猾, he had 椎根津彦 and 弟猾 disguise themselves as an old man and an old woman and fetch earth from the summit of Mount Ame-no-Kagoyama (天香山); with that clay he made eighty flat dishes (八十平瓮) and sacred jars (嚴瓮), worshipped the deities of heaven and earth at the upper reaches of the 丹生川 (reading unconfirmed), and obtained the results of divination in which sweet syrup (飴) formed of itself and fish floated up because of a jar sunk in the river. The emperor himself performed the manifest worship (顯齋) of Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto (高皇産靈尊), making 道臣命 the ritual master and giving him the name 嚴媛 (reading unconfirmed).

In the tenth month, the emperor defeated the Eighty Bandits of 国見丘 (reading unconfirmed), and at 忍坂 (reading unconfirmed) 道臣命 prepared a banquet in a great chamber (大室), lured the remaining enemies, and at a signal given by a song cut them all down at once. In the eleventh month, when the 頭八咫烏 was sent as messenger, 兄磯城 shot arrows at it, but 弟磯城 (reading unconfirmed) was afraid and submitted, and reported his elder brother's preparations. On the plan of 椎根津彦, a women's army was sent out from 忍坂 to draw the enemy, while a men's army crossed 墨坂 (reading unconfirmed) and caught them in a pincer attack from the rear, cutting down 兄磯城 and the others.

In the twelfth month, in the battle against Nagasunebiko, they were unable to win, but as the sky grew dark and hail fell, a golden, miraculous kite perched on the tip (弭) of the emperor's bow, and its light dazzled the eyes of Nagasunebiko's soldiers so that they could not fight (the origin of the name 鵄邑, now 鳥見, readings unconfirmed). Nagasunebiko sent a messenger to say that Kushitama-Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (櫛玉饒速日命), who had descended from heaven in a heavenly rock boat, had married his younger sister Mikashikiya-hime (三炊屋媛), and Umashimade-no-Mikoto (可美眞手命) had been born, and that he served Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto as his lord. The emperor and Nagasunebiko showed each other a heavenly feathered arrow and a quiver (歩靭), but Nagasunebiko did not change his mind, so Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto killed Nagasunebiko and submitted, leading Nagasunebiko's people. The emperor praised this and favored him, and it is recorded that Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto is the distant ancestor of the Mononobe clan.

quotes.note: In the east there is a beautiful land, surrounded on all sides by green mountains. The emperor tells this as something he heard from Shiotsuchi-no-Oji.
The emperor's reflection: although he was a descendant of the Sun Deity, attacking the enemy while facing the sun went against the way of heaven.
The words of Takemikazuchi-no-Kami telling 高倉下 (reading unconfirmed) that the name of his sword is Futsunomitama (韴靈).
A golden, miraculous kite came flying and perched on the tip of the emperor's bow.

figures.name: Itsuse-no-Mikoto (五瀬命)
figures.role: The emperor's elder brother. He was struck by a stray arrow at 孔舍衞坂 (reading unconfirmed), died at 竃山 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Kii, and was buried at 竃山.

figures.name: 珍彦 (椎根津彦) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An earthly deity, a fisherman met at 速吸之門 (reading unconfirmed). He became the guide for the sea route and was given the name 椎根津彦; he also served in fetching the earth of Mount Ame-no-Kagoyama and with his plan for the attack on 磯城. First ancestor of the 倭直部 (reading unconfirmed). A gloss says 「椎。此云辭毘」.

figures.name: Nagasunebiko (長髄彦)
figures.role: The chieftain of Yamato who met the emperor's army in battle at 孔舍衞坂 (reading unconfirmed). He looked up to Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto as his lord, and was finally killed by Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (饒速日命; Kushitama-Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto, 櫛玉饒速日命)
figures.role: A child of the heavenly deities who had earlier descended from heaven in a heavenly rock boat. He killed Nagasunebiko and submitted, and is regarded as the distant ancestor of the Mononobe clan. A gloss says 「饒速日。此云爾藝波揶卑」.

figures.name: Mikashikiya-hime (三炊屋媛)
figures.role: Younger sister of Nagasunebiko and wife of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto. Her other names are 長髄媛 and 鳥見屋媛 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: Umashimade-no-Mikoto (可美眞手命)
figures.role: Child of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto and Mikashikiya-hime. A gloss says 「可美眞手。此云于魔詩莽耐」.

figures.name: 高倉下 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of Kumano. Following the instruction of a dream, he found the sword (Futsunomitama) in his storehouse and presented it to the emperor.

figures.name: Futsunomitama (韴靈)
figures.role: The sword with which Takemikazuchi-no-Kami had pacified the land, which he sent down into the storehouse of 高倉下 (reading unconfirmed). A gloss says 「韴靈。此云赴屠能瀰哆磨」.

figures.name: 頭八咫烏 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The crow that Amaterasu-Ōmikami announced in a dream she would send. It guided the way from Kumano to 菟田 (reading unconfirmed) and also served as messenger to the brothers of 磯城 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 道臣命 (日臣命) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Distant ancestor of the Ōtomo clan. For his merit in following the crow and opening a mountain road he was renamed 道臣; he carried out the punishment of 兄猾 and the stratagem at 忍坂, and became the ritual master of the manifest worship.

figures.name: 兄猾 and 弟猾 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Brothers who were chieftains of the district of 菟田 (reading unconfirmed). 兄猾 plotted and brought about his own destruction, and 弟猾 served the emperor. A gloss says 「猾。此云字介志」.

figures.name: 稻飯命 and Mikeirino-no-Mikoto (三毛入野命)
figures.role: The emperor's elder brothers. In a storm at sea on the way to Kumano, 稻飯命 (reading unconfirmed) entered the sea and became 鋤持神 (reading unconfirmed), and Mikeirino-no-Mikoto departed for the Eternal Land.

figures.name: 井光 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An earthly deity who came out of a well at Yoshino, shining and with a tail. Regarded as the first ancestor of the 吉野首部 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — beginning of the section on Emperor Jinmu (the departure and route of the eastern expedition)
compare.text: The Kojiki holds that he set out east after consulting with his elder brother Itsuse-no-Mikoto at the Takachiho palace, and stayed one year at the 岡田宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Tsukushi, seven years at the 多祁理宮 palace in 阿岐 (readings unconfirmed), and eight years at the 高嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Kibi. The Nihon Shoki holds that the emperor himself spoke of the eastern expedition to his elder brothers and the princes, and that, passing through the 埃宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Aki, he stayed three years at the 高嶋宮 palace in Kibi.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — section on Emperor Jinmu (the death in battle of Itsuse-no-Mikoto)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Itsuse-no-Mikoto dies at 男之水門 (reading unconfirmed) in 紀国 (Kii), crying out, “Am I to die of a wound from a lowly wretch's hand?” (written 「崩」), and his tomb is said to be at 竈山 (reading unconfirmed). In the Nihon Shoki, 雄水門 (reading unconfirmed) is the name of the place at 山城水門 in 茅渟 (readings unconfirmed) where he raised a war cry, and Itsuse-no-Mikoto is said to have died at 竃山 in the province of Kii (written 「薨」).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — section on Emperor Jinmu (the arrival of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto)
compare.text: The Kojiki records only that Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (邇藝速日命) descended from heaven following the child of the heavenly deities, presented the heavenly tokens (天津瑞), and served him; the story of his killing 登美毘古 (reading unconfirmed) does not appear. The Nihon Shoki has the scene in which he and Nagasunebiko show each other heavenly feathered arrows and quivers, and the story of Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto killing Nagasunebiko and submitting.

variants.name: A certain book says (高尾張邑)
variants.text: Regarding 「高尾張邑」 (reading unconfirmed), where the 赤銅八十梟帥 (the Eighty Bandits of red copper) are, as mentioned in the words of 弟猾 (reading unconfirmed), a small note says that a certain book (或本) gives it as the village of 葛城 (reading unconfirmed).

jinmu-sokui.title: The Pacification of Yamato and the Enthronement
jinmu-sokui.lead: This page covers the period from the year 己未, when the emperor struck down the earth spiders (土蜘蛛) remaining in Yamato and declared that he would build a palace at Kashihara (橿原), through his accession at the Kashihara palace in the first month of the year 辛酉, until his death in his 76th year. The choice of a principal consort, the rewards to meritorious retainers, the worship of the imperial ancestors and heavenly deities at Mount 鳥見山 (reading unconfirmed), the origin of the name 「秋津洲」 (reading unconfirmed), and other matters are recorded year by year.

points.text: In a decree in the third month of the year 己未, the emperor declared that six years had passed since he began the eastern expedition and that the central land (中洲) was at peace, and that he would build a palace at Kashihara, southeast of Mount Unebi (畝傍山), and take the throne; he stated, “uniting the six directions, I will open a capital, and covering the eight cords (八紘), I will make them one roof (宇).”

On the first day (庚辰) of the first month of spring in the year 辛酉, the emperor ascended the imperial throne at the Kashihara palace, and this year was made the first year of the emperor. He made Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto (媛蹈韛五十鈴媛命), who had been recommended as the child of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed), his empress, and 神八井命 and 神渟名川耳尊 (readings unconfirmed) were born.

In the conferring of rewards for merit in the second month of the 2nd year, he gave 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed) a residence at the village of 築坂邑 (reading unconfirmed) and 大來目 (reading unconfirmed) land by the river west of Mount Unebi (the village of 來目邑, reading unconfirmed); he made 珍彦 (reading unconfirmed) governor (國造) of Yamato (倭), 弟猾 (reading unconfirmed) district chief (縣主) of 猛田 (reading unconfirmed), 弟磯城 (黒速) (reading unconfirmed) district chief of 磯城 (reading unconfirmed), and 釼根 (reading unconfirmed) governor of 葛城 (reading unconfirmed), and he included the 頭八咫烏 (reading unconfirmed) crow among those rewarded as well.

In the fourth month of the 31st year (「卅有一年」 in the original), the name 「秋津洲」 (reading unconfirmed) is said to have begun from the words of the emperor, who viewed the shape of the land from the hill 嗛間丘 at 腋上 (readings unconfirmed); the names by which Izanagi-no-Mikoto, Ōanamuchi-no-Ōkami (大己貴大神), and Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto called this land are also recorded.

In the Kojiki, the empress is 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Ōmononushi-no-Kami, and the emperor's age is given as 137 years. The Nihon Shoki makes Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto, daughter of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami, empress, and holds that he died at 127. Passages corresponding to the year of accession, the conferring of rewards for merit, the worship at Mount 鳥見山, and the naming of 秋津洲 could not be confirmed in the Kojiki.

According to the deity-name database of Kokugakuin University, the governors of Yamato (倭国造) are the clan who worship Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大国魂神), and it has been pointed out that the Nihon Shoki story in which 椎根津彦 (珍彦) (reading unconfirmed) fetches the earth of Mount Ame-no-Kagoyama (天香山), foreshadowing the pacification of Yamato, is a tale of meritorious deeds that legitimizes the worship conducted by the governors of Yamato.

story.text: In the second month of the year 己未, the emperor had his generals train their troops. Since the earth spiders in three places, namely 新城戸畔 at 波哆丘岬 in the district of 層富縣, 居勢祝 at 和珥坂下, and 猪祝 at 臍見長柄丘岬 (readings unconfirmed), would not submit, he sent separate detachments and executed them all. The earth spiders of the village of 高尾張邑 (reading unconfirmed) were short of stature with long arms and legs, so they were killed by throwing nets of kudzu (葛) over them, and the village's name was changed to 葛城 (reading unconfirmed). The place that had been called 片居 or 片立 (readings unconfirmed) was renamed 磐余 (reading unconfirmed) because the imperial army gathered and filled it. Besides these, the origins of place names are told, such as 猛田, 城田, and 頬枕田 (readings unconfirmed), and the place where the clay of Mount Ame-no-Kagoyama was taken being called 埴安 (reading unconfirmed).

In the third month, the emperor issued a decree stating that six years had passed since he began the eastern expedition, that through the might of imperial heaven (皇天) the wicked had been struck down, and that although the borderlands were not yet at peace, there was no longer strife in the central land. He held that though the people were still simple and lived in nests and caves, nothing should stand in the way of construction if it was for the benefit of the people, and declared that he would clear the mountain forests and build a palace, above responding to the virtue of the heavenly deities who had granted him the land, and below spreading the righteous heart of the imperial grandson. He then chose the land of Kashihara, southeast of Mount Unebi, as a good, secluded place in the land, and in that month ordered officials to begin building the imperial residence.

In the eighth month of the year 庚申, when the emperor sought widely for a principal consort, Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto, born to Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 三嶋溝橛耳神 (reading unconfirmed), was recommended as the most beautiful person in the land, and in the ninth month he made her principal consort. On the first day (庚辰) of the first month of spring in the year 辛酉, the emperor ascended the imperial throne at the Kashihara palace, made this year the first year of the emperor, and made the principal consort empress, and 神八井命 and 神渟名川耳尊 (readings unconfirmed) were born. In the old language (古語), he is praised as 神日本磐余彦火火出見天皇 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor who firmly planted the pillars of his palace at Kashihara in Unebi (畝傍) and first ruled the realm. It is also said that on the day the emperor laid the foundations of the state, 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed), leading the 大來目部 (reading unconfirmed), dispelled evil influences with allusive songs (諷歌) and inverted words (倒語), and that this was the beginning of inverted words.

In the second month of the 2nd year, the emperor determined merits and conferred rewards. To 道臣命 he gave a residence at the village of 築坂邑 (reading unconfirmed), and he had 大來目 (reading unconfirmed) live by the river west of Mount Unebi (the origin of the village of 來目邑, reading unconfirmed). He made 珍彦 governor of Yamato, 弟猾 district chief of 猛田 (distant ancestor of the 菟田主水部, reading unconfirmed), 黒速 of 弟磯城 (readings unconfirmed) district chief of 磯城, and 釼根 (reading unconfirmed) governor of 葛城; the 頭八咫烏 also received a reward, and its descendants are regarded as the 葛野主殿縣主部 (reading unconfirmed). In the second month of the 4th year, the emperor issued an edict saying that since the spirits of the imperial ancestors had looked down from heaven and helped him, now that the rebels were subdued he should perform the suburban sacrifice (郊祀) to the heavenly deities and show his great filial piety; he set up a sacred ritual ground (靈畤) within Mount 鳥見山 (reading unconfirmed) and worshipped the imperial ancestors and heavenly deities. That place is called 上小野榛原 and 下小野榛原 (readings unconfirmed).

In the fourth month of the 31st year (卅有一年), the emperor made a royal tour and climbed the hill 嗛間丘 at 腋上 (readings unconfirmed), and, looking around at the shape of the land, said that though it was a land as narrow as the inner bark-cloth (内木綿), it was like the 臀呫 of dragonflies (蜻蛉之臀呫); this is said to be the beginning of the name 秋津洲 (reading unconfirmed). It goes on to record that in the past Izanagi-no-Mikoto called this land 浦安國, 細戈千足國, and 磯輪上秀眞國 (readings unconfirmed), that Ōanamuchi-no-Ōkami called it 玉牆内國 (reading unconfirmed), and that Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto, because he had flown through the great sky in a heavenly rock boat, seen this land, and descended, called it 虚空見日本國 (reading unconfirmed). In the first month of the 32nd year (卅有二年), 神渟名川耳尊 (reading unconfirmed) was made crown prince. In the third month of the 76th year, the emperor died at the Kashihara palace, at the age of 127. In the ninth month of the following year he was buried in the mausoleum northeast of Mount Unebi (畝傍山東北陵).

quotes.note: A passage from the decree on building at Kashihara: uniting the four quarters of the realm, he will open a capital, and covering everything to the ends of the eight directions, he will make it one house.
Records that in the first month of the year 辛酉 the emperor ascended the imperial throne at the Kashihara palace.
From this, the name 秋津洲 (reading unconfirmed) first came into being.
The emperor died at the Kashihara palace, at the age of 127.

figures.name: Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto (媛蹈韛五十鈴媛命)
figures.role: Child of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed). She became principal consort in the ninth month of the year 庚申, and was made empress at the emperor's accession.

figures.name: Kotoshironushi-no-Kami (事代主神)
figures.role: A deity named as the father of Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 三嶋溝橛耳神 (reading unconfirmed) and mother of Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: 神八井命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of the emperor and the empress.

figures.name: 神渟名川耳尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of the emperor and the empress. He became crown prince in the 32nd year (卅有二年).

figures.name: 道臣命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Distant ancestor of the Ōtomo clan. Leading the 大來目部 (reading unconfirmed), he dispelled evil influences with allusive songs and inverted words, and was granted a residence at the village of 築坂邑 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 珍彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A name of 椎根津彦 (reading unconfirmed), who guided the eastern expedition. He was appointed governor of Yamato. A gloss says 「珍彦。此云于砮毘故」.

figures.name: 弟猾 and 弟磯城 (黒速) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Chieftains of 菟田 and 磯城 (readings unconfirmed) who followed the emperor during the eastern expedition. 弟猾 became district chief of 猛田, and 弟磯城 district chief of 磯城.

figures.name: Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊弉諾尊)
figures.role: Cited by name as having called this land 「浦安國」, 「細戈千足國」, and 「磯輪上秀眞國」 in the past.

figures.name: Ōanamuchi-no-Ōkami (大己貴大神)
figures.role: Cited by name as having called this land 「玉牆内國」.

figures.name: Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto (饒速日命)
figures.role: Said to have called this land 「虚空見日本國」 because he flew through the great sky in a heavenly rock boat, saw this land, and descended.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — section on Emperor Jinmu (the choice of the empress)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), who becomes empress, is said to be the daughter born when Ōmononushi-no-Kami of 美和 (reading unconfirmed) turned into a red-lacquered arrow (丹塗矢) and visited 勢夜陀多良比賣 (reading unconfirmed). The empress of the Nihon Shoki, Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto, is said to be the child of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and 玉櫛媛 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — end of the section on Emperor Jinmu (age at death and tomb)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives the emperor's age as 137 years and places his tomb at 白檮尾上 (reading unconfirmed), north of Mount Unebi (畝火山). The Nihon Shoki holds that he died at 127 and was buried in the mausoleum northeast of Mount Unebi (畝傍山東北陵).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — section on Emperor Jinmu (rule at the Kashihara palace)
compare.text: The Kojiki records briefly that he subdued the unruly deities, drove away those who would not submit, and ruled the realm at the Kashihara palace (白檮原宮) in Unebi (畝火). Passages corresponding to the accession in the year 辛酉, the conferring of rewards for merit, the worship at Mount 鳥見山 (reading unconfirmed), and the naming of 秋津洲 found in the Nihon Shoki could not be confirmed in the Kojiki.

variants.name: Another account says (the origin of the name 磐余)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which attributes the name 磐余 (reading unconfirmed) to the imperial army's gathering and filling the place, a different origin is recorded under 「或曰」: when the emperor ate the provisions of the sacred jars (嚴瓮) and set out to battle, the 八十梟帥 (Eighty Bandits) of 磯城 (reading unconfirmed) were massed there and were destroyed, so the place was named the village of 磐余邑.

kesshi.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 4 — Emperor Suizei to Emperor Kaika
kesshi.title: From Emperor Suizei to Emperor Kaika (Including the Rebellion of 手研耳命)
kesshi.lead: This page covers the eight reigns from the emperor 神渟名川耳 (Emperor Suizei), who took the throne after striking down his elder half-brother 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed) following the death of Emperor Jinmu, to the emperor 稚日本根子彦大日日 (Emperor Kaika). Apart from the rebellion of 手研耳命, it consists mainly of short entries recording, with years and months, each emperor's parents, appointment as crown prince, accession, capital, empress and children, the burial of the previous emperor, and death.

points.text: After the death of Emperor Jinmu, his elder half-brother 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed) seized power at will during the mourning period and sought to harm his two younger brothers. 神渟名川耳尊 (reading unconfirmed), together with his elder brother Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto (神八井耳命), attacked 手研耳命 as he slept in a chamber at 片丘 (reading unconfirmed), and, taking the place of his elder brother, whose hands and feet trembled so that he could not shoot, shot him dead himself.

Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto, saying, “Though I am the elder brother, I was cowardly and could not carry the matter through,” yielded the heavenly throne to his younger brother, and stated that he himself would take the role of worshipping the deities of heaven and earth to help his younger brother. Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto is regarded as the first ancestor of the 多臣 (reading unconfirmed).

Each entry from Suizei to Kaika is written as a short record of the same pattern: parents, the year of appointment as crown prince, accession, honoring the empress as empress dowager, the move of the capital and the name of the palace, the empress and children, the burial of the previous emperor, and death; other names for the empress are often added under “a certain writing says” (一書云) or “an alternative version” (一云).

Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命) and 彦五十狹芹彦命 (reading unconfirmed; also called 吉備津彦命) were born to a consort of Emperor Kōrei, and 武埴安彦命 (reading unconfirmed) to 埴安媛 (reading unconfirmed), a consort of Emperor Kōgen; Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命) is regarded as the first ancestor of seven clans including the 阿倍臣 (reading unconfirmed), and 彦太忍信命 (reading unconfirmed) as the grandfather of Takeuchi-no-Sukune (武内宿禰). These are people who appear in the section on Emperor Sujin in Book 5.

The Kojiki holds that the elder half-brother 當藝志美美命 (reading unconfirmed) took as wife 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), Jinmu's empress, and that the empress warned her children of the danger by means of songs, but the Nihon Shoki has no such story and holds that the younger brothers perceived 手研耳命's scheme by themselves.

The deity-name database of Kokugakuin University states that in the Nihon Shoki the name of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami appears as the father of Himetatara-isuzu-hime (媛蹈鞴五十鈴媛), Emperor Jinmu's empress, and of 五十鈴依媛 (reading unconfirmed) in the preface to the record of Annei, and as the grandfather of 鴨王 (reading unconfirmed) in the preface to the record of Itoku, and that these are traditions of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami not recorded in the Kojiki.

story.text: The emperor 神渟名川耳 (reading unconfirmed) was the third child of the emperor 神日本磐余彦 (Emperor Jinmu), and his mother was Himetatara-isuzu-hime-no-Mikoto (媛蹈■五十鈴媛命; one character is missing in the original text), eldest daughter of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami. When he was forty-eight, the emperor 神日本磐余彦 died, and he devoted himself to the mourning and funeral, but his elder half-brother 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed), being older and experienced in government, had been entrusted with affairs. 手研耳命 seized power at will during the mourning period and schemed to harm his two younger brothers. This was the year 太歳己卯. In winter, in the eleventh month, 神渟名川耳尊 and his elder brother Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto learned of the plot, and when the matter of the mausoleum was finished, they had 弓部稚彦 (reading unconfirmed) make a bow, 倭鍛部天津眞浦 (reading unconfirmed) make arrowheads, and the arrow-makers (矢部) make arrows. The two burst in on 手研耳命 as he slept alone on a large bed in a chamber at 片丘 (reading unconfirmed), but Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto's hands and feet trembled and he could not shoot, so 神渟名川耳尊 took his elder brother's bow and arrows and shot; the first arrow struck the chest and the second the back, and 手研耳命 died. Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto yielded the throne to his younger brother, stating that he himself would worship the deities of heaven and earth and help his younger brother, and he is regarded as the first ancestor of the 多臣 (reading unconfirmed).

In the first month of the 1st year, 神渟名川耳尊 took the throne and made his capital at 葛城 (reading unconfirmed), calling it the 高丘宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. This was the year 太歳庚辰. In the first month of the 2nd year, he made 五十鈴依媛 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor's aunt, empress, and the emperor 磯城津彦玉手看 (reading unconfirmed) was born. In the fourth month of the 4th year Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto died and was buried north of Mount Unebi (畝傍山), and in the first month of the 25th year (「廿五年」 in the original) 磯城津彦玉手看尊 was made crown prince. In the fifth month of the 33rd year (「卅三年」 in the original) the emperor fell ill and died. He was eighty-four years old.

The emperor 磯城津彦玉手看 (Emperor Annei), whose mother was 五十鈴依媛命 (reading unconfirmed), youngest daughter of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami, took the throne in the seventh month after his father's death, and in the tenth month of the 1st year buried his father in the 倭桃花鳥田丘上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum. This was the year 太歳癸丑. In the 2nd year he moved the capital to 片鹽 (reading unconfirmed), making it the 浮孔宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, and in the 3rd year he made 渟名底仲媛命 (reading unconfirmed; also called 渟名襲媛) empress, and 息石耳命 and the emperor 大日本彦耜友 (readings unconfirmed) were born. In the 11th year 大日本彦耜友尊 was made crown prince, and his younger brother 磯城津彦命 (reading unconfirmed) is regarded as the first ancestor of the 猪使連 (reading unconfirmed). He died in the twelfth month of the 38th year, at the age of fifty-seven. The next emperor, 大日本彦耜友 (Emperor Itoku), whose mother was 渟名底仲媛命, daughter of 鴨王 (reading unconfirmed), a grandson of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami, took the throne in the second month of the 1st year, and in the year 太歳辛卯 buried his father in the 畝傍山南御陰井上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum. In the 2nd year he moved the capital to the land of 輕 (reading unconfirmed), making it the 曲峽宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, and made 天豐津媛命 (reading unconfirmed) empress, and the emperor 觀松彦香殖稻 (reading unconfirmed) was born; in the 22nd year he appointed the crown prince, and he died in the ninth month of the 34th year.

The emperor 觀松彦香殖稻 (Emperor Kōshō) had as his mother 天豐津媛命 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 息石耳命 (reading unconfirmed). In the tenth month of the year after his father's death he buried his father in the 畝傍山南纎沙谿上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum; he took the throne in the first month of the 1st year, and in the seventh month moved the capital to 掖上 (reading unconfirmed), making it the 池心宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. This was the year 太歳丙寅. In the 29th year he made 世襲足媛 (reading unconfirmed) empress, and 天足彦國押人命 and the emperor 日本足彦國押人 (readings unconfirmed) were born, and in the 68th year 日本足彦國押人尊 was made crown prince. The elder brother 天足彦國押人命 is regarded as the first ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed) and others. He died in the eighth month of the 83rd year. The emperor 日本足彦國押人 (Emperor Kōan), whose mother was 世襲足媛, younger sister of 瀛津世襲 (reading unconfirmed), distant ancestor of the Owari no Muraji (尾張連), took the throne in the first month of the 1st year (太歳己丑); in the 2nd year he moved the capital to the land of 室 (reading unconfirmed), making it the 秋津嶋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace; in the 26th year he made his niece 押媛 (reading unconfirmed) empress, and the emperor 大日本根子彦太瓊 (reading unconfirmed) was born; in the 38th year he buried his father in the 掖上博多山上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum; in the 76th year he appointed the crown prince; and he died in the first month of the 102nd year.

The mother of the emperor 大日本根子彦太瓊 (Emperor Kōrei) was 押媛 (reading unconfirmed), and it is recorded that she was perhaps the daughter of 天足彦國押人命 (reading unconfirmed). In the ninth month of the year his father died, he buried his father in the 玉手丘上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum; in the twelfth month he moved the capital to 黒田 (reading unconfirmed), making it the 廬戸宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace; and he took the throne in the first month of the 1st year (太歳辛未).
