In the 2nd year he made 細媛命 (reading unconfirmed) empress, and the emperor 大日本根子彦國牽 (reading unconfirmed) was born; from the consort 倭國香媛 (reading unconfirmed) were born Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto, 彦五十狹芹彦命 (also called 吉備津彦命), and 倭迹迹稚屋姫命 (readings unconfirmed), and from another consort 彦狹嶋命 and 稚武彦命 (readings unconfirmed). 稚武彦命 is regarded as the first ancestor of the Kibi no Omi (吉備臣). In the 36th year 彦國牽尊 was made crown prince, and he died in the second month of the 76th year.

The emperor 大日本根子彦國牽 (Emperor Kōgen), whose mother was 細媛命 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大目 (reading unconfirmed), district chief of 磯城 (磯城縣主), took the throne in the first month of the 1st year (太歳丁亥); in the 4th year he moved the capital to the land of 輕 (reading unconfirmed), making it the 境原宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace; and in the 6th year he buried his father in the 片丘馬坂陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum. In the 7th year he made 欝色謎命 (reading unconfirmed) empress, and Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命), the emperor 稚日本根子彦大日日 (reading unconfirmed), and 倭迹迹姫命 (reading unconfirmed) were born; from the consort 伊香色謎命 (reading unconfirmed) was born 彦太忍信命 (reading unconfirmed), and from the consort 埴安媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 河内青玉繋 (reading unconfirmed), was born 武埴安彦命 (reading unconfirmed). Ōbiko-no-Mikoto is regarded as the first ancestor of seven clans including the 阿倍臣 and the 膳臣 (readings unconfirmed), and 彦太忍信命 as the grandfather of Takeuchi-no-Sukune. In the 22nd year he appointed the crown prince, and he died in the ninth month of the 57th year.

The emperor 稚日本根子彦大日日 (Emperor Kaika), whose mother was 欝色謎命 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 欝色雄命 (reading unconfirmed), distant ancestor of the 穗積臣 (reading unconfirmed), took the throne in the eleventh month of the year his father died. In the tenth month of the 1st year he moved the capital to the land of Kasuga (春日), making it the 率川宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace (太歳甲申), and in the 5th year he buried his father in the 劒池嶋上陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum. In the 6th year he made 伊香色謎命 (reading unconfirmed), who was his stepmother (庶母), empress, and the emperor 御間城入彦五十瓊殖 (reading unconfirmed) was born; before that, 彦湯産隅命 (reading unconfirmed) had been born from the consort 竹野媛 (reading unconfirmed) of 丹波 (reading unconfirmed), and 彦坐王 (reading unconfirmed) from the consort 姥津媛 (reading unconfirmed). In the 28th year he made 御間城入彦尊 crown prince at the age of nineteen; he died in the fourth month of the 60th year and was buried in the tenth month in the 春日率川坂本陵 (reading unconfirmed) mausoleum.

quotes.note: 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed), harboring an evil heart, schemed to harm his two younger brothers.
Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto's hands and feet trembled, and he could not shoot the arrow.
Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto's words praising his younger brother: “With your outstanding martial valor, you yourself struck down the chief of evil.”
彦太忍信命 (reading unconfirmed) is the grandfather of Takeuchi-no-Sukune.

figures.name: 神渟名川耳天皇 (神渟名川耳尊) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The third child of Emperor Jinmu. He shot his elder half-brother 手研耳命 dead with his own hand, took the throne, and made his capital at the 高丘宮 palace in 葛城 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 手研耳命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A child whom Emperor Jinmu fathered in Hyūga with 吾平津媛 (reading unconfirmed). He seized power at will during the mourning period, sought to harm his younger brothers, and was struck down.

figures.name: Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto (神八井耳命)
figures.role: Elder brother of 神渟名川耳尊. Unable to shoot 手研耳命, he yielded the throne to his younger brother and took the role of worshipping the deities of heaven and earth. First ancestor of the 多臣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 五十鈴依媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Youngest daughter of Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and empress of Emperor Suizei. She was the emperor's aunt.

figures.name: Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命)
figures.role: Daughter of Emperor Kōrei and his consort 倭國香媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 彦五十狹芹彦命 (吉備津彦命) (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Kōrei and his consort 倭國香媛. Also called 吉備津彦命.

figures.name: 稚武彦命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A child of Emperor Kōrei. Regarded as the first ancestor of the Kibi no Omi.

figures.name: Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命)
figures.role: First child of Emperor Kōgen and the empress 欝色謎命 (reading unconfirmed). Regarded as the first ancestor of seven clans including the 阿倍臣 and the 膳臣 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 武埴安彦命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Kōgen and his consort 埴安媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 彦太忍信命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Child of Emperor Kōgen and his consort 伊香色謎命 (reading unconfirmed). Regarded as the grandfather of Takeuchi-no-Sukune.

figures.name: 伊香色謎命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A consort of Emperor Kōgen, who later became the empress of Emperor Kaika and gave birth to the emperor 御間城入彦五十瓊殖 (reading unconfirmed). The main text notes 「是庶母也」 (she was his stepmother).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — end of the section on Emperor Jinmu (the rebellion of 當藝志美美命)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the elder half-brother 當藝志美美命 (reading unconfirmed) took as wife 伊須氣余理比賣 (reading unconfirmed), Jinmu's empress, and tried to kill his three younger brothers, so 伊須氣余理比賣 warned her children by means of songs. The Nihon Shoki has neither the story of his marrying the empress nor the songs, and holds that 神渟名川耳尊 and Kamuyaimimi-no-Mikoto learned of the plot by themselves and forestalled it.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — section on Emperor Suizei
compare.text: The Kojiki gives the age of 神沼河耳命 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Suizei) as forty-five and places his tomb at 衝田岡 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki holds that he died at eighty-four, and records his mausoleum, in the entry for the 1st year of the next emperor, as the 倭桃花鳥田丘上陵 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2 — section on Emperor Kōrei
compare.text: The Kojiki holds that Emperor Kōrei's sons Ōkibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto (大吉備津日子命) and Wakahiko-Takekibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto (若日子建吉備津日子命) pacified the province of Kibi, using 針間 (reading unconfirmed) as the entrance. The section on Emperor Kōrei in Book 4 of the Nihon Shoki only records the births of 彦五十狹芹彦命 (吉備津彦命) and 稚武彦命 (readings unconfirmed) and that 稚武彦命 is the first ancestor of the Kibi no Omi; no passage on the pacification of Kibi could be confirmed.

variants.name: A certain writing says (Emperor Suizei's empress)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which makes the empress 五十鈴依媛 (reading unconfirmed), one writing makes her 川派媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the district chief of 磯城 (磯城縣主), and another writing makes her 糸織媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大日諸 (reading unconfirmed), district chief of Kasuga (春日縣主).

variants.name: A certain writing says (Emperor Annei's empress)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which makes the empress 渟名底仲媛命 (reading unconfirmed), one writing makes her 川津媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 葉江 (reading unconfirmed), district chief of 磯城, and another writing makes her 糸井媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大間宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Annei's princes)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which gives two princes, the alternative version (一云) gives three: the first 常津彦某兄, the second the emperor 大日本彦耜友, and the third 磯城津彦命 (readings unconfirmed).

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Itoku's empress and princes)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which makes the empress 天豐津媛命 (reading unconfirmed), one alternative version makes her 泉媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 猪手 (reading unconfirmed), younger brother of 葉江, district chief of 磯城, and another alternative version makes her 飯日媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 太眞稚彦 (reading unconfirmed), district chief of 磯城. In addition, a note of an alternative version, 「天皇母弟武石彦奇友背命」, is attached (this note runs over into the next paragraph).

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Kōshō's empress)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which makes the empress 世襲足媛 (reading unconfirmed), one alternative version makes her 渟名城津媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 葉江, district chief of 磯城, and another alternative version makes her 大井媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 倭國豐秋狹太雄 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Kōan's empress)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which makes the empress 押媛 (reading unconfirmed), one alternative version makes her 長媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 葉江, district chief of 磯城, and another alternative version makes her 五十坂媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 五十坂彦 (reading unconfirmed), district chief of 十市 (十市縣主, reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Kōrei's empress)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which makes the empress 細媛命 (reading unconfirmed), one alternative version makes her 春日千乳早山香媛 (reading unconfirmed), and another alternative version makes her 眞舌媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of an ancestor of the district chiefs of 十市 and others.

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Kōgen's princes)
variants.text: To the entry giving the empress's children as three is attached a note of an alternative version: 「天皇母弟少彦男心命也」.

variants.name: An alternative version (Emperor Kaika's mausoleum)
variants.text: In contrast to the main text, which gives the mausoleum as the 春日率川坂本陵 (reading unconfirmed), the alternative version gives it as the 坂上陵 (reading unconfirmed), and also records his age as 「時年百十五」.

sujin-miwa.title: Emperor Sujin and the Deity of Miwa: 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed)
sujin-miwa.lead: This page covers the period from the accession of 御間城入彦五十瓊殖天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sujin) to his 9th year, when an epidemic and the people's defection led him to reform the worship of the deities. It records that he had Amaterasu-Ōmikami and Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大國魂神) worshipped outside the palace, and that when, at the request of Ōmononushi-no-Kami, he had the deity's son 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) worship him, the epidemic ceased and the land became peaceful.

points.text: In the 5th year an epidemic killed more than half of the people, and in the 6th year the peasants wandered from their homes and some rebelled. The emperor, in awe of the divine power of the two deities Amaterasu-Ōmikami and Yamato-Ōkunitama (倭大國魂), whom he had been worshipping side by side inside the great hall of the palace, moved them outside. He entrusted Amaterasu-Ōmikami to 豐鍬入姫命 (reading unconfirmed) to be worshipped at 笠縫邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato, and entrusted Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (日本大國魂神) to 渟名城入姫命 (reading unconfirmed), but 渟名城入姫命 lost her hair, grew thin, and was unable to perform the worship.

In the 2nd month of the 7th year, the emperor gathered the eighty myriad deities at 神淺茅原 (reading unconfirmed) and performed divination, and Ōmononushi-no-Kami possessed Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto and declared that he should be worshipped. When this still had no effect, the emperor purified himself and prayed; Ōmononushi-no-Kami then appeared in a dream and told him that if he had his son 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) worship him, the land would at once be at peace and the countries beyond the sea would submit of their own accord.

大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed), who was found at 陶邑 in 茅渟縣 (readings unconfirmed), answered that his father was Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and his mother was 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 陶津耳 (reading unconfirmed). In the 11th month of the 7th year, 大田田根子 was made the master of worship for Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and 長尾市 (reading unconfirmed) the master of worship for Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大國魂神); the eighty myriad deities were worshipped and heavenly shrines, earthly shrines, divine lands and shrine households (天社, 國社, 神地, 神戸) were established, after which the epidemic ceased and the five grains ripened.

In the 12th month of the 8th year, on the day 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) was made to worship the Great Deity, 活日 (reading unconfirmed), the sake steward, offered sacred sake and sang, and the ministers and the emperor exchanged songs containing the phrase "瀰和能等能". 大田田根子 is regarded as the founding ancestor of the present-day Miwa no Kimi and others.

The Kojiki also has the story of the epidemic and 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed), but there the place where he is found is 美努村 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi, and 意富多多泥古 names himself a descendant counted down from Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami. In the Nihon Shoki he is found at 陶邑 in 茅渟縣 (readings unconfirmed) and names himself the son of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami.

According to Kokugakuin University's database of deity names, 墨坂 (Sumisaka) was a main route linking Yamato and Ise, and 大坂 (Ōsaka) a main route linking Yamato and Kawachi, and the worship of Sumisaka-no-Kami and Ōsaka-no-Kami in the 9th year is thought to have been the worship of boundary deities in order to keep the epidemic from entering.

story.text: 御間城入彦五十瓊殖天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sujin) was the second son of 稚日本根子彦大日日天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 伊香色謎命 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大綜麻杵 (reading unconfirmed), a distant ancestor of the Mononobe clan. He became crown prince at nineteen. He was intelligent by nature and fond of bold strategies from his youth; when he grew up he was broad-minded and prudent, deeply revered the deities of heaven and earth, and had the will to rule the realm. When his father died in the 4th month of the 60th year, he acceded to the throne in the 1st month of his 1st year, and in the 2nd month he made 御間城姫 (reading unconfirmed) his empress. The empress bore 活目入彦五十狹茅天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and others; the consort 遠津年魚眼眼妙媛 (reading unconfirmed) bore Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto and 豐鍬入姫命 (reading unconfirmed); and the consort 尾張大海媛 (reading unconfirmed) bore 八坂入彦命, 渟名城入姫命 and 十市瓊入姫命 (readings unconfirmed). This year was the sexagenary year (太歳甲申). In the 9th month of the 3rd year he moved the capital to 磯城 (reading unconfirmed) and called it the 瑞籬宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, and in the 10th month of the 4th year he issued an edict calling on all his ministers and officials to serve with full loyalty, so that he might bring peace to the realm by following in the footsteps of the imperial ancestors.

In the 5th year there was much pestilence in the land, and more than half of the people died. In the 6th year the peasants wandered from their homes and some rebelled, so that it became hard to govern by virtue, and the emperor apologized to the deities of heaven and earth for his offences from early morning until night. Before this, the two deities Amaterasu-Ōmikami and Yamato-Ōkunitama (倭大國魂) had been worshipped within the emperor's great hall, but he was in awe of their power and uneasy living together with them. He therefore entrusted Amaterasu-Ōmikami to 豐鍬入姫命 (reading unconfirmed) to be worshipped at 笠縫邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato, and set up the sacred enclosure called 磯堅城神籬 (reading unconfirmed). He entrusted Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (日本大國魂神) to 渟名城入姫命 (reading unconfirmed) to be worshipped, but 渟名城入姫命 lost her hair, grew thin, and was unable to perform the worship.

In the 2nd month of the 7th year, the emperor declared in an edict that the disasters continuing in his reign might be because his government was bad and he had incurred the censure of the deities, and he went out to 神淺茅原 (reading unconfirmed), gathered the eighty myriad deities and performed divination. Then a deity possessed Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto and declared that if the emperor revered and worshipped him, the land would become peaceful of itself, naming himself Ōmononushi-no-Kami, the deity dwelling within the land of Yamato. The emperor worshipped him as instructed, but it had no effect, so he bathed, observed abstinence, purified the inside of the palace, and prayed to be instructed in a dream. That night a noble person appeared in his dream, standing facing the door of the hall; he named himself Ōmononushi-no-Kami and said that the land was not at peace because it was his will, and that if the emperor had his son 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) worship him, it would at once be at peace and the countries beyond the sea would submit of their own accord.

In the 8th month, three people — 倭迹速神淺茅原目妙姫 (reading unconfirmed), 大水口宿禰 (reading unconfirmed; a distant ancestor of the 穗積臣), and 伊勢麻績君 (reading unconfirmed) — reported that they had all had the same dream, in which a noble person had told them to make 大田田根子命 (reading unconfirmed) the master of worship for Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and 市磯長尾市 (reading unconfirmed) the master of worship for Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大國魂神). The emperor proclaimed throughout the realm that 大田田根子 should be sought, and he was found at 陶邑 in 茅渟縣 (readings unconfirmed). When the emperor, at 神淺茅原 (reading unconfirmed), asked whose son he was, 大田田根子 answered that his father was Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and his mother was 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 陶津耳 (reading unconfirmed). Divination found it auspicious to make 伊香色雄 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the Mononobe no Muraji, the one who apportions the offerings to the deities, but found it inauspicious to worship other deities at the same time.

In the 11th month, the emperor ordered 伊香色雄 (reading unconfirmed) to use the ritual objects made by the eighty craftsmen (八十手) of the Mononobe, and made 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) the master of worship for Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and 長尾市 (reading unconfirmed) the master of worship for Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大國魂神). After that, divination about worshipping other deities proved auspicious, so the eighty myriad deities were worshipped separately, and heavenly shrines and earthly shrines (天社, 國社) and divine lands and shrine households (神地, 神戸) were established. With this the epidemic ceased for the first time, the land gradually became calm, the five grains ripened, and the peasants prospered.

In the 4th month of the 8th year, 活日 (reading unconfirmed), a man of the village of 高橋邑 (reading unconfirmed), was made sake steward of the Great Deity. In the 12th month, on the day the emperor had 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) worship the Great Deity, 活日 himself offered sacred sake to the emperor and composed a song. A banquet was held at the shrine, and at its end the ministers sang a song containing the phrase "瀰和能等能"; the emperor answered with a song containing the same phrase, opened the gate of the shrine and went out. 大田田根子 is regarded as the founding ancestor of the present-day Miwa no Kimi and others. In the 3rd month of the 9th year, a divine person instructed the emperor in a dream to worship Sumisaka-no-Kami with eight red shields and eight red spears, and Ōsaka-no-Kami with eight black shields and eight black spears, and in the 4th month he worshipped them as instructed.

quotes.note: The deity who possessed Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto names himself: "I am a deity dwelling within the land of Yamato, and my name is Ōmononushi-no-Kami."
The message in the dream: if you have my son 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) worship me, the land will at once be at peace.
The names of his father and mother that 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) gave in answer to the emperor.
With this the epidemic ceased for the first time.

figures.name: Ōmononushi-no-Kami (大物主神; also 大物主大神)
figures.role: Named himself the deity dwelling within the land of Yamato. He possessed Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto and also appeared in the emperor's dream, asking that his son 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed) be made to worship him.

figures.name: Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命)
figures.role: The woman whom Ōmononushi-no-Kami possessed at the divination in the 2nd month of the 7th year.

figures.name: 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man who named himself the son of Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami and 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed). He was found at 陶邑 in 茅渟縣 (readings unconfirmed) and made master of worship for Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami. Founding ancestor of the Miwa no Kimi and others.

figures.name: 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 陶津耳 (reading unconfirmed) and mother of 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 豐鍬入姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the emperor and the consort 遠津年魚眼眼妙媛 (reading unconfirmed). Entrusted with Amaterasu-Ōmikami, she worshipped her at 笠縫邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato.

figures.name: 渟名城入姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the emperor and the consort 尾張大海媛 (reading unconfirmed). She was entrusted with Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (日本大國魂神) but lost her hair, grew thin, and could not perform the worship.

figures.name: 市磯長尾市 (also 長尾市; reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The man made master of worship for Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大國魂神) in accordance with the instruction in the dream.

figures.name: 伊香色雄 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the Mononobe no Muraji. He was made the one who apportions the offerings to the deities, and used the ritual objects made by the eighty craftsmen of the Mononobe.

figures.name: 活日 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of 高橋邑 (reading unconfirmed). He was made sake steward of the Great Deity, and offered sacred sake and sang. A reading note in the text says "掌酒。此云佐介弭苔".

figures.name: Sumisaka-no-Kami (墨坂神)
figures.role: The deity worshipped with eight red shields and eight red spears according to the instruction in a dream in the 9th year.

figures.name: Ōsaka-no-Kami (大坂神)
figures.role: The deity worshipped with eight black shields and eight black spears according to the instruction in a dream in the 9th year.

figures.name: Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto (豐城入彦命)
figures.role: Son of the emperor and the consort 遠津年魚眼眼妙媛 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Sujin (the worship of the deities and the story of Mount Miwa)
compare.text: In the Kojiki too, in the midst of the epidemic Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami appears in the emperor's dream and tells him to have 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed) worship him, but 意富多多泥古 is found at 美努村 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi and names himself a descendant several generations down from Ōmononushi-no-Ōkami. The Kojiki further records the story in which a needle threaded with hemp yarn is stuck into the clothing of the man who visits 活玉依毘賣 (reading unconfirmed), and by following the thread he is found to be the deity of Mount Miwa (美和山); this could not be confirmed in this part of the Nihon Shoki.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Sujin (the worship of the deities)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the worship of Sumisaka-no-Kami with red shields and spears and of Ōsaka-no-Kami with black shields and spears is recorded as part of the same series of rites to quell the epidemic as the worship performed by 意富多多泥古 (reading unconfirmed). In the Nihon Shoki they are worshipped with eight red shields and eight red spears and with eight black shields and eight black spears, in accordance with a separate dream instruction in the 3rd month of the 9th year.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Sujin (genealogy of consorts and children)
compare.text: In the Kojiki there is only a small note in the genealogy saying that 豐鉏比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) worshipped at the shrine of the Great Deity of Ise; the story of Amaterasu-Ōmikami and Yamato-Ōkunitama-no-Kami (倭大國魂神) being brought out of the great hall to be worshipped could not be confirmed. In the Nihon Shoki, 豐鍬入姫命 (reading unconfirmed) worships Amaterasu-Ōmikami at 笠縫邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato.

variants.name: One account (一云): the consort 尾張大海媛 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: Whereas the main text gives the consort as 尾張大海媛 (reading unconfirmed), one account (一云) in a small note gives her as 八坂振天某邊 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大海宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Another account (亦云): the mother of 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: Besides giving 活玉依媛 (reading unconfirmed), the mother of 大田田根子 (reading unconfirmed), as the daughter of 陶津耳 (reading unconfirmed), the text records, as "亦云" (another account), a tradition that she was the daughter of 奇日方天日方武茅渟祇 (reading unconfirmed).

sujin-shido.title: The Generals of the Four Roads and the Rebellion of 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed), up to Hashihaka and the Sacred Treasures of Izumo
sujin-shido.lead: This page covers the period from the edict of the 10th year sending generals in the four directions, through the rebellion of 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed) that broke out before they departed and the story of Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto, Ōmononushi-no-Kami and Hashihaka (箸墓), to the census of the people in the 12th year and the title "御肇國天皇". It then records the dream divination to choose the crown prince, the quarrel between brothers over the sacred treasures of Izumo, the building of ponds, and tribute from Mimana, and the book ends with the emperor's death in the 68th year.

points.text: In the 9th month of the 10th year, Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命) was sent to Hokuriku (北陸), 武渟川別 (reading unconfirmed) to Tōkai (東海), 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) to the western road (西道), and 丹波道主命 (reading unconfirmed) to Tanba, with orders to raise troops and attack any who did not follow the teachings; they were given seals and ribbons of office and made generals.

Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto saw that the song of a girl heard by Ōbiko-no-Mikoto at 和珥坂 (reading unconfirmed) was a sign of rebellion by 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed), and also told how his wife 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed) had taken earth from Mount Kagu (香山) in Yamato and prayed, saying "倭國之物實". The rebellion was put down when 五十狹芹彦命 (reading unconfirmed) struck down 吾田媛 at Ōsaka (大坂), and 彦國葺 (reading unconfirmed) shot 武埴安彦 dead in Yamashiro (山背).

Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto became the wife of Ōmononushi-no-Kami, but the deity came only at night. When she asked to see his form, the deity answered that in the morning he would be inside her comb box; when she looked, there was a beautiful small snake, and she cried out, and the deity, ashamed, returned to 御諸山 (reading unconfirmed). The princess stabbed her genitals with a chopstick and died; she was buried at 大市 (reading unconfirmed), and her tomb was called Hashihaka (箸墓).

In the 9th month of the 12th year, the people were surveyed for the first time, and the bow-tip tribute (弭調) was imposed on men and the hand-end tribute (手末調) on women. Because the deities of heaven and earth were appeased and the realm became peaceful, the emperor was praised as "御肇國天皇".

The Kojiki also records the first imposition of the bow-tip tribute on men and the hand-end tribute on women (男弓端之調, 女手末之調), and praises that reign with the title "所知初國之御眞木天皇". The way this title of praise is written differs from the Nihon Shoki's "御肇國天皇".

Kokugakuin University's database of deity names states that it has been argued that the form of Ōmononushi-no-Kami is not clearly shown in the Kojiki, but that in the Nihon Shoki's entry for the 9th month of the 10th year of Emperor Sujin it is revealed to be a "small snake" (小蛇).

story.text: In the 7th month of the 10th year, the emperor told his ministers that the basis of guiding the people lies in teaching and civilizing them, and that because he had revered the deities of heaven and earth the disasters had ceased, but that people in distant regions still did not follow the king's teachings; and he issued an edict to select ministers and send them in the four directions. In the 9th month he sent Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命) to Hokuriku (北陸), 武渟川別 (reading unconfirmed) to Tōkai (東海), 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) to the western road (西道), and 丹波道主命 (reading unconfirmed) to Tanba, ordering them to raise troops and attack any who would not accept the teachings, and he gave them seals and ribbons of office and made them generals.

When Ōbiko-no-Mikoto reached the top of 和珥坂 (reading unconfirmed), a girl was singing an enigmatic song. When he asked what she meant, the girl answered that she was only singing, repeated the same song, and vanished. When Ōbiko-no-Mikoto went back and reported this, Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto, the emperor's aunt, who was wise and able to know things before they happened, said that this was a sign that 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed) would rebel. She told him she had heard that 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed), the wife of 武埴安彦, had come secretly, taken earth from Mount Kagu (香山) in Yamato, prayed, saying, "This is the 物實 of the land of Yamato," and gone back, and she urged him to act quickly. While the generals were being held back for consultation, 武埴安彦 and 吾田媛 raised troops and tried to attack the capital, the husband from Yamashiro (山背) and the wife from Ōsaka (大坂).

The emperor sent 五十狹芹彦命 (reading unconfirmed), who met the army of 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed) at Ōsaka (大坂), crushed it, and killed 吾田媛. Ōbiko and 彦國葺 (reading unconfirmed), a distant ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed), headed for Yamashiro; they set down a sacred jar (忌瓮) at the top of the 和珥 (reading unconfirmed) slope and then encamped on Mount Nara (那羅山) (it is called Mount Nara because the soldiers trampled the grass and trees flat). Facing 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed) across the river 輪韓河 (reading unconfirmed) (the origin of the name 挑河, the present 泉河; readings unconfirmed), 彦國葺 answered that his were righteous troops acting on the emperor's command. The arrow that 武埴安彦 shot first missed, while 彦國葺's arrow struck 武埴安彦 in the chest and killed him. It is said that from the places where the fleeing soldiers were pursued and cut down, where soldiers took off their armor, where they soiled their loincloths, and where they bowed their heads, came the place names 羽振苑, 伽和羅, 屎褌 (the present 樟葉) and 我君 (readings unconfirmed).

After that, Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto became the wife of Ōmononushi-no-Kami, but the deity was never seen by day and came only at night. The princess asked him, since she could not see his form in the daytime, to stay until the next morning and show her his beautiful form. The deity said this was reasonable, and answered that the next morning he would be inside her comb box, but asked her not to be startled by his form. When morning came and she looked in the comb box, there was a beautiful small snake about the size of a garment cord, and the princess was startled and cried out. The deity, ashamed, took human form and said, "You have put me to shame, so now I will put you to shame," and he trod the great sky and climbed to 御諸山 (reading unconfirmed). The princess looked up after him in regret, sat down abruptly, stabbed her genitals with a chopstick and died. She was buried at 大市 (reading unconfirmed), and her tomb was called Hashihaka (箸墓). It is said that the tomb was built by people by day and by the deity by night, and the text records that the people passed the stones of Mount Ōsaka (大坂山) from hand to hand from the mountain to the tomb; a song of the people of the time is added.

In the 10th month, the emperor issued an edict stating that the rebels had all been struck down and the home provinces were at peace, but that the unrest of the wild peoples beyond the sea had not yet ceased, and he ordered the generals of the four roads to set out quickly; on the day (丙子) the generals set out. In the 4th month of the 11th year, the generals of the four roads reported that they had pacified the barbarians (戎夷), and in that year many people of foreign customs submitted and the land was at peace. In the 3rd month of the 12th year, the emperor stated that at first his virtue had been insufficient and disasters such as epidemics had occurred, but that he had amended his offences, revered the deities of heaven and earth, spread his teachings and attacked those who would not obey, so that now even people beyond the sea had come to submit; and he issued an edict to survey the people anew and make known the order of their ages and the precedence of labor duties. In the 9th month the people were surveyed for the first time, and the bow-tip tribute (弭調) was imposed on men and the hand-end tribute (手末調) on women. The deities of heaven and earth were appeased, wind and rain came in their season, the hundred grains ripened and the realm became peaceful, so the emperor was praised as "御肇國天皇". In the 17th year, because the people of the coast were suffering for lack of boats, he had the provinces build boats, and in the 10th month ships were built for the first time.

In the 1st month of the 48th year, the emperor decided to determine by dream divination which of 豐城命 (Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto) and 活目尊 (reading unconfirmed) should be his heir. The elder brother, 豐城命, reported a dream in which he climbed 御諸山 (reading unconfirmed), faced east, thrust a spear eight times and swung a sword eight times; the younger, 活目尊, reported a dream in which he climbed to the summit of 御諸山, stretched ropes in the four directions and drove away sparrows eating the millet. The emperor judged that since the elder had faced only east he should govern the eastern lands, and since the younger had looked out over all four directions he should succeed to the throne; in the 4th month he made 活目尊 crown prince and had 豐城命 govern the eastern lands. 豐城命 is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 上毛野君 and the 下毛野君 (readings unconfirmed).

In the 7th month of the 60th year, the emperor said he wished to see the sacred treasures that 武日照命 (reading unconfirmed) had brought from heaven and deposited in the great shrine of the Great Deity of Izumo (出雲大神宮), and sent 武諸隅 (reading unconfirmed). Since 出雲振根 (reading unconfirmed), who had charge of the sacred treasures, had gone to Tsukushi, his younger brother 飯入根 (reading unconfirmed) received the imperial command and presented them. When 振根 returned he resented his younger brother; he lured him to the pool of 止屋 (reading unconfirmed), wore a fake sword made of wood himself, and while they bathed took his brother's real sword and wore it. The younger brother could not draw the wooden sword and was killed, and the people of the time composed a song. Receiving a complaint, the court sent 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) and 武渟河別 (reading unconfirmed) to strike down 出雲振根. The Izumo no Omi and others were afraid and for a time did not worship the Great Deity, but 氷香戸邊 (reading unconfirmed) of 氷上 (reading unconfirmed) in Tanba conveyed the strange words of an infant to the crown prince, and the emperor had the worship performed. In the 62nd year, declaring that agriculture is the great foundation of the realm, he had ponds and channels dug, and the ponds 依網池, 苅坂池 and 反折池 (readings unconfirmed) were built. In the 7th month of the 65th year, the country of Mimana sent 蘇那曷叱知 (reading unconfirmed) to bring tribute, and in the 12th month of the 68th year the emperor died at the age of one hundred and twenty; in the 8th month of the following year he was buried in the 山邊道上陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

quotes.note: The words of 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed) as she wrapped up the earth of Mount Kagu (香山) and prayed: this is the 物實 of the land of Yamato (the thing that represents the land).
The words of Ōmononushi-no-Kami: tomorrow morning I will be inside your comb box, but please do not be startled by my form.
This tomb (Hashihaka) was built by people by day and by the deity by night.
Therefore the emperor was praised as "御肇國天皇".

figures.name: Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命)
figures.role: The general sent to Hokuriku. He heard a girl's song at 和珥坂 (reading unconfirmed) and reported it, and together with 彦國葺 (reading unconfirmed) struck down 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro.

figures.name: 武渟川別 (also 武渟河別; reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The general sent to Tōkai. Later, together with 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed), he struck down 出雲振根 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 吉備津彦 (also 五十狹芹彦命; reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The general sent to the western road. He defeated the army of 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed) at Ōsaka (大坂), and later struck down 出雲振根 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 丹波道主命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The general sent to Tanba.

figures.name: Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto (倭迹迹日百襲姫命)
figures.role: The emperor's aunt. She saw that the girl's song was a sign of rebellion; later she became the wife of Ōmononushi-no-Kami and was buried at Hashihaka (箸墓).

figures.name: Ōmononushi-no-Kami (大物主神)
figures.role: He visited Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto only at night as her husband; when he was seen in the form of a small snake inside the comb box, he departed to 御諸山 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He rebelled together with his wife 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed), and was shot dead by 彦國葺 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro.

figures.name: 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Wife of 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed). She took earth from Mount Kagu (香山) in Yamato and prayed, then attacked from Ōsaka (大坂) and was struck down.

figures.name: 彦國葺 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A distant ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed). He went to Yamashiro with Ōbiko-no-Mikoto and shot 武埴安彦 (reading unconfirmed) dead.

figures.name: Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto (豐城命; also 豐城入彦命)
figures.role: The prince who, through the dream divination, came to govern the eastern lands. Founding ancestor of the 上毛野君 and the 下毛野君 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 活目尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The prince chosen as heir by the dream divination, who became crown prince in the 4th month of the 48th year.

figures.name: 出雲振根 and 飯入根 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Brothers who were distant ancestors of the Izumo no Omi. Over the presentation of the sacred treasures, the elder brother 振根 killed his younger brother 飯入根, and 振根 was struck down by the court's army.

figures.name: 蘇那曷叱知 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The man sent from the country of Mimana in the 65th year to bring tribute.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Sujin (dispatch to the provinces)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大毘古命) is sent to the 高志道 (reading unconfirmed), his son Takenunakawawake-no-Mikoto (建沼河別命) to the twelve roads of the east (東方十二道), and 日子坐王 (reading unconfirmed) to the province of 旦波 (reading unconfirmed); no dispatch to Kibi is recorded. The Nihon Shoki sends four men — Ōbiko-no-Mikoto (大彦命), 武渟川別 (reading unconfirmed), 吉備津彦 (reading unconfirmed) and 丹波道主命 (reading unconfirmed) — to Hokuriku, Tōkai, the western road and Tanba.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Sujin (the rebellion of 建波邇安王, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the emperor himself interprets the meaning of the girl's song as a sign of rebellion by "我之庶兄建波邇安王" (my elder half-brother 建波邇安王), and neither 吾田媛 (reading unconfirmed) nor Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime-no-Mikoto appears. The plot in which the two sides face each other across a river and 建波邇安王 (reading unconfirmed) dies by the arrow of 日子國夫玖命 (reading unconfirmed), and the origin of the place name "屎褌" (which the Kojiki identifies with the present 久須婆 and the Nihon Shoki with the present 樟葉; readings unconfirmed), resemble the Nihon Shoki.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto's slaying of 出雲建, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: A song closely resembling the song of the people of the time when, in the Nihon Shoki, 出雲振根 (reading unconfirmed) kills his younger brother with a wooden sword appears in the Kojiki, in the section on Emperor Keikō, as a song of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (倭建命) after he killed 出雲建 (reading unconfirmed) using a fake sword (詐刀) of 赤檮 (reading unconfirmed) wood.

variants.name: One account (一云): where Ōbiko-no-Mikoto heard the girl's song
variants.text: Whereas the main text says that Ōbiko-no-Mikoto heard the girl's song at the top of 和珥坂 (reading unconfirmed), one account (一云) says that a young girl by the roadside sang when he arrived at 平坂 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro.

variants.name: One account (一云): another form of the girl's song
variants.text: For the girl's song, one account (一云) gives a different form of the song, beginning with "於朋耆妬庸利".

variants.name: One account (一云) and another account (又云): 武日照命 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: Of 武日照命 (reading unconfirmed), who brought the sacred treasures from heaven, one account (一云) gives the name as 武夷鳥 and another account (又云) as 天夷鳥 (readings unconfirmed).

variants.name: Variant account (一書云): 武諸隅 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: Of 武諸隅 (reading unconfirmed), who was sent to have the sacred treasures presented, a variant account (一書) gives another name, 大母隅 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): the three ponds
variants.text: Of the ponds 依網池, 苅坂池 and 反折池 (readings unconfirmed), one account (一云) says that the emperor built these three ponds while he was living at the 桑間宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

suinin-sahohiko.title: The Accession of Emperor Suinin, the Rebellion of 狭穂彦王, and 誉津別命 (readings unconfirmed)
suinin-sahohiko.lead: This page covers the period from the accession of Emperor Suinin, through the rebellion of 狭穂彦王 (reading unconfirmed), elder brother of the empress 狭穂姫 (reading unconfirmed), and his end in the rice-stack fortress, to the time when the prince 誉津別命 (reading unconfirmed), who did not speak, gained the power of speech on seeing a swan (鵠). In between, it also records the beginning of the enmity between Mimana and Silla, the arrival of the Silla prince Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍), the contest of strength between 野見宿禰 and 当麻蹶速 (readings unconfirmed), and the entry into the palace of five daughters from Tanba.

points.text: In the 9th month of the 4th year, 狭穂彦王 (reading unconfirmed) asked his younger sister the empress, "Which do you love more, your brother or your husband?" and gave her a dagger with which to stab the emperor. In the 10th month of the 5th year, the empress could not bring herself to stab the emperor as he slept with his head on her lap; her tears fell on the emperor's face, and the emperor's dream of "a small brocade-colored snake, and heavy rain from 狭穂 (reading unconfirmed)" led her to confess the plot.

狭穂彦王 (reading unconfirmed) piled up rice to make a "rice-stack fortress" (稲城) and resisted. The empress entered the fortress holding the prince 誉津別命 (reading unconfirmed), but when it was attacked with fire she sent the prince out of the fortress, asked that the women's quarters of the palace be entrusted to the five daughters of 丹波道主王 (reading unconfirmed), and died in the fortress together with her brother.

誉津別命 (reading unconfirmed) did not speak even when he was thirty and his beard had grown long, but in the 10th month of the 23rd year, seeing a swan (鵠) flying across the sky, he said "是何物耶". 天湯河板挙 (reading unconfirmed) caught the swan and presented it; the prince played with it and became able to speak, and the title of 鳥取造 and the groups 鳥取部, 鳥養部 and 誉津部 (readings unconfirmed) were established.

In the 7th month of the 7th year, 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), summoned from Izumo, fought 当麻蹶速 (reading unconfirmed) in a contest of strength in which they kicked at each other with their feet, killed 蹶速, and was given his land. This is regarded as the origin of the "腰折田" (reading unconfirmed) of the village of 当麻邑.

Kokugakuin University's database of deity names (entry: the Great Deity of Izumo, 出雲大神) introduces an argument that, whereas in the Kojiki 本牟智和気 (reading unconfirmed) becomes able to speak when the curse of the Great Deity of Izumo is appeased, the Great Deity of Izumo does not appear in the chronicle of Emperor Suinin in the Nihon Shoki, and the swan story places its emphasis on telling of the merit of the 鳥取造 (reading unconfirmed) and the origin of the 鳥取部 and similar groups.

The belongings of the Silla prince Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍), who came in the 3rd month of the 3rd year, are in the main text seven kinds, such as 羽太玉, 出石小刀, 日鏡 and 熊神籬 (readings unconfirmed), which were deposited in Tajima; in one account (一云) they are eight kinds, with the addition of 膽狭浅大刀 (reading unconfirmed). The database of deity names (entry: Izushi-Yamae-no-Ōkami, 伊豆志之八前大神) points out that these differ greatly, in both items and character, from the eight treasures of the Kojiki (jewels, scarves (比礼) and mirrors).

story.text: 活目入彦五十狭茅天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Suinin) was the third son of 御間城入彦五十瓊殖天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Sujin), and his mother was 御間城姫 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Ōbiko-no-Mikoto. He was born in the 瑞籬宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in the 1st month of the 29th year of Emperor Sujin, and his father loved him for his unaffected character. At twenty-four he became crown prince on the strength of a sign in a dream, and his father died in the 12th month of the 68th year of Emperor Sujin. He acceded to the throne in the 1st month of his 1st year; in the 10th month he buried his father in the 山辺道上陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb, and in the 11th month he made the empress the empress dowager. In the 2nd month of the 2nd year, 狭穂姫 (reading unconfirmed) became empress and bore 誉津別命 (reading unconfirmed). The emperor doted on this prince and always kept him at his side, but even when he grew up he did not speak. In the 10th month the capital was moved to 纒向 (reading unconfirmed), and the palace was called 珠城宮 (reading unconfirmed).

In this year 蘇那曷叱智 (reading unconfirmed), a man of Mimana, asked to return to his country, so the emperor gave him generous rewards and had him carry one hundred bolts of red silk for the king of Mimana. But people of Silla seized them on the way, and it is said that the enmity between Mimana and Silla began at this time. In the 3rd month of the 3rd year, the Silla prince Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍) came, bringing seven items such as jewels, a small sword, a halberd, a mirror and a 熊神籬 (reading unconfirmed); these were deposited in the province of Tajima and made sacred objects.

In the 9th month of the 4th year, 狭穂彦王 (reading unconfirmed), the empress's elder brother by the same mother, plotted to endanger the state. He asked the empress which she loved more, her brother or her husband, and when the empress answered her brother, he argued that favor that relies on beauty does not last long, and gave her a dagger, telling her to kill the emperor in his sleep. The empress trembled with fear but could not admonish her brother either, and kept the dagger hidden in her clothing.

In the 10th month of the 5th year, the emperor took a midday nap at the 高宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in 来目 (reading unconfirmed), with his head on the empress's lap. Thinking of her brother's plan, the empress shed tears, which fell on the emperor's face. When the emperor woke and said he had dreamed that a small brocade-colored snake wound around his neck and heavy rain came from 狭穂 (reading unconfirmed) and wet his face, the empress could no longer hide it and confessed the plot, and the emperor said it was not the empress's crime. The emperor had 八綱田 (reading unconfirmed) attack 狭穂彦 (reading unconfirmed), but 狭穂彦 shut himself up in a rice-stack fortress (稲城) made of piled rice, and the empress, too, entered the fortress holding 誉津別命 (reading unconfirmed). When 八綱田 set fire to the fortress, the empress sent the prince out of the fortress, asked that the five daughters of 丹波道主王 (reading unconfirmed) be taken into the women's quarters of the palace, and died in the fortress together with her brother. The emperor praised 八綱田's achievement and gave him the name 倭日向武日向彦八綱田 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 7th month of the 7th year, because 当麻蹶速 (reading unconfirmed) of the village of 当麻邑 was boasting everywhere that no one was stronger than he, the emperor summoned 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) of Izumo and had them compete in strength. The two raised their feet and kicked at each other, and 野見宿禰 stamped on 蹶速, broke his ribs and his back, and killed him. 蹶速's land was given to 野見宿禰, who then remained and served at the court.

In the 15th year, the five daughters from Tanba entered the women's quarters of the palace, and in the 8th month 日葉酢媛命 (reading unconfirmed) became empress. Only the youngest, 竹野媛 (reading unconfirmed), was sent back to her province on account of her looks; ashamed of this, she fell from her palanquin at 葛野 (reading unconfirmed) and died, so that place is called 堕国, and it is said that the present 弟国 is a corruption of that name (readings unconfirmed). The empress bore 五十瓊敷入彦命, 大足彦尊, 大中姫命, 倭姫命 and 稚城瓊入彦命 (readings unconfirmed).

In the 9th month of the 23rd year, the emperor consulted his ministers because Prince 誉津別王 (reading unconfirmed), though thirty years old and with a long beard, still cried like an infant and did not speak. In the 10th month, the prince looked up at a swan (鵠) crossing the sky and said, "What is that?"; the emperor rejoiced and sought someone to catch the swan. 天湯河板挙 (reading unconfirmed) pursued the swan and caught it in Izumo, and when he presented it in the 11th month, the prince played with it and at last became able to speak. 天湯河板挙 was granted the title of 鳥取造 (reading unconfirmed), and the groups 鳥取部, 鳥養部 and 誉津部 (readings unconfirmed) were established.

quotes.note: The words with which 狭穂彦王 (reading unconfirmed) questioned his younger sister the empress: "Which do you love more, your brother or your husband?"
The dream the emperor had: a small brocade-colored snake wound around his neck, and heavy rain came from 狭穂 (reading unconfirmed) and wet his face.
狭穂彦 (reading unconfirmed) piled up rice to make a fortress, and it was so solid that it could not be broken. This is called a rice-stack fortress (稲城).
The scene in which the prince who had not spoken looks up at a swan (鵠) and says, "What is that?"

figures.name: 活目入彦五十狹茅天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The third son of Emperor Sujin, and the emperor of this book (Emperor Suinin).

figures.name: 狹穗彦王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother by the same mother of the empress 狭穂姫 (reading unconfirmed). He incited the empress to kill the emperor, shut himself up in the rice-stack fortress, and died.

figures.name: 狹穗姫 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The empress installed in the 2nd year. She confessed her brother's plot, and later died together with her brother in the rice-stack fortress.

figures.name: 譽津別命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The prince borne by 狭穂姫 (reading unconfirmed). For a long time he did not speak, but he became able to speak after the swan was obtained.

figures.name: 八綱田 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A distant ancestor of the 上毛野君 (reading unconfirmed). He attacked 狭穂彦 (reading unconfirmed) and was granted the name 倭日向武日向彦八綱田 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A brave man of Izumo. He won the contest of strength against 当麻蹶速 (reading unconfirmed) and served at the court.

figures.name: 當麻蹶速 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A strongman of the village of 当麻邑 (reading unconfirmed). He was defeated by 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and died.

figures.name: 日葉酢媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 丹波道主王 (reading unconfirmed), who became empress after 狭穂姫 (reading unconfirmed). Mother of 大足彦尊 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Keikō).

figures.name: 竹野媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The youngest of the five daughters from Tanba. She died on the way after being sent back to her province, and became the origin of the place name 堕国 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 天湯河板擧 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 鳥取造 (reading unconfirmed). He caught and presented the swan, and was granted the title of 鳥取造.

figures.name: 蘇那曷叱智 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of Mimana. The red silk he was given when returning home was seized by Silla.

figures.name: 都怒我阿羅斯等 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince of the country of 意富加羅国 (reading unconfirmed) who appears in one account (一云). He is regarded as the origin of the place name 角鹿 and of the country name 彌摩那国 (readings unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Suinin (the rebellion of 沙本毘古王, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the empress enters the rice-stack fortress while pregnant, the prince is born inside the fortress, and because he was born in the midst of fire he is said to have been named 本牟智和気 (reading unconfirmed). In the Nihon Shoki, 誉津別命 (reading unconfirmed) had already been born in the 2nd year, and the empress enters the fortress holding him.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Suinin (the prince 本牟智和気, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the prince still does not speak even after the swan is caught; a curse of the Great Deity of Izumo is revealed in the emperor's dream, and only when the prince has worshipped the Great Deity of Izumo does he become able to speak. In the Nihon Shoki, he becomes able to speak by playing with the swan, and the Great Deity of Izumo does not appear.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Suinin (latter part of the story of the prince 本牟智和気, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: The daughter who is sent back to her province, dies, and becomes the origin of the name "堕国 (弟国)" is, in the Kojiki, 円野比売 (reading unconfirmed), who is said to have tried to hang herself at 相楽 (reading unconfirmed) and then to have fallen into a deep pool at 弟国 and died. In the Nihon Shoki, 竹野媛 (reading unconfirmed) falls from her palanquin at 葛野 (reading unconfirmed) and dies.

variants.name: One account (一云): variant tradition in the "this year" entry of the 2nd year, part 1
variants.text: It says that in the time of Emperor Sujin, 都怒我阿羅斯等 (reading unconfirmed), a prince of the country of 意富加羅国 (reading unconfirmed) with a horn on his forehead, arrived at the bay of 笥飯浦 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Koshi (越国), and named the place 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed). When he returned home after serving Emperor Suinin for three years, he was told to name his country 彌摩那国 (reading unconfirmed) after the name of 御間城天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and was given red woven silk; Silla's seizure of it was the beginning of the enmity between the two countries.

variants.name: One account (一云): variant tradition in the "this year" entry of the 2nd year, part 2
variants.text: It says that a white stone, a deity worshipped within a district, which 都怒我阿羅斯等 (reading unconfirmed) had obtained in place of an ox, turned into a beautiful girl, and when she vanished he followed her and came to Japan. The girl is said to have been worshipped as the deity of the 比売語曾社 (reading unconfirmed) shrine in Naniwa and in the district of 国前郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Toyo (豊国).

variants.name: One account (一云): variant tradition in the entry for the 3rd month of the 3rd year
variants.text: It says that Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍) first arrived at the village of 完粟邑 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Harima and presented eight items, including the sword 膽狭浅大刀 (reading unconfirmed). Wishing to choose a place to live himself, he went from the Uji River (菟道河) through Ōmi and Wakasa and settled in Tajima, and the text records that his descendants by a woman of Tajima continued down to 清彦 (reading unconfirmed) and then 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the entry for the 10th month of the 5th year
variants.text: Against the note in the main text that makes 丹波道主王 (reading unconfirmed) the son of 彦坐王 (reading unconfirmed), it makes him the son of 彦湯産隅王 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Some say (或曰): entry for the 10th month of the 23rd year
variants.text: It says that 天湯河板挙 (reading unconfirmed) caught the swan not in Izumo but in the province of Tajima.

suinin-jidai.title: 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) and the Worship at Ise, the Origin of Haniwa, the Sacred Treasures of Ame-no-Hiboko, and 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed)
suinin-jidai.lead: This page covers the entries from the 25th year of Emperor Suinin onward, recording that 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) worshipped Amaterasu-Ōmikami at Ise, that the practice of following the dead in death was stopped and haniwa were set up instead, the development of ponds and channels, the sacred treasures of Isonokami Shrine (石上神宮), and the presentation of the sacred treasures of Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍). The emperor died in the 99th year, and 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed), who brought back the 非時香菓 from the Land of Tokoyo (常世国), wept and cried out at the emperor's tomb and died.

points.text: In the 3rd month of the 25th year, Amaterasu-Ōmikami was taken from 豊耜入姫命 (reading unconfirmed) and entrusted to 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed). 倭姫命 traveled through 菟田 (reading unconfirmed), Ōmi and Mino and reached Ise; following the Great Deity's instruction, she built a shrine in Ise and established the abstinence palace (斎宮) by the Isuzu River.

In the 28th year, when attendants were buried alive at the tomb of the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, 倭彦命 (reading unconfirmed), they wept and cried out for several days and then died. The emperor grieved over this and ordered that the practice of following the dead in death be stopped.

When the empress 日葉酢媛命 (reading unconfirmed) died in the 32nd year, 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) summoned one hundred clay workers (土部) from Izumo and proposed making figures of people, horses and other things out of clay and setting them up at the tomb in place of living people. These clay objects were called haniwa (埴輪), or "standing objects" (立物), and 野見宿禰 was granted the title 土部臣 (reading unconfirmed) and is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 土部連 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 90th year, the emperor sent 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed) to the Land of Tokoyo (常世国) to seek the 非時香菓 (what is now the tachibana, 橘). 田道間守 returned in the following year (the 1st year of Emperor Keikō), but the emperor had already died, and he wept and cried out toward the tomb and died.

In the 39th year, 五十瓊敷命 (reading unconfirmed) made one thousand swords, deposited them at Isonokami Shrine (石上神宮), and took charge of the sacred treasures. In the 87th year, 五十瓊敷命, now old, wished to entrust them to his younger sister 大中姫命 (reading unconfirmed), but 大中姫命 had 物部十千根大連 (reading unconfirmed) manage them; this is regarded as the origin of the Mononobe no Muraji managing the sacred treasures of Isonokami to this day.

In the 88th year, 清彦 (reading unconfirmed), the great-grandson of Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍), presented the sacred treasures but tried to hide only the small sword called 出石 (reading unconfirmed); even after it had been presented, the small sword returned of its own accord to 清彦's house, and it is said that it then moved to Awaji Island and was worshipped in a shrine. The database of deity names (entry: Izushi-Yamae-no-Ōkami, 伊豆志之八前大神) introduces a theory that draws attention to the point that, whereas in the Kojiki the treasures remain at 出石, in the Nihon Shoki they are presented and deposited in the divine storehouse (神府), and takes this to show that the sacred treasures of 出石 were absorbed into the rituals of the royal court.

story.text: In the 2nd month of the 25th year, the emperor told five high officials, distant ancestors of the Abe no Omi, the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed), the Nakatomi no Muraji, the Mononobe no Muraji and the Ōtomo no Muraji, that because the previous emperor, Emperor Sujin, had reverently worshipped the deities, the realm had been at peace, and that in his own reign too the worship of the deities must not be neglected. In the 3rd month, Amaterasu-Ōmikami was taken from 豊耜入姫命 (reading unconfirmed) and entrusted to 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed). Seeking a place where the Great Deity would settle, 倭姫命 went to 筱幡 in 菟田 (readings unconfirmed), and passing through the province of Ōmi and the province of Mino, reached the province of Ise. The Great Deity instructed her that Ise was a beautiful land where the waves of Tokoyo (常世) roll in, and that she wished to stay there; so a shrine was set up in the province of Ise and the abstinence palace (斎宮) was established by the Isuzu River. In the 26th year, 物部十千根大連 (reading unconfirmed) went to Izumo to examine the sacred treasures and was entrusted with their management. In the 27th year, divination about making weapons into offerings to the deities proved auspicious, so bows and arrows and swords (横刀) were deposited at the various shrines, and divine lands and shrine households (神地, 神戸) were established. Worshipping the deities with weapons is regarded as having begun at this time. In this year a royal granary (屯倉) was established at the village of 来目邑 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 28th year, the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, 倭彦命 (reading unconfirmed), died, and his attendants were buried alive around his tomb. They did not die for several days but wept and cried out day and night, and the emperor, hearing their voices, grieved and had the ending of following the dead in death deliberated. In the 30th year, the emperor asked two princes what they wished for; the elder, 五十瓊敷命 (reading unconfirmed), wished for a bow and arrows, and the younger, 大足彦尊 (reading unconfirmed), wished for the throne, so he granted each his wish.

In the 32nd year, the empress 日葉酢媛命 (reading unconfirmed) died. The emperor knew that following the dead in death was not good, but was uncertain how to conduct the burial; 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) offered advice, summoned one hundred clay workers (土部) from the province of Izumo, had them make figures of people, horses and other things from clay (埴土), and presented them. The emperor was pleased and set these up for the first time at the tomb of 日葉酢媛命, named them haniwa (埴輪) or "standing objects" (立物), and ordered that from then on these clay objects must always be set up at tombs. 野見宿禰 was given the title 土部臣 (reading unconfirmed) and the office of the clay workers, and this is regarded as the origin of the 土部連 (reading unconfirmed) and others presiding over the funerals of emperors.

In the 34th year, the emperor went to Yamashiro, took the beautiful 綺戸辺 (reading unconfirmed) into the women's quarters of the palace, and 磐衝別命 (reading unconfirmed) was born. It is said that when the emperor prayed for a sign, a large turtle came out of the river as he was arriving at the temporary palace, and when he stabbed it with a spear it turned into a white stone. In the 35th year, he had 五十瓊敷命 (reading unconfirmed) build the ponds 高石池 and 茅渟池 (readings unconfirmed) in the province of Kawachi, and further the ponds 狭城池 and 迹見池 (readings unconfirmed) in Yamato, and had more than eight hundred ponds and channels dug in the provinces to promote agriculture, so that the people became prosperous. In the 37th year, 大足彦尊 (reading unconfirmed) was made crown prince.

In the 39th year, 五十瓊敷命 (reading unconfirmed) made one thousand swords at the 菟砥川上宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed) and deposited them at Isonokami Shrine, and thereafter he took charge of the sacred treasures of Isonokami Shrine. In the 87th year, 五十瓊敷命, now old, wished to entrust the sacred treasures to his younger sister 大中姫命 (reading unconfirmed), but 大中姫命 had 物部十千根大連 (reading unconfirmed) manage them. The text also records the story that when the dog of 甕襲 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Tanba killed a wild beast, a curved jewel (八尺瓊勾玉) came out of the beast's belly, and that it is kept at Isonokami Shrine.

In the 88th year, the emperor said he wished to see the treasures that Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍) had brought, and had his great-grandson 清彦 (reading unconfirmed) present them. 清彦 hid only the small sword called 出石 (reading unconfirmed) in his clothing, but it was discovered and he presented it, and the treasures were deposited in the divine storehouse (神府). However, the small sword disappeared and returned to 清彦's house, and it is said that it then moved to Awaji Island and was worshipped by the people of the island. Next the text records that Ame-no-Hiboko stayed in Tajima, married the daughter of 前津耳 (reading unconfirmed), and fathered 但馬諸助 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 90th year, the emperor sent 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed) to the Land of Tokoyo (常世国) to seek the 非時香菓 (what is now the tachibana, 橘). In the 7th month of the 99th year, the emperor died at the 纒向宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace at the age of one hundred and forty, and in the 12th month he was buried in the 菅原伏見陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb. In the 3rd month of the following year, 田道間守 returned bringing the 非時香菓, eight on stalks and eight on strings (八竿八縵), but the emperor was already dead; lamenting the hardship of the ten years spent going and returning, he wept and cried out toward the tomb and died of his own accord. 田道間守 is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 三宅連 (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The words of Amaterasu-Ōmikami to 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed): Ise is a land where the waves of Tokoyo (常世) roll in, wave upon wave.
The emperor's words: to make those one loved in life follow the dead in death is a very painful thing.
These objects made of clay were named haniwa (埴輪), and were also called "standing objects" (立物).
The emperor sent 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed) to the Land of Tokoyo (常世国) and had him seek the 非時香菓.

figures.name: 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A daughter of Emperor Suinin. She was entrusted with Amaterasu-Ōmikami and set up a shrine in Ise.

figures.name: 豐耜入姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The princess who had been entrusted with Amaterasu-Ōmikami before 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 物部十千根大連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He examined the sacred treasures of Izumo, and later managed the sacred treasures of Isonokami Shrine.

figures.name: 倭彦命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The emperor's younger brother by the same mother. The following in death at his funeral led to the ending of the practice.

figures.name: 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He proposed setting up haniwa and was granted the title 土部臣 (reading unconfirmed). Founding ancestor of the 土部連 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: 日葉酢媛命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The empress. Haniwa were set up for the first time at her tomb.

figures.name: 五十瓊敷命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of the emperor. He built ponds, deposited one thousand swords at Isonokami Shrine, and took charge of the sacred treasures.

figures.name: 大足彦尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of the emperor. He wished for the throne and became crown prince in the 37th year (later Emperor Keikō).

figures.name: 大中姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 五十瓊敷命 (reading unconfirmed). She had 物部十千根大連 (reading unconfirmed) manage the sacred treasures.

figures.name: 清彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Great-grandson of Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍). He presented the sacred treasures, but tried to hide the small sword 出石 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He brought the 非時香菓 back from the Land of Tokoyo (常世国), but on learning of the emperor's death he died at the tomb. Founding ancestor of the 三宅連 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Suinin (多遅摩毛理, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, 多遅摩毛理 (reading unconfirmed) presents half of the eight strings and eight spears (縵八縵, 矛八矛) he brought back to the empress, places the rest at the emperor's tomb, and weeps and cries out and dies. In the Nihon Shoki he brings back "八竿八縵" and dies before the tomb lamenting his ten years of hardship, and no presentation to the empress is recorded.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Sujin (small note in the genealogy of his children) and the end of the section on Emperor Suinin
compare.text: The Kojiki records, in a small note in the section on Emperor Sujin, that a "human hedge" (人垣) was first set up at a tomb at the time of 倭日子命 (reading unconfirmed), and in the section on Emperor Suinin says that the 土師部 (reading unconfirmed) was established at the time of the empress 比婆須比売命 (reading unconfirmed). A story like that of the Nihon Shoki — that the emperor, grieving over the following in death for 倭彦命 (reading unconfirmed), stopped the practice, and that haniwa were set up on the proposal of 野見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) — could not be confirmed.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (Ame-no-Hiboko, 天之日矛)
compare.text: The Kojiki places the story of Ame-no-Hiboko (天之日矛) in the section on Emperor Ōjin as an event of "long ago" (昔); the treasures are eight kinds — two strings of jewels, four kinds of scarves (比礼) and two kinds of mirrors — and are regarded as Izushi-Yamae-no-Ōkami (伊豆志之八前大神). In the genealogy too, 清日子 (reading unconfirmed) is made a brother of 多遅摩毛理 (reading unconfirmed), which differs from the Nihon Shoki's one account (一云), which makes 清彦 (reading unconfirmed) the father of 田道間守 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): variant tradition in the entry for the 3rd month of the 25th year
variants.text: It says that 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) worshipped Amaterasu-Ōmikami at the foot of the sacred oak (厳橿) of 磯城 (reading unconfirmed), and afterwards, in the 10th month of the year (丁巳), moved her to the 渡遇宮 (reading unconfirmed) shrine in the province of Ise. It also records that the Great Deity of Yamato (倭大神) possessed 大水口宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), a distant ancestor of the 穂積臣 (reading unconfirmed), and declared that the previous emperor had been short-lived because he had not searched out the root of the worship of the deities; that 渟名城稚姫命 (reading unconfirmed) was chosen by divination but was too weak in body to perform the worship; and that 長尾市宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 倭直 (reading unconfirmed), was made to perform the worship.

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the entry for the 7th month of the 32nd year
variants.text: It gives the name of the empress 日葉酢媛命 (reading unconfirmed) as 日葉酢根命 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): variant tradition in the entry for the 10th month of the 39th year
variants.text: It says that Prince 五十瓊敷 (reading unconfirmed) had a smith named 河上 (reading unconfirmed) make one thousand swords (大刀), and was granted ten occupational groups (品部), including the 楯部 and the 倭文部 (readings unconfirmed). It says that the swords were first deposited at the village of 忍坂邑 (reading unconfirmed) and later moved to Isonokami Shrine, and that at the deity's request 市河 (reading unconfirmed), of the kin of the 春日臣 (reading unconfirmed), was made to manage them, and it makes him the founding ancestor of the 物部首 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the entry for the 7th month of the 88th year
variants.text: It gives 前津耳 (reading unconfirmed), the father of the woman Ame-no-Hiboko (天日槍) married, as 前津見 or 太耳 (readings unconfirmed).

keiko-junko.title: The Accession of Emperor Keikō and His Tour of Kyūshū
keiko-junko.lead: After recording the accession of Emperor Keikō and his consorts and children, including the twins 大碓 and 小碓 (readings unconfirmed; 小碓 is Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto), this page records the tour in which, after the Kumaso rebelled in the 12th year, the emperor himself set out for Tsukushi, travelled through Buzen, Bungo, Hyūga, Hi and Chikugo, and subdued the tsuchigumo (土蜘蛛) and the Kumaso. Many origins of local place names are told, and the page extends to the return to the capital in the 19th year and Takeuchi-no-Sukune's inspection of the eastern lands.

points.text: In the 2nd year, the empress 播磨稲日大郎姫 (reading unconfirmed) bore Prince 大碓 and 小碓尊 (readings unconfirmed) as twins on a single day, and these names are said to have arisen because the emperor cried out toward a mortar (碓). 小碓尊 was also called 日本童男 (reading unconfirmed) and Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (日本武尊); he was one jō (一丈) tall and strong enough to lift a cauldron (鼎).

In the 12th year, because the Kumaso neglected their tribute, the emperor set out for Tsukushi. The text records that at 娑麼 in 周芳 (readings unconfirmed), a female chieftain, 神夏磯媛 (reading unconfirmed), hung a sword, a mirror and a jewel (瓊) on a sakaki tree (賢木), raised a white flag and submitted, and that at 碩田 (reading unconfirmed) in Bungo the tsuchigumo were struck down with mallets made of camellia wood (海石榴), giving rise to the place names 海石榴市 and 血田 (readings unconfirmed).

At the 高屋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Hyūga, the emperor deliberated on attacking the Kumaso, and won over 市乾鹿文 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the Kumaso chieftain, by pretending to favor her. 市乾鹿文 made her father drunk and cut his bowstring, and an attendant killed her father, but the emperor, hating her lack of filial piety, put 市乾鹿文 to death, and in the 5th month of the 13th year he pacified the land of 襲国 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 17th year, at 子湯県 (reading unconfirmed), the emperor looked to the east and named the land "Hyūga" (日向), saying that it faced straight toward the direction where the sun rises; climbing a large rock in the fields, he sang the "Song of Longing for Home" (思邦歌), yearning for the capital.

The "Song of Longing for Home" (思邦歌) that Emperor Keikō sings in Hyūga in the Nihon Shoki has almost the same words as the "Song of Longing for the Land" (思国歌) that Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (倭建命) sings at 能煩野 (reading unconfirmed) just before his death in the Kojiki. The singer and the scene differ between the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki.

On the return journey in the 18th year, the origins of the names of various places, such as the land of Hi (火国), Aso, 御木 and 八女 (readings unconfirmed), are told as the words of the emperor or the answers of local people. In the section on Emperor Keikō in the Kojiki, no entry corresponding to a tour of Tsukushi by the emperor himself could be confirmed.

story.text: 大足彦忍代別天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Keikō) was the third son of Emperor Suinin, and his mother was the empress 日葉洲媛命 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 丹波道主王 (reading unconfirmed). He became crown prince in the 37th year of Emperor Suinin, and when his father died in the 99th year, he acceded to the throne in the 7th month of that year and changed the era (改元). This year was the year (辛未). In the 3rd month of the 2nd year, he made 播磨稲日大郎姫 (reading unconfirmed) his empress, and the empress bore Prince 大碓 and 小碓尊 (readings unconfirmed) as twins on the same day. 小碓尊 was also called 日本童男 (reading unconfirmed), or Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (日本武尊); he was brave from his childhood, and when he grew up he was one jō tall and strong enough to lift a cauldron. In the 3rd year, the emperor intended to worship the deities in the province of Kii, but the divination was inauspicious, so he sent 屋主忍男武雄心命 (reading unconfirmed). He lived for nine years at the 柏原 of 阿備 (readings unconfirmed), married 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 菟道彦 (reading unconfirmed), a distant ancestor of the 紀直 (reading unconfirmed), and Takeuchi-no-Sukune (武内宿禰) was born.

In the 4th year, the emperor sought 弟媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Prince 八坂入彦 (reading unconfirmed), in Mino, but 弟媛 hid in a bamboo grove. The emperor stayed for a time at the 泳宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, set carp floating in the pond and amused himself with them, and detained 弟媛 when she came secretly to look. 弟媛, saying that she did not care for relations between men and women, asked that her elder sister 八坂入媛 (reading unconfirmed) be taken into the women's quarters of the palace in her place. 八坂入媛 bore seven sons and six daughters, including 稚足彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Seimu), and the emperor's children numbered eighty in all. Apart from Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto, 稚足彦天皇 and Prince 五百城入彦 (reading unconfirmed), the seventy-odd others were enfeoffed in provinces and districts, and it is said that the "別" of the various provinces are their descendants. In this month, 大碓命 (reading unconfirmed), who had been sent to see the two beautiful daughters of 神骨 (reading unconfirmed), the provincial chief (国造) of Mino, secretly had relations with them and did not report back, so the emperor resented 大碓命. In the 11th month the emperor returned to 纒向 (reading unconfirmed) and made the 日代宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace his capital.

In the 7th month of the 12th year, the Kumaso rebelled, and in the 8th month the emperor set out for Tsukushi. In the 9th month, at 娑麼 in 周芳 (readings unconfirmed), he saw much smoke rising to the south and sent messengers, whereupon the female chieftain 神夏磯媛 (reading unconfirmed) submitted and told him that there were four bandits: 鼻垂, 耳垂, 麻剥 and 土折猪折 (readings unconfirmed). 武諸木 (reading unconfirmed) and others lured out 麻剥's followers with red garments and other gifts, and captured and killed all four. The emperor built a temporary palace at 長峡県 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Buzen, and named that place 京 ("the capital").

In the 10th month, the emperor reached the land of 碩田国 (reading unconfirmed), and heard from 速津媛 (reading unconfirmed), the female chieftain of the village of 速見邑 (reading unconfirmed), that tsuchigumo (土蜘蛛) — 青 and 白 of the 鼠 rock cave, and 打猿, 八田 and 国摩侶 of 禰疑野 (readings unconfirmed) — would not submit. The emperor had mallets made of camellia wood (海石榴) and gave them to his picked soldiers, and they struck down the tsuchigumo of the rock cave at the upper reaches of the 稲葉 (reading unconfirmed) river. It is said that the place was called 海石榴市 and the place where the blood flowed 血田 (readings unconfirmed). Next he defeated 八田, and 打猿, seeing that he could not win, asked to surrender, but this was not permitted, and they all threw themselves into a valley and died. When the emperor kicked a stone on the great plain of 柏峡 (reading unconfirmed), it flew up like an oak leaf, so the stone was called 蹈石 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 11th month, he reached the province of Hyūga and built the 高屋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. In the 12th month, as a plan to strike down 厚鹿文 (reading unconfirmed), chieftain of the Kumaso, and his men, he tricked the chieftain's two daughters with gifts and invited them. The elder, 市乾鹿文 (reading unconfirmed), made her father drunk, cut his bowstring, and had an attendant kill her father, but the emperor, hating her lack of filial piety, put 市乾鹿文 to death, and gave the younger sister, 市鹿文 (reading unconfirmed), to the 火国造 (reading unconfirmed). In the 5th month of the 13th year he pacified the land of 襲国 (reading unconfirmed), and during the six years he stayed at the 高屋宮 palace he took Mihakashi-hime (御刀媛) as consort, and Prince 豊国別 (reading unconfirmed) was born. In the 17th year, at 子湯県 (reading unconfirmed), he named the land "Hyūga" (日向), and sang the Song of Longing for Home (思邦歌), yearning for the capital.

In the 18th year, the emperor toured Tsukushi while heading for the capital. At 熊県 (reading unconfirmed) he had soldiers strike down 弟熊 (reading unconfirmed), who had not come to him; at a small island in 葦北 (reading unconfirmed), when he prayed, clear water sprang from a cliff, so he named it 水島 (reading unconfirmed). The text records that the name of the land of Hi (火国) came from his reaching the shore guided by a fire of unknown origin on the sea at night; the name Aso (阿蘇) from the deities 阿蘇都彦 and 阿蘇都媛 (readings unconfirmed) appearing in human form on a plain where no houses could be seen; the name of the land of 御木国 (reading unconfirmed) from a great fallen tree, a 歴木 (reading unconfirmed); and the name 八女 (reading unconfirmed) from the goddess 八女津媛 (reading unconfirmed) who dwells in the mountains.
