In the 9th month of the 19th year, the emperor returned from Hyūga.

In the 2nd month of the 20th year, Princess 五百野 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to worship Amaterasu-Ōmikami. In the 7th month of the 25th year, Takeuchi-no-Sukune was sent to the provinces of Hokuriku and the east to investigate the lie of the land and the condition of the people. Takeuchi-no-Sukune, who returned in the 2nd month of the 27th year, reported that among the eastern barbarians there was the land of 日高見国 (reading unconfirmed), whose people tied their hair up like a mallet, tattooed their bodies and were fierce, and were called Emishi (蝦夷); that the land was fertile and broad; and that it should be attacked and taken.

quotes.note: They were born as twins on the same day, and the emperor, finding this strange, cried out toward a mortar (碓). This is the origin of the names 大碓 and 小碓 (readings unconfirmed).
The place where the camellia-wood (海石榴) mallets were made was called 海石榴市 (reading unconfirmed) by the people of the time.
The emperor, hating her extreme lack of filial piety, killed 市乾鹿文 (reading unconfirmed), who had betrayed her father.
Because this land faces straight toward the direction where the sun rises, it was named Hyūga (日向).

figures.name: 大足彦忍代別天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The third son of Emperor Suinin, and the emperor of this book (Emperor Keikō).

figures.name: 播磨稻日大郎姫 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The empress installed in the 2nd year. Mother of Prince 大碓 and 小碓尊 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大碓皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder twin brother of 小碓尊 (reading unconfirmed). He incurred the emperor's resentment over the matter of the daughters in Mino.

figures.name: 屋主忍男武雄心命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He worshipped the deities in Kii in the emperor's place, and fathered Takeuchi-no-Sukune with 影媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 八坂入媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder sister of 弟媛 (reading unconfirmed). She became a consort and bore thirteen children, including 稚足彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 神夏磯媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A female chieftain at 娑麼 in 周芳 (readings unconfirmed). She submitted to the emperor and told him where the four bandits were.

figures.name: 武諸木 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 多臣 (reading unconfirmed). He was sent to 神夏磯媛 (reading unconfirmed) and captured the four bandits.

figures.name: 速津媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The female chieftain of the village of 速見邑 (reading unconfirmed). She told the emperor about the tsuchigumo.

figures.name: 市乾鹿文 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the Kumaso chieftain. She betrayed her father and had him killed, but was put to death for her lack of filial piety.

figures.name: Mihakashi-hime (御刀媛)
figures.role: She became a consort in Hyūga and bore Prince 豊国別 (reading unconfirmed), founding ancestor of the 日向国造 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 阿蘇都彦 and 阿蘇都媛 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Two deities who appeared before the emperor in human form. They are regarded as the origin of the name of the land of Aso.

figures.name: 八女津媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A goddess said to dwell in the mountains. She is regarded as the origin of the name of the land of 八女 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 五百野皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The princess sent in the 20th year to worship Amaterasu-Ōmikami.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (the death of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto)
compare.text: The Song of Longing for Home (思邦歌) that Emperor Keikō sings at 子湯県 (reading unconfirmed) in Hyūga in the Nihon Shoki appears in the Kojiki as the Song of Longing for the Land (思国歌) that Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (倭建命) sings at 能煩野 (reading unconfirmed) on his way back from the eastern campaign, and the words are almost the same.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (consorts and children)
compare.text: Concerning 大碓命 (reading unconfirmed), who was sent to summon the two daughters in Mino, the Kojiki says that he married the daughters himself and presented other women in their place, pretending they were the daughters. The Nihon Shoki records only that he secretly had relations with them and did not report back, so the emperor resented him.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Kōgen (genealogy)
compare.text: Regarding the parents of Takeuchi-no-Sukune (武内宿禰), the Kojiki, in the section on Emperor Kōgen, makes him the child of 比古布都押之信命 (reading unconfirmed) and 山下影日売 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 宇豆比古 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 木国造 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki, in the entry for the 3rd year of Emperor Keikō, makes him the child of 屋主忍男武雄心命 (reading unconfirmed) and 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 菟道彦 (reading unconfirmed), a distant ancestor of the 紀直 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the entry for the 3rd month of the 2nd year
variants.text: It gives the empress's name as 稲日稚郎姫 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Variant account (一書云): small note in the entry for the 3rd month of the 2nd year
variants.text: It says that the empress bore three sons, the third being Prince 稚倭根子 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the entry for the 2nd month of the 3rd year
variants.text: It gives the name of 屋主忍男武雄心命 (reading unconfirmed) as 武猪心 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the entry for the 2nd month of the 4th year
variants.text: It gives Prince 国背別 (reading unconfirmed), borne by 襲武媛 (reading unconfirmed), as Prince 宮道別 (reading unconfirmed).

yamatotakeru-seito.title: Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto's Campaign against the Kumaso and His Departure on the Eastern Campaign
yamatotakeru-seito.lead: This page records how, in the 27th year of Emperor Keikō, the sixteen-year-old Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto was sent to strike down the Kumaso, who had rebelled again, how he stabbed 川上梟帥 (reading unconfirmed) while disguised as a young girl, and how, on being presented with a name by him, he came to call himself "日本武" (Yamato Takeru). When the eastern barbarians rebel in the 40th year, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto receives the axe of command (斧鉞) in place of Prince 大碓 (reading unconfirmed), who has fled and hidden, and in Ise he is given the sword Kusanagi (草薙剣) by 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) and sets out.

points.text: In the 10th month of the 27th year, the sixteen-year-old Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto was sent to strike down the Kumaso. In the 12th month, he let down his hair to take the appearance of a young girl, hid a sword in his clothing, slipped into the banquet of the Kumaso chieftain 川上梟帥 (also 取石鹿文; readings unconfirmed), and stabbed the drunken 梟帥 in the chest.

The dying 川上梟帥 (reading unconfirmed), saying that he had never met anyone of such martial power, presented the name "日本武皇子" (Prince Yamato Takeru), and it is said that from then on the prince came to be called Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto.

In the 40th year, when the eastern barbarians rebelled, Prince 大碓 (reading unconfirmed) was afraid and hid in the grass, and was enfeoffed in Mino. The emperor gave Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto the axe of command (斧鉞), and, saying, "In form he is my son; in truth he is a divine person," entrusted him with the pacification of the eastern lands; he had 吉備武彦 (reading unconfirmed) and 大伴武日連 (reading unconfirmed) accompany him, and made 七掬脛 (reading unconfirmed) his steward of meals (膳夫).

In the 10th month, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto turned aside from his road to worship at the Ise Shrine, and was given the sword Kusanagi (草薙剣) by 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed), who told him, "Be careful, and do not be negligent."

In the Kojiki, 小碓命 (reading unconfirmed) is sent to the west because he killed his elder brother 大碓命 (reading unconfirmed) and the emperor feared his violent nature; in the Nihon Shoki he is sent because the Kumaso rebelled again, and Prince 大碓 later hides out of fear of the eastern campaign and is enfeoffed in Mino.

On his way back from the Kumaso, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto killed the evil deities of the 穴海 (reading unconfirmed) in Kibi and of the 柏 crossing (reading unconfirmed) in Naniwa. Concerning the "穴戸神" (reading unconfirmed), who is brought to submission by words in the corresponding scene of the Kojiki, the database of deity names lists the theory that it is the 穴門 (reading unconfirmed) of Nagato, the theory that it is the 穴海 of Kibi, and the theory that it refers to straits in general.

story.text: In the 8th month of the 27th year, the Kumaso rebelled again and kept invading the frontier. In the 10th month, the emperor sent the sixteen-year-old Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto to strike down the Kumaso. When the prince sought a skilled archer, he was told that 弟彦公 (reading unconfirmed) of the province of Mino would be good, and he had 宮戸彦 (reading unconfirmed) of Katsuragi (葛城) go to summon him. 弟彦公 followed the prince, bringing with him 石占横立 (reading unconfirmed) and the 稲置 of 田子 and the 稲置 of 乳近 (readings unconfirmed) of Owari.

In the 12th month, the prince arrived in the land of the Kumaso and observed the situation and the lie of the land. Hearing that the Kumaso chieftain 取石鹿文, also called 川上梟帥 (readings unconfirmed), was gathering his kin for a banquet, the prince let down his hair to take the appearance of a young girl, hid a sword in his clothing, and went in among the women at the banquet. 梟帥 was charmed by his appearance, took him by the hand and seated him beside him, offered him the cup and dallied with him. When the night grew late and 梟帥 was drunk, the prince drew his sword and stabbed him in the chest.

Before dying, 梟帥 (reading unconfirmed) asked him to wait a moment and asked who he was. When the prince named himself 日本童男 (reading unconfirmed), son of 大足彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed), 梟帥 said that he himself was the strongest man in the land and had met many men of martial power, but none had equaled the prince; he presented the name 日本武皇子 (Prince Yamato Takeru), and when he had finished speaking he was stabbed to death by the prince. After 弟彦 (reading unconfirmed) and the others had cut down all of 梟帥's followers, the prince, on his way back to Yamato by sea, killed the evil deity at the place where one crosses the 穴海 (reading unconfirmed) in Kibi, and in Naniwa also killed the evil deity of the 柏 crossing (reading unconfirmed).

In the 2nd month of the 28th year, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto reported the pacification of the Kumaso, saying that thanks to the emperor's divine spirit he had struck down their chieftain and the western lands were calm. He also reported that the deity of the 穴済 (reading unconfirmed) in Kibi and the deity of the 柏済 (reading unconfirmed) in Naniwa had been giving off poisonous vapors and afflicting travelers, so he had killed them both and opened the routes by water and by land. The emperor praised the prince's achievement and loved him especially.

In the 6th month of the 40th year, many of the eastern barbarians rebelled, and the frontier was in turmoil. In the 7th month, when the emperor asked his ministers whom to send, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto said that he had labored in the western campaign, so this time it was the task of Prince 大碓 (reading unconfirmed). Prince 大碓 was startled and fled and hid in the grass, and the emperor reproached him and enfeoffed him in Mino. He is the founding ancestor of the 身毛津君 and the 守君 (readings unconfirmed). When Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto came forward to go himself to pacify them, the emperor gave him the axe of command (斧鉞), spoke of the fierceness of the eastern barbarians, especially the Emishi (蝦夷), praised the prince, saying, "In form he is my son; in truth he is a divine person," and ordered him to make them submit by displaying his might and winning them over with virtue. 吉備武彦 (reading unconfirmed) and 大伴武日連 (reading unconfirmed) accompanied him, and 七掬脛 (reading unconfirmed) became his steward of meals (膳夫).

On the day (癸丑) of the 10th month, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto set out. On the day (戊午), he turned aside from his road to worship at the Ise Shrine, and told 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) that he was setting out on the eastern campaign. 倭姫命 took the sword Kusanagi (草薙剣), gave it to the prince, and told him to be careful and never be negligent.

quotes.note: The words of 川上梟帥 (reading unconfirmed): I have met many men of martial power, but there has been none like the prince.
The words with which 川上梟帥 (reading unconfirmed) presented the name: from now on the prince should be called 日本武皇子 (Prince Yamato Takeru).
The emperor's words describing Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto: in form he is my son, but in truth he is a person like a deity.
倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) gave the sword Kusanagi (草薙剣) to Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto and told him to be careful and not be negligent.

figures.name: 大足彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Emperor Keikō. He sent Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto on the campaign against the Kumaso and on the eastern campaign.

figures.name: 弟彦公 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A skilled archer of the province of Mino. He took part in the campaign against the Kumaso and cut down the followers of 梟帥 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 川上梟帥 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Chieftain of the Kumaso, also called 取石鹿文 (reading unconfirmed). As he was dying he presented the name 日本武 (Yamato Takeru).

figures.name: 大碓皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto. Fearing the eastern campaign, he hid, and was enfeoffed in Mino.

figures.name: 吉備武彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: On the emperor's orders, he accompanied Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto on the eastern campaign.

figures.name: 大伴武日連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: On the emperor's orders, he accompanied Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto on the eastern campaign.

figures.name: 七掬脛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He became Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto's steward of meals (膳夫; the person in charge of food) on the eastern campaign.

figures.name: 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: At the Ise Shrine she gave the sword Kusanagi (草薙剣) to Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto.

figures.name: The sword Kusanagi (草薙釼)
figures.role: The sword that 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) gave to Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto as he set out on the eastern campaign.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (the western campaign of 小碓命, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the 熊曾建 (reading unconfirmed) are two brothers; 小碓命 (reading unconfirmed) stabs the elder through the chest and the fleeing younger through the buttocks and kills them, and is presented with the name 倭建 (Yamato Takeru) by the younger brother. In the Nihon Shoki the chieftain is a single man, 川上梟帥 (reading unconfirmed). The Kojiki further includes the story of his killing 出雲建 (reading unconfirmed) by treachery on the way back, but this is not found in this entry of the Nihon Shoki.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (beginning of the western campaign of 小碓命, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, when his elder brother 大碓命 (reading unconfirmed) did not come out for the morning and evening meals, 小碓命 (reading unconfirmed) caught him in the privy, tore off his limbs, wrapped him in a straw mat (薦) and threw him away. In the Nihon Shoki, Prince 大碓 is alive, hides out of fear of the eastern campaign, and is enfeoffed in Mino.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (the eastern campaign of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (倭建命), in Ise, laments to his aunt 倭比売命 (reading unconfirmed), asking whether the emperor wishes him dead, and 倭比売命 gives him the sword Kusanagi (草那芸剣) and a bag (御嚢). In the Nihon Shoki, the emperor praises the prince as a divine person and gives him the axe of command, and 倭姫命 (reading unconfirmed) only gives him the sword Kusanagi (草薙剣) and says, "Be careful, and do not be negligent."

yamatotakeru-saigo.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 7 — Emperor Keikō and Emperor Seimu
yamatotakeru-saigo.title: Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto's Eastern Campaign and Death, the Last Years of Emperor Keikō, and Emperor Seimu
yamatotakeru-saigo.lead: Setting out on the eastern campaign, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto passes through the grass fire in Suruga, the entry of 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed) into the sea, the submission of the Emishi, and the mountain deity of Shinano, and returns to Owari; but, led astray by the deity of Mount Ibuki (膽吹山), he falls ill, dies at the age of thirty at 能褒野 (reading unconfirmed), and flies away as a white bird. The page goes on to record Emperor Keikō's later tour of the eastern lands and his death, and Emperor Seimu's appointment of heads for the provinces and districts (国郡) and for the 県 and 邑 (県邑).

points.text: In Suruga, deceived by bandits who set fire to the plain, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto escaped danger by lighting a counter-fire with a fire-striker, and named the place Yaizu (焼津). When they met a violent storm on the sea crossing from Sagami to Kazusa, his concubine 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed) entered the sea in place of the prince, the wind dropped, and the boat reached the shore.

In Owari, the prince married Miyazu-hime (宮簀媛), left his sword at Miyazu-hime's house, and went to strike down the wild deity of Mount Ibuki (膽吹山); but, taking the mountain deity, who had become a great serpent, for a messenger, he stepped over it and went on, was led astray by clouds and icy rain, and fell ill. He died at the age of thirty at 能褒野 (reading unconfirmed), became a white bird and flew to 琴弾原 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato and to the village of 旧市邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi, and the three tombs were called the White Bird Tombs (白鳥陵).

The text records that the sword Kusanagi (草薙横刀), which Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto wore, is now at the Atsuta Shrine (熱田社) in the district of 年魚市郡 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Owari. It also says that the Emishi presented to the Ise Shrine were noisy, so they were moved, by way of the vicinity of 御諸山 (reading unconfirmed), to five provinces outside the home provinces, and became the ancestors of the 佐伯部 (reading unconfirmed).

Emperor Seimu, troubled in the 4th year that the provinces and districts (国郡) and the 県 and 邑 (県邑) had no heads, in the 9th month of the 5th year placed 造長 over the provinces and districts and 稲置 over the 県 and 邑 (readings unconfirmed), giving them shields and spears as tokens. He divided the provinces and 県 by mountains and rivers and fixed the villages by roads, and called east-west "日縦", north-south "日横", the south side of a mountain "影面", and the north side "背面".

According to the database of deity names (entry: 伊服岐能山之神, reading unconfirmed), the deity of Mount Ibuki, who appears as a white boar in the Kojiki, appears as a great serpent in the Nihon Shoki. The same database also notes that the Engishiki register of deities (延喜式神名帳) lists the 伊夫伎神社 (reading unconfirmed) shrine in the district of 坂田郡 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Ōmi and the 伊富岐神社 (reading unconfirmed) shrine in the district of 不破郡 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Mino.

Regarding the story in the Nihon Shoki in which the mountain deity of Shinano, transformed into a white deer, is killed with wild garlic (蒜), the database of deity names (entry: 科野之坂神, reading unconfirmed) points out that the Kojiki records only that the deity of the slope of 科野 was brought to submission by words, and that the plot of killing a white deer with wild garlic closely resembles the Kojiki's story of the deity of the slope of Ashigara (足柄).

story.text: In this year, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto reached Suruga. Bandits, pretending to submit, invited the prince to hunt, saying there were many beasts on the plain, and set fire to the plain. Realizing he had been deceived, the prince produced fire with a fire-striker and escaped by a counter-fire, and burned all the bandits to death, so that place is called Yaizu (焼津). When he was about to cross from Sagami to Kazusa and said, "It is a small sea; one could even jump across it," a violent storm arose in the middle of the sea. His concubine 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed), who was accompanying him, said that this was the will of the sea deity, and entered the sea in place of the prince's life; the wind dropped, and the boat reached the shore. That sea was called 馳水 (reading unconfirmed).

From Kazusa the prince entered the province of Mutsu, hung a large mirror on his boat, proceeded by sea, and reached the border of the Emishi. The Emishi leaders, who were about to meet him in battle at 竹水門 (reading unconfirmed), saw the prince's boat and, awed by its majesty, threw away their bows and arrows and asked his name. When the prince answered, "I am the son of a god manifest in human form (現人神)," the Emishi drew the boat to the shore and surrendered. Having pacified the Emishi, he returned from the land of 日高見国 (reading unconfirmed), passed through Hitachi, and entered the 酒折宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in the province of Kai, where the prince asked his attendants a question in song; a man tending the fires continued the end of the song, so the prince praised him and gave him a reward.

As Shinano and Koshi had not yet submitted, the prince went round through Musashi and Kōzuke and reached the 碓日坂 (reading unconfirmed) slope, where, longing for 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed), he looked to the southeast and lamented three times, "吾嬬者耶" ("Oh, my wife!"). For this reason the provinces east of the mountains are called the land of Azuma (吾嬬国). He sent 吉備武彦 (reading unconfirmed) to the province of Koshi, and the prince himself entered rugged Shinano. When the mountain deity appeared as a white deer, he flicked a piece of wild garlic (蒜) into its eye and killed it; then he lost his way, but was guided out to Mino by a white dog. It is said that ever since then, anyone crossing this slope who chews wild garlic and smears it on people, oxen and horses is not affected by the deity's vapor.

Returning to Owari, the prince married Miyazu-hime (宮簀媛) and stayed past the month. Hearing that there was a wild deity on Mount Ibuki (膽吹山) in Ōmi, he left his sword at Miyazu-hime's house and went there on foot. The mountain deity became a great serpent and blocked the road, but the prince, thinking it was the deity's messenger, stepped over it and went on. The mountain deity raised clouds and made ice fall, so the prince forced his way through the fog and barely got out; he became as if he had lost his senses, and came to himself by drinking the water of a spring. That spring is called 居醒泉 (reading unconfirmed). It was then that the prince first fell ill; he returned to Owari but did not enter Miyazu-hime's house, and at 尾津 (reading unconfirmed) in Ise, seeing that the sword he had earlier left behind under a pine tree was still there, he composed a song.

When he reached 能褒野 (reading unconfirmed), his illness grew severe; the prince presented the captured Emishi to the Shrine (神宮), sent 吉備武彦 (reading unconfirmed) to convey to the emperor his regret at being unable to report back on his mission, and died at 能褒野 at the age of thirty. The emperor lamented and grieved, and had him buried in the 能褒野陵 tomb. But the prince became a white bird, came out of the tomb and flew toward the land of Yamato, and only his clothes were left in the coffin. The white bird stopped at 琴弾原 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato and then at the village of 旧市邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi, so tombs were built at each place, and these three tombs are called the White Bird Tombs (白鳥陵). The white bird at last ascended to heaven, and the 武部 (reading unconfirmed) was established to hand down the prince's renown.

In the 51st year, 稚足彦尊 (reading unconfirmed) and Takeuchi-no-Sukune, who had not attended a banquet, answered that they had been guarding the gate against emergencies, and the emperor held them in high regard. In the 8th month, he made 稚足彦尊 crown prince and Takeuchi-no-Sukune the chief minister (棟梁之臣). The text also records that the sword Kusanagi (草薙横刀) is at the Atsuta Shrine (熱田社), that the Emishi presented to the Shrine became the ancestors of the 佐伯部 (reading unconfirmed), and the consorts and children of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (including 足仲彦天皇, reading unconfirmed). In the 52nd year the empress died, and 八坂入媛命 (reading unconfirmed) became empress. In the 53rd year, wishing to tour the lands that Prince 小碓 (小碓王, reading unconfirmed) had pacified, the emperor entered the Tōkai region from Ise, and in Kazusa, because 磐鹿六鴈 (reading unconfirmed) made white clams into namasu (膾) and presented them, he granted him the 膳大伴部 (reading unconfirmed). In the 55th year, 彦狭嶋王 (reading unconfirmed), who had been made governor-general (都督) of the fifteen provinces of the Tōsandō (東山道), died before reaching his post, and in the 56th year his son 御諸別王 (reading unconfirmed) governed the eastern lands and made the Emishi submit. In the 58th year the emperor moved to the 高穴穂宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Ōmi, and in the 11th month of the 60th year he died at the age of one hundred and six.

稚足彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Seimu) was the fourth son of Emperor Keikō, and his mother was the empress 八坂入姫命 (reading unconfirmed). He acceded to the throne in the 1st month of his 1st year, and in the 11th month of the 2nd year buried Emperor Keikō in the 山辺道上陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb in the land of Yamato. In the 3rd year he made Takeuchi-no-Sukune, who had been born on the same day as the emperor, Great Minister (大臣). In the 4th year he issued an edict lamenting that the provinces and districts had no lords and heads, and in the 9th month of the 5th year he placed 造長 over the provinces and districts and 稲置 over the 県 and 邑 (readings unconfirmed) and fixed their boundaries, and it is said that the people were at peace. In the 48th year he made his nephew 足仲彦尊 (reading unconfirmed) crown prince, and in the 6th month of the 60th year he died at the age of one hundred and seven.

quotes.note: The words of 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed): I wish to enter the sea, giving my body in place of the prince's life.

The words the prince spoke three times in lament on the pass of 碓日 (reading unconfirmed), longing for 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed). They are regarded as the origin of the name of the land of Azuma (吾嬬国).
When the coffin was opened, only the clothes remained, and there was no body.
Emperor Seimu placed 造長 over the provinces and districts and 稲置 over the 県 and 邑 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 弟橘媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 忍山宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) of the 穂積 (reading unconfirmed) clan, and the prince's concubine. She entered the sea and calmed the violent storm.

figures.name: 吉備武彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He accompanied the eastern campaign, inspected the province of Koshi, and conveyed the prince's last words to the emperor.

figures.name: 大伴武日 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A distant ancestor of the Ōtomo no Muraji. He was granted the 靫部 (reading unconfirmed) at the 酒折宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

figures.name: 稚足彦尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The fourth son of Emperor Keikō, and crown prince; later Emperor Seimu.

figures.name: 八坂入媛命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: She became empress in the 52nd year. Mother of Emperor Seimu.

figures.name: 兩道入姫皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Consort of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto. Mother of 足仲彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Chūai) and others.

figures.name: 磐鹿六鴈 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A distant ancestor of the 膳臣 (reading unconfirmed). He made white clams into namasu (膾) and presented them, and was granted the 膳大伴部 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 彦狹嶋王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Grandson of 豊城命 (Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto). He was made governor-general of the fifteen provinces of the Tōsandō (東山道), but died before reaching his post.

figures.name: 御諸別王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 彦狭嶋王 (reading unconfirmed). He governed the eastern lands and made the Emishi submit.

figures.name: 足仲彦尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto and nephew of Emperor Seimu. He became crown prince in the 48th year.

figures.name: The sword Kusanagi (草薙横刀)
figures.role: The sword Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto wore. The text records that it is now at the Atsuta Shrine (熱田社) in the district of 年魚市郡 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Owari.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (the death of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto; the deity of Mount 伊服岐能山, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the deity of Mount Ibuki appears as a white boar as big as an ox, and Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (倭建命), because he declares aloud that it is the deity's messenger, is struck by great icy rain. In the Nihon Shoki it appears as a great serpent, and the prince, thinking it the deity's messenger, steps over it and goes on.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Keikō (the death of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto; the white bird)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto (倭建命) becomes a great white bird eight fathoms long (八尋白智鳥) and flies off; his consorts and children follow it singing, and it stops at 志幾 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Kawachi, where the White Bird Tomb (白鳥御陵) is built. In the Nihon Shoki, the three tombs at 能褒野 (reading unconfirmed), at 琴弾原 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamato, and at the village of 旧市邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi are called the White Bird Tombs (白鳥陵).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Seimu
compare.text: On Emperor Seimu, the Kojiki records briefly that he made 建内宿禰 (Takeuchi-no-Sukune) Great Minister and established the 国造 of the provinces large and small, the boundaries of the provinces, and the 県主 of the 県 large and small (readings unconfirmed), and gives his age as ninety-five. The Nihon Shoki says that he placed 造長 and 稲置 and that he died at the age of one hundred and seven.

variants.name: One account (一云): small note in the "this year" entry of the 40th year
variants.text: In the scene of the grass fire in Suruga, the main text says that the prince escaped by lighting a counter-fire with a fire-striker, but one account (一云) says that he was able to escape because the sword 叢雲 (reading unconfirmed) that the prince wore drew itself and mowed down the grass beside the prince, and that this is why the sword is called Kusanagi (草薙).

chuai.title: Emperor Chūai: the White Birds, the Campaign against the Kumaso, the Oracle, and His Death
chuai.lead: This book records the period from the accession of 足仲彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed; Emperor Chūai) to his death after he entered Tsukushi to strike down the Kumaso without believing the words of the deity that had possessed the empress. It ends by saying that the emperor's death was concealed by the empress and Takeuchi-no-Sukune, and that he was not buried in that year because of the expedition to Silla.

points.text: In the 9th month of the 8th year, when the campaign against the Kumaso was being deliberated at the 橿日宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Tsukushi, a deity possessed the empress and instructed: "The Kumaso are not a land worth attacking. If you worship me, I will make the land of Silla across the sea, rich in gold and silver, submit without fighting." The emperor did not believe these words, saying that even when he climbed a high hill he could see only the sea.

Still not believing, the emperor attacked the Kumaso but could not win, and in the 2nd month of the 9th year he suddenly felt pain in his body and died the next day (aged fifty-two). The main text states that "he died early because he did not heed the words of the deity," while one account (一云) in a small note says that he went himself to strike down the Kumaso, was hit by a bandit's arrow, and died.

In the 11th month of the 1st year, the emperor, longing for his father Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto, who had become a white bird and ascended to heaven, had the provinces present white birds. His half-brother 蘆髮蒲見別王 (reading unconfirmed), who seized the white birds from Koshi on their way, was put to death for having committed a discourtesy against the late prince.

When the emperor entered Tsukushi in the 1st month of the 8th year, 熊鰐 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 岡県主 (reading unconfirmed), and 五十迹手 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 伊覩県主 (reading unconfirmed), came out to meet him with a white copper mirror, a ten-fist sword (十握剣) and a jewel (八尺瓊) hung on sakaki trees (賢木) set up on their boats. 五十迹手 praised the emperor's reign by likening it to these three objects, and it is said that the name 伊蘇国 (the present 伊覩; readings unconfirmed) arose from the word "伊蘇志" with which the emperor praised him.

In the Kojiki, the emperor, thinking the deity a false deity, pushes the koto (琴) away; urged by 建内宿禰 (Takeuchi-no-Sukune), he plays it, but the sound of the koto stops, and when a light is lit and they look, he has already died. In both works his age at death is fifty-two.

Concerning the temporary palace "笥飯宮" that the emperor built at 角鹿 in the 2nd year, Kokugakuin University's database of deity names explains it by noting the view that Kehi is a place name of 角鹿 (Tsuruga, 敦賀), and by connecting it with Kehi-no-Ōkami (気比大神; written 笥飯大神 in the Nihon Shoki), who dwells in that place.

story.text: 足仲彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was the second son of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto, and his mother was 両道入姫命 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 活目入彦五十狹茅天皇 (reading unconfirmed). He was handsome in appearance, and is said to have been ten shaku (十尺) tall. Because 稚足彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed) had no son, he was made heir apparent in that emperor's 48th year. When 稚足彦天皇 died in his 60th year, he was buried in the 9th month of the following year in the 狭城盾列陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb in the land of Yamato. The heir apparent acceded to the throne in the 1st month of the 1st year, and in the 9th month made his mother empress dowager.

In the 11th month of the 1st year, the emperor told his ministers that his longing for the spirit of his father the prince, which had become a white bird and ascended to heaven, would not cease, and that he wished to keep white birds in the pond at the tomb to console his heart; and he had the provinces present white birds. In the intercalary 11th month, the province of Koshi presented four white birds, but when the messengers stopped for the night beside the Uji River (菟道河), 蘆髮蒲見別王 (reading unconfirmed) said, "Even a white bird, if you burn it, becomes a black bird," seized the white birds and went off with them. The emperor, hating this discourtesy toward the late prince, sent troops and put to death 蒲見別王, his half-brother.

In the 1st month of the 2nd year, he made 気長足姫尊 (reading unconfirmed) empress. Before this, he had taken as consort 大中姫 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of his uncle 彦人大兄 (reading unconfirmed), and had by her Prince ■坂 (one character is missing; in Book 9 the name is 麛坂王, reading unconfirmed) and Prince Oshikuma (忍熊皇子); and he had taken as consort 弟媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大酒主 (reading unconfirmed), and had by her Prince 誉屋別 (reading unconfirmed). In the 2nd month he went to 角鹿 (Tsuruga) and built a temporary palace, which was called the Kehi Palace (笥飯宮), and in the same month he established the royal granary (屯倉) of Awaji. In the 3rd month, leaving the empress and the officials behind, he toured the southern provinces, and while he was at the 徳勒津宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in the province of Kii, the Kumaso rebelled and ceased to bring tribute, so he headed by sea for 穴門 (reading unconfirmed), and ordered the empress to set out from 角鹿 and meet him at 穴門.

In the 6th month, the emperor anchored at 豊浦津 (reading unconfirmed). The empress set out from 角鹿 (Tsuruga) and reached 渟田門 (reading unconfirmed); when she took a meal on the boat and poured sake on the fish that gathered beside the boat (the original text has "海鰤魚"), the fish became drunk and floated up, and the fishermen caught many and rejoiced. It is said that this is why the fish of that place float as if drunk when the 6th month comes. In the 7th month the empress also anchored at 豊浦津, and on that day she obtained a wish-granting jewel (如意珠) in the sea. In the 9th month a palace was built at 穴門 (reading unconfirmed) and they lived there; it is called the 穴門豊浦宮 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 1st month of the 8th year, the emperor set out for Tsukushi. 熊鰐 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 岡県主 (reading unconfirmed), hung a mirror, a sword and a jewel on a sakaki tree (賢木) and came out to meet him at the bay of 沙麼 in 周芳 (readings unconfirmed), presented lands for taking fish and salt, and guided him along the sea route. When the boat would not move at the harbor mouth of 岡浦 (reading unconfirmed), 熊鰐 answered that it was probably the will of the male deity 大倉主 and the female deity 菟夫羅媛 (readings unconfirmed) at the mouth of the bay; when the emperor prayed and had 伊賀彦 (reading unconfirmed), a man of 菟田 (reading unconfirmed), worship them as priest (祝), the boat moved. The empress's boat, which had entered from 洞海 (reading unconfirmed) in a separate boat, could not move because the tide had ebbed; 熊鰐 made a pool for fish and a pond for birds and gathered fish and birds there, and on seeing them the empress's anger subsided somewhat. 五十迹手 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 伊覩県主 (reading unconfirmed), likewise hung a jewel, a mirror and a sword on a sakaki tree and met him at 引嶋 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門, and the emperor praised him. After that the emperor arrived at 儺県 (reading unconfirmed) and lived at the 橿日宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

In the 9th month, when the campaign against the Kumaso was being deliberated, a deity possessed the empress and instructed that, rather than the Kumaso, he should obtain, by worshipping the deity, the land of Silla across the sea, rich in gold, silver and bright colors; and it asked that the emperor's boat and the paddy field (大田) presented by 穴門直踐立 (reading unconfirmed) be made offerings. The emperor retorted that even looking out from a high hill he could see no land, and asked what deity was deceiving him. The deity told him again that if he did not believe, he would not obtain that land, and that the child the empress had now conceived for the first time would obtain it; but the emperor still did not believe, attacked the Kumaso, could not win, and returned.

In the 2nd month of the 9th year, the emperor suddenly felt pain in his body and died the next day. He was fifty-two years old. The empress and the Great Minister Takeuchi-no-Sukune, fearing that if the people of the realm learned of it they would grow slack, concealed the death, and had four high officials — 中臣烏賊津連, 大三輪大友主君, 物部膽咋連 and 大伴武以連 (readings unconfirmed) — lead the officials and guard the palace. The emperor's body was secretly entrusted to Takeuchi-no-Sukune and moved by sea to 穴門 (reading unconfirmed), and a temporary enshrinement without fires (无火殯斂) was held at the 豊浦宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. On the day (甲子), Takeuchi-no-Sukune returned from 穴門 and reported to the empress. In this year the emperor could not be buried because of the expedition to Silla.

quotes.note: The words with which 蒲見別王 (reading unconfirmed) seized the white birds being presented: even a white bird, if burned, becomes a black bird.
The words with which the deity named the land of Silla as the "land of treasure" it was teaching about.
The explanation in the main text: it was understood that he had died early because he did not heed the words of the deity.
The emperor praised 五十迹手 (reading unconfirmed), saying "伊蘇志", and this is regarded as the origin of the place name 伊蘇国 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 兩道入姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Mother of Emperor Chūai. She is regarded as a daughter of 活目入彦五十狹茅天皇 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 蘆髮蒲見別王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The emperor's half-brother. He was put to death for seizing the white birds being presented.

figures.name: 大中姫 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the emperor's uncle 彦人大兄 (reading unconfirmed), and the emperor's consort. She bore Prince 麛坂 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince Oshikuma (忍熊皇子).

figures.name: 熊鰐 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 岡県主 (reading unconfirmed). He met the emperor with a mirror, a sword and a jewel hung on a sakaki tree, and guided him along the sea route.

figures.name: 五十迹手 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 伊覩県主 (reading unconfirmed). He met the emperor with a jewel, a mirror and a sword hung on a sakaki tree, and was praised.

figures.name: 大倉主 and 菟夫羅媛 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: A male and a female deity said to be at the mouth of the bay of 岡浦 (reading unconfirmed). When they were worshipped, the emperor's boat moved.

figures.name: 中臣烏賊津連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: One of the four high officials made to guard the palace when the emperor's death was concealed.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (the divine possession and the emperor's death)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the emperor, thinking the deity's words false, pushes the koto away; urged by 建内宿禰 (Takeuchi-no-Sukune), he reluctantly plays it, but the sound stops, and when a light is lit he has already died. The main text of the Nihon Shoki has a sudden death on the following day, and one account (一云) a death from an arrow wound.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (palaces, consorts and children)
compare.text: The establishment of the royal granary of Awaji also appears in the Kojiki, as something of "this reign"; the Nihon Shoki places it in the 2nd month of the 2nd year. For the story of the white birds and 蒲見別王 (reading unconfirmed), and for the stories of the welcome by 熊鰐 and 五十迹手 (readings unconfirmed), no corresponding entries in the Kojiki could be confirmed.

variants.name: One account (一云): the manner of the emperor's death
variants.text: The main text says that he died early of a sudden illness because he did not heed the words of the deity, but one account (一云) in a small note relates that the emperor went himself to strike down the Kumaso, was hit by a bandit's arrow, and died.

jingu-shiragi.title: Empress Jingū's Oracle and the Expedition to Silla
jingu-shiragi.lead: This page records how, after the death of Emperor Chūai, 気長足姫尊 (reading unconfirmed; Empress Jingū) herself became the medium (神主) and asked the names of the deities, and how, following their instructions, she struck down the Kumaso, 羽白熊鷲 (reading unconfirmed) and the tsuchigumo (土蜘蛛), crossed the sea, and made Silla submit. After her return, 誉田天皇 (reading unconfirmed) is born in Tsukushi, and after the main text two "一云" (one account) passages give other traditions.

points.text: At the abstinence palace (斎宮) in the village of 小山田邑 (reading unconfirmed), the empress herself became the medium (神主), had Takeuchi-no-Sukune play the koto, made 中臣烏賊津使主 (reading unconfirmed) the interpreter of the oracle (審神者), and after seven days and seven nights drew out the names of the deities. Those who named themselves included 撞賢木厳之御魂天疎向津媛命 (reading unconfirmed), who dwells at the Isuzu Shrine (五十鈴宮) in Ise, Kotoshironushi-no-Kami (事代主神), and 表筒男, 中筒男 and 底筒男 (readings unconfirmed).

At the bay of 橿日浦 (reading unconfirmed), the empress washed her hair in the sea and confirmed the deities' will when it parted in two; saying, "For a while I will borrow the form of a man," she announced the western campaign to her ministers. Before departure, since she had reached the month of childbirth, she tucked a stone at her waist and prayed that she would give birth in this land after she returned.

Setting out from 和珥津 (reading unconfirmed) in the 10th month, she reached Silla aided by the wind and by great fish. The king of Silla surrendered without fighting and swore to become her stable-keeper (飼部) and send tribute every year, and the empress set up the spear she had used as a staff at the gate of the king of Silla. The kings of Koguryŏ (高麗) and Paekche (百済) also promised tribute, and it is said that these are called the Three Han (三韓).

In the 12th month, the empress gave birth to 誉田天皇 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi, and that place was called 宇瀰 (reading unconfirmed). Later, following the instruction of the three 筒男 deities (readings unconfirmed) who had accompanied the army, their rough spirit (荒魂) was worshipped at the village of 山田邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門 (reading unconfirmed), and 踐立 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 穴門直 (reading unconfirmed), was made its priest (神主).

In the Kojiki, the deities name themselves as "the will of Amaterasu-Ōmikami" and as the three great deities 底筒男, 中筒男 and 上筒男 (readings unconfirmed); after setting up her staff at the gate of the ruler of Silla, she worships the rough spirit (荒御魂) of the Great Deity of 墨江 (墨江大神, reading unconfirmed) as the deity protecting the land, and returns. In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, more deities name themselves, and the rough spirit is worshipped at the village of 山田邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門 (reading unconfirmed) after her return.

Kokugakuin University's database of deity names lists 表筒男, 中筒男 and 底筒男 (readings unconfirmed) of the Nihon Shoki, and "向匱男聞襲大歴五御魂速狭騰尊" which appears in one account (一云), as corresponding to the 墨江之三前大神 (reading unconfirmed) of the Kojiki (the Great Deity of Sumiyoshi, 住吉大神), and explains that the shrine at the village of 山田邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門 (reading unconfirmed) is regarded as corresponding to the 住吉坐荒御魂神社 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Nagato.

story.text: 気長足姫尊 (reading unconfirmed) was a great-granddaughter of 稚日本根子彦大日々天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and a daughter of Prince 気長宿禰 (reading unconfirmed); her mother was 葛城高顙媛 (reading unconfirmed). She became empress in the 2nd year of 足仲彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed); from her youth she was clever, and her appearance was beautiful. When the emperor died at the 橿日宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in Tsukushi in the 2nd month of the 9th year, the empress grieved that the emperor had died early because he had not followed the deity's instruction, and resolved to learn which deity had cursed him and to seek the land of treasure. She therefore had the ministers and officials expiate their offences and correct their errors, and built an abstinence palace (斎宮) in the village of 小山田邑 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 3rd month, the empress chose an auspicious day, entered the abstinence palace and herself became the medium (神主). She had Takeuchi-no-Sukune play the koto and made 中臣烏賊津使主 (reading unconfirmed) the interpreter of the oracle (審神者), and asked the names of the deities who had earlier instructed the emperor. After seven days and seven nights, 撞賢木厳之御魂天疎向津媛命 (reading unconfirmed), who dwells at the Isuzu Shrine (五十鈴宮) in the district of 度逢県 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Ise, named herself; then the deity dwelling in 淡郡 of 吾田節 in 尾田 (readings unconfirmed), Kotoshironushi-no-Kami (事代主神), and 表筒男, 中筒男 and 底筒男 (readings unconfirmed), who dwell in the depths of the water at 橘小門 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Hyūga, named themselves. The empress worshipped them according to their instructions and had 鴨別 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 吉備臣 (reading unconfirmed), strike down the Kumaso, who soon submitted. In the village of 荷持田村 (reading unconfirmed) there was also 羽白熊鷲 (reading unconfirmed), who had wings, flew high, and plundered the people.

On her way from the 橿日宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace to the 松峡宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, the empress's hat (笠) was blown off by a whirlwind, and that place was called 御笠 (reading unconfirmed). She destroyed 羽白熊鷲 (reading unconfirmed) at 層増岐野 (reading unconfirmed), and because she said that her heart was at ease, she named that place 安 (reading unconfirmed). Further, at 山門県 (reading unconfirmed) she put to death 田油津媛 (reading unconfirmed) of the tsuchigumo (土蜘蛛), and her elder brother 夏羽 (reading unconfirmed), who had raised troops and come to meet her, fled on hearing that his younger sister had been killed.

In the 4th month, by a small stream in the village of 玉嶋里 in the district of 松浦県 in the province of 火前国 (readings unconfirmed), the empress bent a needle into a fishhook, used grains of rice as bait and threads from her skirt as fishing line, and prayed, "If the undertaking of seeking the land of treasure in the west is to succeed, let a fish bite," and she caught a 細鱗魚 (reading unconfirmed). Because she said "mezurashi" (how rare!), the land was called 梅豆羅国 (reading unconfirmed), and it is said that the present 松浦 is a corruption of that name. It is said that the women of that land fish for sweetfish (年魚) in the river in the first part of the 4th month, and that when men fish they catch nothing. To make a sacred rice field (神田), the empress had a channel dug to draw water from the 儺河 (reading unconfirmed) river; when it was blocked by a great rock at 迹驚岡 (reading unconfirmed), she had Takeuchi-no-Sukune offer up a sword and a mirror and pray, and thunder split the rock and the water passed through (the 裂田溝, reading unconfirmed). Further, when she washed her hair in the sea at the bay of 橿日浦 (reading unconfirmed), the hair parted of itself in two, so she tied it up into topknots (髻), and announced her resolve for the western campaign, saying that if it succeeded the credit would be the ministers', and if it failed the fault would be hers alone; and the ministers followed her.

In the 9th month she had ships gathered from the provinces and troops trained, but the troops did not assemble; when she set up the 大三輪社 (reading unconfirmed) shrine and offered swords and spears, the troops assembled. The fisherman 烏摩呂 (reading unconfirmed) reported that no land could be seen to the west, and 名草 (reading unconfirmed), a fisherman of 磯鹿 (reading unconfirmed), reported that there was a mountain with clouds over it to the northwest. The empress took up the axe of command (斧鉞) and set out the military rules, and the deity instructed, "The gentle spirit (和魂) will protect the ruler's body, and the rough spirit (荒魂) will lead the ships as the vanguard"; 依網吾彦男垂見 (reading unconfirmed) was made the priest (神主) for the worship. Since she had just reached the month of childbirth, the empress tucked a stone at her waist and prayed that she would give birth in this land on the day she returned when the undertaking was over. It is said that the stone is still by the roadside in 伊都県 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 10th month, when she set out from 和珥津 (reading unconfirmed), the wind rose and great fish held up the ships, so that they reached Silla without using oars, and the tide, carrying the ships, reached into the interior of the land. The king of Silla, fearing that these were the divine troops of the divine land in the east, surrendered of his own accord; he sealed up his maps and registers and surrendered before the royal ship, and swore again and again to become a stable-keeper (飼部) and send tribute every year. Some called for the king to be killed, but the empress, saying that one who surrenders of his own accord should not be killed, loosed his bonds, sealed the treasure storehouses of the land, and set up the spear she had used as a staff at the gate of the king of Silla as a mark for later ages. The king of Silla, 波沙寐錦 (reading unconfirmed), gave 微叱己知波珍干岐 (reading unconfirmed) as a hostage, and had gold, silver and textiles loaded on eighty ships to accompany her. The kings of the two countries of Koguryŏ (高麗) and Paekche (百済), knowing they could not win, also swore to bring tribute, and the royal granaries (屯倉) of the 内官家 (reading unconfirmed) were established. This is regarded as what are called the Three Han (三韓), and the empress returned from Silla.

In the 12th month, the empress gave birth to 誉田天皇 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi, and the people called the place where she gave birth 宇瀰 (reading unconfirmed). The three deities 表筒男, 中筒男 and 底筒男 (readings unconfirmed), who had accompanied the army, also instructed that their rough spirit be worshipped at the village of 山田邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門 (reading unconfirmed). 踐立 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 穴門直 (reading unconfirmed), and 田裳見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 津守連 (reading unconfirmed), said that the place the deities desired should be determined, and 踐立 was made the priest (神主) to worship the rough spirit, and a shrine was set up at the village of 山田邑 in 穴門.

quotes.note: The name of the deity dwelling at the Isuzu Shrine (五十鈴宮) in Ise, who was the first to name herself during the interpretation of the oracle.
The empress's words: though I am a woman, for a while I will borrow the form of a man and undertake a great plan.
The deity's instruction: the gentle spirit will attach itself to the ruler's body and protect her life, and the rough spirit will become the vanguard and lead the army's ships.
The spear the empress had used as a staff was set up at the gate of the king of Silla as a mark for later ages.

figures.name: 撞賢木嚴之御魂天疎向津媛命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The deity who named herself as dwelling at the Isuzu Shrine (五十鈴宮) in the district of 度逢県 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Ise. She was the first to reveal her name.

figures.name: 向匱男聞襲大歷五御魂速狹騰尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The name by which the deity named itself in the first one account (一云). Kokugakuin University's database of deity names lists it as a name, in a variant tradition, of the Great Deity of Sumiyoshi (住吉大神; 墨江之三前大神).

figures.name: 中臣烏賊津使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: At the oracle in the abstinence palace, he served as the interpreter (審神者) who discerned the words of the deity.

figures.name: 鴨別 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 吉備臣 (reading unconfirmed). He struck down the Kumaso, who soon submitted.

figures.name: 羽白熊鷲 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: One who lived in the village of 荷持田村 (reading unconfirmed) and is said to have had wings and flown. He was destroyed by the empress.

figures.name: 田油津媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A tsuchigumo of 山門県 (reading unconfirmed). She was put to death by the empress. Her elder brother was 夏羽 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 依網吾彦男垂見 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: On the departure of the expedition, he was made the priest (神主) to worship the deity.

figures.name: 波沙寐錦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The name of the king of Silla who surrendered (main text).

figures.name: 微叱己知波珍干岐 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The person the king of Silla handed over as a hostage.

figures.name: 踐立 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 穴門直 (reading unconfirmed). He was made the priest (神主) to worship the rough spirit of the three 筒男 deities at the village of 山田邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門.

figures.name: 田裳見宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 津守連 (reading unconfirmed). Together with 踐立 (reading unconfirmed), he said that a shrine should be set at the place the deities desired.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (the oracle and the naming of the deities)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the deities name themselves as the will of Amaterasu-Ōmikami and as the three great deities 底筒男, 中筒男 and 上筒男 (readings unconfirmed). In the main text of the Nihon Shoki, the deity of the Isuzu Shrine (五十鈴宮) in Ise, the deity of 淡郡 (reading unconfirmed), Kotoshironushi-no-Kami (事代主神) and the three 筒男 deities name themselves in turn, and the name of Amaterasu-Ōmikami does not appear.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (Empress Jingū's personal expedition to Silla)
compare.text: Setting up the staff at the gate of the king of Silla is common to both. In the Kojiki she then worships the rough spirit (荒御魂) of the Great Deity of 墨江 (墨江大神, reading unconfirmed) as the deity protecting the land and returns, whereas in the main text of the Nihon Shoki the rough spirit is worshipped at the village of 山田邑 (reading unconfirmed) in 穴門 (reading unconfirmed) after her return.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (the birth of the child and the fishing at 玉嶋里, reading unconfirmed)
compare.text: The story of fishing for sweetfish (年魚) at 玉嶋里 (reading unconfirmed) is also in the Kojiki, but there it is an event after she has returned from Silla and her child has been born in Tsukushi, whereas the main text of the Nihon Shoki tells it, before the expedition, as fishing to divine whether the undertaking would succeed. The stone she had at her waist is said in the Kojiki to be at the village of 伊斗村 (reading unconfirmed), and in the Nihon Shoki to be by the roadside in 伊都県 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云), the first
variants.text: The deity first possessed 内避高国避高松屋種 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 沙麼県主 (reading unconfirmed), and instructed the emperor, and next possessed the empress, who was playing the koto. The deity named itself with the names 表筒雄, 中筒雄 and 底筒雄 (readings unconfirmed) and with the name 向匱男聞襲大歴五御魂速狭騰尊 (reading unconfirmed), and the emperor, who did not believe, fell ill and died that night. The empress, in men's attire, conquered Silla, and this account gives the name of the king of Silla who surrendered as 宇流助富利智干 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One account (一云), the second
variants.text: It says that the king of Silla was captured, killed on the beach and buried in the sand, and that one man was left behind as governor (宰) when they returned. The king's wife tricked the governor into telling her where the king was buried, then killed the governor and buried him beneath the king's grave. When the emperor heard of this and sent a great army, the people of Silla killed the king's wife and apologized.

jingu-oshikuma.title: The revolt of Oshikuma-no-Miko and the years of the regency
jingu-oshikuma.lead: This section records how, when the Empress returned from Silla, 麛坂王 (reading unconfirmed) and Oshikuma-no-Miko, fearing that the newly born prince would be made ruler, raised troops; how Takeuchi-no-Sukune and others put down the revolt; and how the Empress became regent. After that, it sets out year by year the exchanges with Silla and Paekche, the presentation of the Seven-Branched Sword, quotations from the Records of Wei (魏志) and the Jin court diary (晋起居注), and other matters, and the book ends with her death in the 69th year of the regency.

points.text: 麛坂王 (reading unconfirmed) and Oshikuma-no-Miko said, "How can we, the elder brothers, submit to a younger brother?" and gathered troops while pretending to build the late Emperor's tomb. At a divination hunt (祈狩) on 菟餓野 (reading unconfirmed), 麛坂王 was eaten by a red boar, and Oshikuma-no-Miko, taking this as an ill omen, withdrew to Sumiyoshi.

Takeuchi-no-Sukune had his soldiers hide spare bowstrings in their hair and, claiming to act on the Empress's command, proposed a truce. He made Oshikuma-no-Miko's army cut their bowstrings and throw their swords into the river, then attacked, defeating them at 逢坂 (reading unconfirmed) and in the chestnut grove of 狭々浪 (reading unconfirmed). Oshikuma-no-Miko exchanged songs with 五十狭茅宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and the two sank together at the crossing of 瀬田 (reading unconfirmed) and died.

When the Empress's ship could not advance toward Naniwa, divination was performed at the harbor of 務古 (reading unconfirmed). Amaterasu-Ōmikami instructed that her rough spirit (荒魂) be enshrined in the land of 広田 (reading unconfirmed), Wakahirume-no-Mikoto in the land of 活田長峡 (reading unconfirmed), Kotoshironushi-no-Kami in the land of 長田 (reading unconfirmed), and the three 筒男 deities (reading unconfirmed) instructed that their gentle spirits (和魂) be enshrined at 大津渟中倉之長峡 (reading unconfirmed). When this was done, the crossing by sea became possible.

In the 10th month the ministers honored the Empress as Empress Dowager, and this year (辛巳) was made the first year of the regency. In the 3rd year Prince Homutawake (誉田別皇子) was made Crown Prince. In the entries for the 39th, 40th and 43rd years and the 66th year, passages from the Records of Wei (魏志) and the Jin court diary (晋起居注) recording exchanges with the queen of Wa and the land of Wa are quoted as small-character notes.

In the 46th year contact with Paekche began through the land of 卓淳 (reading unconfirmed). In the 49th year generals were sent who are said to have defeated Silla and subdued seven states, and in the 52nd year 久氐 (reading unconfirmed) and others from Paekche presented one Seven-Branched Sword (七枝刀), one Seven-Child Mirror (七子鏡) and other items.

The Kokugakuin University deity-name database explains that "大津の渟中倉の長峽" (as quoted; reading unconfirmed), where the gentle spirits of the three 筒男 deities (reading unconfirmed) were settled following the oracle at the harbor of 務古 (reading unconfirmed), is regarded as corresponding to Sumiyoshi Taisha.

story.text: In the 2nd month of the year after the attack on Silla, the Empress led her ministers and officials to the 穴門豊浦宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), gathered up the remains of the late Emperor, and set out for the capital by sea. 麛坂王 (reading unconfirmed) and Oshikuma-no-Miko heard of the Emperor's death, the Empress's western campaign and the birth of a prince. Thinking that the ministers would set up the young lord as ruler, they plotted, asking how elder brothers could submit to a younger brother. Pretending to build the Emperor's tomb, the two began a mausoleum at 赤石 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima, had stones carried from Awaji Island, armed the people, and waited for the Empress. 倉見別 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 犬上君 (reading unconfirmed), and 五十狭茅宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 吉師 (reading unconfirmed), sided with 麛坂王 and gathered troops from the eastern provinces. At 菟餓野 (reading unconfirmed) they held a divination hunt (祈狩), praying that if their enterprise was to succeed they would take good game. A red boar climbed onto the temporary platform (假庪) and ate 麛坂王, so Oshikuma-no-Miko decided that they should not wait for the enemy there and withdrew to Sumiyoshi.

The Empress had Takeuchi-no-Sukune hold the prince in his arms and go round by the southern sea to the harbor of Kii, while her own ship headed for Naniwa, but it circled in the sea and could not advance. She returned to the harbor of 務古 (reading unconfirmed) and performed divination. Amaterasu-Ōmikami instructed that her rough spirit (荒魂) should not be brought near the imperial residence but placed in the land of 広田 (reading unconfirmed); Wakahirume-no-Mikoto asked to be enshrined in the land of 活田長峡 (reading unconfirmed), Kotoshironushi-no-Kami in the land of 長田 (reading unconfirmed), and the three 筒男 deities (reading unconfirmed) asked that their gentle spirits (和魂) be enshrined at 大津渟中倉之長峡 (reading unconfirmed). The Empress had 葉山媛 (reading unconfirmed), 海上五十狭茅 (reading unconfirmed), 長媛 (reading unconfirmed) and others perform these rites. Once the deities were settled as instructed, she was able to cross the sea safely, and Oshikuma-no-Miko withdrew further to 菟道 (reading unconfirmed). The Empress met the Crown Prince at 日高 (reading unconfirmed) in Kii Province and moved to the 小竹宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

At this time, days on which the daytime was as dark as night continued for many days. An old man said that this was the offense of 阿豆那比 (阿豆那比之罪; reading unconfirmed). On investigation it was found that the priest (祝) of 小竹 (reading unconfirmed) and the priest of 天野 (reading unconfirmed) had been close friends; when one died of illness the other followed him in death, and the two had been buried in the same grave. When the grave was opened, the coffins were examined and the two were reburied in separate places, the sunlight returned and day and night could again be told apart.

In the 3rd month, Takeuchi-no-Sukune and 武振熊 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed), led tens of thousands of soldiers against Oshikuma-no-Miko and camped north of the 菟道 river (reading unconfirmed). When 熊之凝 (reading unconfirmed), the vanguard of Oshikuma-no-Miko, sang to encourage his side, Takeuchi-no-Sukune had his soldiers tie up their hair with bowstrings hidden inside and wear wooden swords. Then, claiming to act on the Empress's command, he falsely proposed a truce, saying that she did not seek the realm but only to protect the young prince. He made Oshikuma-no-Miko's army cut their bowstrings and throw their swords into the river, after which his own men restrung their bows with the hidden strings, put on real swords, crossed the river and attacked. Deceived, Oshikuma-no-Miko retreated, was defeated at 逢坂 (reading unconfirmed), and many of his men were cut down in the chestnut grove of 狭々浪 (reading unconfirmed). Because blood flooded the chestnut grove, it is said that the chestnuts from there are still not offered to the palace. Oshikuma-no-Miko called 五十狭茅宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and sang, and the two sank together at the crossing of 瀬田 (reading unconfirmed) and died. Takeuchi-no-Sukune also composed a song, and the body was found in the 菟道 river some days later.

In the 10th month the ministers honored the Empress as Empress Dowager, and this year (the Great Year being 辛巳; 太歳辛巳) was made the first year of the regency. In the 11th month of the 2nd year the Emperor was buried in the 長野陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi Province, and in the 1st month of the 3rd year Prince Homutawake (誉田別皇子) was made Crown Prince and the capital was placed at 磐余 (reading unconfirmed) (the 若桜宮 palace; reading unconfirmed). In the 5th year, envoys of the king of Silla deceived the court by pretending to take home the hostage 微叱許智伐旱 (reading unconfirmed): on Tsushima they laid a straw figure in a bed to look like a sick man, and let 微叱許智 escape to Silla. 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed), realizing he had been tricked, put the three envoys in a cage and burned them to death, then stopped at the 蹈鞴津 harbor (reading unconfirmed) in Silla, took the 草羅城 fortress (reading unconfirmed) and returned. The people he brought back at this time are said to be the founding ancestors of the 漢人 (reading unconfirmed) and others of the four villages of 桑原, 佐糜, 高宮 and 忍海 (readings unconfirmed). In the 2nd month of the 13th year, the Crown Prince went with Takeuchi-no-Sukune to worship Kehi-no-Ōkami (笥飯大神) at 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed). On his return the Empress Dowager offered him sake at a banquet and sang, and Takeuchi-no-Sukune answered with a song on the Crown Prince's behalf.

In the entries for the 39th, 40th and 43rd years, passages from the Records of Wei (魏志) recording envoys of the queen of Wa and other matters are quoted as small-character notes. In the 46th year 斯摩宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to the land of 卓淳 (reading unconfirmed), and the king of 卓淳 told him that three men from Paekche, 久氐 (reading unconfirmed) and others, had come asking the way to Japan. When 爾波移 (reading unconfirmed), an attendant of 斯摩宿禰, went to Paekche, King 肖古 (肖古王; reading unconfirmed) gave him silk, bows and arrows, and forty iron ingots. In the 47th year envoys from Paekche came together with envoys from Silla, but the tribute from Paekche was inferior. When questioned, the Paekche envoys answered that they had been seized by Silla on the way and their tribute had been switched, so, following the instruction of a heavenly deity, 千熊長彦 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Silla to reproach it. In the 49th year 荒田別 (reading unconfirmed) and 鹿我別 (reading unconfirmed) were made generals and crossed to the land of 卓淳; together with the troops of 木羅斤資 (reading unconfirmed) and others they defeated Silla and are said to have subdued seven states, including 比自㶱 (reading unconfirmed), and 忱彌多禮 (reading unconfirmed) was given to Paekche. 千熊長彦 climbed 辟支山 and 古沙山 (readings unconfirmed) with the king of Paekche and, on a great rock, received his oath that Paekche would pay tribute for ever. In the 50th and 51st years 久氐 and others from Paekche came to court again, and in the 52nd year they presented one Seven-Branched Sword (七枝刀), one Seven-Child Mirror (七子鏡) and other items.

In the 55th year King 肖古 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche died, and in the 56th year the prince 貴須 (reading unconfirmed) became king. In the 62nd year, because Silla did not pay tribute, 襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to attack it. In the 64th year King 貴須 died and 枕流王 (reading unconfirmed) became king. In the 65th year 枕流王 died, and because his son 阿花 (reading unconfirmed) was young, his uncle 辰斯 (reading unconfirmed) seized the throne. In the entry for the 66th year a passage from the Jin court diary (晋起居注) is quoted. In the 4th month of the 69th year the Empress Dowager died at the 稚桜宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) (a small-character note says at the age of one hundred), and in the 10th month she was buried in the 狭城盾列陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed); on that day she was posthumously honored with the name 気長足姫尊 (reading unconfirmed). This year was the Great Year 己丑 (太歳己丑).

quotes.note: The words of 麛坂王 (reading unconfirmed) and Oshikuma-no-Miko: how can we, who are elder brothers, submit to a younger brother (the newly born prince)?
The instruction of Amaterasu-Ōmikami: my rough spirit must not be brought near the imperial residence.
Takeuchi-no-Sukune's order: let each man hide spare bowstrings in his hair and wear a wooden sword.
This lists the Seven-Branched Sword and the Seven-Child Mirror as items presented by the envoys of Paekche in the 52nd year.

figures.name: 麛坂王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother of Oshikuma-no-Miko. He rebelled against the Empress but was eaten by a red boar during the divination hunt.

figures.name: 倉見別 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 犬上君 (reading unconfirmed). He sided with 麛坂王 and gathered troops from the eastern provinces.

figures.name: 五十狹茅宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 吉師 (reading unconfirmed). He followed Oshikuma-no-Miko and in the end sank with him at the crossing of 瀬田 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 武振熊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed). He attacked Oshikuma-no-Miko together with Takeuchi-no-Sukune.

figures.name: 熊之凝 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Vanguard of Oshikuma-no-Miko's army. He encouraged his side with a song.

figures.name: 葉山媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 山背根子 (reading unconfirmed). She enshrined the rough spirit of Amaterasu-Ōmikami in the land of 広田 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Kehi-no-Ōkami (笥飯大神)
figures.role: A deity at 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed), worshipped by the Crown Prince in the 13th year. The Kokugakuin University deity-name database identifies it with 気比大神 (reading unconfirmed) of the Kojiki.

figures.name: 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Tricked by the Silla envoys while escorting the hostage, he killed the envoys and took the 草羅城 fortress (reading unconfirmed) in Silla. He was sent to Silla again in the 62nd year.

figures.name: 微叱許智伐旱 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A hostage from Silla. In the 5th year he escaped home through a scheme of the Silla envoys.

figures.name: 久氐 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An envoy of Paekche. He opened relations by way of the land of 卓淳 (reading unconfirmed) and presented the Seven-Branched Sword and other items.

figures.name: 千熊長彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Said to have been the envoy sent to reproach Silla; he concluded a pact with the king of Paekche.

figures.name: 木羅斤資 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A figure described in a small-character note as a general of Paekche. He took part in the attack on Silla in the 49th year.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (the revolt of 香坂王 (reading unconfirmed) and Oshikuma-no-Miko)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the Empress, distrusting people's loyalty, put her son on a mourning ship and had it announced that the prince had already died, and so went up to the capital. 香坂王 (reading unconfirmed) climbs a 歴木 tree (reading unconfirmed) and is eaten by a great boar. The Nihon Shoki main text has no mourning-ship stratagem; instead a red boar climbs onto a temporary platform and eats 麛坂王 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (the defeat and death of Oshikuma-no-Miko)
compare.text: The bowstring stratagem also appears in the Kojiki, but there it is carried out by 建振熊命 (reading unconfirmed), who falsely announces that 息長帯日売命 (reading unconfirmed) has already died, and Oshikuma-no-Miko's general is 伊佐比宿禰 (reading unconfirmed). In the Nihon Shoki main text it is Takeuchi-no-Sukune who proposes a truce, claiming it as the Empress's command, and the one who dies with Oshikuma-no-Miko is 五十狭茅宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Chūai (Kehi-no-Ōkami and the songs of the sake feast)
compare.text: The Kojiki has a story in which Takeuchi-no-Sukune (建内宿禰) takes the Crown Prince to 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed) for purification and the prince exchanges names with 伊奢沙和気大神 (reading unconfirmed); on their return the prince's mother brews welcoming sake and sings. The Nihon Shoki main text only records that in the 13th year the Crown Prince worshipped Kehi-no-Ōkami (笥飯大神) and that the Empress Dowager sang at a banquet; the name-exchange story appears in a "one version says" (一云) small-character note at the start of Book 10. No corresponding entries in the Kojiki could be confirmed for the exchanges with Paekche or the quotations from the Records of Wei.

variants.name: One version (一云): the origin of 熊之凝 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: A small-character note makes 熊之凝 (reading unconfirmed) the ancestor of the 葛野城首 (reading unconfirmed), while a "one version says" (一云) makes him a distant ancestor of the 多呉吉師 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One version (一云): the origin of 千熊長彦 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: A small-character note says that the clan name of 千熊長彦 (reading unconfirmed) is unclear, and a "one version says" (一云) makes him a man of Musashi Province and the founding ancestor of the present-day 額田部槻本首 (reading unconfirmed) and others. It further asks whether he may be the 職麻那那加比跪 (reading unconfirmed) who appears in the Paekche Record (百済記).

variants.name: Paekche Record (百済記) and one version (一云): 沙至比跪 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: The main text only records that 襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed) was made to attack Silla, but the Paekche Record (百済記) quoted in a small-character note relates that 沙至比跪 (reading unconfirmed), sent in the year 壬午, accepted beautiful women from Silla and instead destroyed the land of Kara (加羅), and that the Emperor in anger had 木羅斤資 (reading unconfirmed) restore Kara. A further "one version says" (一云) within it states that 沙至比跪, learning that the Emperor's anger had not abated, entered a stone cave and died.

ojin-jidai.title: The birth and accession of Emperor Ōjin and the first half of his reign
ojin-jidai.lead: This section records the birth of Emperor Homuta (誉田天皇; Emperor Ōjin) and the origin of his name, his accession, and his consorts and children, and then describes the events from the 3rd to the 13th year, year by year. It includes the replacement of King 辰斯 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche, the ship 枯野 (reading unconfirmed), the ordeal by boiling water (探湯) between Takeuchi-no-Sukune and 甘美内宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and the songs of the Emperor and 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) concerning 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed).

points.text: The Emperor was born at 蚊田 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi in the 12th month of the year (庚辰) in which the Empress attacked Silla. Because there was flesh on his arm shaped like an archer's wrist guard (鞆), he is said to have been called Emperor Homuta (誉田天皇), from the ancient custom of calling the wrist guard "褒武多".

In the 9th year, the younger brother 甘美内宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) slandered Takeuchi-no-Sukune, saying, "Takeuchi-no-Sukune intends to split off Tsukushi and take the realm." 真根子 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 壱伎直 (reading unconfirmed), who resembled Takeuchi-no-Sukune, killed himself in his place. Takeuchi-no-Sukune pleaded his innocence at court, and by the Emperor's command the two underwent the ordeal by boiling water (探湯) beside the 磯城 river (reading unconfirmed); Takeuchi-no-Sukune won.

In the 13th year, the Emperor, learning that his son 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) had set his heart on 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed), whom the Emperor had summoned from Hyūga, gave her to 大鷦鷯尊 by means of a song at a banquet, and 大鷦鷯尊 answered with a song of joy.

In the 3rd year, because King 辰斯 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche had been discourteous to the Emperor, 紀角宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and three others were sent to reproach him. Paekche killed King 辰斯 and apologized, and 紀角宿禰 and the others set up 阿菟 (as written in the original; reading unconfirmed) as king and returned.

The song the Emperor composed at 菟道野上 (reading unconfirmed) in the 6th year also appears in the Kojiki, in almost the same words, as a song composed at 宇遅野上 (reading unconfirmed) while looking out over 葛野 (reading unconfirmed).

On the origin of the name, a "one version says" (一云) in a small-character note gives a story in which the Crown Prince exchanged names with Kehi-no-Ōkami (笥飯大神) of 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed), and says it is "unclear" (未詳) because there is no record to confirm it. The Kokugakuin University deity-name database notes that there is one view that this note was a later insertion and another that it was there from the time of compilation.

story.text: Emperor Homuta (誉田天皇) was the fourth son of Emperor 足仲彦 (足仲彦天皇; reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 気長足姫尊 (reading unconfirmed). He was born at 蚊田 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi in the winter, in the 12th month of the year 庚辰, the year the Empress attacked Silla. From childhood he was intelligent, and his conduct was outstanding. In the 3rd year of the Empress Dowager's regency, at the age of three, he was made Crown Prince. It is said that while he was in his mother's womb the heavenly and earthly deities granted him the Three Han (三韓). When he was born there was flesh on his arm like an archer's wrist guard (鞆), resembling the wrist guard the Empress Dowager had worn when she dressed as a man, so he was named Emperor Homuta. In the 4th month of the 69th year of the regency the Empress Dowager died (a small-character note says at the age of one hundred).

In the 1st month of the first year, the Crown Prince ascended the throne. This year was the Great Year 庚寅 (太歳庚寅). In the 3rd month of the 2nd year, Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto (仲姫) was made Empress, and she bore 荒田皇女 (reading unconfirmed), Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed) and 根鳥皇子 (reading unconfirmed). Before that, the Empress's elder sister 高城入姫 (reading unconfirmed) had borne 額田大中彦皇子, 大山守皇子 and 去来真稚皇子 (readings unconfirmed) and others, and the other consorts bore 菟道稚郎子皇子, 稚野毛二派皇子 and 隼総別皇子 (readings unconfirmed) and others; the Emperor's children, sons and daughters together, numbered twenty. 根鳥皇子 is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 大田君 (reading unconfirmed), 大山守皇子 of the 土形君 and 榛原君 (readings unconfirmed), and 去来真稚皇子 of the 深河別 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 10th month of the 3rd year, all the Emishi of the east brought tribute, so the Emishi were used to build the 廐坂 road (reading unconfirmed).
