In the 11th month, the fishermen (海人) of various places made disturbances and did not obey orders, so 大浜宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 阿曇連 (reading unconfirmed), was sent to pacify them and was made chief of the fishermen. In this year, because King 辰斯 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche had been discourteous, 紀角宿禰, 羽田矢代宿禰, 石川宿禰 and 木菟宿禰 (readings unconfirmed) were sent to reproach him. Paekche killed King 辰斯 and apologized, and 紀角宿禰 and the others set up 阿菟 (reading unconfirmed) as king and returned. In the 8th month of the 5th year, the provinces were ordered to establish fishermen's groups and mountain wardens (山守部). In the 10th month, a ship ten jō (十丈) long was built in Izu Province; because it ran light and fast it was named 枯野 (reading unconfirmed) (a small-character note suggests this is a corruption of "軽野").

In the 2nd month of the 6th year, the Emperor went to Ōmi Province and composed a song at 菟道野上 (reading unconfirmed). In the 9th month of the 7th year, people from Koguryŏ (高麗), Paekche, Mimana and Silla came to court; Takeuchi-no-Sukune was made to lead the various Korean people (韓人) in building a pond, which was named the 韓人池 pond (reading unconfirmed). In the 3rd month of the 8th year, people from Paekche came to court. The Paekche Record (百済記), quoted in a small-character note, records that because King 阿花 (阿花王; reading unconfirmed) had been discourteous, lands such as 枕彌多禮 (reading unconfirmed) were taken from him, and he sent the prince 直支 (reading unconfirmed) to the heavenly court to renew the friendship of the former king.

In the 4th month of the 9th year, Takeuchi-no-Sukune was sent to Tsukushi to inspect the people. His younger brother 甘美内宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), wishing to set his elder brother aside, slandered him, saying that Takeuchi-no-Sukune intended to split off Tsukushi, bring the Three Han (三韓) under him and take the realm; the Emperor sent a messenger to kill Takeuchi-no-Sukune. 真根子 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 壱伎直 (reading unconfirmed), who closely resembled Takeuchi-no-Sukune in appearance, said that he would take his place and so make plain the minister's loyalty, and fell on his sword and died. Takeuchi-no-Sukune secretly left Tsukushi, went round by the southern sea, reached the harbor of 紀水門 (reading unconfirmed), and pleaded his innocence at court. Since the claims of the two could not be decided, the Emperor petitioned the deities of heaven and earth and had them undergo the ordeal by boiling water (探湯); beside the 磯城 river (reading unconfirmed), Takeuchi-no-Sukune won. Takeuchi-no-Sukune knocked 甘美内宿禰 down and was about to kill him, but the Emperor had him spared and gave him to the ancestors of the 紀伊直 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

In the 10th month of the 11th year, the ponds of 剣池, 軽池, 鹿垣池 and 廐坂池 (readings unconfirmed) were made. In this year the Emperor heard that in Hyūga Province there was a beautiful girl named 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 諸県君牛諸井 (reading unconfirmed), and wished to summon her. In the 3rd month of the 13th year he sent a messenger, and in the 9th month 髪長媛 came from Hyūga and was lodged at the village of 桑津 (reading unconfirmed). The Emperor's son 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) saw her and set his heart on her for her beauty. Learning of this, the Emperor, on the day of a banquet in the inner palace, had 髪長媛 brought to the banquet seats, called 大鷦鷯尊 and sang while pointing to her. 大鷦鷯尊, understanding that she was being given to him, rejoiced and answered with a song, and after becoming intimate with her he composed two more songs.

quotes.note: An explanation of the origin of the name: by the custom of ancient times, the archer's wrist guard (鞆) was called "褒武多".
Because the ship ran light and fast, it was named 枯野 (reading unconfirmed).
Since it could not be decided who was in the right, the Emperor petitioned the deities of heaven and earth and had the ordeal by boiling water (探湯) performed.
大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) was moved by the beauty of 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed) and constantly longed for her.

figures.name: Izasawake-no-Kami (去來紗別神)
figures.role: In the "one version says" (一云) of a small-character note, the name of the great deity of 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed) who is said to have exchanged names with the Crown Prince.

figures.name: Homutawake-no-Mikoto (譽田別尊)
figures.role: The name of the Crown Prince after the exchange of names, according to the "one version says" (一云) of a small-character note.

figures.name: 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of the Emperor (the original also writes 大鷦鷯天皇). He was given 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 菟道稚郎子皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince born to 宮主宅媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大山守皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince born to 高城入姫 (reading unconfirmed). He is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 土形君 and 榛原君 (readings unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大濱宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 阿曇連 (reading unconfirmed). He pacified the unruly fishermen and became chief of the fishermen.

figures.name: 紀角宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sent to reproach King 辰斯 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche for his discourtesy; he set up a new king and returned.

figures.name: 甘美内宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger brother of Takeuchi-no-Sukune. He slandered his elder brother and lost the ordeal by boiling water.

figures.name: 真根子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 壱伎直 (reading unconfirmed). He killed himself in place of Takeuchi-no-Sukune.

figures.name: 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 諸県君牛諸井 (reading unconfirmed) of Hyūga. She was given to 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (the land-viewing song at 宇遅野上 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: The land-viewing song looking out over 葛野 (reading unconfirmed) also appears in the Kojiki in almost the same words. In the Kojiki it is followed by the story of the Emperor meeting 矢河枝比売 (reading unconfirmed) at the village of 木幡 (reading unconfirmed) and the birth of 宇遅能和紀郎子 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (髪長比売 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: In the Kojiki, 大雀命 (reading unconfirmed) asks Takeuchi-no-Sukune (建内宿禰) to make the request to the Emperor on his behalf, and on the day of the court banquet (豊明) the Emperor has 髪長比売 (reading unconfirmed) hold the oak-leaf cup of great sake (大御酒柏) and gives her to the prince. In the Nihon Shoki main text, the Emperor notices the feelings of 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) by himself and gives her to him at a banquet.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (the achievements of this reign)
compare.text: The establishment of the fishermen's groups (海部) and mountain wardens (山守部) and the making of the 剣池 pond (reading unconfirmed) are recorded together in the Kojiki as events of "this reign". No corresponding entry in Part 2 of the Kojiki could be confirmed for the story of the ordeal by boiling water between Takeuchi-no-Sukune and 甘美内宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One version (一云): the origin of the name Homuta (誉田)
variants.text: A "one version says" (一云) in a small-character note states that when the Emperor was Crown Prince he went to the land of 越 (reading unconfirmed), worshipped Kehi-no-Ōkami (笥飯大神) of 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed) and exchanged names with the great deity, so that the deity is called Izasawake-no-Kami (去来紗別神) and the Crown Prince Homutawake-no-Mikoto (誉田別尊). If so, the deity's original name would have been Homutawake-no-Kami (誉田別神) and the Crown Prince's original name Izasawake-no-Mikoto (去来紗別尊); but it records that, since there is no record, this is unclear (未詳).

variants.name: One version (一云): the presentation of 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed)
variants.text: It says that when 諸県君牛 (reading unconfirmed), grown old, retired from service at court, he presented his daughter 髪長媛 (reading unconfirmed). While the Emperor was hunting on Awaji Island, he saw a herd of several dozen deer coming across the sea, but they were in fact people wearing deerskins with the antlers attached. It records that the place where they landed came to be called the harbor of 鹿子水門 (reading unconfirmed), and that the practice of calling boatmen 鹿子 began at this time.

ojin-uji.title: The immigrant peoples and the appointment of 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) as Crown Prince
ojin-uji.lead: Covering the 14th to the 41st year, this section centers on entries about craftswomen, scholars and other people who came from Paekche, Wu (呉) and elsewhere, and also records the visit of the 国樔 people (reading unconfirmed) of Yoshino, 兄媛 (reading unconfirmed) of Kibi, the koto made from the ship 枯野 (reading unconfirmed), and other matters. In the 40th year the Emperor designates 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) as his successor, and the book ends with his death at the 明宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in the 41st year; the revolt of 大山守命 (reading unconfirmed) is not recorded in this book.

points.text: In the 15th year the king of Paekche had 阿直岐 (reading unconfirmed) deliver two fine horses, and 阿直岐, who could read the classics, became tutor to the Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed). Because 阿直岐 named 王仁 (reading unconfirmed) as a better scholar, 王仁 was summoned; he came in the 16th year, and the Crown Prince studied the various classics under him and mastered them all.

In the 14th year 弓月君 (reading unconfirmed) came from Paekche and reported that the laborers of 120 districts he had brought were being held back by Silla and remained in Kara (加羅). 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed) did not return even after three years; in the 16th year, when 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and others advanced troops to the border of Silla, the laborers of 弓月 came together with 襲津彦. In the 20th year 阿知使主 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 倭漢直 (reading unconfirmed), and others came leading their people of seventeen districts.

In the 40th year the Emperor asked 大山守命 (reading unconfirmed) and 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) which they held dearer, an older child or a younger one, and was pleased with 大鷦鷯尊, who answered the younger. The Emperor had long wished to make 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) Crown Prince; he made 菟道稚郎子 his successor, gave 大山守命 charge of the mountains, rivers, forests and fields, and entrusted 大鷦鷯尊 with assisting the Crown Prince and handling the affairs of state.

In the 28th year, because a memorial from the king of Koguryŏ (高麗) contained the words "高麗王教日本國也", the Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed), angered at its discourtesy, reproached the envoy and tore up the memorial.

In the 31st year the old government ship 枯野 (reading unconfirmed) was used as firewood to boil salt, and the salt was distributed to the provinces so that they would build ships. A koto made from the wood left unburned is said to have sounded clear and carried far.

The exchange in which the successor is decided also appears in the Kojiki, but there 大山守命 (reading unconfirmed) is assigned the administration of the mountains and seas, 大雀命 (reading unconfirmed) the government of the realm (食国), and 宇遅能和紀郎子 (reading unconfirmed) is designated to rule as the heavenly successor (天津日継); after the Emperor's death the revolt of 大山守命 is related. For the Emperor's age at death, the Nihon Shoki gives 110 and the Kojiki 130.

story.text: In the 2nd month of the 14th year, the king of Paekche presented 真毛津 (reading unconfirmed), a craftswoman who sewed garments; she is said to be the founding ancestor of the 来目衣縫 (reading unconfirmed). In this year 弓月君 (reading unconfirmed) came from Paekche and reported that he had wished to come and settle with the laborers of 120 districts, but that they had been held back by the people of Silla and remained in the land of Kara (加羅). 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed) was therefore sent to Kara to bring them, but even after three years 襲津彦 did not return.

In the 8th month of the 15th year, the king of Paekche sent 阿直岐 (reading unconfirmed) to present two fine horses. They were kept in the stable on the slope of 軽 (reading unconfirmed), and 阿直岐 was made to look after them, so the place is called 廐坂 (reading unconfirmed). Because 阿直岐 could read the classics, he became tutor to the Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed). When the Emperor asked whether there was a scholar better than he, he named 王仁 (reading unconfirmed), so 荒田別 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 上毛野君 (reading unconfirmed), and others were sent to Paekche to summon 王仁. In the 2nd month of the 16th year 王仁 came, and the Crown Prince studied the various classics with him and there was nothing he did not master. 王仁 is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 書首 (reading unconfirmed) and others. In this year King 阿花 (阿花王; reading unconfirmed) of Paekche died, and the Emperor sent King 直支 (直支王; reading unconfirmed) back to his country to succeed to the throne, granting him the land of 東韓 (reading unconfirmed). In the 8th month, when 平群木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and 的戸田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) were sent to Kara with picked troops, the king of Silla admitted his offense, and the laborers of 弓月 came together with 襲津彦.

In the 10th month of the 19th year, when the Emperor went to the Yoshino Palace, people of the 国樔 (reading unconfirmed) came, presented sweet sake (醴酒) and sang, and when they had finished singing they struck their mouths, looked up to the sky and laughed. It is said that the custom, still followed today on the days when the 国樔 present the products of their land, of striking their mouths and laughing after singing is a rule handed down from ancient times. The 国樔 people are very simple in their ways; they eat the nuts and fruits of the mountains, and boil frogs, which they regard as a fine delicacy and call 毛瀰 (reading unconfirmed). They live in rugged land on the upper reaches of the Yoshino River, southeast of the capital beyond the mountains, and seldom came, but after this they came often and presented chestnuts, mushrooms, sweetfish and other products. In the 9th month of the 20th year, 阿知使主 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 倭漢直 (reading unconfirmed), and his son 都加使主 (reading unconfirmed) came leading their people of seventeen districts.

In the 3rd month of the 22nd year, the Emperor resided at the 大隅宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in Naniwa. When he was gazing into the distance from a high tower, his consort 兄媛 (reading unconfirmed) looked toward the west, sighed deeply and asked to see her parents, so the Emperor had eighty fishermen of 淡路御原 (reading unconfirmed) serve as boatmen and send her to Kibi. In the 4th month, when 兄媛 set sail from 大津 (reading unconfirmed), the Emperor watched her ship from the high tower and sang. In the 9th month the Emperor hunted on Awaji Island, then moved on to Kibi, visited the island of 小豆島 (reading unconfirmed), and stayed at the 葦守宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) at 葉田 (reading unconfirmed). 兄媛's elder brother 御友別 (reading unconfirmed) had his brothers, children and grandchildren serve as stewards of the table (膳夫) and entertained him respectfully, so the Emperor, pleased, divided the land of Kibi: he enfeoffed 川嶋県 (reading unconfirmed) to the eldest son 稲速別 (reading unconfirmed) (founding ancestor of the 下道臣), 上道県 (reading unconfirmed) to 仲彦 (reading unconfirmed) (founding ancestor of the 上道臣 and 香屋臣), 三野県 (reading unconfirmed) to 弟彦 (reading unconfirmed) (founding ancestor of the 三野臣), 波区芸県 (reading unconfirmed) to 御友別's younger brother 鴨別 (reading unconfirmed) (ancestor of the 笠臣), and 苑県 (reading unconfirmed) to the elder brother 浦凝別 (reading unconfirmed) (founding ancestor of the 苑臣), and gave 織部県 (reading unconfirmed) to 兄媛.

In the 25th year King 直支 (直支王; reading unconfirmed) of Paekche died and his son 久爾辛 (reading unconfirmed) became king, but because he was young, 木満致 (reading unconfirmed) took charge of the government of the country; he had relations with the king's mother and repeatedly behaved without propriety, so the Emperor summoned 木満致. In the 9th month of the 28th year, an envoy of the king of Koguryŏ (高麗) presented a memorial, but because it said "The king of Koguryŏ instructs the land of Japan", the Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed), angered at its discourtesy, tore it up. In the 8th month of the 31st year, the Emperor, not forgetting the long service of the government ship 枯野 (reading unconfirmed), which had rotted, ordered that its name be passed down to later ages. The ministers used the ship's timber as firewood to boil salt and distributed five hundred baskets of salt to the provinces so that they would build ships. Many of the five hundred ships that gathered were burned at the harbor of 武庫水門 (reading unconfirmed) by a fire that started in the lodging of the Silla envoys, and the king of Silla, in fear, presented skilled craftsmen (the founding ancestors of the 猪名部 (reading unconfirmed) and others). A koto made from the unburned wood of 枯野 resounded far, and the Emperor composed a song.

In the 2nd month of the 37th year, 阿知使主 (reading unconfirmed) and 都加使主 (reading unconfirmed) were sent to Wu (呉) to seek seamstresses. The two crossed to Koguryŏ (高麗) but did not know the way, so the king of Koguryŏ gave them two guides, 久礼波 and 久礼志 (readings unconfirmed), and they reached Wu; the king of Wu gave them four craftswomen: 兄媛, 弟媛, 呉織 and 穴織 (readings unconfirmed). In the 2nd month of the 39th year, King 直支 (直支王; reading unconfirmed) of Paekche sent his younger sister 新斉都媛 (reading unconfirmed) to serve, and she came bringing seven women with her.

In the 1st month of the 40th year, the Emperor summoned 大山守命 (reading unconfirmed) and 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) and asked whether they loved their children, and which they held dearer, the older or the younger. 大山守命 answered the older child and displeased the Emperor. 大鷦鷯尊, reading the Emperor's expression, answered that an older child is already grown and gives no cause for worry, but a younger child is dear because it is not yet known how he will turn out; the Emperor was greatly pleased. The Emperor had wished to make 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) Crown Prince, and asked this question to learn the minds of the two. On the day 甲子, he made 菟道稚郎子 his successor, had 大山守命 take charge of the mountains, rivers, forests and fields, and had 大鷦鷯尊 assist the Crown Prince and oversee the government of the country. In the 2nd month of the 41st year, the Emperor died at the 明宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). He was 110 years old. In the same month 阿知使主 (reading unconfirmed) and the others arrived in Tsukushi from Wu (呉); 胸形大神 (reading unconfirmed) asked for craftswomen, so 兄媛 (reading unconfirmed) was offered. They arrived with the remaining three at 武庫 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of 津国 (reading unconfirmed) but were too late for the Emperor, who had died, so they presented them to 大鷦鷯尊. Their descendants are said to be the present-day 呉衣縫 and 蚊屋衣縫 (readings unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) studied the various classics under 王仁 (reading unconfirmed), and there was nothing he did not master.
An explanation that the 国樔 (reading unconfirmed) striking their mouths, looking up to the sky and laughing after they finish singing is probably a rule handed down from ancient times.
The words of the memorial from the king of Koguryŏ (高麗). The Crown Prince regarded them as discourteous and tore up the memorial.
The Emperor's words of pleasure at the answer of 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed): "Your words truly accord with my own heart."

figures.name: 真毛津 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A seamstress presented by the king of Paekche. She is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 来目衣縫 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 弓月君 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A figure who came from Paekche, wishing to settle with the laborers of 120 districts.

figures.name: 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sent to Kara (加羅) to bring the laborers of 弓月 (reading unconfirmed); he did not return for three years.

figures.name: 阿直岐 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: As envoy of the king of Paekche he delivered fine horses and became tutor to the Crown Prince. He is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 阿直岐史 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 王仁 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Summoned from Paekche on the recommendation of 阿直岐 (reading unconfirmed), he taught the classics to the Crown Prince. He is regarded as the founding ancestor of the 書首 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of the Emperor. In the 40th year he was designated successor.

figures.name: 直支王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince of Paekche. After the death of King 阿花 (reading unconfirmed) he was sent back by the Emperor and succeeded to the throne.

figures.name: 阿知使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 倭漢直 (reading unconfirmed). He came leading his people and was later sent to Wu (呉) to seek seamstresses.

figures.name: 兄媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger sister of 御友別 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 吉備臣 (reading unconfirmed), and a consort of the Emperor. She returned to Kibi to visit her parents.

figures.name: 御友別 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brother of 兄媛 (reading unconfirmed). He entertained the Emperor, and his family were enfeoffed with the districts of the land of Kibi.

figures.name: 木滿致 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A figure who ran the government of Paekche. The Paekche Record (百済記) quoted in a small-character note makes him the son of 木羅斤資 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大山守命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of the Emperor. He answered that the older child was dearer and was given charge of the mountains, rivers, forests and fields.

figures.name: 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of the Emperor. He answered that the younger child was dearer and was given the task of assisting the Crown Prince in affairs of state.

figures.name: 胸形大神 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A deity who asked for craftswomen in Tsukushi and was offered 兄媛 (reading unconfirmed), who had come from Wu (呉).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (the division of duties among the three princes)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, too, the Emperor asks 大山守命 (reading unconfirmed) and 大雀命 (reading unconfirmed) whether they love an elder child or a younger child more, and is pleased with the answer of 大雀命. The Kojiki then assigns to 大山守命 the administration of the mountains and seas, to 大雀命 the government of the realm (食国), and to 宇遅能和紀郎子 (reading unconfirmed) the heavenly succession (天津日継); after the Emperor's death it relates the revolt of 大山守命 and his end at the crossing of 宇遅 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (the people who came from abroad)
compare.text: The Kojiki records that 阿知吉師 (reading unconfirmed) brought two horses from King 照古 (照古王; reading unconfirmed) of Paekche, and that 和邇吉師 (reading unconfirmed) came bringing the Analects (論語) in ten scrolls and the Thousand Character Classic (千字文) in one scroll. In the Nihon Shoki main text, 王仁 (reading unconfirmed) is summoned on the recommendation of 阿直岐 (reading unconfirmed) and becomes the Crown Prince's tutor, but the titles of the books he brought are not recorded.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 2, section on Emperor Ōjin (the song of the 国主 (reading unconfirmed) of Yoshino)
compare.text: The Kojiki says that the 国主 (reading unconfirmed) of Yoshino brewed great sake (大御酒) in a 横臼 mortar (reading unconfirmed) and presented it, singing while beating a mouth-drum (口鼓), and that this is the song still sung today when the great offerings (大贄) are presented. In the Nihon Shoki, in the 19th year, people of the 国樔 (reading unconfirmed) present sweet sake (醴酒) at the Yoshino Palace, sing, then strike their mouths and laugh.

variants.name: One version (一云): the palace where the Emperor died
variants.text: The main text says that the Emperor died at the 明宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), but a "one version says" (一云) in a small-character note says that he died at the 大隅宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

nintoku.title: Emperor Nintoku, the people's cooking fires, and Empress 磐之媛 (reading unconfirmed)
nintoku.lead: After the death of Emperor Homuta (譽田天皇), 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) and the Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) each yielded the throne to the other, and when the Crown Prince took his own life, 大鷦鷯尊 ascended the throne at the 高津宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in Naniwa. The story of the "people's cooking fires", in which he exempted the people from taxes and labor for three years, the works on the 堀江 canal (reading unconfirmed) and the 茨田 embankment (reading unconfirmed), the conflict over Empress 磐之媛 (reading unconfirmed) and 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed), the wars with Silla and the Emishi, and other matters are recorded year by year up to his death in the 87th year.

points.text: In the 2nd month of the 4th year, the Emperor looked out over the land from a high tower and, seeing that no cooking smoke was rising, realized that the people were poor; in the 3rd month he exempted them from all taxes and labor for three years. Even when the palace fences fell down and the rain leaked in, he did not repair them, and in the 4th month of the 7th year, seeing smoke filling the land, he told the Empress, "When the people are rich, I am rich."

In the 9th year, although the provinces asked to pay taxes and repair the palace, the Emperor did not allow it. When he reimposed taxes and labor in the 10th month of the 10th year, the people, helping the old and bringing their small children, carried timber of their own accord, and the palace buildings were soon completed. The original text records that for this reason "he is called the sage emperor (聖帝) to this day".

Before the accession, 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) and 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) yielded the throne to each other for three years, and fresh fish presented by fishermen went back and forth between 菟道 (reading unconfirmed) and Naniwa. The Crown Prince, saying that he could not take away his elder brother's resolve, took his own life and entrusted his full sister 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed) to his brother.

In the 9th month of the 30th year, Empress 磐之媛命 (reading unconfirmed), hearing that the Emperor had taken 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed) into the palace, threw into the sea the 御綱葉 leaves (reading unconfirmed) she had gathered at Cape Kumano, and instead of returning to Naniwa built a palace south of the 筒城 hill (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro and lived there. Even when the Emperor visited her in person she would not meet him; she died there in the 35th year, and in the 38th year 八田皇女 became Empress.

In the 11th year the 堀江 canal (reading unconfirmed) was dug and the 茨田 embankment (reading unconfirmed) built. At two difficult places, following the instruction of a deity who appeared in a dream, 強頚 (reading unconfirmed), a man of Musashi, sank into the water and died, but 茨田連衫子 (reading unconfirmed), a man of Kawachi, tested the deity by throwing two gourds into the water; because the gourds did not sink, he did not have to die, and he completed the embankment.

The Kojiki also records the three-year exemption from taxes and labor and the "reign of the sage emperor" (聖帝世), but it says that the Emperor climbed a high mountain to look over the land, and it sums the story up briefly in a single section. The year-by-year progress of the 4th, 7th and 10th years and the exchange with the Empress found in the Nihon Shoki do not appear in the Kojiki.

story.text: Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the fourth son of Emperor Homuta (譽田天皇), and his mother was Nakatsuhime-no-Mikoto (仲姫命). When the previous emperor died in the 2nd month of the 41st year of Emperor Homuta, the Crown Prince 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) and 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) each yielded the throne to the other. Meanwhile 額田大中彦皇子 (reading unconfirmed), who tried to take control of the imperial rice fields (屯田) of Yamato, was rebuffed on the basis of a rule from the reign of the emperor of the 纒向玉城宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), reported by 吾子篭 (reading unconfirmed), who had been recalled from the Korean lands (韓国). 大山守皇子 (reading unconfirmed) plotted to kill the Crown Prince and take the throne, but the Crown Prince, forewarned by 大鷦鷯尊, mingled with the ferrymen and tipped the boat in the middle of the 菟道 river (reading unconfirmed), throwing the prince into the water and causing his death. Still the Crown Prince did not ascend the throne, and it stood empty for three years. Fresh fish presented by fishermen were sent back and forth between 菟道 and Naniwa many times, and the fishermen threw the fish away and wept; this is regarded as the origin of the proverb about the fisherman who weeps over his own goods. The Crown Prince, saying that he could not take away his elder brother's resolve, took his own life. 大鷦鷯尊 hurried to him, loosened his hair, straddled the body and called out three times, and the Crown Prince briefly revived, entrusted his full sister 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed) to his brother, died again, and was buried on the mountain of 菟道.

In the 1st month of the first year, 大鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) ascended the throne, made his mother Empress Dowager, and placed the capital at Naniwa, calling it the 高津宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). The palace was a plain one: its fences and pillars were not painted, and the thatch of its roofs was not even trimmed. On the day the Emperor was born a horned owl (木菟) flew into the birthing hall, and on the same day a wren (鷦鷯) flew into the birthing hut of Takeuchi-no-Sukune's wife, so Emperor Homuta (譽田天皇) exchanged the names of the two birds in naming the children, and the minister's son became 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) (founding ancestor of the 平群臣; reading unconfirmed). In the 3rd month of the 2nd year, 磐之媛命 (reading unconfirmed) was made Empress, and 去來穗別, 住吉仲皇子, 瑞齒別 and 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (readings unconfirmed) were born; the consort 日向髮長媛 (reading unconfirmed) bore 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and 幡梭皇女 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 2nd month of the 4th year, the Emperor gazed into the distance from a high tower and, seeing no cooking smoke rising, realized that the people were poor. In the 3rd month he exempted them from all taxes and labor for three years; he did not replace his own clothes or footwear until they wore out, and even when the palace fences fell down and the rain leaked in, he did not repair them. In the 4th month of the 7th year, seeing smoke filling the land, the Emperor told the Empress, "I am already rich." When the Empress asked how this could be when the palace was in ruins, he answered that a ruler takes the people as his foundation. In the 9th year, although the provinces asked to pay taxes and repair the palace, he did not allow it. When he imposed taxes and labor again in the 10th month of the 10th year, the people worked with all their strength day and night to build the palace buildings, and it is recorded that for this reason he is called the sage emperor (聖帝) to this day.

In the 11th year, the Emperor, troubled that the water overflowed and there were few rice fields, had the plain north of the palace dug in the 10th month to lead the water to the western sea, naming the channel the 堀江 (reading unconfirmed), and built the 茨田 embankment (reading unconfirmed). In this work 強頚 (reading unconfirmed) sank into the water and died, while 衫子 (reading unconfirmed) escaped death through his clever use of gourds; the two places were called 強頚斷間 and 衫子斷間 (readings unconfirmed). In the 12th year, of an iron shield and target presented by Koguryŏ (高麗), only 盾人宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 的臣 (reading unconfirmed), shot through them, and he was given the name 的戸田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed). After that the great canal of 栗隈県 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro, the 茨田屯倉 granary (reading unconfirmed), the 和珥池 pond (reading unconfirmed), the 横野堤 embankment (reading unconfirmed), the bridge at 猪甘津 (reading unconfirmed), the great road within the capital, the great canal of 感玖 (reading unconfirmed) and other works were built one after another, and more than forty thousand 頃 of rice fields are said to have been opened.

In the 16th year, the Emperor gave the court lady 桑田玖賀媛 (reading unconfirmed), whom he could not approach because of the Empress's jealousy, to 速待 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 播磨国造 (reading unconfirmed), but 玖賀媛 would not accept him and died of illness while being sent back to 桑田 (reading unconfirmed). In the 22nd year the Emperor asked the Empress in a song to let him take 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed) as a consort, but the Empress answered with a song and did not allow it. In the 9th month of the 30th year, the Empress, on her way back from the land of 紀国 (reading unconfirmed), heard that the Emperor had taken 八田皇女 into the palace; she did not enter Naniwa but went up the Yamashiro river and built a palace south of the 筒城 hill (reading unconfirmed). 口持臣 (reading unconfirmed), sent in the 10th month, kept lying prostrate in the courtyard, soaked by rain and snow, and his younger sister 国依媛 (reading unconfirmed) expressed her concern for her brother in a song, but the Empress answered that she would not return; in the 11th month, even when the Emperor visited the 筒城宮 palace in person, she would not meet him. In the 6th month of the 35th year the Empress died at the 筒城宮 palace; in the 37th year she was buried at 那羅山 (reading unconfirmed), and in the 1st month of the 38th year 八田皇女 was made Empress.

In the 7th month of the 38th year, the call of the deer on 菟餓野 (reading unconfirmed), which the Emperor and Empress had heard every night, ceased. The Emperor concluded that a deer presented by the 佐伯部 (reading unconfirmed) was the deer that had been calling, and moved the 佐伯部 to 渟田 (reading unconfirmed) in Aki. In the 40th year, the Emperor, wishing to take 雌鳥皇女 (reading unconfirmed) as a consort, used 隼別皇子 (reading unconfirmed) as go-between, but 隼別皇子 secretly took the princess as his own wife. Hearing a song of his attendants, the Emperor grew angry and had the two pursued, and they were killed at 蒋代野 (reading unconfirmed) in Ise. 佐伯直阿俄能胡 (reading unconfirmed), who had taken the princess's jewels, was found out later at the banquet of the Niiname (新嘗) festival; he escaped the death penalty by presenting his private land, and that land is said to have been called 玉代 (reading unconfirmed). In the 41st year 紀角宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Paekche. In the 43rd year, a bird called 倶知 (reading unconfirmed) in Paekche (the present-day hawk) was tamed by 酒君 (reading unconfirmed), the Emperor hunted with it on 百舌鳥野 (reading unconfirmed), and the hawk-keepers' group (鷹甘部) was established. In the 50th year a wild goose laid eggs on the 茨田 embankment, and the Emperor and Takeuchi-no-Sukune exchanged questions and answers in song.

In the 53rd year, 竹葉瀬 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 上毛野君 (reading unconfirmed), and his younger brother 田道 (reading unconfirmed) were sent to Silla, which had stopped sending tribute; 田道 defeated the Silla army by striking at a weakness of the enemy learned from a captive. In the 55th year 田道 fought the rebellious Emishi and died at the harbor of 伊寺水門 (reading unconfirmed), but it is said that later, when the Emishi dug up 田道's grave, a great serpent came out and killed many of the Emishi with its poison. In the 62nd year a ship was built from a great tree in Tōtōmi, and in the same year 額田大中彦皇子 (reading unconfirmed) discovered an ice house at 闘鷄 (reading unconfirmed) and presented ice; from then on ice was stored in winter and distributed at the spring equinox. In the 65th year 宿儺 (reading unconfirmed) of Hida, who had one body and two faces, was put to death by 難波根子武振熊 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed). In the 67th year a tomb site was fixed on the 石津原 plain (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi; because on the day construction began a shrike (百舌鳥) flew out of the ear of a deer that had collapsed, the place was named 百舌鳥耳原 (reading unconfirmed). In the same year 縣守 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 笠臣 (reading unconfirmed), slew a creature in a deep pool of the 川嶋河 river (reading unconfirmed) in Kibi that had been spitting poison and tormenting people. It is said that afterward, because the Emperor lightened taxes and cared for the people, there were no troubles for more than twenty years. In the 1st month of the 87th year the Emperor died, and in the 10th month he was buried in the 百舌鳥野陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The Emperor's words: if the people are poor, then I am poor; if the people are rich, then I am rich.
For that reason he is still praised (as) the sage emperor today.
A proverb: though no fisherman, one weeps over one's own goods. The story of the fish offering being sent back and forth is regarded as its origin.
Because no cooking smoke was rising within the land, he concluded that the people had already become poor.

figures.name: 大鷦鷯天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The emperor of this book: fourth son of Emperor Homuta (譽田天皇), he ascended the throne at the 高津宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in Naniwa and was called the sage emperor for exempting the people from taxes and labor.

figures.name: 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Crown Prince of Emperor Homuta (譽田天皇). Wishing to yield the throne to his elder brother, he did not ascend it for three years; he took his own life and entrusted his full sister 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed) to his brother.

figures.name: 大山守皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince who, resenting that the previous emperor had not made him Crown Prince, tried to kill the Crown Prince and died after being thrown into the 菟道 river (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 額田大中彦皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince who was rebuffed when he tried to take control of the imperial rice fields of Yamato himself, and who later discovered the ice house at 闘鷄 (reading unconfirmed) and presented ice.

figures.name: 磐之媛命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: She became Empress in the 2nd year and bore four children, emperors and a prince, but because of 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed) she moved to the 筒城宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) and died there.

figures.name: 八田皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The full sister whom 菟道稚郎子 (reading unconfirmed) entrusted to his brother. The Emperor's taking her into the palace led to conflict with Empress 磐之媛 (reading unconfirmed), and she became Empress in the 38th year.

figures.name: 隼別皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince who, while acting as go-between to bring 雌鳥皇女 (reading unconfirmed) to the Emperor as a consort, took her as his own wife, and was killed while fleeing toward Ise.

figures.name: 雌鳥皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A princess whom the Emperor wished to make his consort; she became the wife of 隼別皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and was killed with him at 蒋代野 (reading unconfirmed) in Ise.

figures.name: 茨田連衫子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of Kawachi who was to be offered to the deity at a difficult place on the 茨田 embankment (reading unconfirmed), but who tested the deity with gourds, escaped death, and completed the embankment.

figures.name: 口持臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 的臣 (reading unconfirmed). The envoy sent to bring back the Empress from the 筒城宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), who kept lying prostrate in the courtyard, soaked by rain and snow.

figures.name: 田道 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger brother of 竹葉瀬 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 上毛野君 (reading unconfirmed). He defeated the Silla army but later died fighting the Emishi.

figures.name: 宿儺 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A figure in Hida Province said to have had two faces and four arms on one body; he disobeyed orders and was put to death.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, beginning of the section on Emperor Nintoku (the story of the people's cooking fires, following the entries on consorts, children and public works)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the Emperor climbs a "high mountain" (高山), looks over the land and learns that no smoke is rising, and a single short section covers everything from the exemption from taxes and labor to the reign being called the "reign of the sage emperor" (聖帝世). The year-by-year progress and the exchange with the Empress found in the Nihon Shoki do not appear.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Nintoku, the Great Empress's journey to Yamashiro (G12–G25)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the Great Empress, learning of the Emperor's marriage on her way back from the land of 木国 (reading unconfirmed), enters the house of 奴理能美 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro (山代); 口子臣 (reading unconfirmed) and others smooth things over by saying she went to see "a wondrous insect that changes into three colors", and the Emperor visits the house and sings. In the Nihon Shoki the Empress does not return from the 筒城宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) and is said to have died there in the 35th year; the insect story could not be confirmed there.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Nintoku, the story of 女鳥王 and 速總別王 (readings unconfirmed) (G30–G40)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, 速總別王 (reading unconfirmed) and 女鳥王 (reading unconfirmed) cross the 倉椅山 mountain (reading unconfirmed) and are killed at 蘇邇 (reading unconfirmed) in 宇陀 (reading unconfirmed); the one who took 女鳥王's jeweled bracelet (玉釧) is the general 山部大楯連 (reading unconfirmed), who is sentenced to death by the Great Empress. In the Nihon Shoki the two are killed at 蒋代野 (reading unconfirmed) in Ise, and 佐伯直阿俄能胡 (reading unconfirmed), who took the jewels, escapes death by presenting land.

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: In the main text, the envoy sent to bring back the Empress from the 筒城宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) is 口持臣 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 的臣 (reading unconfirmed), but this "one version says" (一云) makes the envoy 口子臣 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 和珥臣 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Popular account (俗曰)
variants.text: The main text tells how the 佐伯部 (reading unconfirmed) presented the deer of 菟餓野 (reading unconfirmed), but a different story is also given as a popular account. Beside a man staying overnight on the plain of 菟餓 (reading unconfirmed), a stag dreamed that it was covered with white frost; another deer interpreted this as a sign that it would be shot by a man and smeared with white salt, and before dawn a hunter shot the stag dead.

richu-hanzei.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 12 — Emperor Richū and Emperor Hanzei
richu-hanzei.title: Emperor Richū, Emperor Hanzei and the revolt of 住吉仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
richu-hanzei.lead: Before his accession, Emperor 去來穗別 (去來穗別天皇; Richū; reading unconfirmed) had his palace burned by his younger brother 住吉仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and fled to Yamato, and another younger brother, 瑞齒別皇子 (reading unconfirmed), had 仲皇子 killed and put an end to the revolt. After the accession, the establishment of provincial recorders (国史) and the creation of the Treasury Office (蔵職), among other things, are recorded at the 磐余稚櫻宮 palace (reading unconfirmed); the following ruler, Emperor 瑞齒別 (瑞齒別天皇; Hanzei; reading unconfirmed), reigned for five years at the 柴籬宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in 丹比 (reading unconfirmed), Kawachi.

points.text: After the death of Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed), when the Crown Prince was about to take 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed) as his consort, 住吉仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed), sent as messenger, used the Crown Prince's name to sleep with 黒媛. When this was discovered from the hand bell he left behind, he raised troops, surrounded the Crown Prince's palace and burned it. The Crown Prince, helped by 平群木菟宿禰, 物部大前宿禰 and 阿知使主 (readings unconfirmed), escaped on horseback, and woke up at the 埴生坂 slope (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi to see the fire at Naniwa.

The Crown Prince, having entered the 石上振神宮 shrine (reading unconfirmed), suspected even his younger brother 瑞齒別皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and ordered him to go back to Naniwa, kill 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed), and only then come to him. 瑞齒別皇子 had 刺領巾 (reading unconfirmed), a Hayato attendant of 仲皇子, stab 仲皇子 in the privy, but 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), saying that one who had killed his own lord could not be allowed to live, killed 刺領巾.

Emperor 瑞齒別 (瑞齒別天皇; reading unconfirmed) was born at the 淡路宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), and his teeth were even, like a single bone. It is said that when he was washed with water from the 瑞井 well (reading unconfirmed), a 多遲 flower (the flower of the knotweed, 虎杖) fell into the well, so he was called 多遲比瑞齒別 (reading unconfirmed). It is recorded that after his accession, at the 柴籬宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in 丹比 (reading unconfirmed), Kawachi, wind and rain came in due season and the realm was at peace.

In the 8th month of the 4th year, provincial recorders (国史) were for the first time placed in the provinces, to record words and events and report on conditions in all directions. In the 1st month of the 6th year, the Treasury Office (蔵職) was established and the treasury workers (蔵部) were appointed.

In the 5th year, the three deities who dwell in Tsukushi appeared in the palace and complained that their people had been taken from them, and on Awaji Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊奘諾神) declared that he could not bear the smell of blood from the tattoos (黥) of the horse-keepers (飼部). Then the imperial consort died, and the Emperor, regretting that he had not appeased the deities' curse, had the 車持君 (reading unconfirmed), who had taken the 車持部 (reading unconfirmed) assigned to the deities, perform purification (祓禊), and dedicated the 車持部 to the three deities.

In the Kojiki, the one who raises the revolt is 墨江中王 (reading unconfirmed), and the one who carries the Emperor out is 阿知直 (reading unconfirmed) alone; the circumstances concerning 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed) do not appear. The Hayato who killed 仲皇子 is named 曾婆訶理 (reading unconfirmed), and 水齒別命 (reading unconfirmed) holds a banquet to grant him the rank of minister and then cuts off his head, which differs from the Nihon Shoki, where the punishment is carried out by 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

story.text: Emperor 去來穗別 (去來穗別天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the Crown Prince of Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 磐之媛命 (reading unconfirmed). He became Crown Prince at the age of fifteen in the 31st year of Emperor 大鷦鷯, and his father died in the 87th year. Before his accession, wishing to take 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 羽田矢代宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), as his consort, he sent his younger brother 住吉仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed) as messenger. 仲皇子 used the Crown Prince's name to sleep with 黒媛, and went home leaving his hand bell behind. When the Crown Prince noticed this the next night, he quietly withdrew, but 仲皇子, fearing trouble, surrounded the Crown Prince's palace with troops. Three men, 平群木菟宿禰, 物部大前宿禰 and 阿知使主 (readings unconfirmed), put the Crown Prince on a horse and got him away, and 仲皇子 burned the palace, in which the Crown Prince was no longer present.

The Crown Prince woke at the 埴生坂 slope (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi, was startled to see the fire at Naniwa, and headed for Yamato by way of 大坂 (reading unconfirmed). At the foot of Asuka hill (飛鳥山) a girl he met told him that the mountain was full of soldiers and that he should go round by the 當摩 road (reading unconfirmed), and the Crown Prince put this into a song. After crossing the 龍田山 mountain (reading unconfirmed), he captured with an ambush the fishermen of 野嶋 (reading unconfirmed) in Awaji who were pursuing him; they were men sent by 阿曇連濱子 (reading unconfirmed) on behalf of 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed). 倭直吾子篭 (reading unconfirmed), who had sided with 仲皇子 and blocked the road, feared that the Crown Prince would kill him, and was pardoned after presenting his younger sister 日之媛 (reading unconfirmed); the text suggests that the practice of the 倭直 (reading unconfirmed) offering court ladies (采女) may have begun at this time. The Crown Prince entered the 石上振神宮 shrine (reading unconfirmed).

When his younger brother 瑞齒別皇子 (reading unconfirmed) followed him, the Crown Prince suspected him and would not meet him, sending word that if he truly had no divided loyalty he should go back to Naniwa and kill 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed). 瑞齒別皇子, lamenting that he was doing away with one who had no principles in order to follow one who did, went to Naniwa with 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and gave 刺領巾 (reading unconfirmed), a Hayato attendant of 仲皇子, a brocade robe and trousers to get him to kill 仲皇子. 刺領巾 stabbed 仲皇子 with a spear when he went into the privy, but 木菟宿禰, saying that one who had killed his own lord could not be allowed to live, killed 刺領巾. When 瑞齒別皇子 returned to 石上 (reading unconfirmed) at midnight and reported, the Crown Prince treated his brother generously and granted him the 村合屯倉 granary (reading unconfirmed); on this day 阿曇連濱子 (reading unconfirmed) was arrested.

In the 2nd month of the first year, the Crown Prince ascended the throne at the 磐余稚櫻宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). In the 4th month, the death sentence of 阿曇連濱子 (reading unconfirmed), who had plotted with 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed), was reduced to the punishment of tattooing, and people called this the 阿曇目 ("阿曇 eye"; reading unconfirmed). In the 7th month 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 葦田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), was made imperial consort, and 磐坂市邊押羽皇子, 御馬皇子 and 青海皇女 (readings unconfirmed) were born; the second consort, 幡梭皇女 (reading unconfirmed), bore 中磯皇女 (reading unconfirmed). In the 1st month of the 2nd year, 瑞齒別皇子 (reading unconfirmed) was made heir apparent (儲君), and in the 10th month the capital was placed at 磐余 (reading unconfirmed), and 平群木菟宿禰, 蘇賀滿智宿禰, the Ōmuraji (大連) of the Mononobe (物部) and 圓大使主 (readings unconfirmed) together took charge of the government of the country. In the 11th month of the 3rd year, during a boating party on the 磐余市磯池 pond (reading unconfirmed), cherry blossoms out of season fell into the Emperor's cup; because the blossoms were found and brought back from 掖上室山 (reading unconfirmed), the palace was named the 稚櫻宮 ("young cherry palace"; reading unconfirmed).

In the 8th month of the 4th year, provincial recorders (国史) were for the first time placed in the provinces, and in the 10th month the 石上溝 canal (reading unconfirmed) was dug. In the 3rd month of the 5th year, the three deities who dwell in Tsukushi appeared in the palace and complained that their people had been taken, but the Emperor only prayed and did not perform rites for them. In the 9th month, when he hunted on Awaji, Izanagi-no-Mikoto (伊奘諾神) declared that he could not bear the smell of blood from the tattoos of the horse-keepers (飼部), so from then on tattooing of the horse-keepers was stopped. Immediately afterward a voice like the wind was heard from the sky, and a messenger reported the death of the imperial consort. The Emperor regretted not having dealt with the deities' curse, charged the 車持君 (reading unconfirmed) with his offense, and dedicated the 車持部 (reading unconfirmed) to the three deities. In the 1st month of the 6th year, 草香幡梭皇女 (reading unconfirmed) was made Empress and the Treasury Office (蔵職) was established, but in the 3rd month the Emperor fell ill and died at the 稚櫻宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) (at the age of seventy), and in the 10th month he was buried in the 百舌鳥耳原陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed).

Emperor 瑞齒別 (瑞齒別天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the full younger brother of Emperor 去來穗別 (去來穗別天皇; reading unconfirmed) and became Crown Prince in the 2nd year of Emperor 去來穗別. He was born at the 淡路宮 palace (reading unconfirmed); from birth his teeth were like a single bone and he was handsome in appearance, and it is said that when he was washed with water from the 瑞井 well (reading unconfirmed), a 多遲 flower (reading unconfirmed) fell into the well, so he was called 多遲比瑞齒別 (reading unconfirmed). He ascended the throne in the 1st month of the first year. In the 8th month he made 津野媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 木事 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 大宅臣 (reading unconfirmed), his imperial wife (皇夫人), and 香火姫皇女 and 圓皇女 (readings unconfirmed) were born; her younger sister 弟媛 (reading unconfirmed) bore 財皇女 and 高部皇子 (readings unconfirmed). In the 10th month he placed the capital at 丹比 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi, calling it the 柴籬宮 palace (reading unconfirmed); wind and rain came in due season, the five grains ripened, and the realm was at peace. In the 1st month of the 5th year, the Emperor died in the main bedchamber.

quotes.note: For the first time provincial recorders were placed in the provinces, to record words and events and report on conditions in all directions.
The words of 瑞齒別皇子 (reading unconfirmed): since I am destroying one without principles and following one who has them, who would doubt me?
(Because 濱子 (reading unconfirmed) was tattooed,) people of the time called this the 阿曇目 (reading unconfirmed).
In the reign of Emperor Hanzei, wind and rain came in due season, the five grains ripened, the people were prosperous, and the realm was at peace.

figures.name: 去來穗別天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Crown Prince of Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed); after escaping the revolt of 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed) he ascended the throne at the 磐余稚櫻宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). A reading note says that "去來" is read as "伊弉".

figures.name: 住吉仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A prince who used the name of his elder brother, the Crown Prince, to sleep with 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed) and burned the Crown Prince's palace, but was killed by 刺領巾 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 瑞齒別天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Full younger brother of Emperor 去來穗別 (reading unconfirmed). He had 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed) killed, became heir apparent, and later ascended the throne at the 柴籬宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in 丹比 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Imperial consort of Emperor 去來穗別 (reading unconfirmed). In the entry before the accession she is the daughter of 羽田矢代宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and in the entry for the first year the daughter of 葦田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed); she died in the 5th year.

figures.name: 平群木莵宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: One of the three who got the Crown Prince away; he dealt out punishment to 刺領巾 (reading unconfirmed) and later took charge of the government of the country.

figures.name: 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: One of the three who put the Crown Prince on a horse and got him away.

figures.name: 阿知使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 漢直 (reading unconfirmed), and one of the three who got the Crown Prince away.

figures.name: 阿曇連濱子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: On behalf of 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed) he had the fishermen of 野嶋 (reading unconfirmed) in Awaji pursue the Crown Prince; his death sentence was reduced and he was tattooed.

figures.name: 倭直吾子篭 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He sided with 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and blocked the Crown Prince's road, but was pardoned after presenting his younger sister 日之媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 刺領巾 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A Hayato attendant of 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed). Incited by 瑞齒別皇子 (reading unconfirmed), he stabbed 仲皇子 to death, and was killed by 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 圓大使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A figure who took charge of the government of the country in the 2nd year together with 平群木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and others. A reading note says that "圓" is read as "豆夫羅".

figures.name: 車持君 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: He arbitrarily inspected the 車持部 (reading unconfirmed) of Tsukushi, was charged with taking people assigned to the deities, and was made to perform purification (祓禊).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, beginning of the section on Emperor Richū (G50)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the younger brother 墨江中王 (reading unconfirmed) sets fire to the great hall while the Emperor is lying drunk after the banquet (豊明) of the Daijō (大嘗) festival at the Naniwa palace, and the circumstances concerning 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed) do not appear. The one who carries the Emperor out is 阿知直 (reading unconfirmed), and the place where he wakes up is given as 多遲比野 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Richū, 水齒別命 (reading unconfirmed) and the Hayato 曾婆訶理 (reading unconfirmed) (G56)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the Hayato who kills 墨江中王 (reading unconfirmed), the counterpart of 仲皇子 (reading unconfirmed), is named 曾婆訶理 (reading unconfirmed). 水齒別命 (reading unconfirmed), to reward his deed, holds a banquet to grant him the rank of minister, makes him drink sake from the same cup, and cuts off his head when his face is hidden by it. In the Nihon Shoki it is 木菟宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) who kills the Hayato 刺領巾 (reading unconfirmed), and the banquet story could not be confirmed there.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Hanzei (G57)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives Emperor Hanzei's height as nine shaku two and a half sun (九尺二寸半), and records the length and breadth of his teeth, saying they were like strung jewels. The Nihon Shoki says his teeth were like a single bone and records the origin of his name from the 瑞井 well (reading unconfirmed) and the 多遲 flower (reading unconfirmed), but does not give his height.

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: The main text says that the Crown Prince did not believe the warning of the three men, but this "one version says" (一云) relates that the Crown Prince was drunk and did not get up.

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: The main text says that the three men helped the Crown Prince and put him on a horse, but this "one version says" (一云) states that 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) took the Crown Prince in his arms and mounted the horse.

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: The main text names the master of the fishermen of 野嶋 (reading unconfirmed) who were made to pursue the Crown Prince as 阿曇連濱子 (reading unconfirmed), but this "one version says" (一云) names him 阿曇連黒友 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One source says (一日)
variants.text: A note giving another name, 飯豐皇女 (reading unconfirmed), for 青海皇女 (reading unconfirmed), the daughter borne by 黒媛 (reading unconfirmed).

ingyo-anko.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 13 — Emperor Ingyō and Emperor Ankō
ingyo-anko.title: Emperor Ingyō's oath ordeal and 衣通郎姫 (reading unconfirmed), and the death of Emperor Ankō
ingyo-anko.lead: Emperor 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (雄朝津間稚子宿禰天皇; Ingyō; reading unconfirmed) kept declining the throne on account of a serious illness, but ascended it at the plea of his consort 忍坂大中姫 (reading unconfirmed), and corrected the confusion of clan names and titles through the oath ordeal by boiling water (盟神探湯). After his favor toward the Empress's younger sister 衣通郎姫 (reading unconfirmed) and the affair of the Crown Prince 木梨輕 (木梨輕太子; reading unconfirmed), the next ruler, Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; Ankō; reading unconfirmed), believed a slander and killed 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), and was killed by that prince's son 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed).

points.text: Prince 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (雄朝津間稚子宿禰皇子; reading unconfirmed) kept refusing the ministers' nomination on account of a serious illness, but in the 12th month of the first year his consort 忍坂大中姫 (reading unconfirmed) kept waiting in the cold wind holding out water for washing his hands, until the water in the metal bowl (鋺) overflowed and froze onto her arms, and at last he ascended the throne.

In the 4th year, saying that clan names and titles had fallen into confusion and that some people were making false claims, the Emperor had people undergo the oath ordeal by boiling water (盟神探湯; a reading note gives "區訶陀智") at the 味橿 hill (reading unconfirmed). They wore sashes of bark-cloth (木綿) and were made to reach into the boiling water in cauldrons; those who told the truth were unharmed and those who lied were all injured, and the text records that from then on clan names and titles were settled.

Hearing at a banquet in the 7th year the name of the Empress's younger sister 弟姫 (衣通郎姫) (readings unconfirmed), the Emperor sent 中臣烏賦津使主 (reading unconfirmed) to bring her. Because of the Empress's jealousy he built a residence for her at Fujiwara (藤原), and later at 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi; after the Empress remonstrated with him in the 10th year, citing the hardship of the people, his visits to 茅渟 became rare.

木梨輕皇子 (reading unconfirmed), who became Crown Prince in the 23rd year, had relations with his full sister 輕大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed); in the 24th year this came to light when divination was performed about the strange freezing of the soup at the Emperor's meal. The Crown Prince, being heir apparent, was not punished, and 大娘皇女 was exiled to Iyo; after the Emperor's death the Crown Prince, deserted by the ministers, took his own life in the house of 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

In his first year Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed) believed the slander of 根使主 (reading unconfirmed) and killed 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), took his wife 中蒂姫 (reading unconfirmed) into the palace, and made her Empress in the 2nd year. In the 8th month of the 3rd year, the Emperor was killed by 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed), whom 中蒂姫 had borne to 大草香皇子 (a note says that the details are in the annals of Emperor 大泊瀬; reading unconfirmed).

In the Kojiki, the affair of Crown Prince 軽 (軽太子) and 軽大郎女 (readings unconfirmed) is placed after the death of Emperor Ingyō and before the accession; the one exiled is the Crown Prince (to the Iyo hot springs, 伊余湯), and 軽大郎女 later follows him and the two die together by their own hand. In the Kojiki another name of 軽大郎女 is 衣通郎女 (reading unconfirmed), but in the Nihon Shoki 衣通郎姫 (reading unconfirmed) is portrayed separately, as 弟姫 (reading unconfirmed), the Empress's younger sister.

story.text: Emperor 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (雄朝津間稚子宿禰天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the full younger brother of Emperor 瑞齒別 (瑞齒別天皇; reading unconfirmed). From childhood he was compassionate and modest, but as an adult he fell seriously ill and could not move about freely. When the previous emperor died in the 1st month of the 5th year of Emperor 瑞齒別, the ministers chose this prince, the eldest and most benevolent and filial of the sons of Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed), and offered him the imperial seals. The prince declined, citing how he had secretly injured his own body trying to cure his illness and had been reproached by the former emperor as unfilial, and how he had been slighted by his two elder brothers, the emperors; and even when the ministers pleaded again and again, he would not agree. In the 12th month of the first year, his consort 忍坂大中姫命 (reading unconfirmed) came before the prince holding out water for washing his hands and waited in the cold wind for four or five 剋 without withdrawing, so that the water in the metal bowl (鋺) overflowed and froze onto her arms and she was near to freezing to death. The prince, startled, said that the ministers' plea was plainly reasonable, and at last accepted the seals of office (璽符) and ascended the throne.

In the 2nd month of the 2nd year, 忍坂大中姫 (reading unconfirmed) was made Empress, and the 刑部 (reading unconfirmed) were established. The Empress bore nine children, including 木梨輕皇子 (reading unconfirmed), Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed), 輕大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed) and Emperor 大泊瀬稚武 (大泊瀬稚武天皇; reading unconfirmed). Once, while the Empress was still living at home with her mother, the 闘鷄国造 (reading unconfirmed), passing by, spoke rudely to her from his horse and asked for an orchid; after she became Empress she sought him out, charged him with his offense, spared him the death penalty, and reduced his title to 稻置 (reading unconfirmed). In the 1st month of the 3rd year an envoy was sent to Silla to seek a good physician, and the physician who came in the 8th month cured the Emperor's illness, so the Emperor rewarded him generously and sent him home.

In the 9th month of the 4th year, the Emperor issued an edict to correct clan names and titles, saying that the cause of disorder was that high and low were contending, and that some people had lost their own titles while others falsely claimed high clans. Since people were saying, one after another, that they were descendants of emperors or descendants of those who had descended from heaven, pots for the boiling-water ordeal (探湯瓮) were set up at the 味橿 hill (reading unconfirmed) and the oath ordeal by boiling water (盟神探湯) was carried out; those who were lying grew afraid and did not come forward, and from then on clan names and titles were settled. On the night of an earthquake in the 7th month of the 5th year, it became known that 玉田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), who had been charged with the temporary enshrinement (殯) of Emperor 瑞齒別 (瑞齒別天皇; reading unconfirmed), had left the mortuary palace (殯宮) and was holding a drinking party. 玉田宿禰 killed 尾張連吾襲 (reading unconfirmed), who had come to see how things were, and fled into the grave precinct of Takeuchi-no-Sukune. When 玉田宿禰 was summoned, a court lady (采女) saw that he was wearing armor under his robe; he fled to his house, where he was surrounded and put to death. In the 11th month, Emperor 瑞齒別 was buried in the 耳原陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed).

In the 12th month of the 7th year, at a banquet for a new house, the Emperor played the koto and the Empress danced, but after the dance the Empress did not say the words required by the etiquette of the time, offering a maiden; urged by the Emperor, she said she would offer her younger sister 弟姫 (reading unconfirmed). 弟姫 was so beautiful that her beauty shone through her clothing, and she was called 衣通郎姫 (reading unconfirmed). 弟姫, who lived at 坂田 (reading unconfirmed) in Ōmi, out of consideration for the Empress's feelings did not come though summoned seven times, but when 中臣烏賦津使主 (reading unconfirmed) lay prostrate in her courtyard for seven days, enduring on nothing but the dried rice in the fold of his robe, she at last came up to the capital. Because the Empress was displeased, the Emperor built a hall at Fujiwara (藤原) and had her live there. On the night the Empress was giving birth to Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed), the Emperor went to Fujiwara; the Empress set fire to the birthing hall intending to die, and the Emperor apologized, saying it was his fault. In the 8th year, 衣通郎姫 asked to live far away to escape the Empress's resentment, and the Emperor built a palace at 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi; but in the 10th year the Empress remonstrated, citing the hardship of the people, so his visits to 茅渟 became rare, and in the 11th year the 藤原部 (reading unconfirmed) was established for 衣通郎姫.

In the 9th month of the 14th year, the Emperor hunted on Awaji Island but caught no game all day. When divination was performed, the deity of the island declared that if the pearl at the bottom of the sea of Akashi were offered to it, game would be caught. Among the fishermen, only 男狹磯 (reading unconfirmed) of 長邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Awa Province dived to the deep bottom; he came up holding a large 蝮 (a creature from the seabed) that held something shining, but died then and there. A pearl the size of a peach came out of its body, and when it was offered to the deity much game was caught; it is said that 男狹磯's grave was built with great care and still remains today. In the 3rd month of the 23rd year, 木梨輕皇子 (reading unconfirmed) was made Crown Prince. The Crown Prince had relations with his full sister 輕大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed); in the 6th month of the 24th year, when divination was performed because the soup at the Emperor's meal had frozen, it indicated disorder within the family, and the affair came to light. The Crown Prince, being heir apparent, was not punished, and 大娘皇女 was exiled to Iyo.

In the 1st month of the 42nd year, the Emperor died. The king of Silla, hearing this, sent eighty tribute ships and eighty musicians; the party wept greatly at Tsushima and Tsukushi, and from Naniwa they went to the mortuary palace in mourning clothes, playing their instruments. In the winter, in the 10th month, the Emperor was buried in the 長野原陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi. In the 11th month, the Silla mourning envoys, on their way home, called out to Mount Unebi (畝傍山) and Mount Miminashi (耳成山) with longing in their accented speech; the horse-keepers (飼部) of Yamato suspected them of having had relations with court ladies (采女) and accused them to Prince 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬皇子; reading unconfirmed), and the envoys were arrested and questioned. The suspicion was cleared, but it is said that the people of Silla deeply resented this and reduced the kinds of their tribute and the number of ships.

Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the second son of Emperor 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 忍坂大中姫命 (reading unconfirmed). After the funeral of the previous emperor, the Crown Prince 木梨輕 (木梨輕太子; reading unconfirmed) was censured by the people for his violence and his dissoluteness with women, and the ministers followed Prince 穴穗. The Crown Prince prepared troops but, isolated, fled to the house of 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed); when Prince 穴穗 surrounded the house, after 大前宿禰's mediation, the Crown Prince took his own life in that house. In the 12th month Prince 穴穗 ascended the throne and placed the capital at the 穴穗宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in 石上 (reading unconfirmed). In the 2nd month of the first year he sought 幡梭皇女 (reading unconfirmed), younger sister of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), for his younger brother Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed); but the messenger 根使主 (reading unconfirmed) kept for himself the 押木珠縵 jeweled headdress (reading unconfirmed) that 大草香皇子 had presented and slandered him, so the Emperor in anger killed 大草香皇子. 難波吉師日香蛟 (reading unconfirmed), who had served 大草香皇子, took his own life with his two sons beside their lord's body, and the Emperor took 中蒂姫 (reading unconfirmed), the wife of 大草香皇子, into the palace and made her Empress in the 2nd year. In the 8th month of the 3rd year, the Emperor was killed by 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed), the child 中蒂姫 had brought with her, and three years later he was buried in the 菅原伏見陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The words declared at the oath ordeal by boiling water: those who tell the truth will be unharmed, and those who lie will surely be injured.
Her beauty shone through her clothing, so the people of the time called her 衣通郎姫 (reading unconfirmed).
The water in the metal bowl that 大中姫 (reading unconfirmed) was holding out overflowed and froze onto her arms.
The lament of 日香蛟 (reading unconfirmed) and his sons: our lord has died though guilty of no crime; how sad!

figures.name: 雄朝津間稚子宿禰天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Full younger brother of Emperor 瑞齒別 (瑞齒別天皇; reading unconfirmed). An emperor who, after declining the throne on account of illness, ascended it and corrected clan names and titles through the oath ordeal by boiling water.

figures.name: 忍坂大中姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: She offered water in the cold to plead with the prince to ascend the throne, and became Empress in the 2nd year. Mother of 木梨輕皇子 (reading unconfirmed), Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed), Emperor 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: 衣通郎姫 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: 弟姫 (reading unconfirmed), the Empress's younger sister. She was called by this name because her beauty shone through her clothing; summoned by the Emperor, she lived at Fujiwara (藤原) and later in a palace at 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 中臣烏賦津使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An attendant (舎人) who, on the Emperor's orders, went to 弟姫 (reading unconfirmed) at 坂田 (reading unconfirmed) in Ōmi and, by lying prostrate in her courtyard for seven days, got her to come up to the capital.

figures.name: 玉田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Grandson of 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed). He neglected the temporary enshrinement of Emperor 瑞齒別 (reading unconfirmed) and killed the messenger 吾襲 (reading unconfirmed), and so was put to death.

figures.name: 男狹磯 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A fisherman of 長邑 (reading unconfirmed) in Awa Province. He brought up a pearl from the bottom of the sea of Akashi and died.

figures.name: 木梨輕皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Crown Prince of Emperor Ingyō. He had relations with his full sister, and after the Emperor's death, deserted by the ministers, took his own life in the house of 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 輕大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Full sister of 木梨輕皇子 (reading unconfirmed). When her relations with her brother came to light, she was exiled to Iyo.

figures.name: 穴穗天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of Emperor Ingyō. An emperor who ascended the throne at the 穴穗宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) in 石上 (reading unconfirmed), killed 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), and was then killed by 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of Emperor 大鷦鷯 (大鷦鷯天皇; reading unconfirmed). He agreed to give his younger sister 幡梭皇女 (reading unconfirmed) in marriage to Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed), but was killed because of the slander of 根使主 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 根使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 坂本臣 (reading unconfirmed). He kept for himself the 押木珠縵 jeweled headdress (reading unconfirmed) of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and made a false report that brought about the prince's death.

figures.name: 中蒂姫命 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Wife of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed); after the prince's death she was taken into the palace and became Empress of Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed). Mother of 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and 中蒂姫 (reading unconfirmed). Raised in the palace together with his mother, he killed Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大泊瀬皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A son of Emperor Ingyō. The prince who arrested and questioned the Silla mourning envoys, and for whom his elder brother Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed) arranged to take 幡梭皇女 (reading unconfirmed) as consort.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, beginning of the section on Emperor Ingyō (G58)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the one who cures the Emperor's illness is 金波鎭漢紀武 (reading unconfirmed), chief envoy of the tribute mission from Silla (新良国); it is not, as in the Nihon Shoki, a matter of sending an envoy to seek a physician. The story of settling clan names and titles is also given in a single sentence, saying only that they were settled by setting up 玖訶瓮 pots (reading unconfirmed) at 言八十禍津日前 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Ingyō, Crown Prince 軽 and 軽大郎女 (readings unconfirmed) (G59–G83)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, Crown Prince 軽 (軽太子; reading unconfirmed) has relations with his full sister after Emperor Ingyō's death and before his own accession; deserted by the officials, he is captured by 大前小前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and exiled to the Iyo hot springs (伊余湯). 軽大郎女 (reading unconfirmed) (also called 衣通郎女; reading unconfirmed) follows him, and the two are said to have died together by their own hand. In the Nihon Shoki the affair comes to light during the Emperor's reign, the one exiled is 輕大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed), and the Crown Prince takes his own life in the house of 大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Ankō (G84)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the prince who is killed is 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed), and the one sought as wife for Prince 大長谷 (大長谷王子; reading unconfirmed) is his younger sister 若日下王 (reading unconfirmed); the Emperor makes 長田大郎女 (reading unconfirmed), the principal wife of 大日下王, his Empress, and 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed), aged seven, overhears the Emperor's words and cuts him down while he is taking a nap. In the Nihon Shoki the wife of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed) is 中蒂姫 (reading unconfirmed); it records that 日香蛟 (reading unconfirmed) and his sons died following their lord, and leaves the details of the killing to the annals of Emperor Yūryaku (雄略紀).

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: The main text makes Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed) the second son of Emperor 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), but this "one version says" (一云) makes him the third son.

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: The main text says that the Crown Prince 木梨輕 (木梨輕太子; reading unconfirmed) took his own life in the house of 物部大前宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), but this "one version says" (一云) says that he was exiled to Iyo Province.

variants.name: One version (一云) / Another version (又云)
variants.text: Concerning the treasure presented by 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), the 押木珠縵 jeweled headdress (reading unconfirmed), these give other names for it: 立縵 and also 磐木縵 (readings unconfirmed).

yuryaku-1.title: The accession of Emperor Yūryaku and Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神) of 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed)
yuryaku-1.lead: When Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; Emperor Ankō; reading unconfirmed) was killed by 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed), Prince 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬皇子; reading unconfirmed) struck down, one after another, his elder brothers, 眉輪王, the Great Minister 圓 (圓大臣; reading unconfirmed), Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed) and others, and ascended the throne at 泊瀬朝倉 (reading unconfirmed). For the first to seventh years after the accession, the text records the installation of the Empress and consorts, the Emperor's anger at the hunting ground and the condemnation of him as "a greatly wicked emperor" (太惡天皇), the meeting with Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神) on 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed), the punishment of the Kibi clan, the story of 稚媛 (reading unconfirmed), wife of 田狹臣 (reading unconfirmed), and other matters.

points.text: In the 8th month of the 3rd year of Emperor Ankō, 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed) stabbed Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed) to death as the enemy of his father. Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed) cut down Prince 八釣白彦 (八釣白彦皇子; reading unconfirmed), burned the house of the Great Minister 圓 (圓大臣; reading unconfirmed), who was sheltering Prince 坂合黒彦 (坂合黒彦皇子; reading unconfirmed) and 眉輪王, killing all three, and in the 10th month lured Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed) on a hunt and shot him dead; then in the 11th month he ascended the throne at 泊瀬朝倉 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 2nd month of the 4th year, on 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed), the Emperor met a tall person who closely resembled him, and that person named himself "Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神)". The two hunted side by side, chasing deer, and the deity escorted the Emperor as far as 來目水 (reading unconfirmed). Seeing this, the people said, "A virtuous emperor" (有徳天皇).

The Kokugakuin University deity-name database notes that the Nihon Shoki says only that Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神) closely resembled the Emperor in face and figure, and introduces the observation that, because the Emperor refers to himself as "朕" and the deity to himself as "僕", the Emperor is placed in the higher position.

For the 2nd year, the text says that the Emperor, angered that his ministers could not answer about the task of cutting fresh meat at the hunting ground, cut down his driver, and that people condemned him as "a greatly wicked emperor" (太惡天皇).
