On the other hand, in the story of Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神) in the 4th year, the people said "a virtuous emperor" (有徳天皇), so diametrically opposed reputations stand side by side in the same book.

In the 7th year, 吉備下道臣前津屋 (reading unconfirmed), who had been dividing young girls and roosters into the Emperor's side and his own side, making them fight, and killing them when the Emperor's side won, was killed together with seventy members of his family. In the same year, 吉備上道臣田狹 (reading unconfirmed), because he had boasted of his wife 稚媛 (reading unconfirmed), was sent out as governor of Mimana (任那國司), and the Emperor took 稚媛 into the palace. 田狹's son 弟君 (reading unconfirmed) set out to attack Silla but turned back on the way and was killed by his wife 樟媛 (reading unconfirmed).

The story of the boar on 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed) is also in the Kojiki, but there it is the Emperor himself who, afraid of the boar, climbs an alder (榛). In the Nihon Shoki the one who climbs the tree is an attendant (舍人); the Emperor tramples the boar to death, and when he is about to cut down the attendant he is admonished by the Empress.

story.text: Emperor 大泊瀬幼武 (大泊瀬幼武天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the fifth son of Emperor 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (雄朝津間稚子宿禰天皇; reading unconfirmed), and it is said that when he was born a mysterious light filled the hall. In the 8th month of the 3rd year of Emperor Ankō, Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed) held a drinking party at the mountain palace and told the Empress, "I fear 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed)." The young 眉輪王, who was playing below the tower, heard this, and when the Emperor fell asleep with his head on the Empress's lap he stabbed him to death. Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed), on receiving the news, suspected his elder brothers, and cut down Prince 八釣白彦 (八釣白彦皇子; reading unconfirmed), who stayed silent and did not answer. Prince 坂合黒彦 (坂合黒彦皇子; reading unconfirmed) and 眉輪王 fled into the house of the Great Minister 圓 (圓大臣; reading unconfirmed); the minister offered his daughter 韓媛 (reading unconfirmed) and seven residences (宅七区) in 葛城 (reading unconfirmed) and asked for pardon, but the prince would not listen and burned the house, and the three were burned to death together.

In the 10th month of the same year, Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed), resenting that Emperor 穴穗 (穴穗天皇; reading unconfirmed) had once intended to pass the country on to Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed), lured him out to a hunt at 來田綿蛟屋野 (reading unconfirmed) in Ōmi. The prince falsely cried out, "There is a boar!", shot Prince 市邊押磐 dead, and also killed 佐伯部賣輪 (reading unconfirmed), the prince's retainer, who was holding the body and wailing. In this month Prince 御馬 (御馬皇子; reading unconfirmed) was also captured beside the 磐井 well (reading unconfirmed) at Miwa, and before his execution he cursed that well. In the 11th month the Emperor set up a platform at 泊瀬朝倉 (reading unconfirmed) and ascended the throne, making 平群臣眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed) Great Minister (大臣) and 大伴連室屋 (reading unconfirmed) and 物部連目 (reading unconfirmed) Ōmuraji (大連).

In the 3rd month of the first year, Princess 草香幡梭姫 (草香幡梭姫皇女; reading unconfirmed) was made Empress, and in this month three consorts were installed. 韓媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the Great Minister 葛城圓 (葛城圓大臣; reading unconfirmed), bore Prince 白髪 (白髪皇子; reading unconfirmed) and Princess 稚足姫 (稚足姫皇女; reading unconfirmed), and this princess served at the shrine of the Great Deity of Ise (伊勢大神). 稚媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the 吉備上道臣 (reading unconfirmed), bore Prince 磐城 (磐城皇子; reading unconfirmed) and Prince 星川稚宮 (星川稚宮皇子; reading unconfirmed). 童女君 (reading unconfirmed), who had been a court lady (采女), bore a girl after a single night, so the Emperor doubted her and did not raise the child; but the Ōmuraji 物部目 (物部目大連; reading unconfirmed) persuaded the Emperor by saying that the girl looked like him, and the child was made a princess and her mother a consort.

In the 7th month of the 2nd year, because 池津媛 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche, whom the Emperor intended to summon, had relations with 石河楯 (reading unconfirmed), the Emperor had the two tied to a tree and burned to death. In the 10th month, while hunting at 御馬瀬 (reading unconfirmed) in Yoshino, he was angered that his ministers could not answer about the handling of fresh meat, and cut down his driver 大津馬飼 (reading unconfirmed). The Empress Dowager and the Empress had the court lady (采女) 日媛 (reading unconfirmed) offer him sake to calm him, and because the Empress Dowager presented 膳臣長野 (reading unconfirmed) and others, the cooks' group (宍人部) was established. Because the Emperor took only his own mind as his teacher and wrongly killed many people, the people of the realm condemned him as "a greatly wicked emperor" (太惡天皇); it is said that the only ones the Emperor favored were 身狹村主青 (reading unconfirmed) and 桧隈民使博徳 (reading unconfirmed) and others of the scribes (史部).

In the 4th month of the 3rd year, 阿閇臣國見 (reading unconfirmed) slandered Princess 栲幡 (栲幡皇女; reading unconfirmed), who served the Great Deity of Ise (伊勢大神), and 廬城部連武彦 (reading unconfirmed) about their relationship. 武彦 was killed by his father, and the princess took the sacred mirror, buried it beside the Isuzu River (五十鈴河), and took her own life. When the Emperor had a search made, a rainbow like a serpent rose over the upper reaches of the river; digging there, they found the sacred mirror, and nearby they also found the princess's body. When her belly was cut open there was only water and stones, so the suspicion against 武彦 was cleared, and 國見 fled into the 石上神宮 shrine (reading unconfirmed).

In the 2nd month of the 4th year, the Emperor met Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神) on 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed) and they hunted together. In the 8th month, when he was hunting at 河上小野 (reading unconfirmed) in Yoshino, a dragonfly caught and carried off a horsefly that had bitten the Emperor's arm, so the Emperor composed a song praising it and named the place 蜻蛉野 (reading unconfirmed). In the 2nd month of the 5th year, on 葛城山, he was attacked by an enraged boar; he was about to cut down an attendant (舍人) who had escaped by climbing a tree, but thought better of it on being admonished by the Empress, and said joyfully, "Everyone hunts birds and beasts, but I return having gained good words." In the same year 加須利君 (蓋鹵王) (readings unconfirmed) of Paekche sent his younger brother 軍君 (reading unconfirmed) to Japan, and the pregnant wife who accompanied him gave birth to 嶋君 (reading unconfirmed) on the island of 各羅嶋 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi. It is said that this was 武寧王 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 6th year, the Emperor composed a song praising the small plain of 泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed), and because Sugaru (■■), who had been ordered to gather silkworms (蚕), mistakenly gathered infants (子) instead, he was given the title 少子部連 (reading unconfirmed). In the 7th month of the 7th year, the Emperor told this 少子部連 that he wished to see the form of the deity of 三諸岳 (reading unconfirmed); the great serpent he caught and brought back rumbled like thunder and its eyes blazed, so the Emperor, frightened, had it released on the mountain and gave him the name 雷 ("Thunder"). In the 8th month, the Emperor heard that 吉備下道臣前津屋 (reading unconfirmed) had been dividing young girls and roosters into "the Emperor's" and "mine", making them fight, and killing them when the Emperor's side won, so the Emperor had seventy members of his family killed. In this year, following from the Emperor's taking 稚媛 (reading unconfirmed), wife of 吉備上道臣田狹 (reading unconfirmed), into the palace, there occurred the affair in which 田狹's son 弟君 (reading unconfirmed), on the way to attack Silla, stayed in Paekche and was killed by his wife 樟媛 (reading unconfirmed); and the new craftsmen who had come from Paekche were, by command to 東漢直掬 (reading unconfirmed), moved to and settled at 上桃原, 下桃原 and 眞神原 (readings unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The words of 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed), meaning: "I never sought the imperial throne. I only avenged my father."
An entry saying that because the Emperor wrongly killed many people, the people of the world condemned him as "a very wicked emperor".
The scene on 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed) in which the Emperor first names himself, and then the tall person names himself, saying, "I am Hitokotonushi-no-Kami (一事主神)."
The words of the Emperor after accepting the Empress's admonition, meaning: "Everyone hunts birds and beasts, but I return having hunted good words."

figures.name: 大泊瀬幼武天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Fifth son of Emperor 雄朝津間稚子宿禰 (雄朝津間稚子宿禰天皇; reading unconfirmed). After his elder brother Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed) was killed, he struck down rival members of the imperial family and ascended the throne at 泊瀬朝倉 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and Princess 中蒂姫 (中蒂姫皇女; reading unconfirmed). He stabbed Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed) to death as his father's enemy, and was burned to death in the house of the Great Minister 圓 (圓大臣; reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 圓大臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The Great Minister of 葛城 (reading unconfirmed). He would not hand over Prince 坂合黒彦 (reading unconfirmed) and 眉輪王 (reading unconfirmed), who had fled to him, and offered his daughter 韓媛 (reading unconfirmed) and seven residences, but was not pardoned and was burned to death.

figures.name: 市邊押磐皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The prince to whom Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed) had intended to pass on the country. He was lured out on a hunt and shot dead by Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 八釣白彦皇子 and 坂合黒彦皇子 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder brothers of Prince 大泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed). They were suspected after the killing of Emperor 穴穗 (reading unconfirmed); Prince 白彦 was cut down and Prince 黒彦 was burned to death in the house of the Great Minister 圓 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 韓媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the Great Minister 圓 (圓大臣; reading unconfirmed). She was made a consort in the first year and bore Prince 白髪 (白髪皇子; later Emperor Seinei; reading unconfirmed) and Princess 稚足姫 (稚足姫皇女; reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 物部目大連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Made Ōmuraji (大連) at the accession. He persuaded the Emperor to recognize the girl borne by 童女君 (reading unconfirmed) as a princess.

figures.name: 栲幡皇女 (稚足姫皇女) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: A princess who served at the shrine of the Great Deity of Ise (伊勢大神). Slandered, she buried the sacred mirror beside the Isuzu River (五十鈴河) and took her own life.

figures.name: 吉備上道臣田狹 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Because he boasted of the beauty of his wife 稚媛 (reading unconfirmed), he was sent out as governor of Mimana (任那國司) and his wife was taken by the Emperor. After that he sought to rely on Silla.

figures.name: 樟媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Wife of 弟君 (reading unconfirmed), son of 田狹 (reading unconfirmed). Hating that her husband stayed in Paekche intending to rebel, she killed him.

figures.name: 軍君 (崑攴君) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Younger brother of 加須利君 (蓋鹵王) (readings unconfirmed) of Paekche. He was sent to Japan to serve the Emperor.

figures.name: 嶋君 (武寧王) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: The child born on the island of 各羅嶋 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi to the pregnant wife of 加須利君 (reading unconfirmed), who had accompanied 軍君 (reading unconfirmed). He was sent back to Paekche.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Ankō (the incident of 目弱王 (reading unconfirmed) and the revenge of 大長谷王 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: In the Kojiki, 目弱王 (眉輪王) (readings unconfirmed) is seven years old and cuts off the Emperor's head with the long sword beside him; 大長谷王 (reading unconfirmed) cuts down his elder brother 黑日子王 (reading unconfirmed) and buries 白日子王 (reading unconfirmed) alive at 小治田 (reading unconfirmed). In the Nihon Shoki it is Prince 八釣白彦 (八釣白彦皇子; reading unconfirmed) who is cut down, and Prince 坂合黒彦 (坂合黒彦皇子; reading unconfirmed) is burned to death together with 眉輪王 and the Great Minister 圓 (圓大臣; reading unconfirmed). Also, in the Kojiki 都夫良意美 (reading unconfirmed) stabs 目弱王 and then kills himself.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Yūryaku (Hitokotonushi-no-Ōkami (一言主大神) of 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the retinue of Hitokotonushi-no-Ōkami (一言主大神) appears dressed exactly like the Emperor's procession, and there is a scene in which each side fits arrows to their bows and asks the other's name; the Emperor, afraid, presents long swords, bows and arrows, and the clothing of all his officials. In the Nihon Shoki the Emperor and the deity speak with restraint and hunt side by side, and there is no story of offerings. As for where the deity escorts the Emperor, the Kojiki says the mountain entrance of 長谷 (reading unconfirmed), and the Nihon Shoki says 來目水 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Yūryaku (the great boar of 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the Emperor himself, chased by a boar on 葛城山 (reading unconfirmed), is frightened, climbs an alder (榛) and composes a song. In the Nihon Shoki the one who climbs the tree is an attendant (舍人); the Emperor tramples the boar to death, and the one who composes a song is the attendant who is about to be executed.

variants.name: Another text says (別本云)
variants.text: It gives the name of the wife of 田狹臣 (reading unconfirmed) as 毛媛 (reading unconfirmed), and makes her the daughter of 玉田宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), son of 葛城襲津彦 (reading unconfirmed). It says that the Emperor, hearing of her beauty, killed her husband and took her for himself. In the main text, 田狹 is kept away by being appointed governor of Mimana (任那國司).

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: It says that 吉備臣弟君 (reading unconfirmed) came back from Paekche and presented the 漢手人部, 衣縫部 and 宍人部 groups (readings unconfirmed). In the main text, 弟君 stays in Paekche and is killed by his wife 樟媛 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Some say (或云)
variants.text: Concerning the deity of 三諸岳 (reading unconfirmed), it gives one view that it is 大物代主神 (reading unconfirmed) and another that it is the 墨坂神 (reading unconfirmed) of 菟田 (reading unconfirmed). The main text does not give the deity's name.

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: It gives 吉備下道臣前津屋 (reading unconfirmed), who was killed by the Emperor, as "國造吉備臣山" (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: The New Selection of Paekche (百濟新撰) says
variants.text: It says that in the year 己巳 蓋鹵王 (reading unconfirmed) became king, and that because the Emperor sent 阿禮奴跪 (reading unconfirmed) to ask for a woman, Paekche adorned 適稽女郎 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 慕尼夫人 (reading unconfirmed), and presented her as tribute. She is the 池津媛 (reading unconfirmed) of the main text, and the note to the entry for the 4th month of the 5th year also identifies 池津媛 with 適稽女郎.

yuryaku-2.title: Emperor Yūryaku's expeditions to Silla, the craftsmen of Wu, and his testamentary edict
yuryaku-2.lead: For the 8th to the 23rd years of Emperor Yūryaku, the text records year by year the fighting with Koguryŏ (高麗) over Silla, the expedition to Silla by 紀小弓宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and others, the settling of the craftsmen who came from Wu (呉), the crime of 根使主 (reading unconfirmed) concerning the jeweled headdress, the establishment of groups (部) for the 秦, 漢 and 土師 clans (readings unconfirmed), and other matters. In his last years the Emperor was involved in the fall and restoration of Paekche, and in the 8th month of the 23rd year he died, leaving a testamentary edict warning against Prince 星川 (星川王; reading unconfirmed).

points.text: In the 8th year, Silla, attacked by Koguryŏ (高麗), asked for help through the king of Mimana, and 膳臣斑鳩, 吉備臣小梨 and 難波吉士赤目子 (readings unconfirmed) defeated the Koguryŏ army with a stratagem of tunnels and ambushes. In the 9th year the Emperor intended to attack Silla himself, but was warned by a deity, "Do not go", and sent 紀小弓宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and others as commanders. 小弓 died of illness, and the remaining commanders quarreled among themselves and turned back without reaching the royal palace of Paekche.

In the 14th year, 身狹村主青 (reading unconfirmed) and others arrived at the port of Sumiyoshi (住吉津) together with envoys from Wu (呉), bringing craftswomen including the weavers 漢織 and 呉織 and the seamstresses 兄媛 and 弟媛 (readings unconfirmed). The road for the guests from Wu was named 呉坂 (reading unconfirmed), and 桧隈野 (reading unconfirmed), where the people of Wu were settled, was named 呉原 (reading unconfirmed); 漢織, 呉織 and the seamstresses are regarded as the ancestors of the Asuka seamstress group (飛鳥衣縫部) and the Ise seamstresses (伊勢衣縫).

In the 4th month of the 14th year, at a banquet to entertain the people of Wu, the Empress saw the jeweled headdress (玉縵) worn by 根使主 (reading unconfirmed), recognized it as the item her elder brother 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed) had presented on the occasion of her marriage, and wept. 根使主 admitted his crime and fled to 日根 (reading unconfirmed), where he built a rice-bale fortification (稲城) and fought, but was killed; his descendants were divided between the people of the 大草香部 (reading unconfirmed) and the bag carriers (負嚢者).

The text says that in the winter of the 20th year Koguryŏ (高麗) attacked and destroyed Paekche, but that the king of Koguryŏ stopped the attack on the survivors, saying, "Paekche is an official domain (官家) of Japan." In the 21st year the Emperor gave 久麻那利 (reading unconfirmed) to King ■洲 (■洲王; one character is missing in the original; reading unconfirmed) to restore the country, and in the 23rd year he had 末多王 (reading unconfirmed) escorted by five hundred soldiers of Tsukushi and installed as king, as King 東城 (東城王; reading unconfirmed).

In the 8th month of the 23rd year, the Emperor died in the great hall, leaving a testamentary edict to the Ōmuraji 大伴室屋 (大伴室屋大連; reading unconfirmed) and to 東漢掬直 (reading unconfirmed). In it, after describing how he had striven to give the people peace, he ordered them to beware of the wicked heart of Prince 星川 (星川王; reading unconfirmed) and to govern the realm together with the Crown Prince (Prince 白髪, 白髪皇子; reading unconfirmed).

For the 7th month of the 22nd year, it is briefly recorded that a great turtle caught while fishing by 水江浦嶋子 (reading unconfirmed) of 餘社郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tanba Province turned into a woman, and that the two entered the sea and reached Mount Hōrai (蓬莱山). The detailed story is not given in the main text, which says that it is in a "separate scroll" (別卷).

story.text: In the 2nd month of the 8th year, 身狹村主青 (reading unconfirmed) and 桧隈民使博徳 (reading unconfirmed) were sent to Wu (呉). Silla had not paid tribute for eight years since the Emperor's accession and had allied itself with Koguryŏ (高麗), but when it learned Koguryŏ's true intentions from the words of a Koguryŏ soldier, it killed the Koguryŏ people within its borders. When Koguryŏ, enraged, invaded Silla, the king of Silla asked the generals of the Japanese headquarters (日本府) for help through the king of Mimana. 膳臣斑鳩 (reading unconfirmed) and the others faced the Koguryŏ army for more than ten days, then at night dug tunnels and placed troops in ambush, caught the pursuing Koguryŏ army between them, and defeated it soundly.

In the 2nd month of the 9th year, because 凡河内直香賜 (reading unconfirmed), who had been sent to worship 胸方神 (reading unconfirmed), violated a court lady (采女), the Emperor sent men to cut him down at 藍原 (reading unconfirmed) in 三嶋郡 (reading unconfirmed). In the 3rd month the Emperor intended to attack Silla himself, but gave this up when warned by a deity, and sent 紀小弓宿禰, 蘇我韓子宿禰, 大伴談連 and 小鹿火宿禰 (readings unconfirmed) as commanders. 紀小弓宿禰 subdued the land of 喙 (reading unconfirmed) in Silla, but 大伴談連 and others were killed in battle, and 小弓宿禰 also died of illness. In the 5th month, when 小弓's son 大磐宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) came and took command, quarrels arose among the commanders; 韓子宿禰 was shot from his horse by 大磐宿禰 and died, and the army turned back without reaching the royal palace of Paekche. 小弓宿禰 was buried at the village of 田身輪 (reading unconfirmed), and 小鹿火宿禰 stayed in the land of 角國 (reading unconfirmed) and became the ancestor of the 角臣 (reading unconfirmed). For the 7th month the text records a story in which 田邊史伯孫 (reading unconfirmed) exchanged his own horse for a swift red horse beside the tomb of Homuta (譽田陵), and the next morning that horse had turned into a clay horse.

In the 9th month of the 10th year, a goose presented from Wu (呉) was bitten to death in Tsukushi by a dog belonging to 水間君 (reading unconfirmed), and 水間君 atoned for the offense by presenting swans and bird keepers. In the 10th month of the 11th year, when a bird of the Bird Office (鳥官) was bitten to death by the dog of a man of 菟田 (reading unconfirmed), the Emperor had the man's face tattooed and made him one of the bird keepers' group (鳥養部). Conscript laborers (直丁) from Shinano Province and Musashi Province who said to one another that this was "the deed of an unreasonable, wicked master" were ordered to gather birds and pile them up; they could not do so, and they too were made bird keepers. In the 10th month of the 12th year, the carpenter 鷄御田 (reading unconfirmed), who had built a tower, was suspected of having violated a court lady, but the Emperor came to understand through the koto and song of 秦酒公 (reading unconfirmed), and pardoned him. In the 13th year, the Emperor made 齒田根命 (reading unconfirmed), who had violated a court lady, pay for his offense; had 文石小麻呂 (reading unconfirmed) of Harima attacked; and was about to execute the carpenter 猪名部眞根 (reading unconfirmed), but on hearing his companions' song he regretted it and sent a messenger galloping on a black horse of Kai to stop the execution.

In the 1st month of the 14th year, 身狹村主青 (reading unconfirmed) and others arrived at the port of Sumiyoshi (住吉津) together with envoys from Wu (呉), bringing the weavers 漢織 and 呉織 and the seamstresses 兄媛 and 弟媛 (readings unconfirmed), presented by Wu. In the 3rd month, the people of Wu were settled at 桧隈野 (reading unconfirmed), and that place was named 呉原 (reading unconfirmed); 兄媛 was offered to the Great Deity of Miwa (大三輪神), and 弟媛 was made part of the 漢衣縫部 (reading unconfirmed). In the 4th month, at a banquet to entertain the people of Wu, it was found that the jeweled headdress (玉縵) of 根使主 (reading unconfirmed) had belonged to the Empress's elder brother 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), and 根使主 was killed by government troops at 日根 (reading unconfirmed). Later his son 小根使主 (reading unconfirmed) was also killed, because he had said that his father's fortification was stronger than the Emperor's, and the descendants of 根使主 became the 坂本臣 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 15th year, the people of 秦 (reading unconfirmed), who had been dispersed and used by various ministers and chiefs, were gathered and given to 秦酒公 (reading unconfirmed); 酒公 piled up a great quantity of silk at court as tribute and was granted the title 禹豆麻佐 (reading unconfirmed). In the 16th year, the provinces and districts suited to mulberry were made to plant mulberry, and the 漢部 (reading unconfirmed) were gathered and their chief (伴造) was given the title 直 (reading unconfirmed). In the 17th year, 吾笥 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 土師連 (reading unconfirmed), put forward people who made vessels, and they became the 贄土師部 (reading unconfirmed). In the 18th year, 朝日郎 (reading unconfirmed) of Ise held off the government troops with a powerful bow, but 物部目連 (reading unconfirmed) and 筑紫聞物部大斧手 (reading unconfirmed) killed him, and the 猪名部 (reading unconfirmed) of 物部菟代宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), who had refused to advance, were given to 目連. In the 3rd month of the 19th year, the 穴穗部 (reading unconfirmed) was established.

In the winter of the 20th year, Koguryŏ (高麗) attacked and destroyed Paekche, and the few remaining people gathered at 倉下 (reading unconfirmed). The Koguryŏ generals urged that the rest be destroyed as well, but the king of Koguryŏ stopped them, on the grounds that Paekche was an official domain (官家) of Japan. In the 3rd month of the 21st year, the Emperor gave 久麻那利 (reading unconfirmed) to King ■洲 (■洲王; reading unconfirmed) and had him restore Paekche. In the 1st month of the 22nd year, Prince 白髪 (白髪皇子; reading unconfirmed) was made Crown Prince, and for the 7th month the story of 水江浦嶋子 (reading unconfirmed) reaching Mount Hōrai (蓬莱山) is recorded.

In the 4th month of the 23rd year, when King 文斤 (文斤王; reading unconfirmed) of Paekche died, the Emperor invited 末多王 (reading unconfirmed), the second of the five sons of 昆攴王 (reading unconfirmed), to the palace, encouraged him, and had five hundred soldiers of Tsukushi escort him to become king. This was King 東城 (東城王; reading unconfirmed). In the 7th month the Emperor fell ill and entrusted the affairs of government to the Crown Prince, and in the 8th month he died in the great hall. In his testamentary edict he ordered the Ōmuraji 大伴室屋 (大伴室屋大連; reading unconfirmed) and others to beware of Prince 星川 (星川王; reading unconfirmed), who had a wicked heart, and to govern the realm together with the Crown Prince. At this time five hundred Emishi, led by 吉備臣尾代 (reading unconfirmed), a general for the expedition against Silla, heard of the Emperor's death and attacked the surrounding districts; 尾代 fought them at the harbor of 娑婆水門 (reading unconfirmed), pursued them as far as the harbor of 浦掛水門 (reading unconfirmed) in Tanba Province, and killed them all.

quotes.note: Written as the words of the king of Koguryŏ (高麗), meaning: "Paekche is an official domain of Japan, and its origins go back a long way."
An entry saying that the weaving and sewing craftswomen who came from Wu (呉) are the ancestors of the Asuka seamstress group (飛鳥衣縫部) and the Ise seamstresses (伊勢衣縫).
Meaning that 浦嶋子 (reading unconfirmed) entered the sea with the woman and met the immortals on Mount Hōrai (蓬莱山), and that the details are in a separate scroll.
A passage of the testamentary edict, meaning: "Now Prince 星川 (星川王; reading unconfirmed) harbors a perverse and wicked heart, and lacks conduct that values the bond between brothers."

figures.name: 身狹村主青 and 桧隈民使博徳 (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Members of the scribes (史部) favored by the Emperor. They were repeatedly sent to Wu (呉), and in the 14th year brought back craftswomen from Wu.

figures.name: 膳臣斑鳩 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In the 8th year, at the urging of the king of Mimana, he went to the aid of Silla and defeated the Koguryŏ army with a stratagem of tunnels and ambushes. A reading note says "斑鳩。此云伊柯屡餓".

figures.name: 紀小弓宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In the 9th year he was sent as commander of the expedition against Silla and subdued the land of 喙 (reading unconfirmed), but died of illness in camp. He was buried at the village of 田身輪 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大伴談連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sent to Silla together with 紀小弓宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), he was killed in battle. A reading note says "談。此云箇陀利".

figures.name: 紀大磐宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 小弓宿禰 (reading unconfirmed). After his father's death he went to Silla and took command, quarreled with 蘇我韓子宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), and shot him dead.

figures.name: 根使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In the 14th year it came to light that he had kept for himself the jeweled headdress of 大草香皇子 (reading unconfirmed), and he was killed by government troops at 日根 (reading unconfirmed). His descendants became the 坂本臣 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 秦酒公 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: With koto and song he brought the Emperor to understanding and saved a carpenter; in the 15th year he led the gathered people of 秦 (reading unconfirmed), presented silk, and was granted the title 禹豆麻佐 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 物部目連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In the 18th year he killed 朝日郎 (reading unconfirmed) of Ise and was given the 猪名部 (reading unconfirmed) of 菟代宿禰 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 末多王 (東城王) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Second son of 昆攴王 (reading unconfirmed). In the 23rd year he was escorted back to Paekche by five hundred soldiers of Tsukushi and became king.

figures.name: 星川王 (星川稚宮皇子) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 稚媛 (reading unconfirmed). In the Emperor's testamentary edict he was named as one to be guarded against for his wicked heart.

figures.name: 水江浦嶋子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man of 管川 (reading unconfirmed) in 餘社郡 (reading unconfirmed), Tanba Province. A great turtle he caught turned into a woman, and they entered the sea together and reached Mount Hōrai (蓬莱山).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Yūryaku (consorts, name-bearing groups (御名代) and the people of Wu (呉))
compare.text: At the beginning of the section on Emperor Yūryaku, the Kojiki records only in a single line that because people of Wu (呉人) came across, they were settled at 呉原 (reading unconfirmed) and the place was named 呉原. The Nihon Shoki gives details such as the names of the envoys, the craftswomen 漢織 and 呉織 and the seamstresses 兄媛 and 弟媛 (readings unconfirmed), the origin of the name 呉坂 (reading unconfirmed), and the offering of 兄媛 to the Great Deity of Miwa (大三輪神).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Ankō (the jeweled headdress of 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the story of 根臣 (reading unconfirmed) stealing the 押木 jeweled headdress (押木玉縵; reading unconfirmed) presented by 大日下王 (reading unconfirmed) and slandering the prince is told in the section on Emperor Ankō, but no story could be confirmed in the section on Emperor Yūryaku in which the crime later comes to light. In the Nihon Shoki, the crime of 根使主 (reading unconfirmed) comes to light in the 14th year when the Empress recognizes the headdress.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, end of the section on Emperor Yūryaku (age at death and tomb)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives the Emperor's age as 124 and his tomb as 高鸇 (reading unconfirmed) at 多治比 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi, but has no entry for a testamentary edict. The Nihon Shoki records his death in the 8th month of the 23rd year and a long testamentary edict, and in this book does not give his age.

variants.name: The Paekche Record (百濟記) says
variants.text: It says that in the winter of the year 乙卯 of 蓋鹵王 (reading unconfirmed), a great army of 狛 (Koguryŏ, 高麗) came and attacked the great fortress for seven days and seven nights; the royal fortress fell, the land of 尉禮國 (reading unconfirmed) was lost, and the king, the queen dowager, the princes and others all died at the hands of the enemy. The main text centers on the story of the king of Koguryŏ stopping the destruction of the survivors.

variants.name: The Old Records of Japan (日本舊記) says
variants.text: It makes 末多王 (reading unconfirmed) the one who was given 久麻那利 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki's note says that this is probably a mistake, and records that King ■洲 (■洲王; reading unconfirmed) of the main text was the younger brother by the same mother of 蓋鹵王 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: As another form of the testamentary edict, it says that Prince 星川 (星川王; reading unconfirmed) is known throughout the realm to be ill-natured and rough of heart, and will surely harm the Crown Prince after the Emperor's death, so those who hold many people's groups (民部) should join forces and help the Crown Prince.

variants.name: Another text says (別本云)
variants.text: It says that the dog that bit the goose from Wu (呉) to death was not the dog of 水間君 (reading unconfirmed) but that of 筑紫嶺縣主泥麻呂 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: It says that 吉備臣尾代 (reading unconfirmed), after pursuing as far as 浦掛 (reading unconfirmed), sent men to kill all the Emishi. In the main text, 尾代 himself pursues them to the harbor of 浦掛水門 (reading unconfirmed) and kills them.

seinei-kenzo.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 15 — Emperor Seinei, Emperor Kenzō and Emperor Ninken
seinei-kenzo.title: Emperors Seinei, Kenzō and Ninken, and the brothers 億計 and 弘計 (readings unconfirmed)
seinei-kenzo.lead: In the time of the childless Emperor 白髪 (白髪天皇; Emperor Seinei; reading unconfirmed), Prince 億計 (億計王) and Prince 弘計 (弘計王) (readings unconfirmed), sons of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed), who had been hiding in Harima, were discovered and welcomed to the palace. The text records that the brothers yielded the throne to each other; the younger, Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; Emperor Kenzō), ascended first and buried his father's remains, and after him the elder, Emperor 億計 (億計天皇; Emperor Ninken), ascended the throne and the country was governed in peace.

points.text: In the 11th month of the 2nd year of Emperor Seinei, 來目部小楯 (reading unconfirmed), governor of Harima (播磨國司), discovered the brothers 億計 and 弘計 (readings unconfirmed), sons of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed), at a banquet for the new house of the head of the 縮見 granary (縮見屯倉首; reading unconfirmed) in 赤石郡 (reading unconfirmed). Emperor 白髪 (白髪天皇; reading unconfirmed), who had no children, rejoiced at this, and in the 3rd year welcomed the two to the palace, making Prince 億計 Crown Prince and Prince 弘計 an imperial prince.

At the banquet for the new house, the younger brother, Prince 弘計 (弘計王; reading unconfirmed), after reciting the words and song of house-blessing (室壽), declared that he was a descendant of 押磐尊 (reading unconfirmed), who had ruled the realm from the 市邊宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). 小楯 (reading unconfirmed), astonished, left his seat and bowed twice, gathered the people of the district and built a temporary palace.

When Emperor 白髪 (白髪天皇; reading unconfirmed) died, the brothers yielded the throne to each other, and meanwhile their elder sister, Princess 飯豐青 (飯豐青皇女; reading unconfirmed), conducted the government at the 忍海角刺宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) and was called 忍海飯豐青尊 (reading unconfirmed). The elder brother, Prince 億計 (億計王; reading unconfirmed), yielded, saying that it was his younger brother's achievement that they had declared themselves and been brought out into the world, and Prince 弘計 (弘計王; reading unconfirmed) ascended the throne.

In the first year of Emperor Kenzō, guided by 置目 (reading unconfirmed), an old woman of Ōmi, the Emperor dug up the remains of his father, Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed), which had been buried at 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed). Because they were mixed with the bones of the retainer 佐伯部仲子 (reading unconfirmed), the skulls were told apart by a feature of 仲子, who was said to have lost an upper tooth, and two tombs of the same form were built for the burials. In the 2nd year the Emperor intended to destroy the tomb of Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed), but gave up the idea on the admonition of his elder brother 億計 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 3rd year of Emperor Kenzō, the Moon Deity (月神) and the Sun Deity (日神) each possessed a person and spoke to 阿閇臣事代 (reading unconfirmed), who had been sent to Mimana, asking that rice fields be offered to their ancestor Takamimusubi-no-Kami (高皇産靈). The Kokugakuin University deity-name database explains that in this entry, where Takamimusubi-no-Kami is presented as the ancestor of the Moon Deity and Sun Deity who has "the merit of having forged heaven and earth", a character of a creator deity accompanied by the imagery of smithing can be seen.

Emperor 億計 (億計天皇; Emperor Ninken; reading unconfirmed) ascended the throne at the 石上廣高宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), and the Empress, Princess 春日大娘 (春日大娘皇女; reading unconfirmed), bore Princess 手白香 (手白香皇女; reading unconfirmed), 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) (later Emperor Buretsu), and others. The text records that in the 8th year there were no incidents in the country, the officials fulfilled their duties, and the people were content in their work.

story.text: Emperor 白髪武廣國押稚日本根子 (白髪武廣國押稚日本根子天皇; reading unconfirmed) was the third son of Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed), and had white hair from birth. When his father died in the 8th month of the 23rd year of Emperor Yūryaku, 吉備稚媛 (reading unconfirmed) had her young son, Prince 星川 (星川皇子; reading unconfirmed), seize the office of the Great Treasury (大藏), and Prince 星川 shut the gates of the Great Treasury and used the government's goods as he pleased. The Ōmuraji 大伴室屋 (大伴室屋大連; reading unconfirmed), following the testamentary edict, surrounded the Great Treasury with troops and set fire to it, and Prince 星川, 稚媛, 兄君 (reading unconfirmed), elder half-brother of Prince 磐城 (磐城皇子; reading unconfirmed) by a different father, and others were burned to death. The 吉備上道臣 (reading unconfirmed) and others, who had come with forty ships to save Prince 星川, turned back, but the Emperor reproached them and took away their 山部 (reading unconfirmed). In the 10th month, the Ōmuraji 大伴室屋 and others presented the imperial seals to the Crown Prince.

In the 1st month of the first year, the Emperor ascended the throne at 磐余甕栗 (reading unconfirmed) and made his mother, 葛城韓媛 (reading unconfirmed), Imperial Lady Dowager (皇太夫人). In the 10th month, when Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed) was buried in the 丹比高鷲原陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed), the Hayato wept day and night beside the tomb and died on the seventh day. In the 2nd month of the 2nd year, the Emperor, grieving that he had no children, established attendants, stewards and quiver-bearers (舎人, 膳夫, 靭負) of the 白髪部 (reading unconfirmed). In the 11th month, when 來目部小楯 (reading unconfirmed), governor of Harima (播磨國司), discovered the brothers 億計 and 弘計 (readings unconfirmed) in 赤石郡 (reading unconfirmed) and reported it, the Emperor rejoiced that heaven had granted him two sons; in the 1st month of the 3rd year he welcomed the two to the palace, and in the 4th month made Prince 億計 Crown Prince and Prince 弘計 an imperial prince. By the 4th year the Emperor had received envoys of the foreign lands (諸蕃) as well as the Emishi and the Hayato; in the 1st month of the 5th year he died in the palace and was buried in the 河内坂門原陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed).

The pre-accession annals of Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; reading unconfirmed) go back to recount the circumstances of the brothers. When their father, Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed), was shot dead by Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed) in the 10th month of the 3rd year of Emperor Ankō, his retainer 日下部連使主 (reading unconfirmed) and his son 吾田彦 (reading unconfirmed) fled with the brothers to 余社郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tanba Province. 使主 (Omi), still fearing that he would be killed, entered a stone chamber on 縮見山 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima and took his own life. Without knowing what had become of him, the brothers moved to 赤石郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima Province, changed their names to 丹波小子 (reading unconfirmed), served the head of the 縮見 granary (縮見屯倉首; reading unconfirmed), and lived by tending cattle and horses. In the 11th month of the 2nd year of Emperor 白髪 (白髪天皇; reading unconfirmed), at the banquet for the new house, the brothers yielded the turn to dance to each other, and Prince 弘計 (弘計王), after reciting the words and song of house-blessing (室壽), declared that he was a descendant of 押磐尊 (reading unconfirmed); 小楯 (reading unconfirmed), astonished, bowed twice and reported this to the capital.

After the death of Emperor 白髪 (白髪天皇; reading unconfirmed), the elder brother, Prince 億計 (億計王; reading unconfirmed), and the younger, Prince 弘計 (弘計王; reading unconfirmed), each yielded the throne to the other, and for a long time nothing was decided. Meanwhile their elder sister, Princess 飯豐青 (飯豐青皇女; reading unconfirmed), conducted the government at the 忍海角刺宮 palace (reading unconfirmed), but she died in the 11th month. In the 12th month, Prince 億計 placed the imperial seals on his younger brother's seat and yielded, stating that their declaring themselves and being welcomed was an achievement owed to his younger brother's plan. Prince 弘計 firmly declined, saying that the elder brother should be set up, but on learning that his brother's will would not change he accepted, though he did not ascend the throne at once. In the 1st month of the first year, on the petition of the Great Ministers (大臣), the Ōmuraji (大連) and others, Emperor 弘計 ascended the throne at the 近飛鳥八釣宮 palace (reading unconfirmed) and made 難波小野王 (reading unconfirmed) Empress.

In the 2nd month of the first year, the Emperor searched for his father's remains and, guided by 置目 (reading unconfirmed), an old woman of Ōmi, dug up the place at 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed) where they had been buried. His father's bones were mixed with those of 佐伯部仲子 (reading unconfirmed), but because the wet nurse of Prince 磐坂 (磐坂皇子; reading unconfirmed) said that 仲子 had lost an upper tooth, the skulls were told apart, and two tombs of the same form were built for the burials. The Emperor had 置目 live near the palace and attached a bell to a rope as a signal for her comings and goings. In the 4th month he praised the merit of 小楯 (reading unconfirmed), who had discovered the two, made him head of the Mountain Office (山官), and gave him the title 山部連 (reading unconfirmed); in the 5th month he spared 狹狹城山君韓■宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), who had taken part in the killing of his father, from the death penalty and made him a tomb keeper.

In the 8th month of the 2nd year, the Emperor told the Crown Prince 億計 (reading unconfirmed) that, as revenge for his father, he wished to destroy the tomb of Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed) and scatter his bones. 億計 admonished him, giving two reasons: that Emperor 大泊瀬 was an emperor who had ruled the realm, and that he was the father of Emperor 白髪 (白髪天皇; reading unconfirmed), who had treated them generously. The Emperor accepted this and had the work stopped. In the 9th month 置目 (reading unconfirmed), grown old, returned to her home, and for the 10th month it is recorded that the realm was at peace and one 斛 of rice cost one silver coin (銀銭一文). In the 2nd and 4th months of the 3rd year, the Moon Deity (月神) and the Sun Deity (日神) possessed people and asked for rice fields, and people of Iki and of Tsushima, respectively, served at their shrines. In the 4th month the Emperor died at the 八釣宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). In this year 紀生磐宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) styled himself a divine sage (神聖) in Mimana and fought Paekche, but his strength gave out and he returned home.

Emperor 億計 (億計天皇; reading unconfirmed) (personal name 大脚, courtesy name 嶋郎; readings unconfirmed) was the full elder brother of Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; reading unconfirmed), and after his younger brother's death he ascended the throne at the 石上廣高宮 palace (reading unconfirmed). In the 2nd month he made Princess 春日大娘 (春日大娘皇女; reading unconfirmed) Empress, and she bore one son and six daughters. In the 10th month he buried Emperor 弘計 in the 傍丘磐杯丘陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed). In the 2nd year, Empress 難波小野 (難波小野皇后; reading unconfirmed), fearing because she had once behaved disrespectfully toward the Crown Prince 億計 at a banquet, took her own life. In the 5th year the scattered 佐伯部 (reading unconfirmed) were gathered, and the descendants of 仲子 (reading unconfirmed) were made the 佐伯造 (reading unconfirmed). In the 6th year 日鷹吉士 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Koguryŏ (高麗) to seek craftsmen, and 飽田女 (reading unconfirmed), wife of 麁寸 (reading unconfirmed), who went along with him, lamented at the 御津 harbor (reading unconfirmed) of Naniwa; her complicated family relationships are explained in a note. In that year 日鷹吉士 returned with the craftsmen 須流枳 and 奴流枳 (readings unconfirmed) and others. In the 7th year 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) was made Crown Prince, and for the 8th year it is recorded that the whole country was at peace and the five grains ripened. In the 8th month of the 11th year the Emperor died in the main bedchamber, and in the 10th month he was buried in the 埴生坂本陵 tomb (reading unconfirmed).

quotes.note: The words with which Prince 弘計 (弘計王; reading unconfirmed) declared himself at the banquet for the new house, meaning: "I am a descendant of 押磐尊 (reading unconfirmed), who ruled the realm from the 市邊宮 palace (reading unconfirmed)."
The words of the wet nurse of Prince 磐坂 (磐坂皇子; reading unconfirmed), meaning: "仲子 (reading unconfirmed) had lost an upper tooth, so he can be told apart by that."
The entry for the 10th month of the 2nd year of Emperor Kenzō, meaning that one 斛 of rice cost one silver coin and that the land was so prosperous that cattle and horses covered the fields.
The words of the Moon Deity, who had possessed a person, meaning: "My ancestor Takamimusubi-no-Kami (高皇産靈) has the merit of having forged heaven and earth."

figures.name: 白髪武廣國押稚日本根子天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Third son of Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed), an emperor who had white hair from birth. Having no children, he welcomed the brothers 億計 and 弘計 (readings unconfirmed) to the palace.

figures.name: 星川皇子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 吉備稚媛 (reading unconfirmed). After his father's death he seized the office of the Great Treasury at his mother's urging, but was burned to death by the troops of the Ōmuraji 大伴室屋 (大伴室屋大連; reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 來目部小楯 (磐楯) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Governor of Harima (播磨國司). He discovered the brothers 億計 and 弘計 (readings unconfirmed) in 赤石郡 (reading unconfirmed), and was later made head of the Mountain Office (山官) and granted the title 山部連 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 弘計王 (弘計天皇) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed) and younger brother of Prince 億計 (億計王; reading unconfirmed). He declared himself at the banquet for the new house and, with the throne yielded to him by his elder brother, ascended it first.

figures.name: 億計王 (億計天皇) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed). He yielded the throne to his younger brother and became Crown Prince, and after his brother's death ascended the throne at the 石上廣高宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 飯豐青皇女 (忍海飯豐青尊) (readings unconfirmed)
figures.role: Elder sister of Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; reading unconfirmed). While the brothers were yielding the throne to each other, she conducted the government at the 忍海角刺宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Omi (使主) (日下部連使主; reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Retainer of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed). He fled with the brothers to 余社郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tanba Province, and later took his own life in a stone chamber on 縮見山 (reading unconfirmed) in Harima. A reading note says "使主。此云於瀰".

figures.name: 置目 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An old woman, younger sister of 倭宿禰 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 狹狹城山君 (reading unconfirmed) of Ōmi Province. She revealed where the remains of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed) had been buried.

figures.name: 阿閇臣事代 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: In the 3rd year of Emperor Kenzō, when sent to Mimana, he received the words of the Moon Deity and the Sun Deity and reported them to the throne.

figures.name: 紀生磐宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Based in Mimana, he communicated with Koguryŏ (高麗), styled himself a divine sage (神聖) and fought Paekche, but was defeated and returned home.

figures.name: 春日大娘皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of Emperor 大泊瀬 (大泊瀬天皇; reading unconfirmed) and 童女君 (reading unconfirmed). She became Empress of Emperor 億計 (億計天皇; reading unconfirmed) and bore Princess 手白香 (手白香皇女; reading unconfirmed), 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Seinei (the discovery of the two princes)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the two princes are discovered after Emperor Seinei has died and there is no successor; 小楯 (reading unconfirmed), on hearing their declaration, tumbles off his seat, and 飯豐王 (reading unconfirmed), who is given as the younger sister of 市邊忍齒別王 (reading unconfirmed), rejoices and has the two come up to the palace. In the Nihon Shoki they are discovered during Emperor Seinei's reign, the Emperor himself joyfully welcomes them, and Prince 億計 (億計王; reading unconfirmed) is made Crown Prince. The Nihon Shoki also makes Princess 飯豐青 (飯豐青皇女; reading unconfirmed) the elder sister of Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Kenzō (the old woman 置目 (置目老媼; reading unconfirmed) and the remains of the prince's father)
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the old woman 置目 (置目老媼; reading unconfirmed) comes forward and says that the bones of 市邊王 (reading unconfirmed) can be identified by the teeth, and the tomb is built on the mountain east of 蚊屋野 (reading unconfirmed). In the Nihon Shoki, the clue for telling them apart is the missing upper tooth of 佐伯部仲子 (reading unconfirmed), the one who points this out is the wet nurse of Prince 磐坂 (磐坂皇子; reading unconfirmed), and two tombs are built.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3, section on Emperor Kenzō (the tomb of Emperor 大長谷 (大長谷天皇; reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: In the Kojiki, the elder brother 意祁命 (reading unconfirmed) goes himself and digs only a little at the side of the tomb of Emperor 大長谷 (大長谷天皇; reading unconfirmed), explaining that this is enough to show the disgrace. In the Nihon Shoki, the elder brother 億計 (reading unconfirmed) admonishes the Emperor with two reasons, and the Emperor has the work itself stopped.

variants.name: One version (一云)
variants.text: It says that the reason 小楯 (reading unconfirmed) had come to 赤石郡 (reading unconfirmed) was not to prepare the offerings for the Niiname (新嘗) festival himself, but to tour the districts and counties collecting the rice-field tax (田租).

variants.name: One text (一本)
variants.text: In a genealogy listing the children of Prince 市邊押磐 (市邊押磐皇子; reading unconfirmed), it places Princess 飯豐 (飯豐女王; reading unconfirmed) before Prince 億計 (億計王; reading unconfirmed). In the main text's genealogy, Princess 飯豐 is placed fourth, after Prince 億計 and Prince 弘計 (弘計王; reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: It says that Emperor 弘計 (弘計天皇; reading unconfirmed) had palaces in two places, 少郊 and 池野 (readings unconfirmed), and another text says he had a palace at 甕栗 (reading unconfirmed). The main text says that he ascended the throne at the 近飛鳥八釣宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: It says that Emperor 億計 (億計天皇; reading unconfirmed) had palaces in two places, 川村 and 縮見高野 (readings unconfirmed), and that the pillars of those halls have not rotted even now. The main text says that he ascended the throne at the 石上廣高宮 palace (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: It gives the daughter borne by 大糠娘 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 和珥臣日觸 (reading unconfirmed), as Princess 山田大娘 (山田大娘皇女; reading unconfirmed) (also called Princess 赤見, 赤見皇女; reading unconfirmed). The main text says that 糠君娘 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 和珥臣日爪 (reading unconfirmed), bore Princess 春日山田 (春日山田皇女; reading unconfirmed), and a note says that, though the names differ slightly, they are the same person.

buretsu.title: Emperor Buretsu and the Fall of the Heguri Clan
buretsu.lead: After the death of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Ninken), the Crown Prince 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯尊 (reading unconfirmed) used the troops of Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji to destroy the Great Minister 平群眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed), who had taken the government of the country into his own hands, together with his son Shibi, and then ascended the throne at 泊瀬列城 (reading unconfirmed). After his accession, cruel deeds are recorded year by year, and in the 12th month of the 8th year he died at the 列城宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace without any children.

points.text: The Nihon Shoki describes this emperor as one who was versed in punishments and trials and made the laws clear, yet who also "repeatedly did evil and did not do a single good thing"; it writes that he watched cruel punishments in person, so that everyone in the country trembled with fear.

When 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) died in the 11th year of Emperor Ninken, the Great Minister 平群眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed) monopolized the government of the country and sought to become king of Japan. The Crown Prince wished to marry 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed), but 影媛 was already involved with Shibi, son of 眞鳥, and at the song-gathering place at 海柘榴市 (reading unconfirmed) the Crown Prince and Shibi exchanged songs.

Learning that Shibi had already won 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), the Crown Prince had Shibi killed at 乃樂山 (reading unconfirmed) by the troops of Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji, and in the 11th month burned the house of 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed) and killed him. It is said that as he died, 眞鳥 cursed the salt of every region but forgot only the salt of the sea at 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed), so that the salt of 角鹿 became food for the emperor, while the salt of the other seas became something the emperor avoided.

In the 12th month, Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji offered the Crown Prince the honorific title of sovereign, and the Crown Prince ascended the throne at 泊瀬列城 (reading unconfirmed) and made Kanamura Great Chieftain. From the 2nd year on, cruel deeds are recorded year by year, such as cutting open the belly of a pregnant woman, tearing out people's nails and making them dig up yams, and making people climb trees and then cutting the trees down.

In the 9th month of the 6th year, the emperor said that to pass on the country it is precious to establish a child, but that he had no heir; so, to leave his name behind, he established the 小泊瀬舍人 (reading unconfirmed). In the 12th month of the 8th year, the emperor died at the 列城宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

The section on Emperor Buretsu in the Kojiki records only his palace and his reign of eight years, the fact that because he had no crown prince he established the 小長谷部 (reading unconfirmed), and the location of his tomb; accounts of the fall of the Heguri clan or of his cruel deeds could not be confirmed there.

story.text: 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was the Crown Prince of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was Empress 春日大娘 (reading unconfirmed). He became Crown Prince in the 7th year of 億計天皇. When he grew up, he was fond of the principles of punishment and made the laws clear; he would sit in court until the sun set and without fail bring hidden false accusations to light, and in trials he grasped the true facts. At the same time, it is said, he repeatedly did evil and did not do a single good thing, and he watched every kind of cruel punishment in person, so that everyone in the country trembled with fear.

When 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) died in the 8th month of the 11th year, the Great Minister 平群眞鳥臣 (reading unconfirmed) monopolized the government of the country and sought to become king of Japan; saying it was for the Crown Prince, he had a palace built and lived in it himself. The Crown Prince wished to marry 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed), and sent a messenger, but because 影媛 was already involved with Shibi, son of 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed), she answered that she would meet him at 海柘榴市 (reading unconfirmed). When the Crown Prince asked the house of the Heguri Great Minister for official horses, the Great Minister answered as if mocking him and never sent the horses. At the song-gathering place where they had arranged to meet, while the Crown Prince was holding the sleeve of 影媛, Shibi pushed in between the two of them, and the Crown Prince and Shibi exchanged a number of songs.

The Crown Prince learned that Shibi had already won 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), realized the insolence of 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed) and his son, and became very angry. That night he went to the house of Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji and discussed gathering troops, and Kanamura killed Shibi at 乃樂山 (reading unconfirmed) with several thousand soldiers. 影媛 followed all the way to that place, watched him being killed, and composed a song lamenting in grief. Even when she was about to return home after burying Shibi, she wept, saying, "Today I have lost my beloved husband," and composed another song.

In the 11th month, Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji asked the Crown Prince to let him strike down 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed), led troops to surround the house of the Great Minister, and set it on fire. 眞鳥, resenting that his plans had failed, pointed at salt and cursed it as he was killed together with his sons and younger kin; but because he forgot to curse only the salt of the sea at 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed), it is said, the salt of 角鹿 became food for the emperor, while the salt of the other seas became something the emperor avoided. In the 12th month, Kanamura returned the government to the Crown Prince and offered him the honorific title of sovereign; the Crown Prince set up an altar at 泊瀬列城 (reading unconfirmed), ascended the throne, and made Kanamura Great Chieftain. In the 3rd month of the 1st year, he made 春日娘子 (reading unconfirmed) his empress; it is recorded that her father's name is not known.

In the 9th month of the 2nd year, he cut open the belly of a pregnant woman to look at the fetus. In the 10th month of the 3rd year, he tore out people's nails and made them dig up yams; in the 11th month he ordered the Great Chieftain 大伴室屋 (reading unconfirmed) to send out able-bodied men of 言濃國 (reading unconfirmed) and had them build the shape of a fortress at 水派邑 (reading unconfirmed), which was called 城上 (reading unconfirmed). In the 4th month of the 4th year, he pulled out people's hair, made them climb up trees, and enjoyed watching them fall to their deaths when the trees were cut down. In this year in Paekche, 末多王 (reading unconfirmed) was removed by the people of the country because he had acted tyrannically toward the people, and 嶋王 (reading unconfirmed) was set up and became King Muryŏng.

In the 6th month of the 5th year, he made people go into the sluice of a pond and enjoyed stabbing them to death with a three-bladed spear as they were washed out. In the 9th month of the 6th year, because he had no heir of his own, the emperor decided to establish the 小泊瀬舍人 (reading unconfirmed) to pass on his name, and in the 10th month he did not let the Paekche envoy 麻那君 (reading unconfirmed) go home, on the grounds that tribute had not been paid for several years. In the 2nd month of the 7th year, he made people climb trees, shot them down with a bow, and laughed; in the 4th month, the king of Paekche newly sent 斯我君 (reading unconfirmed). In the 3rd month of the 8th year, he engaged in a cruel amusement that humiliated women; it is also recorded that he made ponds and gardens and gathered birds and beasts, loved hunting, and indulged in drinking with the palace attendants, forgetting the people's cold and hunger. In the 12th month, the emperor died at the 列城宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

quotes.note: It means: "He also repeatedly did many evil deeds and did not do a single good thing."
The passage stating that the troops of Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji killed Shibi no Omi at 乃樂山 (reading unconfirmed).
The passage stating that when 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed) cursed the salt as he died, he forgot only the salt of the sea at 角鹿 (reading unconfirmed) and did not curse it.
The edict of the 9th month of the 6th year. It means: "The key to passing on the country lies in establishing a child, but I have no heir."

figures.name: 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and Empress 春日大娘 (reading unconfirmed). He destroyed the Heguri clan, ascended the throne at 泊瀬列城 (reading unconfirmed), and died in his 8th year without any children.

figures.name: 平群眞鳥臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Great Minister. After the death of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) he monopolized the government of the country and sought to become king, and was attacked and killed by Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji.

figures.name: Shibi (鮪)
figures.role: Son of 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed). He was involved with 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), exchanged songs with the Crown Prince at the song-gathering place, and was afterward killed at 乃樂山 (reading unconfirmed). A reading note says "鮪、此云茲寐".

figures.name: 影媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed). She was sought by the Crown Prince but was involved with Shibi, and composed songs lamenting his death.

figures.name: 物部麁鹿火大連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Father of 影媛 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji (大伴金村連)
figures.role: On the Crown Prince's orders he struck down Shibi and 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed), and on the day of the accession he was made Great Chieftain.

figures.name: 春日娘子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Made empress in the 3rd month of the 1st year. It is recorded that her father's name is not known.

figures.name: 末多王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A king of Paekche. In the 4th year he was removed by the people of the country because he had acted tyrannically toward the people.

figures.name: 嶋王 (reading unconfirmed) (King Muryŏng, 武寧王)
figures.role: The king of Paekche who was set up after 末多王 (reading unconfirmed) was removed.

figures.name: 麻那君 (reading unconfirmed) and 斯我君 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Envoys sent from Paekche. 麻那君 (reading unconfirmed) was detained in the 6th year; 斯我君 (reading unconfirmed) was newly sent in the 7th year, and his son 法師君 (reading unconfirmed) is regarded as the ancestor of the 倭君 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Buretsu
compare.text: The section on Emperor Buretsu in the Kojiki records only that he ruled the realm for eight years from the 列木宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace at 長谷 (reading unconfirmed), that because he had no crown prince he established the 小長谷部 (reading unconfirmed), and that his tomb is at 石坏岡 (reading unconfirmed) in 片岡 (reading unconfirmed); the accounts of cruel deeds found in the Nihon Shoki could not be confirmed there.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Buretsu
compare.text: The Kojiki also says that he established a name-bearing group because he had no heir, but its name is 小長谷部 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki says that he established the 小泊瀬舍人 (reading unconfirmed) by the edict of the 9th month of the 6th year.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Seinei (the song-gathering with 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: The story of exchanging songs at a song-gathering with 志毘臣 (reading unconfirmed) of the Heguri clan over a woman, and then killing 志毘臣, is in the section on Emperor Seinei in the Kojiki; there the rival is 袁祁命 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Kenzō) and the woman is 大魚 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 菟田首 (reading unconfirmed) and others. In the Nihon Shoki, in this book, the Crown Prince (Emperor Buretsu) and Shibi, son of 眞鳥 (reading unconfirmed), contend over 影媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: It says that Shibi stayed at the house of 影媛 (reading unconfirmed) and was killed during that night. In the main text, Ōtomo no Kanamura no Muraji kills Shibi at 乃樂山 (reading unconfirmed) with several thousand soldiers.

variants.name: The Kudara Shinsen says (百濟新撰云)
variants.text: It says that because 末多王 (reading unconfirmed) was lawless and acted tyrannically toward the people, the people of the country removed him and King Muryŏng was set up. It gives King Muryŏng's personal name as 斯麻王 (reading unconfirmed), says he was the son of Prince 混支 (reading unconfirmed) and an elder half-brother of 末多王 by a different mother, and says he was so named because he was born on an island (嶋 (reading unconfirmed)) in Tsukushi while 混支 was on his way to Wa (倭). In a note, the compilers of the Nihon Shoki say that since 嶋王 (reading unconfirmed) was the son of 蓋鹵王 (reading unconfirmed) and 末多王 was the son of 混支王 (reading unconfirmed), it is not clear why he is called an "elder half-brother by a different mother."

variants.name: One text (一本)
variants.text: It gives the first line of the Crown Prince's first song, "之裒世", as "彌儺斗".

variants.name: One text (一本)
variants.text: It gives "耶賦能之魔柯枳" in the Crown Prince's song as "耶陛哿羅哿枳".

keitai.title: The Enthronement of Emperor Keitai and the Rebellion of Iwai, Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Tsukushi
keitai.lead: After 小泊瀬天皇 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Buretsu) died without an heir, the Great Chieftain Ōtomo no Kanamura and others brought 男大迹王 (reading unconfirmed), a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Ōjin, from Mikuni and had him ascend the throne. During his reign, negotiations with Paekche, Silla and Kara over Mimana continued, and in the 21st year Iwai, Kuni-no-Miyatsuko (provincial chief) of Tsukushi, rose in rebellion and was struck down by 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed).

points.text: When 小泊瀬天皇 (reading unconfirmed) died without any children, the Great Chieftain Ōtomo no Kanamura and others brought 男大迹王 (reading unconfirmed), a fifth-generation descendant of 譽田天皇 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Ōjin), from Mikuni. After declining many times, 男大迹王 received the imperial seal in the 2nd month of the 1st year and ascended the throne.

In the 21st year, Iwai, Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Tsukushi, took bribes from Silla, based himself in the two provinces of Hi and Toyo, and blocked the army of 近江毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed), which was heading for Mimana. In the 11th month of the 22nd year, the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) beheaded Iwai in 御井郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi, and Iwai's son 筑紫君葛子 (reading unconfirmed) presented the 糟屋屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate in an effort to escape the death penalty.

In the 6th year, in response to a request from Paekche, the four districts of Mimana — 上哆唎 (reading unconfirmed), 下哆唎 (reading unconfirmed), 娑陀 (reading unconfirmed) and 牟婁 (reading unconfirmed) — were given to Paekche. It is written that at this time a rumor arose that Ōtomo no Kanamura and others had received bribes from Paekche.

The main text records in advance that 天國排開廣庭尊 (reading unconfirmed) (later Emperor Kinmei), born to the empress 手白香皇女 (reading unconfirmed), was the legitimate heir but was young, and that he ruled the realm after his two elder brothers (Prince 勾大兄 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince 檜隈高田 (reading unconfirmed)) had ruled.

The Kojiki gives the emperor's age as forty-three, while the Nihon Shoki gives it as eighty-two. Also, as to who struck down Iwai (written "竺紫君石井" in the Kojiki), the Kojiki names two men, 物部荒甲之大連 (reading unconfirmed) and 大伴之金村連 (reading unconfirmed), while the Nihon Shoki says that 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) was sent as commander-in-chief.

As for the year of his death, the Nihon Shoki gives the 25th year (辛亥), but "a certain text" gives the 28th year (甲寅). The main text notes that it adopted the 25th year on the basis of an entry in the Kudara Hongi.

story.text: 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed) (also called 彦太尊 (reading unconfirmed)) was a fifth-generation descendant of 譽田天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and the son of 彦主人王 (reading unconfirmed); his mother, 振媛 (reading unconfirmed), was a seventh-generation descendant of 活目天皇 (reading unconfirmed). His father sent messengers from his country residence at 三尾 (reading unconfirmed) in 高嶋郡 (reading unconfirmed), Ōmi Province, to 坂中井 (reading unconfirmed) in Mikuni and took 振媛 as his consort, but he died while the future emperor was still young. 振媛 returned to her home of 高向 (reading unconfirmed) in Echizen Province and raised him. When 小泊瀬天皇 (reading unconfirmed) died without children in the 12th month of his 8th year, the Great Chieftain Ōtomo no Kanamura first tried to bring 倭彦王 (reading unconfirmed), a fifth-generation descendant of 足仲彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed), from 桑田郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tanba Province; but 倭彦王, seeing the soldiers sent to escort him, became afraid, fled into the mountains, and his whereabouts became unknown.

In the 1st month of the 1st year, the Great Chieftain Ōtomo no Kanamura put forward 男大迹王 (reading unconfirmed); the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) and the Great Minister 許勢男人 (reading unconfirmed) agreed, and envoys were sent to Mikuni. 男大迹王 sat calmly on a folding chair but still had doubts and did not respond. When 河內馬飼首荒籠 (reading unconfirmed) secretly sent a messenger to convey the true intentions of the Great Minister, the Great Chieftains and the others, he at last set out, and he later treated 荒籠 (reading unconfirmed) generously. In the 2nd month, when Kanamura presented the mirror, the sword and the imperial seal, the emperor declined three times facing west and twice facing south before accepting them; he ascended the throne at the 樟葉宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, and the Great Minister and Great Chieftains were kept in their former posts.

On Kanamura's advice, 手白香皇女 (reading unconfirmed) was made empress in the 3rd month, and she gave birth to 天國排開廣庭尊 (reading unconfirmed). In the same month, citing the precedent that the sovereign himself tills the fields and the empress and consorts themselves raise silkworms, the emperor issued an edict that the realm should be told that neither officials nor common people were to neglect farming and weaving. He also took eight consorts; his first consort, 目子媛 (reading unconfirmed), gave birth to Prince 勾大兄 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince 檜隈高田 (reading unconfirmed). In the 10th month of the 2nd year, 小泊瀬稚鷦鷯天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was buried in the 傍丘磐杯丘陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb. The capital was moved to 筒城 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro in the 5th year, to 弟国 (reading unconfirmed) in the 12th year, and to 磐余玉穂 (reading unconfirmed) in the 20th year.

In the 6th year, Paekche asked for four districts of Mimana; 穂積臣押山 (reading unconfirmed), governor of the province of 哆唎 (reading unconfirmed), and Ōtomo no Kanamura agreed to this, and the four districts were given to Paekche. 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed), who was to deliver the imperial command, was told by his wife of the teachings of the great deity of Sumiyoshi and of the history going back to Empress Jingū, so he claimed illness and withdrew; later Prince 大兄 (reading unconfirmed) tried to revoke the decision, but the Paekche envoy did not comply. In the 7th year, Paekche sent the Doctor of the Five Classics 段楊爾 (reading unconfirmed) and asked for the return of the land of 己汶 (reading unconfirmed), which had been taken by the country of 伴跛 (reading unconfirmed); in the 11th month, 己汶 and 帯沙 (reading unconfirmed) were given to Paekche. In the same year, Prince 勾大兄 (reading unconfirmed) took Princess 春日 (reading unconfirmed) as his consort, and in the 12th month the emperor installed 勾大兄 as Crown Prince. In the 1st month of the 8th year, because Princess 春日 lamented that she had no heir, the 匝布屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate was given to preserve her name.

In the 6th month of the 21st year, 近江毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed) led an army of sixty thousand and was about to head for Mimana to restore 南加羅 (reading unconfirmed) and 喙己呑 (reading unconfirmed), which had been defeated by Silla. Iwai, Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Tsukushi, had long been plotting rebellion; taking bribes from Silla, he based himself in the two provinces of Hi and Toyo, drew in the tribute ships of the various countries, and obstructed the army of 毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed). The emperor made 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) general, and in the 8th month gave him the axe of command, ordering that he himself would rule east of Nagato, while 麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) should rule west of Tsukushi. In the 11th month of the 22nd year, 麁鹿火 fought Iwai in 御井郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi and beheaded him; in the 12th month, Iwai's son 筑紫君葛子 (reading unconfirmed) presented the 糟屋屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate and asked to atone for his death penalty.

In the 23rd year, at Paekche's request, 多沙津 (reading unconfirmed) in Kara was given to Paekche; Kara, resenting this, allied itself with Silla. 毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Ara and summoned the kings of Silla and Paekche to 熊川 (reading unconfirmed), but the kings did not come, and a high minister of Silla came with troops and seized four villages. In the 9th month of the 24th year, envoys from Mimana complained that 毛野臣 had built a house at 久斯牟羅 (reading unconfirmed) and neglected his duties, and had caused many people to die by judging them through ordeal by hot water. 毛野臣 did not respond when recalled and provoked fighting with the troops of Paekche and Silla; later he was summoned, died of illness on Tsushima, and his wife composed a song.

In the 2nd month of the 24th year, citing how emperors of old had relied on wise ministers, the emperor issued an edict that people of integrity be recommended. In the 2nd month of the 25th year, the emperor fell gravely ill and died on the 丁未 day at the 磐余玉穂宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. He was eighty-two years old. In the 12th month he was buried in the 藍野陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

quotes.note: 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed) declined the throne three times facing west and twice facing south.
It is said in the world: do not ask whether a person is of high or low status, but value only his heart (words praising what 荒籠 (reading unconfirmed) had done).
East of Nagato I will rule. West of Tsukushi you (麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed)) shall rule.
The emperor died at the 磐余玉穂宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. He was eighty-two years old.

figures.name: 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed) (彦太尊 (reading unconfirmed))
figures.role: A fifth-generation descendant of 譽田天皇 (reading unconfirmed). The emperor who was brought from Mikuni and ascended the throne.

figures.name: 振媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The emperor's mother. A seventh-generation descendant of 活目天皇 (reading unconfirmed); after her husband's death she raised the emperor at 高向 (reading unconfirmed) in Echizen.

figures.name: The Great Chieftain Ōtomo no Kanamura (大伴金村大連)
figures.role: The Great Chieftain who put forward 男大迹王 (reading unconfirmed) and had him enthroned, and who advised that 手白香皇女 (reading unconfirmed) be made empress.

figures.name: 物部麁鹿火大連 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Great Chieftain. The commander-in-chief who beheaded Iwai in 御井郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi in the 22nd year.

figures.name: 許勢男人大臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The Great Minister who agreed to the enthronement of 男大迹王 (reading unconfirmed). He died in the 9th month of the 23rd year.

figures.name: 倭彦王 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A fifth-generation descendant of 足仲彦天皇 (reading unconfirmed). The first to be sought, he became afraid on seeing the soldiers and fled into the mountains.

figures.name: 河內馬飼首荒籠 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The person who secretly conveyed to 男大迹王 (reading unconfirmed) the true intentions of those sent to bring him, and so helped bring about his accession.

figures.name: 手白香皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The empress. She gave birth to 天國排開廣庭尊 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Kinmei).

figures.name: Prince 勾大兄 (reading unconfirmed) (勾大兄皇子)
figures.role: Son of the first consort 目子媛 (reading unconfirmed). He was installed as Crown Prince and later ruled the realm (Emperor Ankan).

figures.name: 穗積臣押山 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Governor of the province of 哆唎 (reading unconfirmed). He petitioned that the four districts of Mimana be given to Paekche.

figures.name: Iwai, Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Tsukushi (筑紫國造磐井)
figures.role: He took bribes from Silla, rebelled, and obstructed the army of 毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed), but was beheaded by 麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 筑紫君葛子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Iwai. He presented the 糟屋屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate and asked to atone for his death penalty.

figures.name: 近江毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A general sent to Mimana. He caused the people of Mimana suffering, was recalled, and died of illness on Tsushima.

figures.name: 荳角皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 麻績娘子 (reading unconfirmed); the princess who served at the shrine of the Great Deity of Ise. A reading note says "荳角、此云娑佐礙".

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Keitai (genealogy and death)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives the emperor's age as forty-three and places his tomb at 藍 (reading unconfirmed) in 三嶋 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki says that he died at eighty-two and was buried in the 藍野陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Keitai (the rebellion of 石井)
compare.text: The Kojiki writes Iwai as "竺紫君石井" and says that two men, 物部荒甲之大連 (reading unconfirmed) and 大伴之金村連 (reading unconfirmed), were sent to kill him. The Nihon Shoki writes "筑紫國造磐井" and says that 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed), as commander-in-chief, beheaded him in 御井郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — end of the section on Emperor Buretsu (bringing in Emperor Keitai)
compare.text: The Kojiki records briefly that 袁本杼命 (reading unconfirmed) was brought up from the land of 近淡海 (reading unconfirmed) and, joined with 手白髮命 (reading unconfirmed), was given the realm. The Nihon Shoki says he was raised at 高向 (reading unconfirmed) in Echizen and brought from Mikuni, and describes in detail how he declined and then ascended the throne.

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: The main text places the emperor's death in the 25th year (辛亥), but a certain text places it in the 28th year (甲寅). The main text notes that it adopted the 25th year because the Kudara Hongi says that in the year 辛亥 it was heard that the emperor, the crown prince and the princes of Japan had all died together.

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text dates the move of the capital to 磐余玉穂 (reading unconfirmed) to the 9th month of the 20th year, but one text places it in the 7th year.

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text says that 毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed) stayed at 熊川 (reading unconfirmed), but one text says he stayed at 久斯牟羅 (reading unconfirmed) in Mimana. Also, for the four villages seized by the high minister of Silla, the main text gives 金官 (reading unconfirmed), 背伐 (reading unconfirmed), 安多 (reading unconfirmed) and 委陀 (reading unconfirmed), while one text gives 多多羅 (reading unconfirmed), 須那羅 (reading unconfirmed), 和多 (reading unconfirmed) and 費智 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: Some say (或曰)
variants.text: It adds a view that the seizure of 多々羅 (reading unconfirmed) and the other three villages was due to the fault of 毛野臣 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: The Kudara Hongi says (百濟本記云)
variants.text: Regarding the entry on sending an envoy to Paekche in the 3rd year, the Kudara Hongi records that "久羅麻致支彌" came from Japan, but the main text notes that the details are not known.

ankan-senka.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 18 — Emperor Ankan and Emperor Senka
ankan-senka.title: Emperor Ankan, Emperor Senka and the Establishment of Miyake Estates
ankan-senka.lead: This book records two reigns: that of 勾大兄 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Ankan), son of Emperor Keitai, and that of his full younger brother 武小廣國押盾 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Senka).
