In Emperor Ankan's reign many miyake (crown estates) were established in various regions, and in Emperor Senka's reign an order was given to gather the grain of the miyake at the government office at 那津之口 (reading unconfirmed).

points.text: Because Emperor Ankan had no children even after taking four wives, on the advice of Ōtomo no Kanamura he established miyake estates (小墾田屯倉 (reading unconfirmed), 櫻井屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) and 難波屯倉 (reading unconfirmed)) to preserve the names of his empress and consorts for later generations.

In the 5th month of the 2nd year of Emperor Ankan, more than twenty miyake estates were established at once in provinces including Tsukushi, Toyo, Hi, Harima, Bingo, Awa, Kii, Tanba, Ōmi, Owari, Kamitsukeno and Suruga.

Stories follow of miyake estates being presented in atonement for offenses. The Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of 伊甚 (reading unconfirmed) presented the 伊甚屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate for the offense of frightening the empress, and the Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Musashi, 笠原直使主 (reading unconfirmed), presented four miyake estates, including 横渟 (reading unconfirmed), in thanks for being confirmed in the position of Kuni-no-Miyatsuko.

In the 5th month of his 1st year, Emperor Senka issued an edict that "food is the foundation of the realm," had the grain of the miyake estates in various regions transported, built a government office at 那津之口 (reading unconfirmed), and had it prepared for emergencies.

In the 2nd month of the 1st year of Emperor Senka, Soga no Iname no Sukune was appointed Great Minister. In the 10th month of the 2nd year, because Silla attacked Mimana, 磐 (reading unconfirmed) and 狭手彦 (reading unconfirmed), sons of Ōtomo no Kanamura, were sent; 磐 stayed in Tsukushi and 狭手彦 in Mimana.

For Emperor Ankan, the Kojiki records only his palace, the fact that he had no children, and his tomb, and does not tell of the miyake estates. As for Emperor Senka's children, the Kojiki makes 惠波王 (reading unconfirmed) (ancestor of the 韋那君 (reading unconfirmed) and the 多治比君 (reading unconfirmed)) a child of 川内之若子比賣 (reading unconfirmed), whereas the Nihon Shoki makes Prince 上殖葉 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 丹比公 (reading unconfirmed) and the 偉那公 (reading unconfirmed), a child of the empress 橘仲皇女 (reading unconfirmed).

story.text: 勾大兄廣國押武金日天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was the eldest son of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 目子媛 (reading unconfirmed). On the 丁未 day of the 2nd month of the 25th year of Emperor Keitai, 男大迹天皇 set up 大兄 (reading unconfirmed) as emperor and died that same day. Ōtomo no Kanamura and 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) were made Great Chieftains as before. In the 1st month of the 1st year, the capital was moved to 勾金橋 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of 大倭 (reading unconfirmed); in the 3rd month, Princess 春日山田 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed), was made empress, and three women, 紗手媛 (reading unconfirmed), 香香有媛 (reading unconfirmed) and 宅媛 (reading unconfirmed), were made consorts.

In the 4th month of the 1st year, when 膳臣大麻呂 (reading unconfirmed) sought pearls from 伊甚 (reading unconfirmed), the Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of 伊甚 and the others arrived late; when questioned, they fled into the rear palace and frightened the empress so that she fell down. To atone for their offense, the Kuni-no-Miyatsuko and the others presented the 伊甚屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate. In the 7th month, when an imperial envoy sought land for a miyake for the empress, 大河内直味張 (reading unconfirmed), begrudging his good rice fields, told a lie. In the intercalary 12th month, at 三嶋 (reading unconfirmed), the district chief 飯粒 (reading unconfirmed) willingly presented forty chō of land, so Ōtomo no Kanamura rebuked 味張 (reading unconfirmed) and removed him as district official, and 味張 promised to provide five hundred mattock laborers each in spring and autumn.

In the 10th month, the emperor grieved that although he had four wives he had no children, and that his name would die out. Ōtomo no Kanamura recommended that, whether or not one has children, one's name should be preserved through things, and that miyake estates be built for the empress and consorts; the 小墾田屯倉 (reading unconfirmed), 櫻井屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) and 難波屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estates were given to the consorts. In this month there was an incident in which 幡媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of the 廬城部連 (reading unconfirmed), stole a jeweled necklace belonging to Mononobe no Okoshi and presented it to the empress, and a group of workers and land were presented in atonement. Also, 笠原直使主 (reading unconfirmed) and 小杵 (reading unconfirmed) contended for the position of Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Musashi; the court made 使主 (reading unconfirmed) Kuni-no-Miyatsuko and executed 小杵, so 使主 presented four miyake estates: 横渟 (reading unconfirmed), 橘花 (reading unconfirmed), 多氷 (reading unconfirmed) and 倉樔 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 1st month of the 2nd year, rejoicing that abundant harvests had continued and the country had grown rich, the emperor permitted a great five-day feast throughout the realm. In the 5th month, many miyake estates were established in provinces from Tsukushi to Suruga and Kamitsukeno; in the 8th month, groups of dog-keepers were established in the provinces; and in the 9th month, the 櫻井田部連 (reading unconfirmed) and others were put in charge of the taxes of the miyake estates. In the 12th month, the emperor died at the 勾金橋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. He was seventy years old. He was buried in the 舊市高屋丘陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb in Kawachi, and the empress, Princess 春日山田 (reading unconfirmed), and the emperor's younger sister, Princess 神前 (reading unconfirmed), were buried together with him in the same tomb.

武小廣國押盾天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was the second son of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and the full younger brother of 勾大兄天皇 (reading unconfirmed). When his elder brother died without children, the assembled ministers presented the sword and mirror to him and had him ascend the throne. In the 1st month of the 1st year, the capital was moved to 檜隈廬入野 (reading unconfirmed); in the 2nd month, Ōtomo no Kanamura and 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) were made Great Chieftains as before, Soga no Iname no Sukune was made Great Minister, and 阿倍火麻呂臣 (reading unconfirmed) was made a high official (大夫). In the 3rd month, Princess 橘仲 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed), was made empress, and the empress gave birth to Princess 石姫 (reading unconfirmed), Princess 小石姫 (reading unconfirmed), Princess 倉稚綾姫 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince 上殖葉 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 5th month of the 1st year, declaring that "food is the foundation of the realm," the emperor ordered that, since Tsukushi was the gateway through which countries far and near came to the court, the grain of the miyake estates of 茨田郡 (reading unconfirmed), Owari, 新家 (reading unconfirmed), Iga and elsewhere be transported, and that a government office be built at 那津之口 (reading unconfirmed) to prepare for bad years and emergencies. In the 7th month, the Great Chieftain 物部麁鹿火 (reading unconfirmed) died. In the 10th month of the 2nd year, because Silla invaded Mimana, 磐 (reading unconfirmed) and 狭手彦 (reading unconfirmed), sons of Ōtomo no Kanamura, were sent; 磐 governed in Tsukushi and kept watch against the Three Han, while 狭手彦 pacified Mimana and rescued Paekche. In the 2nd month of the 4th year, the emperor died at the 檜隈廬入野宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. He was seventy-three years old; in the 11th month he was buried in the 身狹桃花鳥坂上陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb, and the empress, Princess 橘 (reading unconfirmed), and her young child were buried together with him.

quotes.note: I have taken four wives, but even now I have no heir. After my death my name will die out.
There is no place on the earth that is not the king's domain, and no place under heaven that is not the king's land (words rebuking 味張 (reading unconfirmed)).
Food is the very foundation of the realm. However much gold there may be, it cannot cure hunger.
磐 (reading unconfirmed) stayed in Tsukushi, governed that land, and kept watch against the Three Han.

figures.name: 勾大兄廣國押武金日天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Eldest son of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed). Emperor Ankan, who ruled the realm from the 勾金橋宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

figures.name: 春日山田皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and empress of Emperor Ankan. She was later buried together with him in the same tomb.

figures.name: The Great Chieftain Ōtomo no Kanamura (大伴金村大連)
figures.role: The Great Chieftain who advised preserving the consorts' names through miyake estates and who punished 味張 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 大河內直味張 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man who, begrudging his good rice fields, deceived an imperial envoy, and later apologized for his offense and provided mattock laborers.

figures.name: 笠原直使主 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man who contended for the position of Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Musashi, was confirmed in it by the court, and presented four miyake estates.

figures.name: 武小廣國押盾天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Second son of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and full younger brother of Emperor Ankan. Emperor Senka, who ruled the realm from the 檜隈廬入野宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace.

figures.name: 橘仲皇女 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of 億計天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and empress of Emperor Senka. She gave birth to Princess 石姫 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: Soga no Iname (蘇我稻目宿禰)
figures.role: The man appointed Great Minister in the 1st year of Emperor Senka.

figures.name: 磐 (reading unconfirmed) and 狭手彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Sons of Ōtomo no Kanamura. 磐 (reading unconfirmed) governed Tsukushi and kept watch against the Three Han, while 狭手彦 (reading unconfirmed) crossed over to Mimana.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Ankan
compare.text: The section on Emperor Ankan in the Kojiki records only that he lived at the 勾之金箸宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, that he had no children, and that his tomb is at the village of 古市高屋 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi; the story of the miyake estates could not be confirmed there. The Nihon Shoki says that the empress and the emperor's younger sister were also buried with him in the 舊市高屋丘陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb in Kawachi.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Senka (genealogy)
compare.text: The Kojiki makes 惠波王 (reading unconfirmed) (ancestor of the 韋那君 (reading unconfirmed) and the 多治比君 (reading unconfirmed)) a child of 川内之若子比賣 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki makes Prince 上殖葉 (reading unconfirmed) (also called 椀子 (reading unconfirmed)), ancestor of the 丹比公 (reading unconfirmed) and the 偉那公 (reading unconfirmed), a child of the empress 橘仲皇女 (reading unconfirmed), and gives only one child, Prince 火焔 (reading unconfirmed), to 大河内稚子媛 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text says that the 櫻井屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate was given to 香香有媛 (reading unconfirmed), but one text says that she was given the 茅渟山屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate as well.

kinmei-1.title: The Accession of Emperor Kinmei, the Talks on Restoring Mimana, and the Presentation of a Buddha Image
kinmei-1.lead: 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed) (Emperor Kinmei), the legitimate heir of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed), ascended the throne and took the daughters of Soga no Iname as consorts. In the first half of his reign, talks with King Sŏngmyŏng of Paekche about restoring Mimana continued, and in the 10th month of the 13th year King Sŏngmyŏng presented a gilt-bronze image of the Buddha Śākyamuni together with sutras and treatises.

points.text: In the 10th month of the 13th year, King Sŏngmyŏng of Paekche presented one gilt-bronze image of the Buddha Śākyamuni, together with banners and canopies and sutras and treatises, and submitted a memorial saying that this Dharma was excellent. The emperor was pleased but did not decide for himself; he asked the assembled ministers. Soga no Iname said it should be worshiped, while Mononobe no Okoshi and Nakatomi no Kamako opposed it, saying it would bring on the anger of the gods of the land.

The emperor entrusted the image to Iname and let him worship it as a trial; Iname enshrined it in his house at 小墾田 (reading unconfirmed) and made his house at 向原 (reading unconfirmed) into a temple. Later, when an epidemic spread, on the advice of Okoshi and Kamako the image was thrown away into the canal (堀江) at Naniwa and the temple was burned; at that time, though there was neither wind nor cloud, the great hall caught fire.

From the 2nd to the 5th year, King Sŏngmyŏng of Paekche repeatedly called together the chiefs (旱岐) of Mimana and the Japanese Office in Mimana (任那日本府) and discussed plans for rebuilding Mimana in accordance with the emperor's edict. King Sŏngmyŏng accused 河内直 (reading unconfirmed), 移那斯 (reading unconfirmed), 麻都 (reading unconfirmed) and others of the Japanese Office of being in league with Silla, and asked the emperor to send them back to their home country.

In the 9th month of the 1st year, when asked how many troops would be needed to attack Silla, Mononobe no Okoshi answered that Silla had long held a grudge because Ōtomo no Kanamura had given four districts of Mimana to Paekche in the 6th year of Emperor Keitai. Kanamura claimed illness and stopped attending court, but the emperor did not treat it as a crime.

In the 3rd month of the 2nd year, 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Soga no Iname, gave birth to seven sons and six daughters, among them Prince 大兄 (reading unconfirmed) (橘豐日尊 (reading unconfirmed)) and 豐御食炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed). 堅鹽媛's full younger sister 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed) gave birth to four sons and one daughter, including 泥部穴穗部皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and 泊瀬部皇子 (reading unconfirmed).

The section on Emperor Kinmei in the Kojiki contains only genealogy, and entries corresponding to the presentation of the Buddha image or the talks on Mimana could not be confirmed there. In the genealogy as well, the Kojiki calls 小兄比賣 (reading unconfirmed) the "姨" (aunt) of 岐多志比賣命 (reading unconfirmed), whereas the Nihon Shoki makes 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed) the full younger sister of 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed).

story.text: 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was the legitimate heir of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was Empress 手白香 (reading unconfirmed). When he was young, he dreamed that if he favored a man called 秦大津父 (reading unconfirmed) he would rule the realm, and he found 大津父 (reading unconfirmed) at the village of 深草里 (reading unconfirmed) in 紀伊郡 (reading unconfirmed), Yamashiro Province. 大津父 told how, on his way back from Ise, he had stopped two wolves fighting on a mountain and let them go; the future emperor took this as the reason for his reward, kept him in close attendance, and on ascending the throne appointed him to the office of the treasury. When Emperor Senka died in the 10th month of his 4th year, the prince tried to entrust the government to Empress 山田 (reading unconfirmed), but the empress declined. On the 甲申 day of the 12th month, the prince ascended the throne and made Ōtomo no Kanamura and Mononobe no Okoshi Great Chieftains and Soga no Iname Great Minister.

In the 1st month of the 1st year, 石姫 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Emperor Senka, was made empress, and the empress gave birth to Prince 箭田珠勝大兄 (reading unconfirmed), 譯語田渟中倉太珠敷尊 (reading unconfirmed) and Princess 笠縫 (reading unconfirmed). In the 7th month, the capital was moved to 磯城嶋 (reading unconfirmed) and named the 金刺宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace; in the 8th month, people who had come from overseas, such as the 秦人 (reading unconfirmed) and the 漢人 (reading unconfirmed), were settled in the provinces and districts and entered in the household registers, and the 秦人 numbered 7,053 households. In the 9th month, at the 難波祝津宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, when the emperor asked how many troops would be needed to attack Silla, Mononobe no Okoshi answered that Silla had held a grudge ever since the four districts were ceded in the reign of Emperor Keitai, and Ōtomo no Kanamura shut himself up in his house at Sumiyoshi. The emperor sent a messenger to console him and did not treat it as a crime.

In the 3rd month of the 2nd year, the emperor took five consorts. The empress's younger sister, Princess 稚綾姫 (reading unconfirmed), gave birth to Prince 石上 (reading unconfirmed), and Princess 日影 (reading unconfirmed) gave birth to Prince 倉 (reading unconfirmed). 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Soga no Iname, gave birth to seven sons and six daughters, including Prince 大兄 (reading unconfirmed) (橘豐日尊 (reading unconfirmed)) and 豐御食炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed); her full younger sister 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed) gave birth to four sons and one daughter, including Prince 茨城 (reading unconfirmed), 泥部穴穗部皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and 泊瀬部皇子 (reading unconfirmed); and 糠子 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 春日日柧臣 (reading unconfirmed), gave birth to Princess 春日山田 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince 橘麻呂 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 4th month of the 2nd year, the chiefs (旱岐) of Ara, Kara and other places and 吉備臣 (reading unconfirmed) of the Japanese Office in Mimana went to Paekche, and King Sŏngmyŏng asked them how the restoration of Mimana, which was the emperor's edict, should be carried forward. King Sŏngmyŏng said that 喙己呑 (reading unconfirmed), 南加羅 (reading unconfirmed) and 卓淳 (reading unconfirmed) had been destroyed by Silla because each of them had weaknesses within. In the 7th month, hearing that the Japanese Office in Ara had been in league with Silla, he rebuked 河内直 (reading unconfirmed). In the 11th month of the 4th year, 津守連 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to convey an edict that the Paekche district governors and fortress commanders in 下韓 (reading unconfirmed) should be placed under the Japanese Office, and King Sŏngmyŏng consulted with his ministers.

Paekche repeatedly summoned Mimana and the officials of the Japanese Office, but they did not come, saying they would come after the New Year had passed or after the festival was over, and sent only people of low rank. In the 3rd month of the 5th year, Paekche submitted a memorial asking that 移那斯 (reading unconfirmed) and 麻都 (reading unconfirmed) be transferred to their home country, on the grounds that they were monopolizing the government of the Japanese Office and coming and going wearing Silla caps. In the 11th month, 吉備臣 (reading unconfirmed) of the Japanese Office and the chiefs (旱岐) of Mimana at last assembled, and King Sŏngmyŏng presented three plans: to ask the emperor for three thousand soldiers and repair six fortresses; to keep district governors and fortress commanders stationed in 南韓 (reading unconfirmed); and to send 吉備臣, 河内直 (reading unconfirmed), 移那斯 and 麻都 back to their home country.

In the 12th month of the 5th year, a report came from the land of Koshi that people of 肅愼 (reading unconfirmed) had come by boat to Sado Island and settled there, and that they were feared as being like demons. In the 9th month of the 6th year, Paekche made a jōroku (sixteen-foot) Buddha image and composed a prayer asking for blessings for the emperor and all living beings. In the 11th month, 膳臣巴提便 (reading unconfirmed), who had returned from Paekche, told how, when his child was carried off by a tiger, he pursued the tiger, grabbed its tongue and stabbed it to death. From the 8th to the 12th year, Paekche asked for reinforcements for its war with Koguryŏ; the emperor sent 370 men to help build a fortress at 得爾辛 (reading unconfirmed), and in the 12th year granted one thousand koku of wheat seed. In this year, King Sŏngmyŏng, together with the troops of Silla and Mimana, attacked Koguryŏ, took the land of 漠城 (reading unconfirmed), also attacked P'yŏngyang, and recovered his former lands.

In the 4th month of the 13th year, Prince 箭田珠勝大兄 (reading unconfirmed) died. In the 5th month, Paekche, Kara and Ara asked for reinforcements, saying that Koguryŏ and Silla had joined hands and were planning to attack. In the 10th month, King Sŏngmyŏng presented a gilt-bronze image of the Buddha Śākyamuni together with banners and canopies and sutras and treatises, and the emperor asked the assembled ministers whether it should be worshiped. Soga no Iname recommended worshiping it, while Mononobe no Okoshi and Nakatomi no Kamako opposed it, so the emperor let Iname worship it as a trial. Later, when an epidemic spread, the image was thrown away into the canal (堀江) at Naniwa and the temple was burned, but though there was neither wind nor cloud, the great hall caught fire. In this year, Paekche abandoned 漢城 (reading unconfirmed) and P'yŏngyang, and Silla entered 漢城.

quotes.note: This Dharma is the most excellent of all teachings (words from King Sŏngmyŏng's memorial).
The countries of the west all worship it. Can Japan alone turn its back on it? (words of Soga no Iname).
If we now worship a foreign god, we may bring on the anger of the gods of the land (words of Mononobe no Okoshi and Nakatomi no Kamako).
If I and you now unite our strength and hearts and rely on the emperor, Mimana will surely stand again (words of King Sŏngmyŏng).

figures.name: 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Legitimate heir of 男大迹天皇 (reading unconfirmed). Emperor Kinmei, who ruled the realm from the 磯城嶋金刺宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace. A reading note says "開、此云波羅企".

figures.name: 秦大津父 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man who appeared in the emperor's dream. He told the story of stopping the wolves' fight and, after the accession, was appointed to the office of the treasury.

figures.name: 石姫 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of Emperor Senka and empress. She gave birth to 譯語田渟中倉太珠敷尊 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: Soga no Iname no Sukune (蘇我稻目宿禰)
figures.role: Great Minister. His daughters 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed) and 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed) became consorts, and he worshiped the Buddha image that had been presented.

figures.name: Mononobe no Okoshi (物部尾輿)
figures.role: Great Chieftain. He stated the cause of Silla's grudge and opposed the worship of the Buddha image.

figures.name: Nakatomi no Kamako (中臣鎌子)
figures.role: A man who, together with Mononobe no Okoshi, opposed the worship of the Buddha image.

figures.name: 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of Soga no Iname. She gave birth to seven sons and six daughters. A reading note says "堅鹽、此云岐施志".

figures.name: 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Full younger sister of 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed). She gave birth to 泥部穴穗部皇子 (reading unconfirmed), 泊瀬部皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: King Sŏngmyŏng of Paekche (百濟聖明王)
figures.role: King of Paekche. He led the talks on restoring Mimana and in the 13th year presented a Buddha image and sutras and treatises.

figures.name: 河內直 (reading unconfirmed), 移那斯 (reading unconfirmed) and 麻都 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: People at the Japanese Office in Mimana at Ara. They were accused by Paekche of being in league with Silla.

figures.name: 膳臣巴提便 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An envoy to Paekche. He told how he grabbed the tongue of the tiger that had carried off his child with his left hand and stabbed it to death with his right.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Kinmei (genealogy)
compare.text: The Kojiki calls 小兄比賣 (reading unconfirmed) the "姨" (aunt) of 岐多志比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) and lists five children. The Nihon Shoki makes 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed) the full younger sister of 堅鹽媛 (reading unconfirmed) and says she gave birth to four sons and one daughter.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Kinmei (genealogy)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives three children of 糠子郎女 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 春日之日爪臣 (reading unconfirmed): 春日山田郎女 (reading unconfirmed), 麻呂古王 (reading unconfirmed) and 宗賀之倉王 (reading unconfirmed); the Nihon Shoki gives two children of 糠子 (reading unconfirmed): Princess 春日山田 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince 橘麻呂 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Kinmei (opening)
compare.text: The section on Emperor Kinmei in the Kojiki records only that he lived at the 師木嶋大宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace and his genealogy, and entries corresponding to the talks on Mimana or the presentation of the Buddha image could not be confirmed there. The Nihon Shoki gives his palace as the 磯城嶋金刺宮 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: A variant account says (一書云)
variants.text: Concerning the names and order of 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed)'s children, two variant accounts are given alongside the main text. The main text states that because the 帝王本紀 (reading unconfirmed) had become confused in the course of being copied, one version was chosen as the main text and the differences were recorded in notes.

variants.name: The Kudara Hongi says (百濟本記云)
variants.text: In the memorial in the main text, Mimana treats Ara as its elder brother and Ara treats the Japanese Office as heaven, but the Kudara Hongi records that Ara is treated as father and the Japanese Office as the root.

variants.name: The Kudara Hongi says (百濟本記云)
variants.text: The main text records only that the Paekche envoy returned in the 10th month of the 5th year, but the Kudara Hongi relates that there was no reply from the emperor to the report made about 河内直 (reading unconfirmed), 移那斯 (reading unconfirmed), 麻都 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

variants.name: The Kudara Hongi says (百濟本記云)
variants.text: The main text records only that there was a great disturbance in Koguryŏ in the 6th year, but the Kudara Hongi relates that the 細群 (reading unconfirmed) and the 麁群 (reading unconfirmed) fought at the palace gate and the descendants of the 細群 were executed, and that the king of 狛 (reading unconfirmed) died.

variants.name: The Kudara Hongi says (百濟本記云)
variants.text: Concerning the great disturbance in Koguryŏ in the 7th year, the Kudara Hongi relates that, of the king's three wives, the 麁群 (reading unconfirmed) and the 細群 (reading unconfirmed), maternal relatives of the sons of the middle wife and the junior wife, fought over the throne.

kinmei-2.title: The Death of King Sŏngmyŏng in Battle and the Fall of Mimana
kinmei-2.lead: From the 14th year of Emperor Kinmei onward, Paekche kept asking for reinforcements for its wars with Koguryŏ and Silla, and in the 15th year King Sŏngmyŏng was killed in a battle with Silla. In the 23rd year Silla destroyed the government post (官家) of Mimana, and on his deathbed the emperor left word to the Crown Prince to attack Silla and rebuild Mimana.

points.text: In the 12th month of the 15th year, when 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed), a prince of Paekche, built the fort of 久陀牟羅塞 (reading unconfirmed) in Silla territory, his father King Sŏngmyŏng set out to reward his son for his labors, but his road was cut off by the Silla army and he was beheaded by 苦都 (reading unconfirmed), a slave who kept horses in the village of 佐知村 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 1st month of the 23rd year, Silla attacked and destroyed the government post (官家) of Mimana. In the 6th month the emperor issued an edict condemning Silla, and in the 7th month he sent 紀男麻呂宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and others; but the deputy general 河邊臣瓊缶 (reading unconfirmed) was defeated and captured, and 調吉士伊企儺 (reading unconfirmed) refused to surrender and was killed.

In the 4th month of the 32nd year, the emperor, whose illness had grown grave, took the Crown Prince by the hand and left word that he should attack Silla and rebuild Mimana. The emperor died that month and in the 9th month was buried in the 檜隈坂合陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

In the 6th month of the 14th year, the court asked Paekche to send doctors of medicine, doctors of divination and doctors of the calendar in rotation, and to send books of divination, calendars and medicines. In the 2nd month of the 15th year, Paekche sent, as replacements, a Doctor of the Five Classics, monks, a doctor of divination, a doctor of the calendar, a doctor of medicine, herbalists and musicians.

In the 5th month of the 14th year, a shining camphor log was found floating in the sea of 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed), and the emperor ordered painters to make two Buddha images from it. The main text identifies these as the light-emitting camphor-wood images now at 吉野寺 (reading unconfirmed).

The section on Emperor Kinmei in the Kojiki records only genealogy, summing up that he had twenty-five royal children, four of whom ruled the realm. Entries corresponding to the death of King Sŏngmyŏng, the fall of Mimana, or the emperor's death and tomb could not be confirmed there.

story.text: In the 1st month of the 14th year, Paekche asked for reinforcements. In the 5th month, a report came from Kawachi Province that in the sea of 茅渟 (reading unconfirmed) there was a Buddhist chanting sound resounding like thunder and something shining like the sun; 溝邊直 (reading unconfirmed) went into the sea, found a shining camphor log and presented it, and the emperor had two Buddha images made from it. In the 6th month, 内臣 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Paekche with gifts of horses, ships, and bows and arrows, and the court asked for doctors of medicine, divination and the calendar to be sent in rotation and for books of divination, calendars and medicines to be sent. In the 7th month, Soga no Iname had 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed) record the taxes on ships; 王辰爾 was made head of ships and was granted the title 船史 (reading unconfirmed). In the 8th month, Paekche submitted a memorial asking that reinforcements be sent quickly, saying that Silla and 狛 (reading unconfirmed) were in league and intended to take Ara and cut off the route to Japan.

In the 10th month, 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed), a prince of Paekche, raised all the troops of the country, advanced toward Koguryŏ, and built a stronghold at 百合野 (reading unconfirmed). After exchanging names with the Koguryŏ cavalry, he fought them, killed a Koguryŏ champion, and pursued the king of Koguryŏ to the top of 東聖山 (reading unconfirmed). In the 1st month of the 15th year, 渟中倉太珠敷尊 (reading unconfirmed) was installed as Crown Prince. Paekche asked 内臣 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi how many reinforcements there would be, and 内臣 answered that one thousand soldiers, one hundred horses and forty ships would be sent. In the 2nd month, a Doctor of the Five Classics, monks, a doctor of divination, a doctor of the calendar, a doctor of medicine, herbalists and musicians were sent from Paekche as replacements, and in the 5th month 内臣 led a naval force across to Paekche.

According to a memorial from Paekche in the 12th month, together with the troops of Wa (倭) they attacked the Silla fortress of 函山城 (reading unconfirmed), and burned the fortress down with the fire arrows of 物部莫奇委沙奇 (reading unconfirmed) of 竹斯 (reading unconfirmed). However, 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed) ignored the warnings of his old ministers, entered Silla and built the fort of 久陀牟羅塞 (reading unconfirmed), and his father King Sŏngmyŏng went in person to reward his hard-pressed son. Hearing of this, Silla cut off the road, and 苦都 (reading unconfirmed), a slave who kept horses, captured 明王 (reading unconfirmed) and cut off his head. 餘昌, who was surrounded, was able to escape and return because a Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Tsukushi kept shooting arrows and broke through the encirclement, and 餘昌 named this Kuni-no-Miyatsuko 鞍橋君 (reading unconfirmed). One of the Silla generals, fearing the anger of the emperor of Japan, stopped the others from destroying Paekche.

In the 2nd month of the 16th year, 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed) sent Prince 惠 (reading unconfirmed) to report the death of King Sŏngmyŏng. 蘇我臣 (reading unconfirmed) told 惠 how, in the reign of 大泊瀬天皇 (reading unconfirmed), when Paekche was attacked by Koguryŏ, the emperor ordered the head of the Department of Divinities to receive a plan from the gods, invited the deity who founded the country (建邦之神) and sent it to the rescue. He then said that he had heard Paekche had stopped worshiping that deity, but that if it repaired the deity's shrine and worshiped it, the country would prosper. In the 8th month, 餘昌 wished to take holy orders for his father's sake, but was stopped by his ministers and instead had one hundred people take holy orders. During this period, the 白猪屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate was established in five districts of Kibi, an estate in 兒嶋郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Bizen, and the 韓人大身狹屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) and 高麗人小身狹屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estates and others in 高市郡 (reading unconfirmed) in the province of Yamato (倭国). In the 1st month of the 17th year, 惠 was given weapons and fine horses and sent home, and in the 3rd month of the 18th year 餘昌 succeeded to the throne and became King Widŏk.

In the 21st and 22nd years, Silla's tribute envoys left in anger at their poor treatment, and Silla built a fortress at 阿羅波斯山 (reading unconfirmed) to guard against Japan. In the 1st month of the 23rd year, Silla attacked and destroyed the government post (官家) of Mimana, and in the 6th month the emperor issued an edict condemning Silla for betraying the kindness of 氣長足姫尊 (reading unconfirmed) (Empress Jingū) and harming Mimana. In the 7th month, 紀男麻呂宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) defeated the Silla army, but the deputy general 河邊臣瓊缶 (reading unconfirmed), knowing nothing of the art of war, advanced and was defeated; he was captured together with his wife 甘美媛 (reading unconfirmed) and gave up his wife in exchange for his life. 調吉士伊企儺 (reading unconfirmed), though pressed to shout words of disgrace toward Japan, instead kept shouting words reviling the king of Silla and was killed; his son 舅子 (reading unconfirmed) also died holding his father, and his wife 大葉子 (reading unconfirmed) composed a song. In the 8th month, 大伴連狹手彦 (reading unconfirmed) used a plan of Paekche to defeat Koguryŏ, brought back a seven-fold woven curtain (七織帳), an iron house (鉄屋) and other things, and sent 美女媛 (reading unconfirmed) and others to Soga no Iname.

In the 26th year, people of Koguryŏ came to Tsukushi and were settled in Yamashiro Province. In the 28th year there were great floods and famine in the provinces. In the 30th year, 膽津 (reading unconfirmed), nephew of 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed), fixed the registers of the laborers of the 白猪田部 (reading unconfirmed) and was granted the title 白猪史 (reading unconfirmed). In the 3rd month of the 31st year, Soga no Iname died. In the 4th month, 江渟臣裾代 (reading unconfirmed) reported that the district officials were hiding an envoy of Koguryŏ who had drifted ashore in Koshi, and the emperor had a lodging built in 相樂郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Yamashiro Province and had the envoy entertained generously. The Koguryŏ ambassador saw through the lies of 道君 (reading unconfirmed), who had seized the tribute for himself; 膳臣傾子 (reading unconfirmed) recovered the tribute and gave it back, and in the 7th month the envoys were brought from Ōmi and received at the 高威館 (reading unconfirmed) and 相樂館 (reading unconfirmed) lodgings in Yamashiro.

In the 3rd month of the 32nd year, 坂田耳子郎君 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Silla to ask why Mimana had been destroyed. In the 4th month, the emperor's illness grew grave; he hurriedly summoned the Crown Prince, who was away, took him by the hand, and left word that he should attack Silla and rebuild Mimana. That month the emperor died in his inner chamber. In the 5th month a temporary enshrinement (殯) was held at 古市 (reading unconfirmed) in Kawachi; in the 8th month a Silla envoy of condolence offered words of mourning at the temporary enshrinement; and in the 9th month he was buried in the 檜隈坂合陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

quotes.note: It is not fitting for a king's head to fall into the hands of a slave (words of King Sŏngmyŏng).
Silla attacked and destroyed the government post (官家) of Mimana.
Even in victory do not forget defeat; even in safety think of danger (words issued to the army by 紀男麻呂 (reading unconfirmed)).
You must attack Silla and rebuild Mimana (the emperor's last words).

figures.name: King Sŏngmyŏng of Paekche (百濟聖明王; also 明王)
figures.role: King of Paekche. On his way to reward his son 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed), he was captured by the Silla army and beheaded.

figures.name: 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of King Sŏngmyŏng. He fought Koguryŏ and Silla, and in the 18th year succeeded to the throne and became King Widŏk.

figures.name: Prince 惠 (reading unconfirmed) (王子惠)
figures.role: Younger brother of King Widŏk. He came to the court to report the death of King Sŏngmyŏng and was sent home in the 17th year.

figures.name: 苦都 (reading unconfirmed) (谷智 (reading unconfirmed))
figures.role: A slave who kept horses in the village of 佐知村 (reading unconfirmed) in Silla. He beheaded King Sŏngmyŏng.

figures.name: A Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of Tsukushi (鞍橋君 (reading unconfirmed))
figures.role: A master archer. He rescued the surrounded 餘昌 (reading unconfirmed) and was named 鞍橋君 (reading unconfirmed). A reading note says "鞍橋、此云矩羅賦".

figures.name: 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man who recorded the taxes on ships and was granted the title 船史 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 膽津 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Nephew of 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed). He fixed the registers of the 白猪田部 (reading unconfirmed) and was granted the title 白猪史 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 渟中倉太珠敷尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The prince who was installed as Crown Prince in the 15th year and received the emperor's last words.

figures.name: 紀男麻呂宿禰 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The commander-in-chief sent to Mimana in the 23rd year.

figures.name: 河邊臣瓊缶 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Deputy general. He was defeated by Silla and captured together with his wife.

figures.name: 調吉士伊企儺 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man who did not yield even when captured by Silla, and was killed.

figures.name: 大伴連狹手彦 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The commander-in-chief who defeated Koguryŏ in the 8th month of the 23rd year and brought back treasures.

figures.name: 膳臣傾子 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A man sent to Koshi to entertain the Koguryŏ envoys. A reading note says "傾子、此云舸陀部古".

figures.name: Soga no Iname no Sukune (蘇我稻目宿禰)
figures.role: Great Minister. He was sent to establish miyake estates and died in the 3rd month of the 31st year.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Kinmei (end of the genealogy)
compare.text: The Kojiki gives Emperor Kinmei twenty-five royal children in all and sums up that four of them — 沼名倉太玉敷命 (reading unconfirmed), 橘之豐日命 (reading unconfirmed), 豐御氣炊屋比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) and 長谷部之若雀命 (reading unconfirmed) — ruled the realm. This part of the Nihon Shoki records that 渟中倉太珠敷尊 (reading unconfirmed) was installed as Crown Prince in the 15th year.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Kinmei
compare.text: In the section on Emperor Kinmei in the Kojiki, neither entries on his death, temporary enshrinement and tomb nor entries corresponding to the death of King Sŏngmyŏng or the fall of Mimana could be confirmed. The Nihon Shoki records his death in the 4th month of the 32nd year and his burial in the 檜隈坂合陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text says that 苦都 (reading unconfirmed) cut off King Sŏngmyŏng's head, but one text says that 明王 (reading unconfirmed) sat on a folding chair, handed the sword he was wearing to 谷知 (reading unconfirmed) (苦都), and had him behead him with it.

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text says that 苦都 (reading unconfirmed) cut off the head and buried it in a pit, but one text says that Silla kept the king's skull and sent the rest of his bones to Paekche with due ceremony, and relates that the skull was buried beneath the steps of the north hall (北廳), called 都堂 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text dates the destruction of the government post of Mimana to the 1st month of the 23rd year, but one text says that Mimana fell in the 21st year, and records that "Mimana" is a collective name for ten countries, including the country of Kara and the country of Ara.

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: The main text dates 狹手彦 (reading unconfirmed)'s attack on Koguryŏ to the 8th month of the 23rd year, but one text says that in the 11th year 大伴狹手彦連 (reading unconfirmed), together with Paekche, drove the Koguryŏ king 陽香 (reading unconfirmed) away to 比津留都 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: One text says (一本云)
variants.text: Concerning the names of the 大身狹屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) and 小身狹屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estates, one text explains that they were so named because people of Han (韓人) and of Koguryŏ (高麗人) from various places were made the field laborers of the respective estates.

bidatsu.title: Emperor Bidatsu, the Koguryŏ Letter, and the Beginnings of the Buddhist Dharma
bidatsu.lead: Emperor Bidatsu was the second son of Emperor Kinmei, and it is recorded that he did not believe in the Buddhist Dharma and was fond of literature and history. Book 20 records, year by year, 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed), who deciphered a letter from Koguryŏ; 日羅 (reading unconfirmed), who was summoned from Paekche to help restore Mimana and was killed; the promotion of the Buddhist Dharma by Soga no Umako and its destruction by Mononobe no Moriya; and the emperor's death and the conflict at the site of his temporary enshrinement.

points.text: An entry before his accession says that the emperor did not believe in the Buddhist Dharma and loved literature and history. The conflict over the Buddhist Dharma in this book takes place in this emperor's reign.

In the 5th month of the 1st year, none of the scribes could read a memorial from Koguryŏ even after three days, and only 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 船史 (reading unconfirmed), deciphered it. It says that the characters written on crow feathers were copied onto silk by steaming the feathers over the steam of cooking rice.

In the 13th year, Umako received a stone image of Maitreya and other images that had come from Paekche; taking as teacher the former monk 恵便 (reading unconfirmed), who had returned to lay life and was found in Harima, he had 嶋 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Shiba Tatto, and others take holy orders (as the nun Zenshin), and built a Buddha hall. The main text records "佛法之初自而作".

In the 14th year, citing the spread of an epidemic, Mononobe no Moriya and Nakatomi no Katsumi petitioned that the Buddhist Dharma be stopped; Moriya cut down the pagoda and burned it, and threw the Buddha images that survived the fire into the canal (堀江) at Naniwa. In the 6th month, Umako alone was permitted to practice the Buddhist Dharma.

In the 12th year, the emperor summoned 日羅 (reading unconfirmed), a Paekche official of the rank 達率 (reading unconfirmed), from Paekche to consult about restoring Mimana. 日羅 advised not to hurry into war but to make the people prosperous, but he was killed by 徳爾 (reading unconfirmed) and others who had accompanied him.

The section on Emperor Bidatsu in the Kojiki gives his palace as the "他田宮" and records only that he ruled the realm for fourteen years, together with his empresses and consorts, children and tomb; entries on 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed), 日羅 (reading unconfirmed) or the Buddhist Dharma could not be confirmed there.

story.text: Emperor Bidatsu (渟中倉太珠敷天皇 (reading unconfirmed)) was the second son of 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was Empress 石姫 (reading unconfirmed). He became Crown Prince in the 29th year, and in the 4th month of the 32nd year 天國排開廣庭天皇 died. He ascended the throne in the 4th month of the 1st year, set up his palace at 百済大井 (reading unconfirmed), kept Mononobe no Yuge no Moriya as Great Chieftain, and made Soga no Umako no Sukune Great Minister. In the 5th month, when none of the scribes could read the memorial from Koguryŏ, 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed) deciphered it; he was praised by the emperor and the Great Minister and came to serve in close attendance within the palace. In the 6th month, the deputy envoys of Koguryŏ killed their ambassador and falsely claimed it was because the ambassador had refused a wife given to him by the emperor.

In the 5th month of the 2nd year, Koguryŏ envoys reached the coast of Koshi, but their ship broke up and many drowned; the court, suspicious that they kept losing their way, sent them home without entertaining them and had 吉備海部直難波 (reading unconfirmed) escort them. In the 7th month, 難波 (reading unconfirmed) set out after exchanging people between the two ships, but, fearing the waves, he threw two of the Koguryŏ men into the sea. On his return in the 8th month, 難波 reported that his ship had been blocked by a whale, but the emperor saw through the lie and did not let him return to his province. In the 7th month of the 3rd year, Koguryŏ envoys asked why the escort had not come, so the emperor held 難波 guilty of deceiving the court and of drowning the envoys of a neighboring country. In the 10th month, Umako was sent to the province of Kibi to enlarge the 白猪屯倉 (reading unconfirmed) estate and its field laborers, and the register of the field laborers was given to 白猪史膽津 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 1st month of the 4th year, 広姫 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Prince 息長眞手王 (reading unconfirmed), was made empress, and 押坂彦人大兄皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and others were born. In this year, after divination, a palace was built at 譯語田 (reading unconfirmed) and called the 幸玉宮 (reading unconfirmed). In the 11th month 広姫 died, and in the 3rd month of the 5th year 豐御食炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed) was made empress. In the 11th month of the 6th year, the king of Paekche entrusted to Prince 大別王 (reading unconfirmed) and others sutras and treatises and six people — a vinaya master, a meditation master, a nun, a spell-master, a maker of Buddha images and a temple builder — as a gift; they were placed in the temple of Prince 大別王 in Naniwa. In the intercalary 2nd month of the 10th year, 綾糟 (reading unconfirmed) and the other chiefs of the Emishi who had raided the frontier went down into the river at 泊瀬 (reading unconfirmed), sipped the water facing 三諸岳 (reading unconfirmed), and swore that they and their descendants would serve with pure hearts.

In the 7th month of the 12th year, to plan the restoration of Mimana that his father had been unable to accomplish, the emperor sought to summon 日羅 (reading unconfirmed), holder of the rank 達率 (reading unconfirmed), who was in Paekche and was the son of 阿利斯登 (reading unconfirmed), Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of 火葦北 (reading unconfirmed). The king of Paekche, unwilling to lose 日羅, would not let him go, but when 吉備海部直羽嶋 (reading unconfirmed) pressed hard as 日羅 himself had advised, 日羅 came to the court. 日羅 said that the people should first be made prosperous so that food and troops were sufficient, and that many ships should then be built to confront Paekche; he also advised preparing against Paekche's scheme to obtain Tsukushi. However, 徳爾 (reading unconfirmed) and others, incited by the 恩率 (reading unconfirmed) and 参官 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche, killed 日羅 on the last day of the 12th month. 日羅 came back to life once, said that this was the work of the slaves he employed and not of Silla, and died. 徳爾 and the others were handed over to 葦北君 (reading unconfirmed) and others and killed, and 日羅 was reburied at 葦北 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 9th month of the 13th year, 鹿深臣 (reading unconfirmed), who had come from Paekche, had one stone image of Maitreya, and 佐伯連 (reading unconfirmed) had one Buddha image. In this year Umako received these two images, had Shiba Tatto and 池辺氷田 (reading unconfirmed) search for practitioners, and took as his teacher 恵便 (reading unconfirmed) of Koguryŏ, who had returned to lay life in Harima. He had 嶋 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Shiba Tatto, take holy orders as the nun Zenshin, then had the nuns 禅蔵尼 (reading unconfirmed) and 恵善尼 (reading unconfirmed) take holy orders, built a Buddha hall to the east of his residence, and enshrined the stone image of Maitreya there. A relic obtained from the food at a Buddhist feast could not be broken even when placed on an iron stand and struck with a hammer, and when thrown into water it floated or sank as one wished, so Umako and the others came to believe deeply in the Buddhist Dharma. In the 2nd month of the 14th year, Umako built a pagoda north of 大野丘 (reading unconfirmed) and placed the relic in the top of the pagoda's pillar.

In the 2nd month of the 14th year, Umako fell ill, and the diviner answered that it was a curse of the Buddha-deity worshiped in his father's time; with the emperor's permission he worshiped the stone image and prayed for his life to be prolonged. Around this time an epidemic spread in the country and many people died; in the 3rd month Moriya and Nakatomi no Katsumi petitioned that this was because the Soga had promoted the Buddhist Dharma, and the emperor ordered that the Buddhist Dharma be stopped. Moriya went to the temple himself, cut down the pagoda and burned it, burned the Buddha images and the Buddha hall too, threw the images that survived the fire into the canal (堀江) at Naniwa, and had the nun Zenshin and the others stripped of their robes and flogged at 海石榴市 (reading unconfirmed). The emperor and Moriya also suddenly fell ill with sores; people dying of the sores filled the country, and people whispered among themselves that it was punishment for burning the Buddha images. In the 6th month, when Umako petitioned that without the power of the Three Treasures his illness would not be cured, the emperor permitted Umako alone to practice the Buddhist Dharma and returned the three nuns to him.

In the 8th month of the 14th year, the emperor died in the great hall, and a temporary enshrinement palace was set up at 広瀬 (reading unconfirmed). When Umako, wearing a sword, delivered his eulogy, Moriya laughed that he looked "like a sparrow shot with an arrow." When Moriya delivered his eulogy with his hands and feet trembling, Umako laughed that "it would be good to hang bells on him," and resentment arose between the two. 三輪君逆 (reading unconfirmed) had the Hayato guard the enshrinement court, and Prince Anahobe, who sought to take the realm, angrily asked why they served in the court of a dead king and not at the side of a living king.

quotes.note: The emperor did not believe in the Buddhist Dharma and was fond of literature and history.
王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed) steamed the feathers over the steam of cooking rice, pressed silk against them, and copied all the characters.
The beginning of the Buddhist Dharma arose from this.
Moriya's words mocking Umako, who was delivering his eulogy while wearing a sword, as being "like a sparrow shot with an arrow."

figures.name: 渟中倉太珠敷天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Emperor Bidatsu. Second son of 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed); it is recorded that he did not believe in the Buddhist Dharma.

figures.name: Soga no Umako no Sukune (蘇我馬子宿禰)
figures.role: Great Minister. He received Buddha images, had nuns take holy orders, and built a Buddha hall and a pagoda.

figures.name: The Great Chieftain Mononobe no Yuge no Moriya (物部弓削守屋大連)
figures.role: Great Chieftain. Together with Nakatomi no Katsumi he petitioned that the Buddhist Dharma be stopped, and burned the pagoda and the Buddha images.

figures.name: 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Ancestor of the 船史 (reading unconfirmed). He deciphered the Koguryŏ memorial that no one else could read.

figures.name: 日羅 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of 阿利斯登 (reading unconfirmed), Kuni-no-Miyatsuko of 火葦北 (reading unconfirmed), and a Paekche official of the rank 達率 (reading unconfirmed). He was summoned to consult on restoring Mimana and was killed by 徳爾 (reading unconfirmed) and others.

figures.name: 吉備海部直難波 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Escort for the Koguryŏ envoys. He threw two of the Koguryŏ men into the sea, made a false report, and was held guilty.

figures.name: 吉備海部直羽嶋 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: The envoy who was sent to Paekche and brought back 日羅 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Shiba Tatto (司馬達等)
figures.role: A 鞍部村主 (reading unconfirmed). He searched for practitioners and had his daughter 嶋 (reading unconfirmed) take holy orders. He obtained a relic at a Buddhist feast and presented it to Umako.

figures.name: The nun Zenshin (善信尼)
figures.role: 嶋 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of Shiba Tatto. She took holy orders at the age of eleven, and on Moriya's orders was stripped of her robes and flogged.

figures.name: 恵便 (reading unconfirmed) of Koguryŏ (高麗惠便)
figures.role: A former monk who had returned to lay life in Harima. He became Umako's teacher.

figures.name: Nakatomi no Katsumi (中臣勝海)
figures.role: A high official (大夫) who, together with Moriya, petitioned that the epidemic was caused by the promotion of the Buddhist Dharma.

figures.name: 廣姫 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Daughter of Prince 息長眞手王 (reading unconfirmed). She became empress in the 4th year, gave birth to 押坂彦人大兄皇子 (reading unconfirmed), and died in the same year.

figures.name: 豐御食炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: She became empress in the 5th year. Later Empress Suiko.

figures.name: Prince Anahobe (穴穂部皇子)
figures.role: The prince who, at the court of the emperor's temporary enshrinement, spoke angry words in his desire to take the realm.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — opening of the section on Emperor Bidatsu (沼名倉太玉敷命 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: The Kojiki gives his palace as the 他田宮 (reading unconfirmed) and records that he ruled the realm for fourteen years. The Nihon Shoki says that he set up his palace at 百済大井 (reading unconfirmed) in the 1st year and built the 幸玉宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace at 譯語田 (reading unconfirmed) in the 4th year, and places his death in the 8th month of the 14th year.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — entry on the empresses, consorts and children in the section on Emperor Bidatsu
compare.text: The Kojiki lists first his half-sister 豐御食炊屋比賣命 (reading unconfirmed) and gives her eight children, whereas the Nihon Shoki says that 広姫 (reading unconfirmed) was made empress in the 4th year and, after her death, 豐御食炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed) was made empress in the 5th year, and gives her children as two sons and five daughters.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — end of the section on Emperor Bidatsu (tomb)
compare.text: The section on Emperor Bidatsu in the Kojiki ends with his empresses and consorts, children and tomb; for the entries on 王辰爾 (reading unconfirmed), 日羅 (reading unconfirmed), and the promotion and destruction of the Buddhist Dharma, no corresponding entries could be confirmed in the Kojiki.

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: In a certain text, those who plotted to destroy the Buddhist Dharma by burning the temple and pagoda and throwing away the Buddha images were three men — the Great Chieftain Mononobe no Yuge no Moriya, 大三輪逆君 (reading unconfirmed) and 中臣磐余連 (reading unconfirmed) — and Umako opposed them and did not comply. In the main text, those who petitioned that the Buddhist Dharma be stopped were Moriya and Nakatomi no Katsumi.

variants.name: An old text (舊本)
variants.text: Regarding the 恩率 (reading unconfirmed) and 参官 (reading unconfirmed) of Paekche who directed the killing of 日羅 (reading unconfirmed), a note says that the old text treats them as one 恩率 and one 参官.

yomei-sushun.kan_en: Nihon Shoki, Book 21 — Emperor Yōmei and Emperor Sushun
yomei-sushun.title: Emperor Yōmei, Emperor Sushun and the Fall of Mononobe no Moriya
yomei-sushun.lead: It is recorded that Emperor Yōmei believed in the Buddhist Dharma and revered the way of the gods (神道); in his 2nd year he fell ill and consulted his ministers, saying he wished to take refuge in the Three Treasures, but he died within that month. Before the accession of the next ruler, Emperor Sushun, Soga no Umako, together with the princes and ministers, destroyed Mononobe no Moriya, and construction of Hōkō-ji began; but in his 5th year the emperor was killed by 東漢直駒 (reading unconfirmed), who had been sent by Umako.

points.text: In the 4th month of the 2nd year, Emperor Yōmei, having fallen ill, consulted his ministers, saying, "I wish to take refuge in the Three Treasures." Moriya and Nakatomi no Katsumi objected, asking whether he would turn his back on the gods of the land and revere other gods, while Umako answered that they should follow the edict and assist him.

In the 7th month before Emperor Sushun's accession, Umako, together with the princes and ministers, attacked Moriya at 渋河 (reading unconfirmed). Prince Umayado made images of the Four Heavenly Kings from the wood of a 白膠木 (reading unconfirmed) tree and vowed to build a temple and pagoda if they won, and 迹見首赤梼 (reading unconfirmed) shot Moriya down.

After the conflict, Shitennō-ji was built in Settsu Province, and Umako, as he had vowed, founded Hōkō-ji in Asuka. In the 1st year of Emperor Sushun, monks, temple builders, a 鑪盤 (reading unconfirmed) (pagoda-finial) master, tile masters and a painter came from Paekche, and construction of Hōkō-ji began at 飛鳥眞神原 (reading unconfirmed).

In the 10th month of the 5th year, Umako heard that the emperor, pointing at a boar that had been presented, had said, "Someday I would like to cut off the head of someone I dislike, just as one cuts off the head of this boar." Fearing that he was the one disliked, Umako had 東漢直駒 (reading unconfirmed) kill the emperor in the 11th month.
A certain text says that the one who told Umako of the boar remark and of the weapons being prepared in the palace was 大伴嬪小手子 (reading unconfirmed), who resented the waning of the emperor's favor.

The Kojiki gives Emperor Yōmei's palace as the 池辺宮 (reading unconfirmed) and his reign as three years, and Emperor Sushun's palace as the 倉椅柴垣宮 (reading unconfirmed) and his reign as four years, and records only their empresses and consorts, children and tombs; entries on the attack on Moriya or the killing of the emperor could not be confirmed there.

story.text: Emperor Yōmei (橘豐日天皇 (reading unconfirmed)) was the fourth son of 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 堅塩媛 (reading unconfirmed). When Emperor Bidatsu died in the 8th month of his 14th year, he ascended the throne in the 9th month and lived at the 池辺雙槻宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in 磐余 (reading unconfirmed), making Umako Great Minister and Moriya Great Chieftain. He sent Princess 酢香手姫 (reading unconfirmed) to the Ise Shrine to serve in the worship of the Sun Deity. In the 1st month of the 1st year, Princess Anahobe no Hashihito was made empress, and Prince Umayado, Prince Kume, Prince 殖栗 (reading unconfirmed) and Prince 茨田 (reading unconfirmed) were born. It is recorded that Prince Umayado at first lived at the 上宮 (reading unconfirmed) and later moved to Ikaruga.

In the 5th month of the 1st year, Prince Anahobe, intending to violate Empress 炊屋姫 (reading unconfirmed), tried to force his way into the temporary enshrinement palace, but 三輪君逆 (reading unconfirmed) had the guards secure the gate and did not let him in. The prince demanded that 逆 (reading unconfirmed) be executed for his insolence, and together with Moriya led troops to surround 磐余 (reading unconfirmed) 池辺 (reading unconfirmed). 逆 hid on 三諸岳 (reading unconfirmed) and then at the 海石榴市宮 (reading unconfirmed), a country residence of Empress 炊屋姫, but 白堤 (reading unconfirmed) and 横山 (reading unconfirmed), men of his own clan, revealed where he was. Moriya led troops and executed 逆 and the others, and Umako lamented that disorder in the realm was not far off. A note records that because of this, Empress 炊屋姫 and Umako both came to resent Prince Anahobe.

In the 4th month of the 2nd year, on the day of the Niiname harvest rite, the emperor fell ill and consulted his ministers, saying he wished to take refuge in the Three Treasures. Moriya and Nakatomi no Katsumi objected, and Umako said they should follow the edict; but when Prince Anahobe brought the 豊国法師 (reading unconfirmed) into the palace, Moriya grew furious, withdrew to his country residence at 阿都 (reading unconfirmed), and gathered men. Nakatomi no Katsumi made images of the Crown Prince 彦人皇子 (reading unconfirmed) and of Prince Takeda and cursed them, but later submitted to 彦人皇子, and on his way back he was cut down by 迹見赤梼 (reading unconfirmed). When the emperor's sores grew worse, 鞍部多須奈 (reading unconfirmed) offered to take holy orders for the emperor's sake and to make a jōroku (sixteen-foot) Buddha image and a temple. The emperor died soon afterward and was buried in the 磐余池上陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb in the 7th month.

Emperor Sushun (泊瀬部天皇 (reading unconfirmed)) was the twelfth son of 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and his mother was 小姉君 (reading unconfirmed). In the 6th month after Emperor Yōmei's death, Umako and the others, acting under 炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed), had Prince Anahobe — whom Moriya had intended to make emperor — struck down, and the next day also killed Prince 宅部 (reading unconfirmed), who had been close to him. In the 7th month, Umako led princes including Prince 泊瀬部 (reading unconfirmed), Prince Takeda and Prince Umayado, together with the ministers, and attacked Moriya at his house at 渋河 (reading unconfirmed); but because Moriya built a rice-stalk fortress (稲城) and shot arrows like rain from up in a tree, the princes' army fell back three times. Prince Umayado made images of the Four Heavenly Kings from the wood of a 白膠木 (reading unconfirmed) tree, placed them in his hair, and vowed that if they granted him victory he would build a temple and pagoda for the Four World-Protecting Kings; Umako, too, vowed to build a temple and pagoda for the heavenly kings and great divine kings and to spread the Three Treasures. 迹見首赤梼 (reading unconfirmed) shot Moriya down from the branches and executed Moriya and his sons, and Moriya's army collapsed. After the conflict, Shitennō-ji was built in Settsu Province, and Umako also founded Hōkō-ji in Asuka.

捕鳥部萬 (reading unconfirmed), an attendant of Moriya, was guarding the house at Naniwa, but on hearing of Moriya's fall he fled to the mountains of the village of 有真香邑 (reading unconfirmed) in the district of 茅渟県 (reading unconfirmed). When he was surrounded by guardsmen, he shook bamboo with a rope to mislead them about where he was, killed more than thirty men, and then stabbed himself in the neck with a small knife and died. The court ordered his body to be cut into eight pieces and displayed in eight provinces, but the white dog that 萬 (reading unconfirmed) had kept took his head in its mouth, placed it in an old mound, lay down beside it, and starved to death. The court, moved to pity, had 萬's kin build a grave and bury 萬 and the dog at 有真香邑.

In the 8th month, at the urging of 炊屋姫尊 (reading unconfirmed) and the ministers, Prince 泊瀬部 (reading unconfirmed) ascended the throne and set up his palace at 倉梯 (reading unconfirmed). In the 1st year, a Buddha relic and monks, temple builders, a 鑪盤 (reading unconfirmed) (pagoda-finial) master, tile masters and a painter were sent from Paekche; the nun Zenshin and the others were entrusted to the Paekche envoys and sent abroad to study; and the house of 樹葉 (reading unconfirmed), ancestor of the 飛鳥衣縫造 (reading unconfirmed), was torn down and construction of Hōkō-ji began. In the 3rd month of the 3rd year, the nun Zenshin and the others returned from Paekche and lived at 桜井寺 (reading unconfirmed), and in this year 善徳 (reading unconfirmed), daughter of 大伴狭手彦連 (reading unconfirmed), and others, as well as 鞍部多須奈 (reading unconfirmed), took holy orders. In the 8th month of the 4th year, when the emperor consulted his ministers about rebuilding Mimana, the ministers agreed, and in the 11th month an army of more than twenty thousand under 紀男麻呂宿禰 (reading unconfirmed) and others as commanders-in-chief was sent out to Tsukushi.

In the 10th month of the 5th year, the emperor, pointing at a boar that had been presented, said that someday he would like to cut off the head of someone he disliked, just as one cuts off the head of this boar, and had more weapons prepared than usual. Umako, hearing of this, feared that he was the one disliked, gathered his associates, and plotted to kill the emperor. In the 11th month, Umako deceived the ministers by saying that tribute from the eastern provinces was being presented, had 東漢直駒 (reading unconfirmed) kill the emperor, and buried the emperor in the 倉梯岡陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb that same day. Afterward, it came to light that 駒 (reading unconfirmed) had secretly taken as his wife 河上娘 (reading unconfirmed), Umako's daughter and a consort (嬪) of the emperor, and 駒 was killed by Umako.

quotes.note: The emperor believed in the Buddhist Dharma and revered the way of the gods (神道).
I wish to take refuge in the Three Treasures. You are to discuss it among yourselves.
Why would you turn your back on the gods of the land and revere other gods? (words of objection by Moriya and Nakatomi no Katsumi).
When will I be able to cut down the person I dislike, just as one cuts off the head of this boar?

figures.name: 橘豐日天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Emperor Yōmei. He is regarded as having believed in the Buddhist Dharma and revered the way of the gods, and while ill he consulted his ministers about taking refuge in the Three Treasures.

figures.name: 泊瀬部天皇 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Emperor Sushun. After taking part in the attack on Moriya he ascended the throne, and in his 5th year he was killed by 東漢直駒 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Soga no Umako no Sukune (蘇我馬子宿禰)
figures.role: Great Minister. He destroyed Moriya, founded Hōkō-ji, and had Emperor Sushun killed.

figures.name: The Great Chieftain Mononobe no Moriya (物部守屋大連)
figures.role: Great Chieftain. He opposed the Buddhist Dharma and tried to put Prince Anahobe on the throne, but was destroyed at 渋河 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: Prince Anahobe (穴穗部皇子)
figures.role: A prince who, desiring the realm, had 三輪君逆 (reading unconfirmed) struck down, and was later executed by Umako and the others.

figures.name: 三輪君逆 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: A minister favored by Emperor Bidatsu. He guarded the gate of the temporary enshrinement palace and kept Prince Anahobe out, and was struck down.

figures.name: Prince Umayado (廐戸皇子)
figures.role: A son of Emperor Yōmei. In the battle with Moriya he made images of the Four Heavenly Kings and made a vow.

figures.name: 迹見首赤梼 (reading unconfirmed, except that 赤梼 is read Ichihi according to the reading note in the original)
figures.role: An attendant (舎人). He cut down Nakatomi no Katsumi and shot Moriya down. The reading note in the original says that "赤梼" is read "伊知毘".

figures.name: Nakatomi no Katsumi no Muraji (中臣勝海連)
figures.role: Together with Moriya he opposed taking refuge in the Three Treasures, and was later cut down by 迹見赤梼 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 捕鳥部萬 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: An attendant of Moriya. Cornered, he took his own life, and was buried together with his white dog.

figures.name: 東漢直駒 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: On Umako's orders he killed Emperor Sushun, and was later killed by Umako over the matter of 河上娘 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: The nun Zenshin (善信阿尼)
figures.role: The nun Zenshin. She went to Paekche to study the rules of the precepts, returned in the 3rd year, and lived at 桜井寺 (reading unconfirmed).

figures.name: 鞍部多須奈 (reading unconfirmed)
figures.role: Son of Shiba Tatto. He offered to take holy orders for Emperor Yōmei's sake, later did take holy orders, and took the name 徳齊法師 (reading unconfirmed).

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Yōmei (橘豐日命 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: The Kojiki gives Emperor Yōmei's palace as the 池辺宮 (reading unconfirmed) and records that he ruled the realm for three years. The Nihon Shoki says that he lived at the 池辺雙槻宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace in 磐余 (reading unconfirmed) and died in the 4th month of the 2nd year; its listing of Prince Umayado and others among his children corresponds to the "上宮之厩戶豐聰耳命" of the Kojiki.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — end of the section on Emperor Yōmei
compare.text: The Kojiki places Emperor Yōmei's tomb at 石寸掖上 (reading unconfirmed) and records that it was later moved to the 科長中陵 (reading unconfirmed). The Nihon Shoki records only that he was buried in the 磐余池上陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb.

compare.where: Kojiki, Part 3 — section on Emperor Sushun (長谷部若雀天皇 (reading unconfirmed))
compare.text: For Emperor Sushun, the Kojiki records only the 倉椅柴垣宮 (reading unconfirmed) palace, a reign of four years, and a tomb at 倉椅岡上 (reading unconfirmed). For the attack on Moriya, the construction of Hōkō-ji and the killing of the emperor, no corresponding entries could be confirmed in the Kojiki.

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: A note in the main text says that Princess 酢香手姫 (reading unconfirmed) served in the worship of the Sun Deity from the time of Emperor Yōmei until the reign of 炊屋姫天皇 (reading unconfirmed), but a certain text says that she served for thirty-seven years, then withdrew of her own accord and died.

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: It says that Moriya was sent to strike down 三輪君逆 (reading unconfirmed) after Prince Anahobe had consulted with Prince 泊瀬部 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: In the main text it is reported that Moriya executed 逆 (reading unconfirmed) and the others, but a certain text says that Prince Anahobe shot him dead himself.

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: It says that 東漢直駒 (reading unconfirmed), who killed the emperor, was the son of 東漢直磐井 (reading unconfirmed).

variants.name: A certain text says (或本云)
variants.text: The main text says only that Umako heard the emperor's words, but a certain text says that 大伴嬪小手子 (reading unconfirmed), who resented the waning of the emperor's favor, sent a messenger to tell Umako of the boar remark and of the weapons being prepared in the palace.

suiko-1.title: The Accession of Empress Suiko, the Twelve Cap Ranks and the Seventeen-Article Constitution
suiko-1.lead: After Emperor Sushun was killed, Empress Suiko, urged three times by the officials, ascended the throne at the Toyura Palace, made Prince Umayado no Toyotomimi Crown Prince, and entrusted all government to him. For the 1st to the 12th years, the record includes the edict to promote the Three Treasures and the completion of Hōkō-ji, the war with Silla and the death of Prince Kume, the establishment of the twelve cap ranks, and the Crown Prince's composition of the Seventeen-Article Constitution.

points.text: In the 4th month of the 1st year, Prince Umayado no Toyotomimi was made Crown Prince and, as regent, was entrusted with all affairs of state. It is written that the prince was born upon coming up against the door of a stable of the horse office, and that he could hear the petitions of ten people at once without error.

In the 4th month of the 12th year, the Crown Prince himself composed the Seventeen-Article Constitution. Article 1 teaches that harmony is to be valued; Article 2, that the Three Treasures (the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha) are to be sincerely revered; and Article 3, that when an imperial command is received it must be obeyed with care.

In the 12th month of the 11th year, cap ranks were put into effect for the first time; twelve grades, from Greater Virtue down to Lesser Knowledge, were established, and in the 1st month of the 12th year they were conferred on the ministers.

In the 2nd month of the 2nd year, the empress ordered the Crown Prince and the Great Minister to promote the Three Treasures, and the Omi, Muraji and others competed in building Buddhist halls. In the 3rd year the Koguryŏ monk Eji came and became the Crown Prince's teacher, and in the 11th month of the 4th year Hōkō-ji was completed.

In the 10th year, Prince Kume was made General for Attacking Silla and twenty-five thousand men were assembled in Tsukushi, but the prince fell ill and died in Tsukushi in the 2nd month of the 11th year. Prince 当麻 (reading unconfirmed), who replaced him, also turned back because of his wife's death, and the expedition was not carried out.

The Kojiki gives Empress Suiko's palace only as the "小治田宮", but the Nihon Shoki distinguishes between her accession at the Toyura Palace and her move to the Oharida Palace in the 10th month of the 11th year.

story.text: Empress Suiko (豊御食炊屋姫天皇 (reading unconfirmed)) was a middle daughter of 天國排開廣庭天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and the full younger sister of 橘豊日天皇 (reading unconfirmed); when young she was called Princess Nukatabe. At eighteen she became empress of 渟中倉太玉敷天皇 (reading unconfirmed), and when she was thirty-four that emperor died. When she was thirty-nine, 泊瀬部天皇 (reading unconfirmed) was killed by the Great Minister Umako no Sukune in the 11th month of his 5th year and the throne became vacant, and the ministers asked the empress to ascend the throne. The empress declined, but when the officials submitted memorials three times urging her, she agreed, and the imperial seal was presented to her. In the 12th month, the empress ascended the throne at the Toyura Palace.

In the 1st month of the 1st year, a Buddha relic was placed inside the foundation stone of the central pillar of Hōkō-ji, and the next day the central pillar was erected. In the 4th month, Prince Umayado no Toyotomimi was made Crown Prince and regent and was entrusted with all affairs of state. It is recorded that the prince was the second son of 橘豊日天皇 (reading unconfirmed) and his mother was Princess Anahobe no Hashihito; that he spoke as soon as he was born; that when grown he could hear the petitions of ten people at once without error; and that he studied Buddhist teachings under the Koguryŏ monk Eji and non-Buddhist classics under the scholar 覚哿 (reading unconfirmed). In the 9th month, 橘豊日天皇 was reburied in the 磯長陵 (reading unconfirmed) tomb in Kawachi, and in this year construction of Shitennō-ji began at 荒陵 (reading unconfirmed) in Naniwa.

In the 2nd month of the 2nd year, the empress ordered the Crown Prince and the Great Minister to promote the Three Treasures; the Omi, Muraji and others competed in building Buddhist halls for the sake of the kindness of their lords and parents, and these were called temples. In the 4th month of the 3rd year, aloeswood (沈水) drifted ashore on Awaji Island; the islanders, not knowing what it was, burned it with firewood, and because the fragrance spread far, they presented it to the court. In the same year the Koguryŏ monk Eji came to settle and became the Crown Prince's teacher, the Paekche monk Esō also came, and the two spread Buddhism and became the pillars of the Three Treasures. In the 11th month of the 4th year Hōkō-ji was completed; 善徳臣 (reading unconfirmed), son of the Great Minister, became its temple administrator, and Eji and Esō began to live there. In the 5th year the king of Paekche sent Prince 阿佐 (reading unconfirmed); in the 6th year Silla presented a peacock, and in the 7th year Paekche presented a camel and other animals; and in the 4th month of the 7th year, an earthquake destroyed houses and the empress had the god of earthquakes worshiped.

In the 2nd month of the 8th year, because Silla and Mimana were attacking each other, the empress sought to rescue Mimana. In this year, with 境部臣 (reading unconfirmed) as commander-in-chief and 穂積臣 (reading unconfirmed) as deputy general, more than ten thousand troops were sent out; they captured five Silla fortresses, and the king of Silla raised a white flag, ceded six fortresses and asked to surrender. Silla and Mimana sent envoys bearing tribute and submitted a memorial saying that from then on they would not attack each other and would pay tribute every year; but when the generals were called back, Silla again invaded Mimana. In the 2nd month of the 9th year, the Crown Prince built a palace at Ikaruga for the first time. In the 3rd month, 大伴連囓 (reading unconfirmed) was sent to Koguryŏ and 坂本臣糠手 (reading unconfirmed) to Paekche, with orders to urge them to rescue Mimana quickly, and in the 9th month 迦摩多 (reading unconfirmed), a Silla spy captured on Tsushima, was exiled to Kōzuke.

In the 2nd month of the 10th year, Prince Kume was made General for Attacking Silla and was given an army of twenty-five thousand men including the 神部 (reading unconfirmed), the Kuni-no-Miyatsuko and the Tomo-no-Miyatsuko; in the 4th month the prince set up camp in 嶋郡 (reading unconfirmed) in Tsukushi and gathered ships and provisions. But in the 6th month the prince fell ill, so the expedition could not be carried out. In the 10th month, the Paekche monk Kanroku presented calendars, books of astronomy and geography, and books of 遁甲 (reading unconfirmed) and occult arts, and selected students studied them and mastered those fields. In the 2nd month of the 11th year, Prince Kume died in Tsukushi, and the empress grieved that he had not been able to accomplish the great undertaking before him. In the 4th month, his elder brother Prince 当麻 (reading unconfirmed) was made general in his place, but in the 7th month, because his wife 舎人姫王 (reading unconfirmed), who was accompanying him, died at 赤石 (reading unconfirmed), Prince 当麻 turned back, and the expedition was not carried out.

In the 10th month of the 11th year, the empress moved to the Oharida Palace. In the 11th month, Hata no Kawakatsu received a revered Buddha image that the Crown Prince possessed, worshiped it, and built 蜂岡寺 (reading unconfirmed). In the 12th month, cap ranks were put into effect for the first time, in twelve grades: Greater Virtue, Lesser Virtue, Greater Benevolence, Lesser Benevolence, Greater Propriety, Lesser Propriety, Greater Faith, Lesser Faith, Greater Righteousness, Lesser Righteousness, Greater Knowledge and Lesser Knowledge; caps sewn from silk (絁) of the color of each rank were to be used. In the 1st month of the 12th year, cap ranks were conferred on the ministers for the first time.

In the 4th month of the 12th year, the Crown Prince himself composed the Seventeen-Article Constitution. Article 1 teaches that harmony is to be valued, Article 2 requires that the Three Treasures be sincerely revered, and Article 3 that when an imperial command is received it must be obeyed with care. There follow articles such as: that propriety is to be the foundation; that lawsuits are to be judged fairly; that officials are to come to court early and leave late; that trustworthiness is the foundation of righteousness; that one is to turn away from private interest and toward the public good; and that the people are to be employed only at suitable times; and Article 17 teaches that important matters are not to be decided by one person alone but discussed with many. In the 9th month, court etiquette was revised: it was decided that when entering or leaving the palace gate one should place both hands on the ground and kneel on both knees, and after crossing the threshold rise and walk. In the same month, the 黄書画師 (reading unconfirmed) and 山背画師 (reading unconfirmed) painters were established.

quotes.note: Value harmony above all, and make not opposing others the first principle (Article 1 of the Seventeen-Article Constitution).
Sincerely revere the Three Treasures. The Three Treasures are the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha (Article 2).
